  `display-manager.service` pointing at LordOS, an empty image tree), in `make test`. `docs/INSTALL-DEBIAN.md`,
  Troubleshooting.
- **Settings → Appearance → Browsers: no green "Done" note after the switch (#222).** Every change of "Browsers: tabs in the title bar" left "Done. The browsers use it the next time they
  open." under it, and turning the switch back off kept it there, since the last result is kept for the page's
  life. A change that simply worked now says nothing: the switch shows it, and the group's footer already says that
  it applies the next time each browser opens. What needs the person still shows (Chromium or Brave open, a profile
  that couldn't be changed, a Firefox profile whose own `user.js` sets it). The notes are chosen by
  `browserFrameNotes` in `sdk/browserframe.js` (new, pure); `settings.browserTabs.done` is gone from the 35
  languages. Test: `server/tests/browserframe_notes_test.mjs` (new, in `run_suites.sh`, 8 checks).
- **Settings → Cloud: each row of "Kept on this computer" shows its real size (#206).** Every row said 0 B, the account's whole folder ("In sync with this computer") as well as a
  folder added by hand: the rows asked `lord.fs.du`, which by design doesn't walk a cloud or network mount from the
  interface's thread and answers `size: 0, remote: true` there. `lord-server` now sizes each kept entry itself, in the
  walk of rclone's VFS cache that already gave the account's `keptBytes` (`cf_measure` in
  `server/src/cloud/cloud_files.c`, once a minute and after each pass of the keeper), and the state gives them as
  `keptSizes` (bytes in `kept`'s order, `null` for an entry kept since the last walk; `docs/CLOUD.md` 17 and 17.1).
  Entries that overlap (the whole account and a folder in it) each count their own files (`cloud_kept_tally` in
  `cloud_pure.c`). Settings shows that number (`keptRows` in `sdk/cloudmodel.js`) and never `lord.fs.du`'s on the
  mount: a row not measured yet shows no size instead of 0 B. The dev mock gives sizes too. Tests: `build/cloud-test`
  (per-entry tallies, overlapping entries, a path kept nowhere), `server/tests/cloud_model_test.mjs` (rows, unknown and
  junk sizes, the mock through keep and unkeep), and a `keptSizes` check after Keep on This Computer in
  `server/tests/cloud_integration.sh` (run by hand against rclone v1.75.2; not run for this change).
- **Settings → Cloud: "Only in the cloud" says that folders can still be kept, and an account in sync has no "Add a
  Folder…" (#207).** The choice's text ended "Nothing is kept on this
  computer.", although folders added under "Kept on this computer" are kept here; it now ends "By default nothing is
  kept on this computer; you can choose folders to keep." (`cloud.use.cloudOnlyHint`). An account "In sync with this
  computer" keeps its whole folder, so the list's **Add a Folder…** did nothing useful: it is replaced there by "The
  whole account is kept on this computer, so every folder in it is kept too." (`cloud.keptAllHint`, new; `keptAll` in
  `sdk/cloudmodel.js`). Both texts in all 35 languages. Test: `server/tests/cloud_model_test.mjs`.
- **Backups: a folder inside a Cloud account is refused as the destination (#208).** A person backed up their home into a OneDrive folder, stopped the backup and removed it, and rclone
  kept uploading thousands of small files (browser and mail profiles) for hours, with OneDrive's rate-limit errors in
  the log. A backup there can't work as designed: snapshots hard-link what didn't change, which rclone's mount can't
  do, so every run copies every file again, and what a run wrote sits in rclone's upload queue, which a stopped backup
  can't take back. Refused rather than warned about, because nothing the person can do there makes it work; the cloud
  destination of `docs/CLOUD.md` 10 (an rclone sync job with versions) is still to be built.
  - `valid_dest` (`server/src/backup/backup.c`) answers the new error `backup.destCloud` (35 languages: why, and to
    choose a disk or a folder on this computer) for a folder on rclone's mount: `fsops_cloud_path`, the mount type
    `fuse.rclone` of the longest mount point over the path in `/proc/self/mounts` (`fsops_mount_type_in` in
    `server/src/fsops.c`, which `fsops_remote_path` now uses too). Network shares (SMB, NFS), other FUSE file systems
    and NTFS disks (`fuseblk`) are not affected.
  - A destination chosen before this change is not run: the run ends at once with that error under the app's header,
    retried as a failed run (every 15 minutes) until another destination is chosen.
  - The app no longer lists the Cloud accounts' mounts among the disks (`cloudModel.isCloudVolume`).
  - **Cancelling an account's pending uploads in Settings → Cloud is not built.** rclone's remote control has no call
    that drops what waits in the VFS upload queue (`vfs/queue` lists it, `vfs/queue-set-expiry` only delays it;
    checked against rclone's rc reference on 2026-11-22); doing it would mean deleting files from rclone's cache behind
    its back. Pause holds them, and removing the account past its warning about changes waiting drops them.
  - Test: `build/fsops-test` (mount types from a mounts file: an rclone mount, one with a space in its name, a disk
    mounted inside it, a folder whose name only starts like the mount's, SMB, `fuseblk`, a local FUSE pool, an
    unreadable file).
- **Print Screen said "Screenshots does not have permission to record the screen" with no way to allow it (GitHub
  #219).** Three things together:
  - **The real reason is shown.** `sdk/media.js` turned every exception from `lord.media.screenshot` and `screenRecord`
    into `null`, and Screenshots took `null` as "the permission was refused", so any failure (`media.captureFailed`,
    a capture lord-server could not make) read as a permission problem. The SDK now passes lord-server's code on, and
    Screenshots shows the permission text and **Open Privacy** only for `media.denied.*` and `fw.restricted.*`; any
    other failure is told as it is (`apps/screenshots/toolbarmodel.js` `refusal`, tested).
  - **Screenshots starts with the screen permission allowed** (approved by the maintainer 2026-11-22): pressing Print
    Screen or a capture shortcut is the person asking for the capture. It is a default under the saved decisions, not a
    decision written for the person: `perm_builtin_default`/`perm_get_builtin` in `server/src/sec/perms.c`, read only by
    the desktop's own contexts (`js_media.c`'s check, `lord.perms.get`), never by the broker, and only for the id
    `screenshots` and the `screen` permission (no package can take that id, `lpk_reserved`). A "Don't Allow" saved in
    Settings → Privacy wins and sticks across sessions; firewall restrictions (`no-screen`) still win over both. Tests:
    `tests/perms_default_test.c` (new; only that pair, never perm_get's, a deny wins and survives a new session).
  - **Settings → Privacy lists built-in apps** whose manifest declares a permission even before they ever asked (it
    listed packages and saved decisions only, so Screenshots was missing), and a permission that starts allowed offers
    Allow and Don't Allow (Ask would only bring the default back): `apps/settings/privacymodel.js`, tested by
    `tests/privacy_model_test.mjs` (new); `lord.perms.builtinDefault`.
  - **Protected windows are exactly as protected as before**, now checked by tests: in a capture of the whole screen or
    an area, and in recordings and the remote desktop, a protected window (Passwords, the on-screen keyboard, "Protect
    the front window", a Linux window marked so) is black, painted so by lord-server (`paint.c` capture mode,
    `media/capture.c`, `wl.c`). And a protected window asked for alone (Screenshots' window capture) is now **refused**
    (`media.protectedWindow`, new text in all 35 languages) with nothing painted for it, where before its frame came out
    with its content black: `paint_capture_until` returns -1 for a window that is, holds or is inside a protected node,
    and Screenshots does not fall back to cropping a capture of the screen. `engine-test`'s new
    `test_capture_protected`.
- **Clipboard history: the full panel (❖⇧V) no longer scrolls by itself, and the arrow keys work (GitHub #203, #204).** The list drew a window of 16 entries around the selection and a row
  took the selection when the pointer entered it: with the pointer resting on the list, every arrow key moved that
  window, another row slid under the still pointer and took the selection back, so the list crept up or down on its own
  near the edges and the keys seemed to do nothing. It is now an ordinary scrolling list with every entry (the wheel,
  its bar, the keys), the arrow keys move a highlighted selection that is scrolled into view, and only then, Enter pastes
  it, and a row under the pointer takes the selection only when the pointer itself moves (both panels, ❖V too). Of up
  to 500 entries only the rows in sight and a few around are made, the rest is empty space of their height.
  `sdk/clipboardpanelmodel.js` (`stepSel`, `scrollFor`, `rowWindow`, `hoverGate`), tested by `tests/clipboard_panel_model_test.mjs`
  (new).
- **The screen comes back on when the computer wakes from sleep (GitHub #214).** Opening the lid (or the power button) woke the computer with the screen still dark until a key was pressed.
  On logind's `PrepareForSleep(false)` the session on the monitor now counts it as activity
  (`server/src/hw/sleeplock.c` `woke` → `display_activity`, which turns the displays on and restarts the idle timers),
  right after the theme heard "resume", so the lock on waking (`lockAfterWake`, Settings' lock delay) still comes first and the
  lock screen is what shows. A session that is not on the monitor does not touch the screen. `sleeplock-test` checks
  both.
- **Store: the Flathub home's category tiles keep one width on every row** (`apps/store/flathubpages.js`,
  `CategoryTiles`). The tiles grew to fill their row, so a last row with fewer tiles (four of ten at 1600 px) made each
  of them wider than the ones above; five empty, zero-height cells with the tiles' own flex now fill that row. Seen in
  `server/tests/store_rankings_headless.sh`'s screenshots.
- **Store, Flathub: the counts agree with the lists, and a card's one-line texts end in an ellipsis.** Found on the screenshots of Flathub's home with the rankings (E10), taken in a
  headless lord-server with this machine's Flathub catalog (3381 apps, 2243 verified) and Flathub's recorded answers of
  2026-11-22 (`server/tests/store_rankings_headless.sh`, new; en and es, 1600x900; a live fetch from flathub.org in the
  same setup filled all six lists).
  - **All in the second column** said 2734 over a list of 2243 apps: it was the sum of the categories' counts, and a
    Flathub app is often in several. It is now how many apps the section shows (`flathubModel.shownCount`,
    `useFlathubTotal`); Debian's and the web apps' counts are unchanged (one category per app).
  - **A category listed twice by an app** (some of Flathub's catalog has `Graphics;…;Graphics;`) counted twice:
    Graphics said 217 while its page and its All chip said 216. `categoryCounts` counts each app once per category,
    as `subcategoryCounts` already did.
  - **The kind line and the foot's note of a Store card** (category · developer, "✓ Verified") were cut through a
    letter ("Utilities · Ronnie Nis"); they now end in "…" like the name above them (`apps/store/ui.js`).
  - Tests: `flathub_model_test.mjs` (a category listed twice, `shownCount` against the list on the recorded catalog),
    `store_card_scene.mjs` (new, in `make test`).
- **The capture indicator names what it called "an unknown program".** Found on the maintainer's ws126 (Lord Flow): the panel by the clock said "An unknown program — Screen"
  (with Stop sharing) and "An unknown program — Microphone" while Google Chrome shared the screen in a call.
  - **The cause:** Chrome and Chromium move their browser process into a unit of the user's own service manager
    (`user@<uid>.service/app.slice/app-com.google.Chrome-<pid>.scope`, Chromium's own systemd scope), and every
    process it starts afterwards (the audio service that records the microphone) is created there too. The
    ScreenCast portal's caller (the browser process, from the bus's credentials) and the PipeWire guard's capture
    stream owner (the audio service, the pulse client's checked pid) were then in no app's scope. The renderers and
    the zygote, made before the move, stay in Chrome's scope. Other paths that ended in "unknown": a LordOS web app's
    WebKit process, a pulse client inside WebKit's own bubblewrap sandbox (it reports pid 2 and a made-up Flatpak id
    `org.webkit.app-<hash>`, so the pid can't be verified); PipeWire's own processes (pipewire-pulse's modules, the
    session's pipewire, `filter-chain.service`, WirePlumber); a program started from the Terminal; any process with
    no app at all.
  - **Named from what the kernel says, only to show it** (`sec/appid.c` `appid_of_lineage`, `appid_session_owner`):
    a process is created in its parent's cgroup and only root puts one into the session's root-owned scopes, so a
    process in the user's manager with a child in an app's scope, or whose parent is in one, was in that scope: it is
    that app's. The walk goes up through the user's manager only (never its `init.scope`, never another user's
    process, at most 16 steps) and names an app only when every such child agrees. A unit name under `user@` is never
    trusted, and a process whose parent is lord-server is never called LordOS. A sandboxed pulse client is named by
    the one app whose scope holds a process with its inner pid that holds enough connections to pipewire-pulse
    (`pwguard_sandbox_pick`, the check the Flatpak path already makes); two candidates name neither. The sound
    system's own processes are named by their exact unit and root-owned executable. What still can't be named shows
    its executable (`/proc/<pid>/exe`, never the comm a process sets): "An unknown program (arecord)".
  - **What each case shows now:** Chrome's share and microphone are one row, "Google Chrome", with Stop sharing and
    Turn off (its no-mic, which the guard already enforces on processes that left a restricted app's scope); a web
    app's microphone or camera, the web app's name and Turn off; "The sound system (PipeWire)"; a program started
    from the Terminal, "Terminal"; a running machine's scope and Machines' own microphone, "Machines — <the
    machine's name>" (`markDeviceUse` takes a detail; each machine its own entry); a screenshot taken by such a
    program, its name too. Turn off is offered only for an app's own firewall restriction, never for a machine's
    scope, a LordOS component or LordOS itself.
  - **What is unchanged:** the restrictions, the ScreenCast and Screenshot gates, the restore token and the chooser
    still use only the verified scope (`appid_of_pid`); the new names reach only the indicator (`capture-use` gains
    `sys` and `exe`; `portal-casts` and `portal-shot-taken` gain `seen` and `exe`).
  - **Tests:** `build/pwguard-test` (a fixture process table: Chrome's browser process and audio service, the user
    manager and its children, a user unit named like an app's scope, children in two apps, a parent in an app's
    scope, lord-server as a parent, the Terminal, a machine, another user's and another session's processes, a loop;
    the session owner of a cgroup; the executable's name; the sandbox pick; the indicator's JSON with `sys` and
    `exe`), `tests/capture_model_test.mjs` (the maintainer's case as one row with both buttons, a web app, the sound
    system, executables, the Terminal, a machine, Machines' microphone with two machines),
    `tests/screencast_model_test.mjs` (`castAskerName` for machines and LordOS's parts, `castWhoName`). New text in
    all 35 languages (`shell.cast.unknownExe`, `shell.capture.who.sound`, `shell.capture.appDetail`).
- **Machines: clicks with the mouse free, resolutions, and apps mode's windows on a guest with two displays** (LordOS guest tools **w10**; found on the maintainer's guest with an Intel GVT-g vGPU, ws126 and tools
  w9, whose desktop has the vGPU's output and a second display that isn't on a PCI adapter).
  - **Clicks land where they're aimed with the mouse free.** The guest maps QEMU's absolute tablet (a HID mouse) over
    its *primary* display only, not over its whole desktop: its tablet input carries no `MOUSE_VIRTUAL_DESKTOP`. The
    mapping of before (`vd_abs_map` over the whole desktop) put a click on a 1920x1080 shown display beside a 1784x830
    second one at about half its x (in Notepad the caret went elsewhere, the Start button missed). lord-vm now computes
    the layout with `ag_tablet_layout` (`vmagent.c`): with the shown display primary the picture is all the tablet
    covers (no layout, every pixel 1:1); with another display primary the tablet can't reach the picture at all, which
    is said in lord-vm's log once, and the tools make the shown display primary again (below). The tools no longer
    leave it to an assumption: they read the tablet's own raw input in the background (`RIDEV_INPUTSINK` for mice,
    nothing taken from anyone) and say how the guest maps it (`AGK_TABLET`, 21, one byte: 1 the primary display, 2 the
    whole desktop; a strict parser), and lord-vm uses the whole-desktop layout of before only when they say 2. The tools'
    log (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\LordOS\lordos-guest-win.log`) shows the first three moves with where the guest put the pointer
    against both readings, so the mapping is measured, not guessed. `vm-test` checks every layout of the maintainer's
    log in both mappings (each picture pixel within 2 of its guest pixel through QEMU's scale) and the parser.
  - **The shown display stays the guest's primary.** w8 made it primary once per set of displays; a change of size on
    it then let the guest put the other display at 0,0 as primary (the log flipped between "at 0,0 primary" and "at
    1784,0" within a second, and sometimes stayed so: clicks, the taskbar and new windows went out of sight). The tools
    now put it back after every change of mode and whenever they find another display primary, at most once in 2 s and
    five times a minute (a guest that keeps undoing it isn't fought with).
  - **Resolutions settle.** The tools asked the guest's display configuration for a size that wasn't listed yet on
    every 250 ms try for 4 s, each one a mode set the person saw (the flicker after a change of resolution); now twice
    at most. A size the guest changes by itself right after it was set (a vGPU's monitor comes back with a new EDID
    after QEMU's ui_info, and the guest applies the mode it remembers for it: 1920x1080 set, 1400x1050 half a second
    later, and it stayed) is asked again, twice at most per request and within 30 s of it, never when it is the closest
    mode the tools themselves ended with.
  - **Apps mode's windows show their own window after a change of resolution.** The tools made the window list with
    the shown display's corner from before the change until 500 ms after it, so a window's crop showed part of one
    display, part of the other and a black block. The list now looks the displays up again every time, a change of
    the displays marks it at once and sends it even when nothing in it changed, and Machines holds a window's picture
    (black, not a wrong part) after a change of the picture's size until the guest's next list, 1.5 s at most
    (`cropsStale`, model.js).
  - **The ~1 s stutter after a change of resolution, also with the mouse captured**: not reproduced here (it needs the
    GVT-g guest). QEMU's "Failed to call update: Timeout was reached" lines in that log mean a display update waited
    1 s for its answer; lord-vmdisplay answers within 250 ms in `vmdisplay-test`, so the wait is either QEMU's own main
    loop or lord-server reading the vGPU's picture. The changes above remove the mode sets and display flips that came
    after each change; whether the stutter goes with them is still to be checked on that guest.
- **Machines: apps mode's windows have no LordOS frame, and the panel has the machine's bar.** A guest
  window in apps mode is now only the guest's window, with its own title bar and caption buttons (`args.csd`, as a
  Linux app that draws its own bar; every theme then shows the content with its shadow; rounded 8 px unless it fills
  the guest's screen), as other hypervisors' seamless modes do: its own buttons minimize, maximize and close it in
  the guest and dragging its title bar moves it there, and the LordOS window follows from the guest's next list. A
  press on a guest window is now mapped as the window was at the press for as long as the button is held, also when
  the pointer leaves it (`anchorPoint`, model.js): mapped through the window as it was a moment later, each move of
  the guest's window pushed the point further and a dragged window ran away from the pointer. Resizing from the
  LordOS window's edges asks the guest as before. The machine's menus stay in the menu bar, the Dock's menu, the
  machine's panel and its status item by the clock. Apps mode's panel (Running, Open an app) now has the machine's
  bar: the agent, clipboard, shared folders; keys, devices, sound; the console, logs, screenshot, recording; pause and
  power; Configure, wrapped over the rows it needs (the resolution, Capture mouse and full screen have no use in apps
  mode). With the console open the panel is taller.
- **The Screenshots bar's Options menu opened below the bar, off the bottom of the screen.** The bar sits near the
  bottom of the screen in a bare floating window only as tall as the bar, and the menu chose its side by that window, so
  it always opened downward. A `Popover` can now be given an `area` (a screen box) in place of the window: the bar passes
  the work area of the display it is on, so the menu opens above the bar when there is more room there, moves sideways
  to stay on that display, and is never taller than the room on its side (`popoverRoom` in `sdk/controlmodel.js`); the
  rows scroll when even that is too short, for example on a small screen with the bar dragged to the middle. Other
  popovers keep their behaviour. Tests: `control_model_test.mjs` (the room above a bar near the bottom, below a control
  near the top, a second display) and the toolbar scene.
- **The Timer desktop widget fits its card at every size and in every language**
  (`sdk/deskwidgets.jsx` TimerBody, new `sdk/timerwidgetmodel.js`; `server/tests/timer_widget_test.mjs`,
  `server/tests/workspaces_scene.mjs`). At the small size (one 170 px cell) and on the timer half of the medium one,
  the three presets ("1 min", "5 min", "25 min") sat on a wrapping row of 30 px pills, so "25 min" fell to a second
  row that the card's bottom edge cut off; the stopwatch's "Start"/"Reset" pills could overflow their half the same
  way in German ("Starten"/"Zurücksetzen"). The layout now comes from a pure model: each row of pills is a single row
  whose style (font 13 → 12 → 11 → 10.5 px, smaller padding and height) is the largest that keeps every label whole,
  measured with `lord.measureText`; when even the smallest doesn't fit, the "1 min" preset is dropped first, then
  "25 min" ("5 min" stays), and a label still too long is cut with an ellipsis. The ring's size and the time's font
  follow the room left under it, the stopwatch's figure shrinks to its column, and the medium size splits into two
  columns of equal width with the rule between them. An idle timer's ring now shows the duration a tap starts (the
  last one used, else 5:00) instead of "—", and tapping the ring starts, pauses or resumes it; tapping the
  stopwatch's figure starts or pauses it. The ring also fills again as the time runs (its fraction divided the
  remaining milliseconds by the duration × 1000, so it barely moved). The new test lays the widget out at both of
  its sizes (the timer has no large size), in each state, with times up to 10:00:00, in all 35 UI languages with a
  measure wider than the UI font, and checks that every part stays inside the card's content box, each row of pills
  inside its column, the columns apart and equal, and all three presets whole in English and Spanish; the workspaces
  scene checks the idle widget shows 5:00, the presets and the stopwatch.
- **Machines: lord-vm's log no longer goes silent for the rest of a run** (seen live on 2026-11-22).
  After a machine's window closed, QEMU went on calling the closed D-Bus display listener and wrote `Failed to call
  update: The connection is closed` twice every 30 ms; 32,000 such lines reached `lord-vm.log`'s 4 MB cap in 15 minutes,
  and from then on lord-vm wrote nothing (no agent, display or state lines). Now a child's stderr (QEMU, passt) is logged
  in whole lines (a QEMU message used to come out cut in two, its timestamp on one line); a line that comes again with
  the same text, QEMU's own timestamp aside, is logged once and then counted (`qemu: (the line before came N more times
  in S s)`, at most every 10 s and when another line comes); and a full log is rotated (`lord-vm.log` → `lord-vm.1.log`
  → `lord-vm.2.log`, at most 12 MB in all) instead of stopping. QEMU's dead listener itself is QEMU's (its D-Bus display
  has no call to drop one; lord-vmdisplay already closes its connection). `src/vm/vmlog.c`, test `build/vmlog-test`
  (the incident's 60,000 lines give one line and a summary every 10 s; cut writes; rotation keeps three files).
- **Machines' apps mode with an Intel vGPU: the two linear copies of the picture never show rows of an older frame** (`src/gpu/gband.h`, `ui/js_vm.c`; `docs/MACHINES-GPU.md`). The rows a copy lacked were added only to the
  copy shown; with none shown (the shown copy had just been imported again by the desktop's GPU, e.g. after a new GPU
  context) the other copy kept an old frame's rows and showed them next. They are now added to the other copy whether it
  is shown or not; both copies are copied whole when the picture's dmabuf changes (a new attach, the guest flipping to
  another buffer) and when lord-vmdisplay announces a picture (an attach or another size), when the texture of the
  picture before is also dropped; and a new copy is cleared to black on the iGPU before its first use, so a row never
  shows what its memory held. Seen as stripes of coloured noise in an apps mode window after lord-server restarted while
  the machine ran; the cause on that computer isn't proven (no log: see above), **to be checked** on the maintainer's
  RX 580 + UHD 630. Test `build/gband-test`: a model of both copies over 200,000 random frames with attaches, re-imports
  and dmabuf changes (it caught the copy-not-shown bug).
- **Machines' apps mode: a guest window's own icon in the Dock after a re-attach** (`apps/machines/
  appsmode.jsx`, `model.js` `iconsToAsk`; `src/vm/lordvm.c`). Icons were asked of the session only when the guest's icons
  changed, so a window whose LordOS window opened from a later list (minimized in the guest when apps mode began, or
  listed after its icon came, as when lord-server restarted while the machine ran) kept a letter tile for good. Now every
  window without its icon asks on each new list. And lord-vm keeps the last icon of each listed window and gives them to
  a client that turns apps mode on, since the guest sends each window's icon once. Checks in `tests/vm_model_test.mjs`.
- **Firefox's drop-down lists and tooltips show and go away again** (the open item of October 19,
  "Firefox ignored mouse clicks", checked on VM 127 on 2026-11-22; `docs/WAYLAND.md`, "Two wl_seat bindings (Firefox)").
  Firefox binds `wl_seat` twice (GTK 3's and its own) and gets two pointers and two keyboards: that was checked with
  `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and is right, each resource gets every event once with its own `frame` and serial, and the page's
  clicks, links, fields, tabs, menus and drag and drop all reacted. What looked dead were the `<select>` lists: GTK 3
  maps them (and tooltips) as desync subsurfaces of the window, and lord-server's partial repaint painted only the
  window's own last damage for a subsurface's commit and nothing when one was destroyed, unmapped or moved, so a closed
  list stayed on screen and the next one never showed. A subsurface's commit now damages its own box, and one that
  comes, moves, is unmapped or destroyed damages its whole window (drawn again on the GPU path); `set_position` now takes
  effect when the parent's commit is applied (a held one brings the places it was committed with), not with the
  subsurface's own commit. Also, a `wl_pointer` made while the pointer is already over that client's surface
  gets its `enter` at once (it got none until the pointer left and came back, so its clicks had no focus). Tests:
  `build/seat2-client` (`tests/seat2_client.c`, inside a session: two `wl_seat` bindings, the event stream of each
  pointer and keyboard, a third pointer made over the window) and `wlperf-client subsurface` in
  `tests/wlperf_headless.sh` (desync subsurfaces shown, redrawn, destroyed, made elsewhere and moved; every frame equals
  a full repaint; the old build's stale menus were shown with the same client on VM 127, captured step by step).
- **Drag and drop with X11 apps works** (XDND, built in 0.8.8.8, checked on VM 127 for the first time on
  2026-11-22 with Firefox on X11 and on Wayland and with Files; `docs/WAYLAND.md`, "Drag and drop"). Wayland → X11 and
  Files → X11 already worked. X11 → anything never did: the X app's answer to the conversion of `XdndSelection` was
  ignored as forged because it came with `SendEvent`, which is how every selection owner answers (ICCCM), so no X drag
  delivered its data; the right check is that it answers our conversion exactly, then who owns the selection, which is
  asked again before each read. And X drags of files never reached Files: Xwayland itself, the X server's own entry in
  X-Resource's list (resource base 0), runs in a user namespace of its own and counted as a sandboxed client; it is not
  a client and is left out. Last, a drop Files claimed at the release (before the app's `XdndDrop`) told the X app it was
  refused although the files were copied; it is now told the result. `build/xwm-test` covers the first two.
- **lord-server crashed when a theme switch failed and the running theme could not be loaded back** (`src/main.c`
  `switch_theme`, `src/ui/js.c`; reported by the maintainer, 2026-11-22 13:41, package ws123). The crash was
  `segfault at 170 … lord-server[2b8f60]`. A rebuild of `test/ws123` (`ad983794`) has `.text` byte-for-byte the
  package's, and 0x2b8f60 is the first instruction of QuickJS's `JS_GetGlobalObject()`, reading `ctx->global_obj`
  with a NULL context. The session log shows the path:
  - The maintainer chose another theme (Workspaces). The verified-code check refused it: "size differs from the
    manifest". The package had been updated under the running session, and the code manifest checked is the one read
    at login.
  - Going back to Default was refused for the same reason ("did not load again either").
  - That left lord-server with no JavaScript context at all, and the main loop's next `js_tick` → `call_hot` →
    `call_global_atom` crashed on it.

  Now a switch that can't go back shows the recovery screen, as a failed start already did (`start_theme`). Every
  entry point from C into the theme (`js_tick`, `js_wants_frame`, `js_frame`, input, Wayland and the other events)
  also does nothing when there is no context.

  Test: `tests/theme_switch_headless.sh` (in `run_suites.sh`) switches a headless lord-server to a theme that throws,
  after the running theme's file was removed. The ws123 binary crashes there with the same `segfault at 170` at
  `2b8f60`. Now lord-server goes on with the recovery screen.
- **Theme switches work after a package update, without logging out** (`server/src/sec/codesig.c` `codesig_reload`, approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-22). lord-server read
  and verified the signed code manifest only once, at login, so after `dpkg` updated LordOS under a running session
  every theme switch was refused ("size differs from the manifest") until the next log in; this is also what led to the
  crash above. Now, before each bundle check, the verified-code check looks at the manifest pair's identity
  (`code-manifest.json` and `code-manifest.sig`: device, inode, size, change and modification times), and when it
  changed, or when a bundle does not match the manifest in use, it reads the pair again:
  - From the same LordOS folder, through the descriptor opened at login (never a path the user can change), with the
    same reader as the login check (now shared): each file read whole from one descriptor, `O_NOFOLLOW` (a link is
    refused, at login too), regular files only, the same size limits.
  - Only in a **verified** session (signed manifest at login), only a **signed** manifest whose signature verifies with
    the key compiled into lord-server, through the same `codesig_parse` as at login, and only when the folder and both
    files are owned by root and writable by nobody else.
  - **Never an older version**: the manifest's `version` is compared in dpkg's order and an older one is refused; the
    same version (a rebuild signed again) is accepted.
  - **Rate-limited:** each pair on disk is read at most once (a pair caught half-written by `dpkg`, new manifest and
    old signature, is refused, and read again when the signature arrives), and reads are at least one second apart.
  - Only when everything verifies is the new manifest put in place, with one atomic pointer store (the app host's
    bytecode thread sees the old one or the new one, never a mix; the replaced one is kept until the process ends, at
    most 32 per session). The bundle is then checked once more, with the same bytes already read, so what is checked
    is still what runs. Otherwise the manifest read before stays, and the refusal says why ("the updated manifest was
    not accepted: …").
  - A theme the check refused during an update can be chosen again once a newer manifest is in use
    (`codesig_generation`; Settings → Appearance no longer marks it as failed). The running theme keeps working; a
    development session (unsigned manifest) never reads a changed manifest.

  Tests: `build/codesig-test` (100 checks, a throwaway key): a valid new manifest is accepted and the updated bundle
  loads; a bad signature, another key, a truncated manifest, no signature, a symlinked manifest, a manifest, signature
  or folder writable by others, a manifest not owned by the trusted owner and an older version are all refused with the
  old manifest kept; the rate limit; no reload in a development session; a symlinked manifest at login; dpkg's version
  order. `tests/theme_switch_headless.sh` adds "package updated under the session": a headless lord-server with a code
  manifest, theme b and the manifest replaced as `dpkg` does, then the switch: b is refused, the changed unsigned
  manifest is not taken, and the running theme comes back and keeps working.
- **Two lord-server crashes in the maintainer's session: what was found, the fixes, and a crash report for the next
  one** (reported by the maintainer, 2026-11-22). Neither crash left a stack: the package's `lord-server` is stripped
  and no core is kept. What could be established, and what was changed:
  - *10:06, package ws119* (`segfault at 20 … in lord-server[2c45e7]`): `ff27c948` was rebuilt with the same flags,
    and its `.text` is byte-for-byte the package's. Offset `0x2c45e7` is QuickJS's `find_own_property()` inlined in
    `JS_DefineProperty()`, reading `p->shape->prop_hash_mask` with `shape == NULL`. `free_object()` sets the shape to
    NULL, so a property was defined on a **JS object that had already been freed**. The caller is not known. A
    reference-count audit of every native binding (`server/src/ui/js*.c`) found no over-release. The likeliest
    remaining suspect, now removed, is the stall sampler: in that session it ran once a second (the log shows a stack
    sample on every slow `__lordTick`) and it evaluated `new Error().stack` from QuickJS's interrupt handler. That
    means compiling and running JavaScript and allocating objects at any point of the interpreter (a loop's back edge,
    a call's entry, inside a regex). The sampler and the watchdog's JS stack now read QuickJS's frames directly with
    `JS_GetStackText()`, a LordOS patch in `third_party/quickjs`: it runs no JavaScript, creates no JS value and
    prints the same one-line format.
  - *12:05, package ws122* (`segfault at 7fffeaa61e1c … error 6 in libc.so.6[6259d]`): a write 0x4c bytes above
    the stack pointer, in the frame of glibc's printf engine (`sub $0x4f8,%rsp` just before). That is a **main-thread
    stack overflow** with a printf at the bottom. A call graph of the ws122 build (`gcc -fcallgraph-info=su`, `.text`
    byte-for-byte the package's) lists every recursive cycle. Each directory walk has a depth limit, and the
    JavaScript engine's own limit (4 MB) is half the stack, so the overflow had to come from a cycle in a tree or
    from re-entry. The ones found and closed:
    - **wl_subcompositor accepted a surface as the child of itself or of its own descendant.** wayland.xml requires
      `bad_parent`; only "itself" was refused, and with the wrong error. A cycle sent `damage_node()` and the paint,
      hit-test and output walks round it for ever: against the ws122 binary, `tests/cycle_client.c` hangs the main
      loop at 100 % CPU until the watchdog steps in. `get_subsurface` now refuses a parent that is the surface or one
      of its descendants (`bad_parent`) and a surface that already has a window or menu role (`bad_surface`).
      `xdg_surface.get_popup` refuses a parent that is the popup itself or one of its own menus
      (`invalid_popup_parent`).
      A security review then found a mixed case. A surface could first get an xdg_surface, then become a subsurface,
      then a menu. It ended up linked twice, in its parent's `kids[]` and as a menu of another surface, and the
      parent-chain check did not follow the edges the walks use. Now a surface with an xdg_surface can't become a
      subsurface (`bad_surface`), and a subsurface can't take a window or menu role (`role`). The cycle check walks
      exactly the edges the walks follow (`surf_reaches`: subsurfaces and menus). As a safety net, the recursive walks
      (`origin`, `paint_tree`, `draw_tree`, `blit_tree`, `surface_at`) stop 64 levels down and log it once, so a tree
      that is cut never runs the stack out.
    - **The X window manager could re-enter its own shutdown** (`src/wl/xwm.c`). When a write to Xwayland failed,
      `lost()` called `xwm_stop()`, which ends a drag and unmaps every X window through wl.c. Those calls send to X
      again, so a second failed write called `xwm_stop()` from inside itself and freed the same window twice. The
      connection is now marked closed before anything is torn down, a nested call returns, and `free_win` unlinks the
      window before it calls out.
    - **UI node cycles:** `lord.appendChild`/`insertBefore` with a node and its own ancestor (a stale id: ids are
      reused once a node is destroyed) closed a cycle that `invalidate_measure` would loop on for ever, and that
      layout and paint would recurse on. Such a call is now ignored (`src/ui/node.c`).
  - **Crash report** (`src/wdog.c` `wdog_crash_hooks`, called first thing in `main`): on SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGILL,
    SIGFPE or SIGABRT, lord-server writes the signal, the faulting address, its version and build, and the C stack
    (`backtrace_symbols_fd`, `lord-server(+0x2c45e7)` frames) to the session log. The handler runs on an alternate
    stack, so a stack overflow is reported too. It allocates nothing. A fault then happens again with the default
    action, so the kernel still logs it; an abort is raised again. `tools/iso/mkdeb.sh` gains `DEBUG_SYMBOLS=1`, which
    keeps lord-server's and lord-sessiond's symbols as `<package>.debug/*.debug` next to a test package (never inside
    it), for `addr2line`.
  - **Smaller bugs found on the way:**
    - **Passwords were wiped inside QuickJS's own strings.** Five native functions wiped the pointer
      `JS_ToCString` returns (Machines' unattended-install and root passwords, the Imager's password hash and Wi-Fi
      key, the Terminal's SFTP request). For an ASCII string that pointer is the `JSString` itself, so the value
      JavaScript still held turned into zeros. They now copy the secret and wipe the copy (`src/ui/js_secret.h`).
    - `lord.sys` keyboard layouts read a string after freeing it (`f_kb_list`).
  - Tests: `tests/cycle_client.c` (run by `tests/run_suites.sh` against a headless lord-server, through
    `tests/popup_headless.sh cycle-client`) covers a subsurface of itself, under its child and under its grandchild,
    a popup of itself, two popups each the other's parent, and a nested subsurface tree that must still work. Further
    cases: a surface with an xdg_surface made a subsurface, a subsurface given an xdg_surface, a menu made a
    subsurface of its own subsurface, and a window → menu → subsurface → subsurface chain that must work, with a cycle
    in it refused.
    `wdog_test.c` covers the JS stack read from the interrupt handler and the crash report: a stack overflow ends in
    SIGSEGV with a complete report on the alternate stack, and an abort ends in SIGABRT.
- **Store → For this computer: no firmware card for a file no package has** (`sdk/suggestengine.js`,
  `assets/store/suggestions.json` `firmware.notShipped`; reported by the maintainer): on a computer that gives its Intel
  graphics to a machine (GVT-g), the kernel asks for `i915/gvt/vid_…_rid_….golden_hw_state`, a cache of the vGPU's
  starting state that GVT-g builds itself when the file isn't there and that no Debian package ships. The Graphics
  firmware card named it as if firmware-intel-graphics would bring it. Such files are now left out: the card appears
  only for real missing firmware (here `i915/kbl_dmc_ver1_04.bin`, the display engine's power-saving firmware) and
  names only that. Tests: `suggest_engine_test.mjs`.
- **Store: a Flathub app's license reads as a license, with a link** (`sdk/flathubmodel.js` `licenseView`,
  `apps/store/ui.js` `Facts`, `apps/store/flathubpages.js`; reported by the maintainer): the License fact showed
  Flathub's raw value, so a proprietary app read "LicenseRef-proprietary=https://gitlab.com/…", cut off. It now says
  "Proprietary" and, when the app names where its license is, is a link that opens it in the default browser; a single
  SPDX license (GPL-3.0-or-later, MIT…) links to its page on spdx.org, and an expression (MIT AND Apache-2.0) shows as
  given. Only an https address with no spaces or control characters, at most 512 bytes, becomes a link; the Store
  never downloads the license itself. Tests: `flathub_model_test.mjs`. New text in all 35 languages.
- **Machines: a machine's ··· menu is never cut by the window** (`apps/machines/library.jsx` `CardMenu`, `model.js`
  `menuSpot`, `popMenuHeight`, `displayUnder`; reported by the maintainer): the library's card and row menu was drawn
  inside the window and placed for a menu of 330 px, so with Clone, Logs, Show in Files and Open Transfer Folder its
  last rows went past the window's bottom edge. It is now drawn in the desktop's popover layer, over the window and
  the Dock, below the ··· button or the pointer, above them when the display has no room below, and always inside the
  display it opened on (a second, shorter monitor too). Tests: `vm_model_test.mjs` (placement below, above, too tall
  both ways, the screen's edges, a second display).

- **Machines: a guest with more than one display shows the right one, in apps mode too**
  (`lordos-guest-win` **w7**; Machines offers the update). On a guest with an Intel GVT-g vGPU, the guest had a
  1022 × 724 primary display next to the 1920 × 1080 output the machine's window shows. `lordos-guest-win` measured and
  moved everything on the primary and the virtual desktop: lord-vm kept logging "the guest's display is 1022x724 (not
  the size asked for)", each apps mode window showed the wrong part of the picture (Explorer about 200 pixels lower, the
  browser only wallpaper), and after leaving apps mode the guest's windows were on the display nobody sees (only
  Win+Shift+← brought one back).
  - The tools now pick the **shown display**: the only one; else the one they chose before while it stays; else the one
    whose mode is the size the host asked for (a PCI adapter first, then the primary); else the primary on a PCI
    adapter, the first on a PCI adapter, the primary. The size the host asks for is set on it.
- **Machines: a guest with more than one display shows the right one, in apps mode too** (the guest
  tools `lordos-guest-win` **w9**; Machines offers the update). On the maintainer's guest with an Intel GVT-g vGPU, the
  guest system had a 1022 × 724 primary display that isn't on a PCI adapter (a basic or indirect display) next to the
  vGPU's output, the one the machine's window shows. The tools measured and moved everything on the primary and the
  virtual desktop: lord-vm kept logging "the guest's display is 1022x724 (not the size asked for)", each apps mode
  window showed the wrong part of the picture (Explorer about 200 pixels lower, the browser only wallpaper), and after
  leaving apps mode the guest's windows were on the display nobody sees. w7 (never released) chose by size alone and
  locked onto the basic display; the real guest's log showed it.
  - The tools pick the **shown display** (`ag_shown_pick` in `vmagent.c`, tested with that guest's displays as a
    fixture): the host's picture only ever comes from a PCI GPU (GVT-g, virtio-gpu, QXL, a passed-through card), so a
    display on a PCI adapter always wins over one that isn't; among those, the one chosen before by size while it
    stays, else the one whose mode is the size the host asked for (the primary first), else the primary, else the
    first. A change of which displays there are forgets the choice. The size the host asks for is set on it.
  - The shown display is made the guest's **primary** (the display configuration, as Settings' "Make this my main
    display" does, saved): the taskbar, the desktop's icons, new windows and a consent prompt are where the person
    looks. Once per topology, logged. Nothing is detached: the other display stays, to the shown one's right.
  - Apps mode's rectangles (`LAG_WINDOWS`, a move, a drop's point) are relative to the shown display's corner and kept
    inside it, instead of the primary's and `MonitorFromRect(…, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY)`.
  - A window on another display is moved onto the shown one as the tools start, after the primary changes, when apps
    mode starts (or when it appears) and when apps mode ends: the same place relative to the display's corner, its size
    kept, clamped to the work area; a minimized window stays minimized (only where it comes back moves), a maximized
    one is maximized there; a window on no display at all, or one that runs as administrator, is left alone. A
    minimized window's place is read in screen coordinates now (it was workspace coordinates).
  - The guest's displays go to lord-vm's log at hello and on every change (`AGK_DISPLAYS`, 18, guest → host, log only;
    a strict parser: exact length, 1..8 displays, sane rectangles, at most one primary, printable ASCII names of at most
    32 bytes; cases in `vm-test`): `agent: guest displays: \\.\DISPLAY1 1022x724 at 0,0 primary; \\.\DISPLAY2
    1920x1080 at 1022,0 (shown)`. The tools' own log (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\LordOS\lordos-guest-win.log`) lists every adapter
    and monitor, the choice, and each apps mode translation and move.
  - Still to check on the maintainer's guest. Not changed: the guest's taskbar and desktop icons stay on its primary display.
    32 bytes; cases in `vm-test`): `agent: guest displays: \\.\DISPLAY2 1920x1080 at 0,0 primary (shown);
    \\.\DISPLAY1 1022x724 at 1920,0 (not a PCI adapter)`. The tools' own log (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\LordOS\lordos-guest-win.log`)
    lists every adapter and monitor, the choice, the primary made, and each apps mode translation and move.
  - **Clicks and typing land where they're aimed again** (found with w8 on that guest: nothing could be clicked or
    typed). The guest spreads its absolute tablet over its whole desktop, both displays, while QEMU scales a position by
    the picture's width, so a click landed scaled across both (often on the display nobody sees, which then took the
    keyboard's focus). lord-vm now passes where the picture sits in the guest's desktop (`ag_displays_layout`, from
    `AGK_DISPLAYS`) to lord-server (`VM_GUEST_LAYOUT`) and on to lord-vmdisplay (`VD_LAYOUT`), which gives QEMU the
    position that lands on the shown display's pixel (`vd_abs_map`; tested with that layout: every pixel within 2, the
    limit of QEMU's integer position). Without a layout, as before.
  - **Turn Off the Extra Display** (tools **w9**): the agent's popover offers it when the guest has a display that
    isn't on a PCI adapter next to the PCI one it shows; the tools leave that display out of the guest's display
    configuration (never the shown one), remember it, and **Turn the Extra Display Back On** puts every display back
    (also by itself when no PCI display is left). Not automatic: what that display is isn't known for sure, so the
    tools log its adapter and the person decides. `AGK_EXTRA` (20, one byte), the tools' hello words `extra` and
    `extraoff`, `VAG_EXTRA_OFF` / `VAG_EXTRA_ON`, `VAC_EXTRA` / `VAC_EXTRA_OFF`; strict parsers with tests.
  - The popover shows the LordOS tools' version next to the agent's ("agent 109.1.0 · LordOS tools w9"): the first is
    qemu-guest-agent's.
- **Machines: a guest window that runs as administrator can't be closed from LordOS, and LordOS is told** (tools w8). The tools run with the person's normal rights, so the guest system drops their close
  message to a program running as administrator (Computer Management, `mmc.exe`) and refuses its moves; the × in the
  Running list did nothing. The tools now tell: such a window is flagged in the list (`LAGW_ELEVATED`, 16, set only when
  the host's hello says `elevated`, so an older host never sees a flag it refuses), a refused close, move, minimize or
  restore is answered (`LAG_WINREFUSED`, 19: window, action, reason; exactly 6 bytes, strict parser in `vmagent.c`),
  lord-vm logs it and passes it on (`VM_WINREFUSED`), and lord-server keeps the last refused close per window for the
  app: `lord.vm.closeRefusals(session)` → `[{ gid, reason: 'elevated' | 'other', at }]`, with `closeRefusedSeq` in the
  machine's status and `elevated` on each of `lord.vm.windows()`. Apps mode copies it into `guests[dir].closeRefused`
  (`closeRefusedOf` in `model.js`, tested), where the window says to close it from inside the machine. The tools are
  never elevated to get around it.

- **Videos and songs with 44.1 kHz sound no longer freeze after about half a minute** (lord-media's
  player, `src/media/helper/lm_aqlevel.h`). The player counted the decoded sound waiting for lord-server in
  milliseconds, rounded down every time a piece of it went into the audio ring. Sound at 44.1 kHz, resampled to the
  ring's 48 kHz, comes in chunks that never fit the ring's free space whole, so each one was split and the count lost
  about 1 ms per chunk: after 30–45 s it read a full second queued with nothing queued, the decoder stopped making
  sound, the audio clock stopped and the picture froze with it (reported with a 4K60 AV1 video that VLC played; the
  same happened with a 640 × 360 AV1 clip and with an audio-only 44.1 kHz file, while 48 kHz sound and playback
  without sound were never affected). The level is now counted in bytes, which add up exactly. The 4K60 AV1 video
  plays in software at 59.9 frames a second past 75 s (it stopped at 31.5 s before), and `build/aqlevel-test` checks
  that the level comes back to zero after 70 s of 44.1 kHz chunks split as the ring takes them.

- **GTK apps from Flathub use LordOS's font** (`docs/FLATPAK.md`, "Fonts"). A GTK 3 app such as CPU-X
  drew its text in DejaVu Sans 11, bigger, wider and softer than the desktop's: the settings portal gave GTK no font
  keys, so it fell back to its built-in `Adwaita Sans 11`, which isn't installed, and the sandbox couldn't see Inter
  (it sees only the host's `/usr/share/fonts`). Checked offline inside CPU-X's sandbox (`ReadAll` gave no font key;
  `fc-match` of both names gave DejaVu Sans). lord-server's settings portal (`server/src/ui/portal.c`) now serves
  `font-name` and `document-font-name` `Inter 10`, `monospace-font-name` `JetBrains Mono 10`, `font-antialiasing`
  `grayscale` (as LordOS draws its own text), `font-hinting` `slight`, `font-rgba-order` `rgb`, `text-scaling-factor`
  `1.0` and `icon-theme` `Adwaita` in `org.gnome.desktop.interface`, the three antialiasing keys also in
  `org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.xsettings` for older runtimes, with `SettingChanged` when the fonts appear or go;
  without LordOS's fonts it names fontconfig's `Sans 10` and `Monospace 10`. The same keys go to the GSettings keyfile
  for GTK 3 apps outside Flatpak. The lordos package also installs Inter and JetBrains Mono in
  `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/lordos` (copies; fontconfig's dpkg trigger refreshes its cache; new files, no migration),
  and the SBOM lists each font's checksum once. No new privilege: the portal only answers with fixed values. Cursor
  theme and size aren't served: GTK asks for cursors by shape and LordOS draws them. Tests: `build/portal-gs-test`
  (every key through `ReadOne` and `ReadAll`, and the keyfile) and `tests/gtk_defaults_test.mjs` (the font folder
  against `mkdeb.sh`, the values against Debian's schema).
- **Machines: a click lands where the pointer is** (`docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 6.25, "Buttons in both
  modes"). On a guest with an Intel GVT-g vGPU, right-click did nothing while the mouse was free (the tablet)
  and worked while captured. lord-vmdisplay sent a button to QEMU as soon as it arrived, but the pointer's position that
  the machine's window sends just before it only at the end of its turn. So the tablet pressed at the previous position
  and then moved with the button down: a short drag, which the guest's shell doesn't take as a right-click. Now any motion
  gathered so far goes out before each button and wheel step, free and captured. To be confirmed on that machine.
- **Machines: QEMU's "Failed to call update: Timeout was reached" explained, and lord-vmdisplay's answers measured** (`docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 3.2). QEMU gives each display listener call 1 s. lord-vmdisplay answers every
  call from its loop at once, or holds an `UpdateDMABUF` for lord-server 250 ms at most, and never waits on QEMU. The new
  `build/vmdisplay-test` (a mock QEMU display and a mock lord-server, in `make test`) checks it: with lord-server reading
  every frame, reading none, slow with the picture after a resize to 1920x1080, and 200 updates at once with input
  arriving, every call is answered and the slowest takes 251 ms. It also checks that buttons follow the pointer's position.
  The likely source of the timeouts is QEMU itself: when it sends a new picture buffer (`ScanoutDMABUF`) or `Disable`, it
  throws away the updates still in its queue (`ui/dbus-listener.c`), and those calls never get an answer. On a GVT-g
  machine that doesn't stop the picture. To tell the two causes apart in a real session, lord-vmdisplay now logs a turn of
  its loop that took 200 ms or more, and at the end how many answers it held and the longest. Not fixed, and noted: QEMU
  keeps calling a display connection after it closed, about 66 log lines a second in `lord-vm.log`.
- **Linux apps' damage is honoured and their buffer transform applied** (Wayland audit item 5, approved
  by the maintainer 2026-11-22; `docs/WAYLAND.md`, "Frames, titles and damage"). Every commit of a shared-memory app
  copied its whole buffer, uploaded the whole texture and, on the CPU path, repainted the whole window, whatever it
  damaged: a blinking caret cost a full window each time. Now only the damaged box is copied, uploaded and repainted
  (`wl_surface.damage` through the buffer scale and viewport, and `damage_buffer`); every partial frame equals a full
  repaint (`LORD_PAINT_VERIFY=1`, 206 frames, 0 differing pixels). Headless, CPU path, lord-server's CPU over 20 s: a
  10 × 10 square changed 60 times a second 1130–1250 ms before, 340 ms after; foot at 180 × 50 cells updating a few
  characters ten times a second 1910–1920 ms before, 210–360 ms after. `wl_surface.set_buffer_transform` was ignored, so
  a turned buffer showed turned and at the wrong size: shared memory is copied upright and a dmabuf's texture is drawn
  with turned coordinates (`build/buftf-test` checks the eight transforms).

- **A Linux app's new frame composes only the displays it is on** (Wayland audit item 3, approved by the
  maintainer 2026-11-22; `docs/WAYLAND.md`, "Frames, titles and damage"). On the GPU path any app's new buffer made
  every display compose and flip again; a video or a terminal on one monitor kept all of them busy. Now only the
  displays the window (or its menu, the drag icon, a fullscreen app's display) is on present it; a window in the
  Overview or not yet placed still marks every display.

- **Linux apps' frame callbacks and presentation feedback follow their own display** (Wayland audit
  item 2, approved by the maintainer 2026-11-22; `docs/WAYLAND.md`, "Frames, titles and damage"). Every window's frame
  callbacks went with any display's frame, so with displays of different refresh rates an app was paced by the fastest
  one and drew frames nobody saw (three displays at 60, 60 and 144 Hz, simulated in `build/outpick-test`: 198
  callbacks a second for a window on a 60 Hz display, now 61; 145 on the 144 Hz one). A window's callbacks now go with a
  frame of its main display (the one with most of it) or when that display has nothing waiting, and its
  `wp_presentation` feedback is answered by that display's flip with its own time and refresh, not the main
  display's. A headless lord-server now answers presentation feedback at all (`wlperf-client frames`: 0 of 180 before,
  180 of 180).

- **A Linux app's title costs a JS event only when it changes, at most once a frame** (Wayland audit item
  1, approved by the maintainer 2026-11-22; `docs/WAYLAND.md`, "Frames, titles and damage"). Every
  `xdg_toplevel.set_title`, even the same title again, went to the theme as a `title` event and re-rendered its window
  list. Now an unchanged title is dropped, and a burst reaches JS once per 16 ms per window with its last title (Wayland
  and X11 windows). `wlperf-client titles` against a headless lord-server: 1000 repeats of the current title give 0
  events (1000 before), 1000 different titles in a burst give 2 (1000 before). The stall detector's `__lordWayland` and
  `__lordTerm` lines now name the event (`js __lordWayland title`).

- **The Terminal no longer re-renders whole windows for a program's title** (Wayland and main-thread
  audit, item 6, approved by the maintainer 2026-11-22; `docs/MAIN-THREAD.md`). A program that animates its title (Claude
  Code's spinner, progress counters) sent a `__lordTerm` "title" event per change, and each one re-rendered the whole
  Terminal window (it subscribed to every session's metadata) and the theme's root (the window title), about 270 React
  updates each: the maintainer's session logged 1310 `__lordTerm` pauses in two hours, the longest 329 ms. Now the
  window reads only the active session's profile and title, session titles are applied at most once per frame (the last
  of each session), a metadata patch that changes nothing updates nothing, and the window's title goes to the window
  manager at most four times a second. Measured headless (`tests/perf_headless.sh default terminal`, 1920 × 1080, CPU
  path) with a title changed about 60 times a second: JavaScript 1043–1162 ms per 1.5 s step (29 160–36 990 React
  updates, longest run 47 ms) before, 140–160 ms (3380–3424 updates, longest 19 ms) after; output alone (`yes | head -c
  50M`) caused no React work before or after (the rows are drawn in C). The perf driver has `terminal` and
  `terminalBg` plans for it.

- **A microphone, camera or screen restriction keeps working with many Flatpak apps open** (`server/src/hw/hw.c`,
  `server/src/main.c`; found by Claude Security, MEDIUM). Each running Flatpak app's Spawn helper took a slot in a
  16-slot poll set ahead of pwguard's PipeWire socket, so with about 11 apps open pwguard stopped hearing new capture
  streams and a restricted app could record (the polkit agent was starved too). pwguard and the polkit agent are now
  polled before the helpers, and the set holds 48 (16 fixed + 32 helpers); a helper that doesn't fit is drained on the
  tick.
- **Apps that start their real process and leave no longer vanish: VS Code from Flathub opened a window and closed at
  once** (`server/src/sec/sandbox.c`, `server/src/fpspawner.c`; found by the Flathub compatibility run of 2026-11-22).
  VS Code's `code` runs `cli.js`, which starts Electron detached and exits. The view every Flatpak app (and every
  restricted Linux app) runs in had its PID 1 leave as soon as that first process did, and the kernel then killed
  everything else in the view. PID 1 now stays while anything the app started is still running, as bubblewrap's own
  PID 1 does, and leaves with the app's status; stopping an app (a SIGTERM to the view) still ends what it left behind
  at once. The app's Spawn helper no longer dies with the app's first process (its Electron keeps asking for
  sub-sandboxes): PID 1 ends it once nothing else is left (`sandbox_view_helper`). Nothing in what the view, its scope
  or Landlock allow changed. Test: `build/sandbox-view-lifetime-test` (a process left behind runs to its end, the helper
  is ended, a stop still ends everything; it fails on the old PID 1).
- **Steam from Flathub starts: LordOS's Spawn portal answers `org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer`** (`server/src/fpspawn.c`,
  `fpak_bus_peer` in `server/src/fpak.c`). Steam's Flatpak pings the portal on "/" before anything else and, answered
  "no such object", stopped on "The unofficial Steam Flatpak app requires a working D-Bus session bus and flatpak-portal
  service". Every D-Bus connection answers `Peer.Ping` and `GetMachineId` on any path; now this one does too. Test:
  `build/fpak-test`.
- **Session restore opens a Flatpak app once, whatever its window count** (`sdk/sessionmodel.js` `launchesOnce`,
  `sdk/sessionrestore.jsx`). Each launch of a Flatpak app is a view of its own, so a second launch never reaches the
  first (Chromium's and Electron's single-instance lock, Firefox's profile lock): four saved VS Code windows became four
  copies of VS Code on one profile ("argv.json contains errors"), Chromium showed "Profile error occurred". The frames
  still go to the windows the app brings back. Test: `tests/session_model_test.mjs`.
- **The screen-share chooser and its indicator name a Flatpak app, and each window's app** (`sdk/screencastmodel.js`
  `castAskerName`, `castWindowOf`; `sdk/hardware.jsx`, `sdk/screencast.jsx`). They said
  "flatpak:org.chromium.Chromium wants to see your screen", and every Linux window in the list was labelled "Linux".
  Still only from lord-server's verified identity (the app's root-owned scope): a Flatpak app's name comes from its own
  metadata, so it is always shown with that verified id ("Chromium · org.chromium.Chromium"; an app calling itself
  "Firefox" still shows its real id), and it is looked up by that exact id only, never by a window class.
  Test: `tests/screencast_model_test.mjs` (a spoofed name included).
- **Flatpak apps built on Chromium or Electron no longer die at start** (Whatsie from Flathub: it showed its tray icon
  and quit, with `trap int3` in libQt6WebEngineCore at every launch). Chromium (QtWebEngine, CEF, the browser) and zypak
  (Electron) ask Flatpak's Spawn for a sub-sandbox that joins the app's own user and PID namespaces (EXPOSE_PIDS /
  SHARE_PIDS). LordOS served the Spawn, but its `flatpak run` started in a new Landlock domain (Landlock's scoping applied
  again), and the kernel lets only the app's own domain open the app's `/run/.userns` and PID namespace: bubblewrap ran
  without them, stopped on "creation of new user namespaces was not disabled as requested", the zygote never started
  and Chromium's CHECK ended the app. Now the launcher forks a small **Spawn helper** inside each Flatpak app's view
  right after the app's Landlock scoping (`server/src/fpspawner.c`): same scope, namespaces and Landlock domain as the
  app, no capabilities, not dumpable, executing only `/usr/bin/flatpak run` with the command line lord-server builds,
  and talking only to lord-server over a socket pair. lord-server no longer enters any namespace for a Spawn; it checks
  the caller as before, hands the helper the argv, environment and fds (a sealed memfd and SCM_RIGHTS), accepts the new
  process only in the caller's scope and signals it through its pidfd. SpawnStarted waits for bubblewrap's
  `bwrapinfo.json` (up to 3 s) so Chromium gets the real relative pid instead of 0 ("Already died").
  `sandbox-expose-fd(-ro)` (the Chromium browser's WidevineCdm folder) is read and left out, as flatpak-portal does
  with an fd it can't resolve: Flatpak would be given a path the app could swap for a link before the bind. Tests:
  `build/fpspawner-test` (52 checks: header and payload rules, the helper over a real socket pair placing Chromium's fds
  0-2 and its zygote socket, the instance fd, stdin on /dev/null, its own process group, exit statuses, refusals, no
  capabilities) and the session test `server/tests/fwflatpak/spawn.sh` with `build/fpspawn-cli` (18 checks with
  Whatsie, Chromium and FreeTube: Spawn served, bubblewrap joins the app's namespaces, helpers nested in the app's PID
  namespace, the helper in the app's scope, a window drawn, no CHECK failure).
- **Qt 6 apps open on the real display instead of a placeholder screen** ("qt.qpa.wayland: There are no outputs -
  creating placeholder screen"): `zxdg_output_v1` version 3 now sends `name` and `description`, as version 2 did (only
  its `done` gave way to `wl_output.done`); Qt waits for the name before it takes a display (`server/src/wl/wl.c`).

- **Machines: a machine with an Intel graphics card (GVT-g) no longer takes most of a CPU core**
  (`docs/MACHINES-GPU.md`, "A vGPU's picture without a readback"). Live on the maintainer's computer (the new-card guest on
  the vGPU at 1920 × 1080, an RX 580 drawing the desktop) lord-server's main thread used ~90 % of a core: QEMU's vfio
  display sends the whole picture about 33 times a second, changed or not, and each time lord-server read all 8 MB back
  from the iGPU on its main thread, scaled it into the window with the CPU and uploaded it to the desktop's GPU again.
  - With the GPU composing, a machine's picture is now a GPU texture drawn below the UI like a Linux app's window and
    scaled by the GPU (`wl_paint_media`, `media_paint_note`). An Intel vGPU's Y-tiled picture is copied on the iGPU into
    one of two linear buffers that the desktop's GPU imports (PRIME, rows a multiple of 256 bytes), only the rows the
    copy lacks; the main thread never waits: the copy's fence is in lord-server's poll. A Linux 3D machine is drawn
    straight from the desktop GPU's import of QEMU's dmabuf (it was read back and uploaded again too). A new frame
    presents only the displays its window is on, with no paint and no UI damage.
  - Unchanged frames are found on the GPU (a pass that drops equal pixels, counted with
    `GL_EXT_occlusion_query_boolean`) and acknowledged at once with nothing presented; on the CPU path (`LORD_GPU=0`)
    the same test runs before the readback, and an unchanged frame isn't read.
  - Measured with `build/dmaread-test bench` on that computer (1920 × 1080 at 33 frames a second, main-thread CPU):
    13.4 ms a frame before (readback, CPU scaling and upload; 44 % of a core) → 0.37–0.38 ms on the GPU path, changed
    or not (1.2–1.3 %); the CPU path 0.37 ms unchanged, 1.47 ms changing. The live session's numbers are still to
    measure.
  - The CPU's pixels are read back only when something needs them (a screenshot, a snapshot's thumbnail, a recording,
    a rotated or transformed view). `LORD_VM_GPUTEX=0` goes back to the readback. `dmaread-test` checks the linear
    copies on the other GPU, flipped too, and the change test.
  - lord-vmdisplay answers an `UpdateDMABUF` that comes while there's no dmabuf picture without logging it (the vfio
    display sends one every refresh during a mode change; the last picture stays).

- **Machines: the pointer is shown over a machine with an Intel graphics card, in window, full screen and apps mode**. Intel's driver puts the guest's pointer on the vGPU's cursor plane, not in the picture, but LordOS hid its
  own arrow over any machine with the new-card devices until the guest handed a shape over, which a vGPU machine didn't: there was no
  pointer at all. A vGPU machine now shows the host's arrow until QEMU hands the plane's shape over (and again when
  that shape is blank); lord-vmdisplay takes a cursor without a hotspot (VFIO's 0xffffffff) with its hotspot at the
  top left instead of refusing it; Configure → Display → *Pointer drawn by* (the VirtIO driver's `HWCursor`) isn't
  offered for a machine with an Intel graphics card.

- **Machines: older LordOS tools in a machine are said, and Files explains a missing "Open with"** (`docs/FILES.md`,
  `docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 7.3). A machine still running the first guest tools (hello `w1`) never appeared in
  Files' Open with for a `.exe` (only tools that say `open`, `w3` and later, are listed), and nothing said why: the right
  click on WinBox.exe had no Open with at all. Now lord-vm passes the tools' own version from their hello to lord-server
  (`VM_AGENT_STATE` text `version\tsystem\ttools`, letters, digits and `. - _` only; `lord.vm.poll().agent.tools`).
  Machines compares it with the tools this LordOS ships (`TOOLS_SHIPPED`: `w4` for `tools/guest-win`, `5` for
  `tools/guest`, checked against their `VERSION` by `vm-model-test`; `toolsOutdated`): the agent's popover says "A newer
  version of the LordOS tools is available" and its install button reads "Update LordOS Tools", and the bar's agent
  button gets a small blue dot. "Open with" providers can now be hints (`{ id, hint(file) }`, `openHintsFor`): while
  there is a machine whose app.json `os` is `windows` and none whose tools open files (`windowsNeedsTools`), Files' menu for a
  `.exe`, `.msi`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.lnk`, `.com`, `.msix` or `.appx` shows Open with with a dim note (`machines.win.openWithUpdate`:
  no machine can open it yet, update the LordOS tools in the machine, from its agent button), and a double click says
  the same; with no such machine nothing changes. Context menus take a wrapping `{ note }` row. In all 35
  languages. Tests: `vm-model-test`, `vm-openwith-test`, `openwith-model-test`.
- **Machines: an apps mode window moved to another monitor no longer closes** (`docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 7.2). The
  guest was asked to move its window to the LordOS window's place, off its own one screen (x ≥ the main display's width,
  or negative); the guest hid it, stopped listing it, and its LordOS window closed. The place asked of the guest is now
  always inside its screen (`guestPlace`, size kept as far as it fits) and the LordOS window stays where it was put,
  following the guest's moves at that distance; a window the guest minimized right after such a move is restored; the
  guest tools clamp a move to the screen too. Model tests (monitor 2 at x = 2500 → inside 0..1920, a monitor to the
  left, a larger window, a scaled display, 2,000 random places) and checked on a test machine: moves to x = 2500 and
  x = −1500 stayed on its screen.
- **Machines: the clipboard in apps mode, a click that brings a new copy**: a click on a guest window that carried a new
  clipboard offer reaches the guest 150 ms later, as on the machine's window, so a right-click's Paste finds it.
  Checked end to end in apps mode on a test machine: LordOS → Notepad paste (one request, answered) and Notepad's copy
  back.

- **Machines: the close question fits a small window and Esc cancels it** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`): in apps mode
  the controller window is small, so "Close ‹machine›?" was wider than it and its buttons were cut off, with the copy's
  progress line drawn over them; Esc there left apps mode behind the card instead of cancelling it. Cards now fit the
  window (buttons wrap), the copy's progress shows inside the close question instead of over it, and Esc is Cancel.
- **Machines: "Ask before each paste" can't be clicked through or raced** (`apps/machines/clipask.jsx`,
  `server/src/ui/js_vm.c`; found by Claude Security, two LOW). The guest chooses when the bar appears and sees where the
  pointer is, so it could raise the bar under a click already on its way: Paste/Bring now answer only after the bar has
  been in view for 0.7 s and only to a press that started after that (Don't paste/Ignore and Esc work at once). And a
  guest flipping its on-demand capability could turn an offer into a full push nobody approved: in ask mode lord-server
  now refuses a full push unless it carries the hash of the preview the person said yes to.
- **Machines: "Ask before each paste" pastes only what it showed, and a click opens the clipboard for a moment only**
  (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`, `server/src/ui/js_vm.c`; found by the commit security review, two MEDIUM). A yes to
  the bar's preview applied whatever the machine had copied by then, so a guest could swap the contents after the
  preview: `clipboardApply`/`clipboardTake` now take the copy's number and refuse a later one, and a yes to push this
  computer's clipboard checks it is still the one previewed. A click on a machine whose window wasn't in front opened
  the clipboard's gate until the window's state next changed; it now opens it for the grace period only.
- **Machines: the library is always one step away** (`apps/machines/index.jsx`; `sdk/dock.js` `registerDockActivate`,
  `sdk/windowmenu.js` `registerWindowMenuItems`). With a machine's window open and the library closed there was no way
  back to it without closing the machine. Now "Machines Library" is the first item of the app's Dock menu and of every
  Machines window's Window menu (❖0 in a machine's window, which never reaches the guest), and a click on the Dock item
  while only machines are open opens the library instead of raising a machine. The two SDK hooks are generic (any app
  can add its own Window menu items or decide its Dock click) and every theme uses them through the shared Dock and
  Window menu code. In all 35 languages.
- **Machines: the Requirements sheet fits** (`apps/machines/library.jsx`, `model.js` `reqRows`). With the TPM row the
  list was taller than the sheet and its buttons were cut off; the rows now scroll inside the sheet with Back and
  Install Missing always visible. The TPM row showed its raw key ("machines.req.use.tpm"): it now says what swtpm is
  for, in all 35 languages, and a test checks that every row the page can show has its title and line in English.
- **Machines: a Clone's computer name, for a guest with the LordOS guest tools, is the one it will use**
  (`apps/machines/clone.jsx`, `model.js` `winNameValid`, `cloneWinName`). The "Name inside the machine" field offered
  a Linux hostname (for example 26 characters) that lord-vm then shortened to a 15-character computer name (first 10 +
  "-" + 4 hex), so the name shown wasn't the one used. For a machine with the `windows` devices the default is now a
  valid computer name (the machine's name cut to 9, then "-clone"), the field takes at most 15 letters, digits and
  dashes and not only digits (lord-vm's own rule), and the note says what happens: the guest tools give the copy this
  computer name, used from the guest's next restart, and its SID doesn't change. Linux machines are unchanged.
- **Machines: a linked clone's card shows the frozen base it shares** (`ui/js_vm.c` `stats` `baseBytes`,
  `apps/machines/library.jsx`). After a linked clone, both the original and the clone showed about 1 MB "on disk",
  since only their own overlays were counted and the frozen base in `<library>/.shared/` was counted nowhere on the
  cards. The card now shows the machine's own size with "own · 19 GB shared" under it; sorting by disk still uses the
  own size.
- **Machines: a machine whose description this LordOS can't read** (`apps/machines/library.jsx`, `vmwindow.jsx`,
  `model.js` `unreadableOf`, `actionsOf`; `ui.jsx` `gb`, `bytes`). A `machine.json` written by a newer LordOS (a newer
  schema) or damaged showed "undefined MB" in the list and its window tried to start it. The card and the list now say
  "Needs a newer LordOS" or "Its description can't be read" instead of numbers, Start is disabled with that reason, and
  the machine's window explains it without trying to start; sizes never print "undefined".

- **Machines: a right-click Paste in a machine has what was just copied on this computer** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`):
  this computer's clipboard went into the machine only when its window came to the front, so copying with a context
  menu and then right-clicking Paste in the machine found the old clipboard (a keyboard paste worked, after the window's
  focus). It is now also sent with a click on the machine's picture, and a click that carried a new clipboard reaches
  the machine 150 ms later, so its Paste menu has it. A pass of the pointer sends nothing (found by the background
  security review: a machine in the background must not read what was copied); contents that didn't change are not
  sent again.
- **Machines: copy and paste with a Linux guest that has no clipboard tool** (`tools/guest/lordos-guest.c`,
  `server/src/vm/lordvm.c`, `vmagent.c`, `vmproto.h`, `server/src/ui/js_vm.c`, `apps/machines/model.js`, `vmwindow.jsx`).
  The clipboard helper reads and writes the guest's clipboard only through `xclip` or `wl-paste`/`wl-copy`, and a stock
  desktop install ships neither: every run failed in silence, nothing went either way, and the agent's popover still
  said the clipboard worked (the helper's hello always said "clipboard"). Now:
  - the helper (version 4) looks for the tools in PATH at the start, every 30 seconds and whenever one couldn't be
    started, so installing `xclip` later starts working without a restart. It tells the guest's journal once which tool
    it uses, or "no clipboard tool: install xclip or wl-clipboard". Without one its hello says `noclip` instead of
    `clipboard clipx`, and again with `clipboard` once a tool appears;
  - on GNOME with `DISPLAY` set it uses only `xclip`, through Xwayland, whose clipboard Mutter bridges: Mutter has no
    data-control protocol, so `wl-paste` in the background needs a focus-stealing popup there. Elsewhere it keeps
    `wl-clipboard` under Wayland first, then `xclip`. When the service starts before the session exported its display,
