    the helper reads `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `DISPLAY`, `XAUTHORITY` and `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` from the user's systemd
    manager (10 tries at most);
  - lord-vm sets the clipboard capability only when the hello says `clipboard`, and a new `VAC_CLIP_NOTOOL` (2048) when it
    says `noclip`; the log says when the guest gains or loses its tool. The popover's clipboard line says "Needs xclip"
    with a hint (install the helper again, which installs it, or `sudo apt install xclip` in the machine), and the bar's
    clipboard menu says it too, in every language;
  - Install Clipboard Helper's fixed script also installs `xclip` and `wl-clipboard` through the guest's own package
    manager (apt-get, dnf, zypper or pacman) when `xclip` is missing. It is best effort: offline or with the package
    manager locked the helper is still installed and the popover says what is missing. It then restarts the helper in
    each signed-in desktop session (`systemctl --user -M <user>@`, uids from 1000 with `graphical-session.target`
    active), so the new version runs at once instead of from the next sign-in;
  - the button could start the script many times (6 runs in 20 seconds in one guest's journal): lord-vm answered as
    soon as the script started. It now follows the script with `guest-exec-status` and answers when it ends (10 minutes
    at most; a failure carries the script's error output), answers `busy` to a second install meanwhile, and gives up
    with an error when qemu-guest-agent stops answering. lord-server treats a click while an install is on its way as
    the same request, so the button stays disabled until the end.
  New test: `server/tests/guest_clip_test.sh` (in `make test`) runs the helper once with stub tools and a socket as its
  port: no tool gives a `noclip` hello and the journal line; `xclip` alone, `wl-clipboard` alone, GNOME choosing `xclip`
  over `wl-paste`, and another Wayland desktop choosing `wl-clipboard` first. Not yet tried on a real GNOME guest.
- **Machines: a copy into a machine always shows its percentage** (`apps/machines/model.js`, `vmwindow.jsx`): a long file
  name (an installer image, for one) pushed the percentage past the line's edge, so the copy looked stuck. The name is
  now shortened in the middle, keeping its end, the line wraps instead of being cut, and a progress bar sits under it.
- **Machines: a machine's input can't be an output's monitor** (`server/src/ui/js_vm.c`, `server/src/sound/snd.c`; found by
  the commit security review, MEDIUM). The input chosen for a machine is used only when it is a microphone or line input,
  never the monitor of an output (which would hand the guest everything this computer plays under the microphone
  permission), and the default is used whenever the sound state isn't known yet (it used to pass the chosen name on).
- **Machines: the agent's panel says when the clipboard is off** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`): a machine made before the
  clipboard setting existed has it off, and the panel only offered to install the helper again, which changed nothing. It
  now says the clipboard is off and opens Configure → Sharing. The duplicated `agent.st.needsTools` key in every language
  is gone too.
- **Machines: Configure's Done keeps changes made in any section** (`apps/machines/configure.jsx`): Done saved the draft
  only when the pane showing at that moment was one that saves, so a choice made in another section was silently dropped
  (Graphics 3D chosen under Display, then Done pressed from Sound, closed without it). Done now saves every change made in
  any section; with the machine running and changes that need it off, it shows the running banner instead of closing, and
  the pane's Cancel/Save footer shows whenever there are unsaved changes.
- **Machines: the window of a machine that's starting no longer shows "Something went wrong"** (`apps/machines/model.js`):
  between the start and the machine's first state, the window read the state of a session that had none yet and failed,
  then said it couldn't connect. A session without its first state now counts as Starting. Model test added.
- **Machines: a password manager's secret copied in a machine stays in the machine** (`tools/guest-win/lordos-guest-win.c`,
  `tools/guest/lordos-guest.c`; found by Claude Security, LOW). With guest-to-host clipboard sharing on, a password copied
  from a password manager inside a machine reached the host's clipboard history (kept 30 days) and outlived
  the manager's own clearing. The guest tools now leave such a copy alone. The guest tools for the new card's guests check for the marks those
  managers set ("ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing", "Clipboard Viewer Ignore", "CanIncludeInClipboardHistory"
  holding 0). The Linux guest tool checks for `x-kde-passwordManagerHint`. Checked with a stub clipboard on Linux (the secret
  is not sent; ordinary text still is); the other guest tools are built but not yet run in a guest.
- **Apps mode: each Store app of the new card's guests is its own Dock entry, with its icon** (`tools/guest-win/lordos-guest-win.c`): every
  Store app's window (Calculator, Settings…) belongs to `ApplicationFrameHost.exe`, so they all shared one Dock entry
  "ApplicationFrameHost.exe (machine)" with a letter for an icon. The guest tools now resolve the app inside the frame
  (its AppUserModelID, from the frame's property store or the hosted `CoreWindow`'s process) and report the Start menu's
  name and picture for it. Checked on a guest of the new card (4.3): Calculator and Settings came as "Calculadora" and
  "Configuración", each with its own 32 × 32 icon (`lordvm-dev` now saves each icon the guest sends as `icon-<id>.png`).
- **Apps mode keeps a guest's window below the menu bar** (`apps/machines/appsmode.jsx`, `model.js` `insideWork`): a guest
  window near the top of the guest's screen (Calculator opens at y = −10) got its LordOS title bar under the menu bar,
  out of reach. It now opens, and follows the guest, just inside the work area, and the guest is asked to move its window
  to the same place, so the picture stays the guest's window 1:1. `vm_model_test.mjs` covers it.
- **A clone of the new card's guests gets its own computer name** (`server/src/vm/lordvm.c`, `vmops.c`): lord-vm ran its `/bin/sh` identity
  script on a clone of the new card's guests (4.3), which failed at every start ("qemu-guest-agent couldn't run the script"), so the copy
  kept the original's name. Such a guest now gets one fixed PowerShell script as SYSTEM: `Rename-Computer` to a name
  checked on both sides against NetBIOS rules (at most 15 letters, digits and `-`, not only digits; a longer hostname
  becomes its first 10 characters and 4 hex digits of the new id), with no forced restart: the guest uses it from its
  next restart. It runs once. The machine SID isn't changed (sysprep's job; `docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` says so). Checked on a
  clone of such a machine: after Shut Down and a start, `hostname` gave the new name. `build/vm-test` covers the
  names.
- **A machine's sound comes back when PipeWire appears late** (`server/src/ui/js_vm.c`, `server/src/media/maudio.c`): a
  machine window opened before PipeWire was reachable stayed silent ("media: no PipeWire to play", never tried again), and
  so did one whose PipeWire restarted. The speakers' stream (and the microphone's) now connect again every 2 s while the
  guest plays, with the same ring, logging only the first failure and the return. Checked with `lordvm-dev` and a private
  PipeWire started after the guest began playing: back after 4 tries, at the real rate.
- **The machine window's menus show their information lines whole** (`apps/machines/ui.jsx`, `vmwindow.jsx`): in the
  Folders menu the transfer folder's line ("In the machine: a drive in This PC, usually Z:") and "No folder is shared with
  this machine" were cut at the menu's edge, and so were long items in other languages. Information lines are now notes
  that wrap under the items' text column (start-aligned, right to left too), and every item's text wraps instead of
  running out of the menu; the resolution menu's notes use the same rows.
- **Installing the guest tools says what went wrong in the person's language** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`, `model.js`
  `installError`): the agent popover showed lord-vm's English error as it came ("the guest agent can't write files or run
  commands"). Its known errors (tools missing on this computer, the agent busy, no file copies or programs allowed, too
  slow, no private folder, the agent gone, the script failed) are now translated lines (`machines.agent.err.*`, all 35
  languages), with lord-vm's text only as a detail when it adds something (a script's output, qemu-guest-agent's
  error). `vm_model_test.mjs` covers the mapping.
- **A bridged machine starts with one Play, showing Starting while its network is made** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`,
  `library.jsx`, `model.js` `startPhase`, `playStarts`): while the admin helper made the macvtap the window kept the
  earlier run's Off (title and Play included), and Play on the library's card only brought an open window forward, so a
  second Play was needed. The window now shows Starting (no second Play) until the network is up and then starts the
  machine itself, once, even if it was remounted meanwhile (and not if it was closed); Play on a card asks an open window
  that shows Off to start. `vm_model_test.mjs` covers the phases; not run against the real admin helper here.
- **Settings → Flatpak counts the Flathub apps installed elsewhere** (`sdk/flathub.js` `watchInstalled`,
  `apps/settings/Flatpak.jsx`, `apps/store/flathubpages.js`): the count was read once when the page opened, so an app
  installed outside the Store while it showed (a terminal's `flatpak install --user`, a `.flatpakref`) left it at 0, and
  it said 0 before the first list came back. It now says "—" until the installation was listed, and while the page (or
  the Store's Flathub updates) shows, the exported apps are compared every 3 s (cheap: the server reads its folders again
  only when they changed) and the installation is listed again when they change.
- **The remote desktop no longer crashes lord-server when a viewer connects after the last one left**
  (`server/src/remote/mirror.c`, `server/src/media/mstream.c`): the mirror freed its copy of the screen while the video
  encoder still held it, and the next viewer's encoder copied from the freed memory. A 1920 × 1080 headless session
  drawing with nobody watching crashed on every third viewer (SIGSEGV in a paint thread); with a monitor the same read
  happened whenever a viewer connected after the last one left. The encoder now drops the pointer before every free.
- **Linux and Flathub apps start with a covered mount under the home** (`server/src/sec/sandbox.c`): the read-only view of
  the home made every mount under it read-only from `/proc/self/mountinfo`, which also lists mounts no path reaches (one
  covered by a later mount on a folder above it); that remount failed with ENOENT and no app started ("could not build
  the app's view"). Such a mount is skipped, since the app can't reach it either; any other failure still stops the
  launch, now with the mount and the reason in the app's log. `build/sandbox-home-mounts-test` covers it. Found with
  Whatsie launched from the launcher in a session with a tmpfs and a bind mount in the home.
- **Machines' window no longer pauses the desktop every 5 s** (`server/src/vm/vmthumb.c`): the card's picture was scaled,
  PNG-encoded and written on the main thread at each snapshot (20 to 57 ms, `stall: call vm.snapshot` in
  compositor.log). A thread of its own does it now from a copy; none of those stalls in a minute of a running machine.
  `build/vmthumb-test` covers it.
- **Open Transfer Folder opens the machine's own folder** (`apps/machines/`, `sdk/sysopen.js`): it showed
  `~/Machines/Transfer`, every machine's folder, one level up. The library's menu, Configure → Sharing and the machine
  window's folder menu (the transfer folder and each shared folder) open the folder itself (`openFolder`).
- **The Store's sidebar edge drags from both sides of the line** (`apps/store/index.jsx`): the column after the sidebar
  took presses on the outer half of the drag handle.
- **Configure → Display saves its choices** (`apps/machines/configure.jsx`): the start resolution and 2D/3D picked there
  were dropped when Done was pressed (the section wasn't one that saves); a machine set to 1920 × 1080 now starts at
  1920 × 1080 (checked with a machine of the new card, `docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 4.3).
- **The agent of a guest without systemd lists only what it does** (`server/src/vm/lordvm.c`, `apps/machines/model.js`):
  on the new card's guests (`docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 4.3) the popover said "Logs: the system's journal" and "Kept awake
  while it runs" worked, which are systemd's (`journalctl`, `systemd-inhibit`); lord-vm no longer claims or tries them
  there, and the popover leaves those lines out.
- **The machine's bar fits a narrow window** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`): between about 640 and 850 px wide (and
  below 620) power, Configure and full screen went past the window's edge; the bar is compact up to 880 px, and the
  smallest windows leave out the shell, logs, screenshot and record group (logs and screenshot are in Actions).
- **Apps mode follows a guest window that keeps its own size** (`apps/machines/appsmode.jsx`, `model.js` `guestKept`):
  a window made smaller than the guest allows (Calculator, Paint) stayed small here with the guest's picture squeezed
  into it; 1.5 s after an unanswered move it goes back to the guest window's real size.
- **Machines in full screen keep a menu open under the pointer** (`apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`): the floating bar hid as
  soon as the pointer left it to reach a menu's items (the resolution menu went away); it now stays while a menu is open.
- **One pointer over a machine that draws its own** (`server/src/media/media.c`, `server/src/ui/js_vm.c`): guests on
  the device set of the new card in `docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 4.3 draw their pointer into the picture and hand none over,
  so LordOS's arrow showed beside it; it's hidden over their picture until the guest hands one over.
- **The guest agent names the guest's system rightly** (`server/src/vm/lordvm.c`): a build of 22000 or more that still
  calls itself "10" is shown as 11, and the clipboard helper (a Linux program) is no longer offered to such a guest,
  where installing it failed on a path that doesn't exist there.
- **An unattended install from the New Machine assistant no longer stops in the firmware's menu**
  (`server/src/vm/lordvm.c`): the Enters that answer the install disc's "Press any key to boot from CD or DVD" were only
  sent when lord-vm started the machine running, and Machines starts it paused until its window is there, so the
  prompt timed out. They're now sent from when the machine first runs, for a guided install too. Machines also finds
  the ISO in Downloads under its newer file name (`Windows11_Client_x64_<language>_<build>.iso`).
- **Machines on compatible devices start in their window** (`server/src/vm/lordvm.c`; the device sets of imported machines
  and of the new card in `docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 4.3): the window's sound output wasn't declared for them, and QEMU refused the sound card with "audiodev 'snd0' not found".
- **Linux and Flathub apps start on a computer with a mount inside the home folder** (`server/src/sec/sandbox.c`): a
  cloud drive (rclone's FUSE mount under `~/Cloud`) or a disk mounted in a folder made the kernel refuse the read-only
  bind of the home in the app's user namespace (EINVAL), and no app with a read-only home started ("could not build
  the app's view"). The home is now bound with what is mounted under it, and each of those mounts is made read-only
  too. **Flathub apps start when the document portal runs** (`server/src/fpak.c`): `flatpak run` now gets
  `--no-documents-portal`, since LordOS's view has no `/run/user/<uid>/doc` and bubblewrap stopped there. Found with
  Whatsie on the maintainer's PC; checked there by launching it through LordOS's launcher.
- **The desktop no longer stalls while the Store installs a Flathub app** (`sdk/flathub.js`, `apps/store/flathubpages.js`):
  every line flatpak printed changed the Store's state, which redrew the 60 cards of the Flathub page and filtered and
  sorted the 2 242 apps of the catalog again, several times a second. Progress now reaches the page at most every
  250 ms and only its progress bar redraws; each card follows only whether its app is installed, the filtered list is
  kept until the catalog, the search or the switch changes, and each name is folded once when sorting.
- **Flatpak's Spawn portal compares fd handles as unsigned numbers** (`server/src/fpspawn.c`): a handle of 2³¹ or more read
  as a negative index before. Not reachable in practice, since LordOS's D-Bus client already refuses any message whose fd index
  is past the fds that came with it; fixed as defense in depth after an automated security review.
- **No compiler warnings on arm64**: two Flatpak functions that only x86-64 PCs use in phase 1 were reported as unused on the
  Raspberry Pi build (`server/src/apps.c`).

### Security
- **A password is never captured: every password surface LordOS draws is protected (the maintainer's rule of 2026-11-22, with GitHub #219).** Until now only Passwords' window,
  the on-screen keyboard and windows marked by hand were protected; a password prompt or field came out in a screenshot,
  a recording, the remote desktop or a shared screen (as dots, but with its length, and the eye could show it).
  - **Every password field** (`TextInput secure`, `sdk/components.jsx`) is a protected node while it is one: Wi-Fi,
    VPN, the Terminal's servers, Cloud, Mail, Users, Sharing, the remote desktop, Databases, Backup, Passwords and the
    login and lock screens. Lord-server paints it black in every capture of the screen or an area, recordings, the
    remote desktop and shared screens and windows, and refuses the window that holds it captured alone
    (`media.protectedWindow`, above).
  - **The keyring's unlock prompt** (`sdk/vault.js` `KeyringPrompt`) and **the administrator prompt a Linux app asks for
    through polkit** (`sdk/hardware.jsx` `PolkitPrompt`, which draws a dot per key) are protected whole. LordOS's own
    administrator actions ask for no password (`admin.c` checks the session user's group).
  - While anything protected is on screen a remote desktop viewer is composed on the CPU and a visitor of the
    screen-sharing API can't type into LordOS's own windows, as for any protected window.
  - Tests: `password_protect_scene.mjs` (new: a password field is protected and stops being so with `secure` off, a
    plain field never is, both prompts are protected whole) and `engine-test` (a protected prompt in a high layer and a
    password field inside a window are black in a capture of the screen, the rest of the window is captured, and that
    window is refused alone).
- **The Wayland table importer no longer runs code from wayland.app** (`tools/wayland-app-import.mjs`, a maintainer
  tool, new in this release; found by the pre-merge security scan). It cut the protocol registry and each
  `JSON.parse('...')` module out of wayland.app's JavaScript bundle and evaluated them with `Function()`, so whoever
  controlled that third-party bundle could run code on the maintainer's machine when the table was refreshed; the
  string scan also let an escaped backslash before a quote end the literal early. The bundle is now read by a small
  literal reader (`readLiteral`, `readString`): string, number and boolean literals, arrays, objects, the bundle's own
  string enum members and module references only, with JavaScript's escape rules, a depth limit and no
  `__proto__`/`constructor` keys; anything else is refused and nothing in the bundle ever runs. Test:
  `server/tests/wayland_import_test.mjs` (both breakouts refused, nothing executed).

- **Machines: keys typed in another window never reach a machine** (`docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 5.8;
  `sdk/components.jsx` `AppHost`/`FloatingWindows`, `sdk/windows.js` `wm.hasKeyboard`/`setFullscreen`,
  `sdk/desktopmodel.js` `keyboardWindow`, `sdk/kbinhibit.js`, `apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`, `appsmode.jsx`, `model.js`).
  Reported on a real session: typing in LordOS's Terminal also typed into the guest of a running machine (its beeps were heard). Every
  key of the session reaches every key listener, and a machine sent keys to its guest whenever its own `focused` flag was
  true, and that flag could be true for two windows at once: `FloatingWindows` gave every full-screen window of the
  desktop the keys, while the theme gave them to its top framed window too. With a machine full screen on one display and
  the Terminal on another, a password typed in the Terminal went into the guest; a system prompt (a password, the
  keyring), the search or the launcher open over the machine window sent their keys there as well.
  - **At each key.** The machine window (picture and serial console), every apps mode window and the Keys panel's held
    keys ask `wm.hasKeyboard(window)` for each key, not a flag from the last render: the front window of the showing
    desktop, with no search, launcher, sheet or system prompt holding the keyboard (the same rule as a Linux app's
    Wayland keyboard). The first key typed elsewhere lets go of everything held in the guest, the held Win or Ctrl
    included, and a release goes to the guest only for a press that went there (`model.js` `guestKeys`).
  - **One focused window.** `AppHost` is focused only when it is also `wm.focused()`, in every theme and in isolated apps;
    a press on a full-screen window brings it to the front (so it has its keys again), and going full screen brings the
    window forward. The desktop's shortcuts held for a machine follow `wm.hasKeyboard` too.
  - **No focus stealing in apps mode.** A window the guest opens or brings back takes the front only while you are in
    that machine (its window or one of its windows in front); otherwise it opens behind the window you are typing in.
  - lord-server needed no change: keys reach a guest only through `lord.vm.key`, capture mode takes only the mouse, and
    lord-vmdisplay lets go of held keys when lord-server goes away (a session that re-attaches finds nothing held).
  - Tested by `server/tests/vm_model_test.mjs` (focus moving to the Terminal or a search between keys: no `lord.vm.key`,
    one release), `desktop_model_test.mjs` (`keyboardWindow`) and the new `vm_keys_scene.mjs` (run by `run_suites.sh`:
    a framed and a full-screen machine with the Terminal in front, and a system prompt over the machine, through the real
    `AppHost`, `FloatingWindows` and `__lordKey`; it fails on the code before this change). `focus_scene.mjs` and
    `list_scene.mjs` now open their window, since an `AppHost` is focused only as the front window.
- **Machines: the clipboard goes into and out of a machine only while you use it, and into it only when something
  there pastes** (`docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md` 6.8; `server/src/vm/vmagent.[ch]`, `lordvm.c`, `ui/js_vm.c`,
  `apps/machines/vmwindow.jsx`, `appsmode.jsx`, `model.js`, `tools/guest-win`, `tools/guest`). A guest is untrusted
  (clipboard stealers, address swappers), and until now this computer's clipboard was pushed into a machine whenever
  its window came to the front, where any program in it could read it later.
  - **On demand.** The machine now gets an *offer* (which forms there are: text, rich text, picture; a generation
    number; no contents) when its window comes to the front or is clicked. The guest's helper puts those forms on its
    clipboard without data and asks for one only when a program there pastes. lord-server answers with the data only
    while the machine is in use (its window in front, one of its apps mode windows in front, or 3 s after, so a paste
    right after switching works) and only for the offer that is still this computer's clipboard; anything else gets
    nothing. lord-vm checks each request first: it parses exactly, is for the last offer and one of its forms, the
    machine's clipboard goes toward the guest, a window is open on the machine, and the guest asks at most 8 times a
    second. Refusals go in the machine's log. Secrets are still never offered.
  - **Guests with `lordos-guest-win`** (w2): the system's delayed rendering (`WM_RENDERFORMAT`), with the offer marked so
    the guest's clipboard history and cloud clipboard skip it; a paste waits at most 2 s for the answer; leaving
    empties the clipboard instead of fetching what nobody pasted.
  - **Linux guests** (lordos-guest 5): the helper owns the X `CLIPBOARD` selection itself, speaking the X11 protocol
    over the display's own socket with the session's cookie (no Xlib, no new package; `tools/guest/x11clip.c`), so it
    works on X11 and through Xwayland, which GNOME, KDE and wlroots desktops bridge to their Wayland clipboard; large
    pictures go as INCR. A guest without an X display and older helpers keep receiving the whole clipboard, at the same
    moments only (window to the front, a click).
  - **Guest → this computer, gated.** What a machine copies reaches this computer's clipboard only while the machine is
    in use; a change in the background is ignored and logged.
  - **Told once per burst.** A machine that asks for the clipboard or changes it in the background gets a notification:
    "‹machine› tried to read your clipboard in the background: blocked" / "… tried to change your clipboard in the
    background: ignored", again only after 30 s without one (or 5 minutes after the last notice). Configure → Sharing's
    clipboard note says how it works. In all 35 languages.
  - New agent frames `AGK_CLIPOFFER`, `AGK_CLIPREQ`, `AGK_CLIPDATA` and hello capability `clipreq`, with strict parsers
    (exact lengths, generation ≥ 1, known forms and flags, UTF-8 or a believable PNG) covered by `vm-test` (cases and
    50 000 random inputs); `tests/guest_clip_test.sh` drives the Linux helper against Xvfb with `xclip` (TARGETS, a
    paste, a refusal, a 300 KB INCR picture, one request per form, giving the selection back).
- **Machines: "Ask before each paste"** (Configure → Sharing → Clipboard trust; `machine.json` schema 9
  `clipboard_ask`, `lord-vm --set --clipboard-ask on|off`; `apps/machines/clipask.jsx`, `model.js` `clipAsk*`,
  `ui/js_vm.c` `clipboardAnswer`, `clipboardPreview`). "Trusted" (the default) is the on-demand clipboard above. "Ask"
  puts a small bar over the machine's picture (over the guest window in front in apps mode) before anything crosses:
  "Paste into ‹machine›?" with a one-line preview (80 characters of text, rich text's text, or "A picture, W×H") and
  [Don't paste] [Paste] when a program in the machine pastes, the program waiting up to 25 s for the answer and getting
  nothing on a no or no answer; one answer covers every form of the same copy. "‹machine› copied" with its preview and
  [Ignore] [Bring to LordOS] for a copy out of the machine, ignored after a minute. With a guest helper that can't ask,
  the bar asks before the clipboard is pushed. Esc says no; Enter says yes only on the focused button; while the bar
  shows nothing typed goes to the machine. Right-to-left aware, in all 35 languages.
- **Machines: "Needs xclip" reached the app** (`server/src/vm/vmproto.h`): lord-server refused every agent state that
  carried the "no clipboard tool" bit (2048, at the limit of the check), so the hint and Install's xclip step never
  showed. The check now allows every known bit.

  and 3). lord-server reads each machine's frames in its own loop and acknowledges a frame right after the paint that
  showed it, instead of at the Machines app's poll after next; a frame repaints only the rectangle that changed, not
  the whole picture. Measured on a viogpudo guest drawing 61 frames a second: 29.5 → 60.0 frames a second shown,
  1.7 → 0.1 ms of paint a frame, lord-server 54 % → 17 % of a core.
- **Monitor: the process list no longer stalls the desktop** (`docs/MACHINES-GPU.md` Part 1 step 6).
  `lord.monitor.processes` read every process's cgroup file and parsed a JSON list on lord-server's only thread
  (~20 ms a second on a busy desktop, a third of the maintainer's stall lines). The monitor's thread now reads each
  scope once and hands over rows that become objects directly: 382 processes 4.0 → 1.3 ms, 1,900 processes
  19.6 → 4.5 ms a call.

## [0.8.9.4-beta] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- **Flatpak apps from Flathub, managed from the Store** (`docs/FLATPAK.md`, lordos.org/features/flatpak). Store →
  Flathub turns it on (it installs Debian's `flatpak`, 6 packages, 11 MB, nothing of it running in the background),
  shows Flathub's verified apps with what each one declares and what LordOS does about it, and installs, updates and
  removes them. Every Flatpak app runs under LordOS's own rules: its own root-owned scope and view, your Firewall and
  restrictions, a read-only home but for its own folder and your folders, LordOS's folders hidden, the session bus
  only through Flatpak's filtering proxy. The apps appear in search, the launcher, the Dock and "Open with". Settings →
  Flatpak shows the space they take and removes Flatpak completely. PCs (x86-64) only for now; Electron and
  Chromium-based apps are marked "not yet supported". Tested: GNOME Text Editor, Decibels, Shortwave, Meld, KCalc,
  Firefox, GNU Emacs; the automated test plan (`server/tests/fwflatpak/flatpak.sh`) passes its 31 checks. The
  entries below are the steps that built it.
- **Flatpak and Flathub, phase 1 (approved 2026-11-19, `docs/FLATPAK.md`).** The groundwork: the
  package masks Flatpak's root helper (`flatpak-system-helper.service`), its sub-sandbox portal
  (`flatpak-portal.service`) and its session helper (`flatpak-session-helper.service`) with links to `/dev/null`, so
  once Flatpak is installed polkit can't reach the helper's actions, no app starts a sandbox outside its LordOS scope
  and `flatpak-spawn --host` has no service behind it; `~/.local/share/flatpak` (installations, trusted keys,
  overrides, exports) joins `lord.fs`'s deny list; desktop ids and app scopes starting with `fp-` are reserved for
  Flatpak apps (`app-lordos-fp-<id>.scope`, identity `flatpak:<id>`). Nothing installs Flatpak yet.
- **The Flatpak launch path**: `lord.apps.launchFlatpak(id)` and `launchFlatpakWith(id, path)` take
  only an installed app's id (Flatpak's id rules, at most 59 bytes), read the installation without following a link
  out of the app's folder (`server/src/fpak.c`) and build the `flatpak run` command line in C, never from an export's
  `Exec` line: no unfiltered session or system bus; no `org.freedesktop.Flatpak`, `systemd1`, `secrets` or the
  sub-sandbox portal; LordOS's own bus names only to talk to, never to own; LordOS's folders, autostart, `~/.local/bin`
  and Flatpak's overrides and exports hidden; **the home folder read-only in the view**, writable only in the app's
  `~/.var/app/<id>`, the person's folders (Documents, Downloads, Pictures…) and an opened file, whatever Flatpak grants
  (checked from inside the app: no startup file, autostart entry or key written, created or renamed into place);
  "Open with" never lends the home folder or a folder holding a protected one, and lends sensitive paths read-only;
  LordOS's restrictions also as Flatpak options. Every Flatpak app runs in its root-owned scope and in the launcher's view,
  which hides the user manager's socket, so `flatpak run` can't move it out (checked on a VM: without the view it
  moves itself under `user@`). `fw_app_canon` reads `app-lordos-fp-<id>.scope` as `flatpak:<id>`, so the firewall,
  the Monitor, notifications and the PipeWire guard know the app, and lord-server's keyboard-shortcuts permission
  names its windows `flatpak:<id>` from that scope too (`kbi_identity`), since the view hides the runtime folder the
  `/.flatpak-info` check reads. Checked in a LordOS session on VM 127: bubblewrap, the app and its D-Bus proxy in
  `app-lordos-fp-<id>.scope`, the window on the desktop. Tests: `fpak-test` (47), `fw-rules-test`;
  `build/flatpak-view-probe` and `launch-cli --flatpak` for the VM.
- **Flatpak apps in the desktop**: `lord.apps.flatpak()` lists the installed ones from their exported
  `.desktop` files (name, comment, categories, MIME types, icon; never `Exec`), so they show in search and the launcher
  as `flatpak:<id>` and open through the Flatpak launch path; the Monitor names every process of one (bubblewrap, its
  D-Bus proxy, the app) from its scope, and its firewall lists take `flatpak:<id>`; notification settings name them;
  a Flatpak window is named and drawn after the app lord-server knows from its client's scope, not the `app_id` it
  chose (an SDL game says `tuxocide`). Their exported SVG icons, links into the installation, are allowed to lord-media.
  The launcher's view process shows as `lordos-view`. Checked on VM 127: Tuxocide found and opened from search, its
  window with its own icon, its five processes under its name in Monitor → Processes.
- **Flathub's management commands** (E3): `lord.flatpak` runs only a closed list of `flatpak --user`
  commands (add Flathub from the `.flatpakrepo` the package ships, update the catalog, info, install, update,
  uninstall, remove unused runtimes, list), one at a time, each in its own child in `lordos-net-flathub.scope`: a new
  firewall component, "Flathub" in Monitor → Network (named in every language), with its own rules. The only argument
  from the shell is a ref, checked in C (`app/<id>/<native arch>/<branch>`, never a runtime); never a URL, remote,
  key, file or option, and never `--no-gpg-verify`. Its output comes back as printable UTF-8 lines. Checked on VM 127
  in a session: install and uninstall of a Flathub app ran in that scope; a ref ending in an option was refused.
- **Flathub's catalog, read in a sandbox** (E7): `lord-appstream`, a new helper that links only the C
  library, reads Flathub's AppStream file (opened by lord-server without following any link but Flatpak's own) and,
  inside `sandbox_apply_helper` (no network, no file opened by path, no exec, a memory cap), writes a compact index:
  id, branch, name and summary in the person's language, icon, categories, license, developer and whether Flathub
  verified the app. lord-server checks every line again before `lord.flatpak.catalog()` hands it to the shell. On
  Flathub's real catalog (52 MB): 3,366 apps, 2,240 verified, in 0.07 s. `fpakas-test` (2,096 checks, under
  AddressSanitizer, with random and cut documents).
- **Flathub in the Store** (PCs only): a "Flathub" section. Turning it on shows the package plan for
  `flatpak` (no Recommends) and installs it with the Store's own package job, then adds Flathub from the shipped file
  and fetches the catalog (again when the Store opens a day later; Refresh does it now). The catalog shows the apps
  Flathub verified, with a switch for the rest (`settings.flathub`), as cards with the category and the developer, in
  Discover's search and in each category. An app's page shows, before installing, what it declares (from
  `flatpak remote-info --show-metadata`) in plain words and what LordOS changes for each: never granted (the whole
  session or system bus, starting programs outside its sandbox, systemd, the keyring), narrowed (the home read-only
  but for the person's folders, X11 off while a restriction is on, other apps' bus names cut off under a device
  restriction) or blockable in the Firewall. Apps built on Chromium or Electron (their base is
  `org.electronjs.Electron2.BaseApp` or `org.chromium.Chromium.BaseApp`) are marked "Not yet supported" and can't be
  installed: they need Flatpak's sub-sandboxes, which LordOS doesn't serve yet. Install, Update and Remove (removing
  also removes runtimes no app uses), with Flatpak's progress; Store → Updates has "Update Flathub apps" and
  Store → Installed removes a Flatpak app. `lord.flatpak.supported()` hides the section on other machines. Every
  text in the 35 languages. `sdk/flathubmodel.js` holds the logic (`flathub-model-test`, run on Flathub's real metadata).
  Checked on VM 127 from a session, after removing `flatpak`: the plan said 6 packages, 2.2 MB to download, 11 MB on
  disk, and exactly those were installed (no portal) with the three Flatpak services still masked; the catalog showed
  2,240 verified apps with their icons; GNOME Calculator showed "Internet and your local network", installed with the
  GNOME runtime, opened from its page in `app-lordos-fp-org.gnome.Calculator.scope`, and its removal took the runtime
  with it; MarkText was marked not supported; "Update Flathub apps" ran.
- **Flatpak apps in the Dock and in "Open with"**: the Dock pins a Flatpak app as `flatpak:<id>`
  (Flatpak's id rules, `sdk/dockmodel.js`), from the launcher's "Keep in Dock" or by dragging; its windows group under
  that icon, and a session restore opens it again. Files' and the Terminal's "Open with" offer the Flatpak apps whose
  export declares the file's type (`lord.apps.launchFlatpakWith`), and lord-server refuses one that declares no
  `MimeType`, as it does for Linux apps. The file is lent to the app alone: checked on VM 127 with GNOME's Audio Player
  (Decibels, which asks for no files), whose sandbox saw only `~/Documents/tono-prueba.mp3` and nothing else of the
  home. GNOME Text Editor was pinned from the launcher, opened from the Dock in `app-lordos-fp-org.gnome.TextEditor.scope`
  under its icon, and opened a text file from Files. Tests: `dock-model-test`, `apps-actions-test`.
- **Flatpak test plan run on VM 127** (`docs/FLATPAK.md`, "Results"). Held: Flathub's downloads in
  their own firewall component (blocked → denied, Monitor row), apps in their own scopes with nothing escaping to the
  user manager, no internet and per-domain rules per app, the never-granted bus names and folders even with user
  overrides, no files, no camera, no USB and no Bluetooth, no notifications, updates and freeing unused runtimes.
  Apps that work: GNOME Text Editor, Decibels, Shortwave (but its radio playback, which also fails outside LordOS), Meld, KCalc (Qt 6), Firefox and GNU Emacs (X11). Electron
  apps (MarkText) still don't start and stay marked. Spotify exits at start on any Wayland desktop (it starts on X11
  only and asks for X only as a fallback); its own flags file fixes it.
- **Flatpak apps get Flatpak's sub-sandbox from LordOS itself** (`server/src/fpspawn.c`, AGENTS.md E9):
  lord-server serves `org.freedesktop.portal.Flatpak` and runs each Spawn as the same app, in its own scope and view,
  under its restrictions; Flatpak's own portal stays masked. GNOME apps that load images through glycin needed it:
  Meld crashed at start, Shortwave showed no images. The service exists only while `flatpak` is installed. A security
  review of the branch then closed `sandbox-expose` (a link in the app's own folder could have exported the session
  bus) and made the never-granted bus names cover their wildcards too (`org.freedesktop.*`…).
- **Settings → Flatpak**: whether Flatpak is installed, how much its apps, runtimes and their data
  take, Flathub shown in the Store or not, and "Remove Flatpak completely" (every Flathub app, the runtimes, Flathub,
  optionally the apps' data to the Trash, then the flatpak package with its plan shown and the administrator password).
  Flatpak is only installed when Flathub is turned on, and nothing of it runs in the background.
- **X11 for Flatpak apps, as GNOME and KDE give it**: an app with no files or device blocked keeps
  the X display (socket and cookie in its view); a restricted one gets none. GNU Emacs, X11 only, now starts.

### Fixed

- **After one app with "no microphone" had run, no Flatpak app could record until the next login** (found
  by the test plan): the PipeWire guard counted an exited app's empty scope as running, and couldn't tell which
  Flatpak app a PulseAudio client was (it reports its pid inside its sandbox). Empty scopes no longer count, and a
  Flatpak app's client is matched to a process of its own scope (pipewire-pulse names the app; the pid and its
  connections are checked). The same empty-scope fix applies to Linux apps.
- **Monitor offered no rule or block for a Flatpak app**, although the firewall applies them (`firewall.enforceable`
  left `flatpak:` out). An exited Flatpak app is named without its `flatpak:` prefix.
- **The Store didn't say why Flathub failed**: with Flathub blocked in the Firewall it showed Flatpak's "No such ref",
  and a failed catalog refresh kept the old catalog silently. It now says the Firewall blocked it and where to allow
  it, or that the catalog couldn't be updated.
- **A Flatpak app's notifications showed a plain square**: they now carry the app's name and icon, from the app
  lord-server finds by the sender's scope.
- **One D-Bus message with too many file descriptors closed the whole connection** of the lord-server service that got
  it; it is now refused alone (16 fds per message, was 4). A message whose signature names an fd but carried none
  (an empty list of fds) was taken as invalid and closed the connection too; each fd index is now checked against the
  fds that came. The Flatpak test plan's checks run as `server/tests/fwflatpak/flatpak.sh` (31 on VM 127).
- **`server/Makefile` didn't rebuild objects when a header outside a few folders changed** (`vault/`, `hw/` and others),
  which could link structs of two sizes; every object now depends on every header under `src/*/`.

- **Some SVG app icons stayed empty** (Print Editor, and most Flathub apps: their icons use gradients). nanosvg sets a
  gradient's focus only for a radial gradient; LordOS's check before drawing also read it on a linear one, where it is
  whatever memory malloc gave back. In lord-media's long-lived worker that was a previous icon's bytes, so a valid icon
  was refused as too complex at some sizes (the Dock's magnification asks for many) and then stayed empty. The focus is
  now checked only on radial gradients (the rasterizer doesn't use it). `svgrast-test` reproduces it with reused memory.

- **Some apps were named in the Shavian alphabet.** A `.desktop` key with a language modifier (`Name[en@shaw]`, which
  GNOME apps ship) was read as the plain language (`Name[en]`) and won over the untranslated name, so GNOME
  Calculator from Flathub showed as "𐑒𐑨𐑤𐑒𐑿𐑤𐑱𐑑𐑼" in English. A key with a modifier now never matches, since LordOS's
  languages have none (`apps-actions-test`).

## [0.8.9.3-beta] - 2026-11-20

### Security

- **On PCs, the per-app firewall enforced no rule in 0.8.8.6 to 0.8.9.2.** `lord-netperm` compiles its cgroup BPF
  programs with clang, and `server/Makefile` quietly built it without them when clang was missing. The PC (amd64)
  packages from 0.8.8.6 on were built on a machine without clang, so every "no internet", per-domain rule and blocklist in Monitor → Firewall
  was stored but not applied (the service logged `BPF not available (fw.bpfNotBuilt): no rule is enforced`, and
  Monitor → Firewall showed it in its status line). The device restrictions lost their kernel-side part as well:
  camera, USB and ALSA microphone nodes (`cgroup/dev`) and Bluetooth sockets. What other parts enforce still held:
  the PipeWire guard (microphone, camera), the private view and Landlock (files), notifyd (notifications).
  Found while testing Flatpak apps on a VM, then checked in every package still in the APT repository: 0.8.1 to
  0.8.8.5 have the programs, 0.8.8.6, 0.8.8.7, 0.8.8.8, 0.8.8.9, 0.8.9, 0.8.9.1 and 0.8.9.2 don't. The Raspberry Pi
  (arm64) packages are built on the Pi and have them in every version (checked: 0.8.8.5, 0.8.8.6, 0.8.9, 0.8.9.2). `tools/iso/mkdeb.sh` now refuses to
  build a package whose `lord-netperm` lacks them, with no way to skip that check, and `make` warns when clang is
  missing. Updating to this version restores the rules already saved; nothing has to be set again.

## [0.8.9.2-beta] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed

- **A Linux app restricted in Settings → Privacy didn't start from the desktop.** With no microphone, camera, USB,
  Bluetooth or files, opening it from the Dock, the launcher or search did nothing ("not launched" in its log), since
  the restricted-app view of 0.8.x. lord-server drops from root to the person when the session starts, so it isn't
  dumpable, and the launcher's child couldn't write its new user namespace's map. The tests run the launcher from a
  test tool that is dumpable, so they passed. The child now re-executes itself (`lord-server --launch-view`): a fresh
  process image, dumpable by `execve` and holding none of lord-server's memory, reads the view's plan from a sealed
  memfd, builds the view, applies Landlock and starts the app (`apps_launch_view_main` in `server/src/apps.c`). Making
  the child dumpable instead would have let the person's other processes read that copy of lord-server's memory unless
  Yama stopped them. Checked on a VM from the search: Foot with no microphone (only the display and sound sockets in its
  runtime folder) and with no files (an empty home).

### Documentation

- `docs/FLATPAK.md` checked again (2026-11-19) against 0.8.9.1's code and Debian 13's security updates: Debian ships
  flatpak `1.16.6-1~deb13u3` and xdg-dbus-proxy `0.1.6-1+deb13u3` (DSA-6524-1, DSA-6510-1); polkit is on every image
  since 0.8.8, so masking `flatpak-system-helper` is now required; lord-server already serves FileChooser, OpenURI,
  Inhibit, GlobalShortcuts and ScreenCast (anonymous for a Flatpak caller); lord-web already runs bubblewrap under an
  exception; a new open question (11): the 0.8.8.8 Flatpak identity checks don't work inside the launcher's private
  view. Still not planned for any release. The roadmap entry names the same scope (`app-lordos-fp-<id>`).
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`: a "Release 0.8.9.2 (planned)" section with the clipboard history that scrolls by itself under the
  pointer (#204) and, probably from the same cause, its arrow keys (#203).

## [0.8.9.1-beta] - 2026-11-19

### Changed

- **Web apps' Browser identity: Edge 158.** The Edge identity now names Edge 158, stable this week
  (`WEBPAGE_EDGE_MAJOR` in `server/src/web/webpage.h`, `docs/WEBAPPS.md`); Chrome stays at 157 and Firefox at 160.

- **A desktop session uses about a third less memory (0.8.9.1 memory work).** Measured on a PC with three 1920×1080
  displays (RX 580, Debian 13, transparent huge pages `always`), Lord Workspaces, 7 widgets and a Terminal running
  Claude Code at rest: lord-server's RSS went from 269 MB to 183 MB (−86 MB, −32 %). With the Terminal open it now
  uses less than the same desktop used before without it (185 MB). Each step was one change, measured in a fresh
  session; the method, the tools and the data are in `docs/perf/MEMORY-HEAPTRACK.md` and `docs/perf/0.8.9.1/`.
  - **Transform rasters are freed at rest** (`server/src/ui/paint.c`). The cached raster of a scaled or rotated subtree
    (a window's open or minimize animation, a preview) was freed only after 600 more transform paints, and a desktop at
    rest makes none, so the rasters of 16 slots stayed for the whole session: 57 MB with widgets, 114 MB with the
    Terminal. Rasters unused for 30 s are now freed from the once-a-minute idle trim (`paint_release_idle`), and a slot
    that holds a small raster gives back a buffer more than four times too big (the slots then held 9×9 icons in
    window-sized buffers).
  - **The Terminal's history grows as it fills** (`server/src/term/vt.c`). The history ring was allocated for its whole
    limit at once: 24 bytes per line, 24 MB for a 1,000,000-line history holding 400 lines. It now starts at 1,024 lines
    and doubles up to the limit (`Buffer.max`); reflow and the alternate screen keep their behaviour (`build/vt-ring-test`, in `make test`). Clearing the
    history (`ESC [ 3 J`, which Claude Code sends on redraw) now frees the cleared lines' cells instead of keeping them.
  - **lord-server's static arrays don't use huge pages** (`server/src/main.c`). Its `.bss` is 31 MB of worst-case
    tables, mostly untouched; with transparent huge pages set to `always`, khugepaged turned each 2 MB region with any
    page in use into a whole huge page, and about 16 MB stayed resident. lord-server now marks only that range
    `MADV_NOHUGEPAGE` at start; the heap keeps huge pages (turning them off for the whole process made it larger).
  - The app list and the font list are cut to what their scan found (`apps.c`, `ui/fonts.c`). They were sized for
    1,024 apps and 8,192 fonts (18.6 and 5.8 MB). This did not change the RSS (those pages were never touched) and is
    kept for a smaller address space.
- **A memory report in `compositor.log`**: 10 minutes after login, then every 6 hours, a few `memory:` lines with the
  process (RSS, anonymous, file, huge pages), glibc's heap and its arenas, QuickJS, the image cache, the per-display
  scenes, the terminals (lines, cells, Instant Replay), the blur cache, the transform rasters, the layer, the glyph
  cache and the nodes. Each report runs after `malloc_trim(0)`.

- **Ctrl+←/→ move by word again in apps (GitHub #201).** In Lord Flow and Lord Workspaces, Ctrl+← → ↑ ↓ were taken for
  desktops (switch, Overview, the app's windows) whenever Settings → Desktop & Dock → Desktops allowed it, and that was
  on for everyone: the default was saved with the rest of the settings since 0.8.7. The option is now off by default and
  settings migration 8 turns off the saved default; someone who turned it on after the update keeps it. ❖⌃←/→ always
  switch desktops in every theme. Help, `docs/DESKTOPS.md` and `docs/SHORTCUTS.md` say so.
- **Weather widget: each widget has its own city (GitHub #193).** Changing one widget's city changed every weather
  widget, because the city was one setting. It is now each widget's own (`opts.city`); settings migration 9 gives every
  existing widget the city it showed, and a new widget starts on the last city chosen. The widget's menu has "Change
  city…" for that widget (it said "Choose cities in Clock…"); on the small size the picker was never drawn, and the other
  sizes drew it twice. Widgets on the same city share one forecast and one request; no timer was added. The offline city
  list is still GeoNames' places of 15,000 people or more, so small towns are not in it yet.
- **Control Center: the Wi-Fi tile works like Bluetooth's (GitHub #192, Lord Flow and Lord Workspaces).** It is the
  accent color when Wi-Fi is on; its icon turns Wi-Fi on or off with the same closed `net-up`/`net-down` actions as
  Settings → Network (no new admin action); the rest of the tile opens Settings → Network → Wi-Fi. The bars use the
  accent as in Settings, and the tile shows the connected network's name, or Not connected / Off, instead of the
  interface's. `lord.net.interfaces()` reports `ssid`, which lord-server reads without root from nl80211
  (`GET_INTERFACE`, as `iw dev` does) and keeps only when it is valid UTF-8 without control characters; isolated apps
  have no `lord.net`.
- **Mail: account names in the sidebar use the folders' font and size (GitHub #191),** 13 px in the normal text color and
  semibold, instead of dim 11 px text. The calendar accounts' headers match.
- **Logs: the sidebar scrolls and its groups fold (GitHub #199).** With many app logs the last sources could not be
  reached. The source list scrolls, and Journal, LordOS, Apps, Web apps and Older logs fold with a disclosure triangle,
  as Mail's accounts; the folded groups are remembered per user (`logs.collapsed`).

### Added

- `tools/bench/heaptrack-session.sh install <user> <binary>` runs one user's next session under heaptrack (and only that
  one; `restore` puts the installed binary back), to see which line of code holds the session's memory. heaptrack runs
  as root there (lord-server drops privileges later), so its trace folder must be an absolute path owned by root and not
  a symlink, or the script refuses it (a folder the user could write to would let them plant a symlink where root writes).
  `docs/perf/MEMORY-HEAPTRACK.md` explains the three tools in order (`session-sample.sh`, the memory report, heaptrack),
  how to read heaptrack's result while the session is still running, and why reserved memory is not resident memory.
- `tools/bench/session-sample.sh <user> <minutes> <out.csv> [seconds]` samples one user's `lord-server` session (never
  the login screen's) into a CSV: RSS, anonymous and file-backed memory, processor time in clock ticks and the system's
  MemAvailable every 10 s, with a header of the version, theme, displays, kernel, processor, the session's pid and start
  and `clk_tck`. It only reads `/proc`. Every run in `docs/PERFORMANCE-0.8.9.md` was taken with it.
- **`docs/PERFORMANCE-0.8.9.md`, the performance report of 0.8.9 and 0.8.9.1** (roadmap 0.8.9.1), with every CSV in
  `docs/perf/0.8.9/` and `docs/perf/0.8.9.1/`. On the maintainer's PC (i9-10900, RX 580, 3 × 1920×1080, Debian 13,
  THP `always`, Lord Workspaces): the 0.8.9 desktop just after login 177 MB and 0.2 % of one core; Lord Workspaces'
  wallpaper slideshow **19.0 % of one core** over two hours (559 MB median RSS) and **2.0 %** once turned off in the
  same session (491 MB); 7 widgets about 1 % of one core; a Terminal running Claude Code about +84 MB before the memory
  work; turning huge pages off for the whole process 229–249 MB against 177; each build of the memory loop with its
  CSV's min, median and max (they match the published figures to the MB except ws04: 260.3 against 262). On a
  Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB, a headless autologin session one hour after a reboot: 0.8.8.9 116 MB and 3.4 % of one core,
  0.8.9 113 MB and **6.1 %** (two runs; the one meant for Lord Workspaces kept Lord Flow, so it counts as a second
  Lord Flow run). It also lists what spoiled runs (an old session kept by `systemctl restart lordos`, opening About,
  the slideshow, the scene being set up, the voice, heaptrack). With 0.8.9.1's `lord-server` the Pi's Lord Flow session is unchanged (113 MB, 6.2 %), and Lord Workspaces, measured on the Pi for the first time, uses **99 MB and 0.06 %** of one core: the extra processor at rest is Lord Flow's theme, not the server.

### Fixed

- **Test Bench closed when F5 ran the checks again.** The fractional-scale check asked for a second
  `wp_fractional_scale_v1` on the same window, which the protocol forbids: the compositor ended the connection and the
  bench quit (seen on a desktop with a Lenovo keyboard; any keyboard did it). The checks now keep the one they made, and
  bind the outputs once instead of adding a copy of each on every run (`server/src/testbench/checks.c`; checked by
  running the checks three times in a row on LordOS: the old code quit on the second).

- **The keypad typed nothing and moved the cursor instead (reported with a Lenovo USB keyboard).** Every session
  started with Num Lock off, whatever the firmware had set, so the keypad's digits were Home, End and the arrows. A
  session on a desktop computer (DMI chassis type, or no DMI, as on a Raspberry Pi) now starts with Num Lock on and its
  light lit; laptops keep it off, since their keypad is often printed on the letter keys. Changing the layout (adding
  one in Settings → Keyboard, or switching between them) also built a fresh keyboard state that turned Caps Lock and
  Num Lock off; it keeps both now (`kb_set`, `kb_set_numlock` in `server/src/keyboard.c`; `test_numlock` in
  `server/tests/osk_test.c`).

- **A paused Cloud account kept talking to its provider (GitHub #194).** Pause only held uploads back: a failed mount
  was retried every 30 s, the check listing ran every 10 minutes and the quota call every 30, Files' background listing
  went on, and rclone polled Google Drive for changes every minute; the reporter's paused account kept getting Google's
  quota errors. While an account is paused none of that runs and the mount's change polling is set to 0 (one more rc
  method in the allowlist, `vfs/poll-interval`; back to 60 s on Resume). An account the person paused is not mounted
  until Resume, which mounts it at once; one paused only by the battery keeps its mount but a failed mount is not
  retried (`cloud_bring_up_ok`). What the person does still reaches the provider (opening a file not on this computer,
  Measure, Empty Trash).
- **Logs: the 15 minutes / 1 hour / 24 hours filters did nothing on LordOS's own files (GitHub #194).** The range went
  only to the journal; `cloud.log` and the other files are now filtered too (`inRange`). The exported text shows each row
  as the list does, one line with the provider's multi-line error joined (⏎); the account is written as provider and id,
  never its name (#183's rule: the file may be attached to a public report).
- **Every Cloud provider read "not verified" on 0.8.9 (GitHub #195).** `tools/iso/mkdeb.sh` never installed
  `assets/cloud/providers.json`, so lord-server reported `verified: false` for all of them, Filen included, and Check
  This Account said "Verified on LordOS: no". The package installs it; without the file Settings uses its own copy.
- **The calendar under the clock showed six days per week (GitHub #197; Lord Flow, Lord Classic, Lord Workspaces).**
  The days were a wrapping row of cells a seventh of the panel wide, which left out the panel's 1 px border, so seven
  cells were 2 px too wide and the seventh day went to the next line. Each week is now its own row (`monthWeeks`).
- **Lord Flow's menu bar didn't answer at the top edge of the display (GitHub #190).** Its items were 22 px pills in a
  28 px bar, so the top 3 px, where the pointer stops when pushed up, did nothing. They take the bar's whole height now.
  While a menu is open, moving onto another title opens that menu (`barHover`).
- **lord-server's forecasts: a full table left new places on "Updating…" for good.** It kept at most 8 places and
  never dropped one; it holds 16 and the one asked least recently makes room (`build/wxsvc-test`).
- `rconnect-run-test` failed 7 checks when run from a Terminal inside a LordOS session: it inherited
  `LORDOS_SESSIOND`, and the real lord-sessiond refused its cgroup scope. The test drops the variable.
- **Lord Workspaces' scene test: a window brought back from Minimized after the layout changed** (roadmap 0.8.9.1).
  The scene showed the window coming back at its old width (923 px in a 1231 px slot). The tiler was right: the scene
  ran more than 60 tiler passes in a second, so the tiler's limit put the next pass 1 s later and the scene checked
  before it. A new check changes Two halves to Main and side while a window is minimized and brings it back after
  waiting out the limit; the window fills its new slot.
- `tools/iso/build-arm64.sh` copies `RCLONE_DEB` into the work folder's `out/` before entering the arm64 chroot.
  The host path meant nothing inside the chroot, so the 0.8.9-beta arm64 ISO stopped with "no lordos-rclone"
  until the package was copied there by hand.

- **The release itself:** the paper (meta, the opening, §10.1's table and §10.3) and the site name **0.8.9.1 Beta**

- **Bar charts** (`[[chart:<id>]]` in a page or the paper, `web/content/charts/<id>.json`, drawn by

  `memory-0891` (lord-server's RSS through the memory loop, 269 → 183 MB, with ws02 without the Terminal at 185 MB as a
  reference line; ws03's snapshot left out and said so) and `memory-left-0891` (what is left at rest after ws08).
- **The paper for 0.8.9.1:** §7.1 has the 0.8.9 rows (the slideshow on and off, the floor), a full

- **Features → Own desktop:** the memory chart, a bullet with 0.8.9's slideshow cost and the Raspberry Pi's session,

  a Pi 5 without a monitor) and a link to the report.
- Downloads point at the 0.8.9-beta release, and the paper says the voices' number reading shipped in 0.8.9.

- **Home: "The faces of LordOS"**, a new dark band between the hero (its slideshow stays) and the features (en, es,
  pt). An eyebrow ("One system · many faces"), a two-line title ("We didn't copy a desktop. / We built the engine to
  create many."), and tabs for Lord Flow (since 0.8.0), Lord Classic (since 0.8.3), Lord Workspaces (new in 0.8.9) and a
  dashed "Your next face". Each face shows a real screenshot in a drawn monitor (Lord Flow in light or dark with the
  site's theme; Lord Classic is the new `docs/screenshots/desktop-classic.png`, Lord Workspaces the new
  `docs/screenshots/desktop-workspaces.png`), a kicker, a lead, three points, a "Who it's for" box and a button to its

  (one engine, switch live, no nudging at first start, built for LordOS; the mockup's wording for this card and the lead

  another desktop is one entry plus its texts (`faces.items.<id>` in `web/i18n/*.json`); "New in" turns into "Since"

## [0.8.9-beta] - 2026-11-18

### Added

- **Lord Workspaces has its own pointer**: the default arrow becomes a rounded tip with no tail, filled with the
  person's accent colour, with LordOS's white outline and soft shadow; it follows the accent when it changes. Only the
  default pointer: the hand, the text cursor and the resize arrows stay LordOS's. Lord Flow and Lord Classic keep the
  black arrow (`startShell` puts it back for every theme). `cursor_set_accent` in `cursor.c` draws it (rounded
  polygons in the signed-distance shapes, a colour fill), `lord.input.pointerAccent('#RRGGBB' | null)` takes only a
  colour, and `setPointerAccent` in the SDK; `build/cursor-test` checks the fill, the size, the text cursor and going
  back. Linux apps that ask for the default shape get it too.
- **The password-and-code drive (`iclouddrive`) confirmed on a Raspberry Pi (GitHub #165).** A user's Check This Account on aarch64 passed
  every step, added to the provider's evidence next to the maintainer's own test on a PC (`assets/cloud/providers.json`).
- **A window that draws its own title bar no longer sticks to the pointer after Minimize (GitHub #189).** Floorp,
  clicked on Minimize while the pointer moved a little, asked to be moved once the button was already up; the move
  then had no release to end it and the minimized window followed the pointer until the next click. lord-server now
  ignores a move or resize request with no button down (xdg-shell allows it), and minimizing a window ends a move of
  it still under way (`wm.cancelGrab`). (`server/src/wl/wl.c`, `sdk/wayland.js`, `sdk/windows.js`)
- **Security (Claude Security review of the 0.8.9 branch).** Four findings, all in code new in this version, fixed:
  - Streams checked no TLS certificate: FFmpeg only verifies when asked, so an https, HLS-over-https or rtmps camera
    or channel accepted any server, and a camera password from the keyring could go to someone in the middle. lord-stream
    now asks for the certificate against the system's CAs and the host name on every open, nested HLS and DASH opens
    included (`lm_tls_verify`, `server/src/media/helper/lm_io.c`); a self-signed server fails with "can't open". rtsps
    can't be checked with FFmpeg 7.1 (its RTSP demuxer passes no TLS options), which docs/MEDIA.md says.
  - The https M3U list download checked no certificate either (`server/src/media/stream/ls_m3u.c`).
  - lord-server leaked a parsed list when lord-stream sent JSON that wasn't an array (`m3u_result`,
    `server/src/media/media.c`).
  - A use-after-free in `lord.setProp(id, 'wave', …)`: a getter on the object could destroy the node while it was
    being written. The values are now read first and the node looked up again by id and serial; `lord.setStyle(id,
    'gradient', …)` and the property key of `setProp` had the same pattern and are fixed the same way
    (`server/src/ui/js.c`). `tests/js_getter_destroy.sh` runs it headless (found with AddressSanitizer on the old code).
- **The clock widget can show a second hand.** Its menu has a third style, "Analog with seconds", next to Analog and
  Digital: a thin hand in the accent colour (and an accent centre) that moves every second; the other two still change
  once a minute. The hand is its own node on a shared one-second feed, so each tick repaints only the square it sweeps,
  and like every widget feed it stops while the widget is behind a window, the displays are off or the session is
  locked. Named in all 35 languages. (`sdk/deskwidgets.jsx`)
- **Cyberpunk City HD, a new wallpaper category** (all themes' Settings → Wallpaper): seventeen pictures made for
  LordOS, in the order of a journey from the road outside into the city: Panorama, Neon Road Entrance, Heart of the
  City, Skyline Highway, Rings and Bridges, Flower Boulevard, Neon Cherry Avenue, Maglev Station, Pier and Train, Sky
  Terrace, Metropolis Lookout, and a closing series with a woman in the same city (Neon Rider, Night Watch, Hooded,
  Unmasked, Night Pose, Portrait). Named in every language; the category's name is a proper name and stays the same
  everywhere. Panorama and Neon Road Entrance are 3840×2160 originals: a 1920×1080 base (quality 92, 4:4:4) and the 4K
  size as an `@3840x2160` variant (quality 95, 4:4:4: neon edges blur with 4:2:0), so a 1080p screen never decodes
  the 4K file. The other fifteen were made again at 1672×941 (the first versions were crops of one picture and looked
  soft) and are brought up to 1920×1080 once with Lanczos, with no 4K file that would add bytes and no detail;
  22.4 MB with the thumbnails. `tools/gen-wallpapers.mjs` now takes JPEG originals, makes the 1920×1080 base for an
  original larger than that (and, for a category that asks for it, for a smaller one), has per-category quality,
  takes the category's order from an `order.txt`, and keeps the categories it isn't given in `index.json`.
  (`assets/wallpapers/cyberpunk/`, `assets/wallpapers/README.md`, `sdk/wallpapers.js`)
- **Lord Workspaces' own default accent: rosa**, to go with Cyberpunk City HD's neon. `settings.accent` is now `null`
  until the person chooses one, and `null` means the theme's default: azul in Lord Flow and Lord Classic, rosa in Lord
  Workspaces (`DEFAULT_ACCENT`, `themes/workspaces/tokens.js`). Each theme's tokens carry `accentName`, so the pickers
  (Settings → Appearance, the Control Centers) mark the accent in use and Linux apps get its name through the portal.
  Settings migration 7 turns the saved `azul` (everyone's default until now, saved with the rest of the settings)
  into `null`, like migration 5 did for the wallpaper; any other accent stays. A new install that picks Lord
  Workspaces starts with the panorama and the pink accent. (`sdk/settings.js`, `themes/*/tokens.js`,
  `apps/settings/index.jsx`, `sdk/theme.js`)
- **Lord Workspaces' own default wallpaper: Cyberpunk City HD's panorama.** `settings.wallpaper` is now `null` until
  a picture is chosen, and `null` is the theme's default: Lord Workspaces declares its own (theme.json
  `"wallpaper": { "default" }`, tokens `defaultWallpaper`), Lord Flow and Lord Classic keep Lumo Celestial
  (`wallpaperIdFor(s, d, def)`, `findWallpaper(list, id, def)`). Settings migration 5 turns the saved
  `"lumo-celestial"` (everyone's default since 0.8.2, saved with the other settings) into `null`; any other picture
  stays, and Lord Flow and Lord Classic look the same. Someone who had picked Celestial on purpose sees the panorama
  the first time they open Lord Workspaces and can pick Celestial again. (`sdk/settings.js`, `sdk/wallpapermodel.js`,
  `sdk/thememeta.js`; tests in `wallpaper_model_test.mjs`, `keyboard_default_test.mjs`, `workspaces_model_test.mjs`)
- **Lord Workspaces: wallpaper slideshow** (Settings → Wallpaper, shown only in Lord Workspaces; off by default).
  "Change the wallpaper automatically" goes through a category's pictures (Cyberpunk City HD unless another is
  chosen) every 1, 5, 15 or 30 minutes or every hour (a minute when turned on), and with several displays "Different
  picture on each display" gives each display its own shuffled order, never a picture another display shows, with the
  changes staggered over the interval. The change is a cross-dissolve with a Ken Burns pan: the next picture fades in
  over 2.4 s while it drifts into place from one of eight directions (every slideshow picture is drawn 2 % larger than
  its display on each side, so no edge shows); with Reduce motion a plain 0.4 s crossfade. A pan, not a zoom: on a
  1080p display on the CPU each frame of the pan takes 9.6–10 ms against 52–53 ms for a 6 % zoom
  (`build/engine-test bench-slideshow`, a window and two blurred bars over it). The next picture is decoded 8 s ahead by
  lord-server's image workers at the size it is drawn at (a
  `thumb:` source may now be an `asset:` path, and `IMG_THUMB_MAX` is 4096), so a change never waits on a decode on the
  interface's thread; the picture that left is unmounted. No change while nobody sees the screen (displays off,
  session locked), on Power Saver or a low battery, or on a display hidden by a window. Off it costs nothing (the same
  `theme_cost_scene` numbers in all three themes); on, two timers per change and no interval. Turning it on turns the
  moving wallpapers off; choosing a picture or a video turns it off. Shared logic in the SDK (`sdk/slideshowmodel.js`,
  `sdk/slideshow.jsx`, `SlideshowWallpapers`), turned on by the theme's theme.json (`"slideshow": true`); all text in
  every language. Not yet checked on real monitors (only the stub scene with three displays) or on the
  GPU path. (`themes/workspaces`, `apps/settings/Slideshow.jsx`, `server/src/ui/js.c`, `server/src/ui/ui.h`,
  docs/WORKSPACES.md "Wallpaper and slideshow"; tests in `server/tests/slideshow_model_test.mjs` (new, in `make test`),
  `workspaces_scene.mjs`, `build/engine-test` `test_image_wallpaper_thumb`, timing in `build/engine-test bench-slideshow`)
- **First start: choose your desktop.** The first session of a new account on an installed system opens a three-step
  chooser in the language picked in the installer (`sdk/firststart.jsx`, `sdk/firststartmodel.js`; docs/SETTINGS.md,
  "First start"). Step 1, over the dimmed desktop: the crown, "Choose your desktop" and three equal cards for Lord Flow,
  Lord Classic and Lord Workspaces, each with a real picture (`assets/desktops/*.jpg`, 640 × 400, about 40 KB each), its
  name and the theme's own description; the cards come in a random order every time, none is chosen and none is
  marked as recommended, and "See it live" waits for a choice. Step 2: the chosen desktop is applied for real with the
  live theme switch, and the panel becomes a small floating box (330 px) on the end side of the work area at about
  mid-height, never over the Dock, the Classic taskbar or the Workspaces spine; its grip drags it anywhere inside the
  display's work area, the three names switch live (a ✓ on the current one), with Back and Use this. Step 3, "Change it
  whenever you like": a drawn replica of Settings → Appearance in the person's language with Desktop style ringed and
  the chosen desktop selected, the path Settings → Appearance → Desktop style, Back and Start. Back works on every
  step; the step, the pick, the order and the box's place are kept in `settings.firstStart` across the theme switch
  (the JS context is discarded) and checked when read back, and a failed switch leaves the theme as it was. Tab, Space,
  Enter and Escape (Back) work throughout, and it follows right-to-left languages. It never shows on the live system,
  on the OVA's first boot, on the login screen or to anyone who already used LordOS: settings migration 6 marks
  `desktopChosen` on a settings file that shows an earlier session (`welcomeShown`, `sessionSaved` or a chosen
  `theme`), while the files the installer, the OVA's first boot and Settings → Users write for a new account don't
  count. It is mounted by the SDK for all three themes, "Welcome to LordOS" and Lord Workspaces' activity onboarding
  wait for it, and once done it leaves no listener or timer (the three themes' idle wakeups are unchanged). Settings →
  Appearance's drawn desktop-style pictures moved into the SDK (`sdk/stylethumb.jsx`, `DesktopStyleThumb`) so the
  replica draws the same ones. 11 new texts in all 35 languages. Tests: `server/tests/firststart_model_test.mjs` (51
  checks: who sees it, the random order, the saved state, Back and forward, the box's place) and
  `firststart_scene.mjs` over each theme (33 checks each: the whole wizard, the switch and resume, the drag, the keys,
  nothing left after Start), both in `make test`.
- **Desktop widgets in Lord Flow and Lord Classic too**, the same as in Lord Workspaces: "Add widget…" in the
  wallpaper's right-click menu opens the catalog (search, categories, sizes), widgets sit on each display's grid, can be
  dragged to another block and keep their data fresh through the shared widget feed. The catalog moved from the theme
  into the SDK (`sdk/widgetpicker.jsx`, `WidgetPicker`, `widgetPicker`), in the theme's colours; a theme can give its own
  panel (Lord Workspaces passes its glass Surface).
- **Settings → Cloud: a color for each account** (issue #184). Each account's page has a row of colors: Automatic (the
  order the account was added in, so two accounts of one provider still differ) or one of the palette's, shown in Files,
  the Cloud menu and Logs (`settings.cloudColors`, read by `accountColor` in `sdk/cloudmodel.js`).
- **Screenshots: another capture without closing the markup editor (GitHub #166).** The markup
  editor's toolbar has **New Screenshot** (also Ctrl+N): it brings the capture panel back (entire screen, window,
  selection, color, text, record), and the editor stays open with its picture, so you can take as many captures as
  you need and mark each one up. Before, the panel closed at the capture and only closing the editor and opening
  Screenshots again gave another one. (`apps/screenshots/editor.jsx` `onNewCapture`, the `screenshots.newCapture` text
  in every language.) Checked in `screenshots_newcapture_scene.mjs`.
- **Display scaling at 75 % and 80 %, for more space on small screens** (GitHub #158; all themes). Settings → Displays
  offers them before 100 % on displays whose desktop stays within 2560 × 1600 logical (1280 × 800, 1366 × 768, 1080p,
  1200p, also rotated): a 1280 × 800 laptop at 75 % is a 1707 × 1067 desktop. They show as one more tile ("more
  space") and in the list, with a note saying the desktop's size and that Linux apps look a little softer. lord-server
  accepts exactly 75 and 80 (`out_scale_valid`; 50–70 % stay refused, and nothing is recommended or rounded below
  100); its drawing already handled a scale below 1 (a mirrored smaller display). Wayland clients are asked for 100 %
  (`client_pct` in `wl.c`) and X11 apps get 100 %, and LordOS draws both smaller; the pointer keeps its size. Not yet
  checked on the VM or a real 1280 × 800 laptop. (`server/src/outputs.c`, `outputs.h`, `server/src/wl/wl.c`,
  `server/src/hw/display.c`, `sdk/displaylayout.js`, `apps/settings/Displays.jsx`, `docs/DISPLAYS.md`; tests in
  `build/outputs-test`, `build/engine-test` `test_scale_below_100`, `server/tests/display_layout_test.mjs`)
- **Settings → Network → Wi-Fi shows which network you are on, and manages saved ones** (GitHub #167). The list is
  now "Available Wi-Fi networks": the network LordOS is connected to comes first whatever its signal, as "<name> —
  Connected" with its own Disconnect button (the header keeps only Scan, and the radio picker with two radios); the
  others follow strongest first, with the Control Center's signal bars instead of the text ones. Saved networks put the
  connected one first, then those in range with a Connect button, then the rest marked "Not in range", each with
  Forget, and a footer says LordOS joins them by itself. `net-wifi-scan` adds `"current"` to the network the
  interface is joined to (wpa_supplicant's `STATUS`, read only; one the scan missed is listed with `SIGNAL_POLL`'s
  level); no new action or argument. (`apps/settings/Network.jsx`, `wifimodel.js`, `server/src/net/wifi.c`
  `wifi_status_ssid`; `server/tests/wifi_model_test.mjs`, `net-test wifi-status`)
- **Window snapping in Lord Flow, and a switch for it** (GitHub #182; all themes). Dragging a window to the left or
  right edge of a display fills that half of its work area, near a corner a quarter, and to the top edge the whole area
  (maximized), with a rounded preview in the accent's color under the window while dragging. Dragging it away gives it
  back the size it had. Lord Classic and Lord Workspaces already did this; Lord Flow now does too (`configureWindows({
  snap: true })`), including a maximized window dragged out by its bar. **Settings → Desktop & Dock → Snap windows to
  the screen edges** (on by default, `settings.windowSnap`, a new key with no migration) turns dragging to the edges off
  in every theme; the window menus' layouts and Lord Classic's ❖ arrows keep working. Workspaces' thirds are unchanged.
  (`sdk/snap.js` `snapAllowed`, `sdk/windows.js`, `themes/default/index.jsx`, `themes/default/components/Window.jsx`,
  `apps/settings/Dock.jsx`; `server/tests/snap_test.mjs`)
- **Settings → Users: a picture for your account, chosen and fitted** (all themes). "Choose image…" opens the file
  chooser instead of a path to type; the picture (any size or format lord-media reads, turned upright) shows in a
  circle, the slider zooms and dragging places it; Save cuts that square from the full picture, scales it to 512 × 512
  and writes a JPEG (`~/.cache/lordos/avatar.jpg`, a few dozen KB even from a 100 MB photo), which `user-avatar` copies
  as before. The preview works on a copy at most 1200 px wide. (`apps/settings/AvatarEditor.jsx`, `avatarmodel.js`)
- **Text consoles while the desktop runs: Ctrl+Alt+F1…F12** (all themes). The keyboard is the session's, so the kernel
  never saw the keys and nothing happened. Now lord-server takes them and asks lord-sessiond, which keeps tty1 in
  `VT_PROCESS` mode: leaving locks the session (as Lock Screen), takes the monitor back and lets the kernel switch;
  Ctrl+Alt+F1 brings tty1 back with the login screen locked for that user. Modifiers held at the switch are released.
  (docs/SESSIONS.md, "Text consoles")
- **Text mode and `startlordos`, for starting the desktop by hand as startx** (docs/SESSIONS.md, "Text mode"): the
  boot menu gets **LordOS (text mode)** (`/etc/grub.d/11_lordos_text`, the system's first entry plus `lordos.text=1`);
  Settings → Users → **Start in text mode** keeps it for every start (the closed admin action `boot-text on|off`,
  administrators only, writes `/etc/lordos/text-mode`). Then lord-sessiond leaves the monitor alone,
  `lordos-text-login.service` puts a login prompt on tty1, and `startlordos` there brings up the login screen (asked
  over `/run/lordos/start.sock`, accepted only from someone logged in on the console in front, typing there; you sign
  in with your password and get the whole session). Without lord-sessiond, `startlordos` runs lord-server as you on
  that console, with Ctrl+Alt+F1…F12 too (lord-server lets the card and the input go while another console is in front).
  `lord.users.list()` tells Settings whether text mode is on (`textMode`).

- **Lord Workspaces: the rest of its proposal.** Checked item by item against the theme's design document:
  - **Context Spine:** at the bottom, the shortcuts' help and Settings beside the Control Center. The activities
    themselves stay on the strip's pills only.
