  English text makes each of the four statements, and it is aligned to the start.

- **26 new interface languages, each one complete** (maintainer's request, 2026-11-12; completed 2026-11-15): Indonesian (`id`), Japanese (`ja`),
  German (`de`), Hindi (`hi`), Malay (`ms`), Bengali (`bn`), Simplified Chinese (`zh-Hans`), Traditional Chinese
  (`zh-Hant`), Ukrainian (`uk`), Polish (`pl`), Arabic (`ar`), Vietnamese (`vi`), Swedish (`sv`), Greek (`el`), Dutch
  (`nl`), Turkish (`tr`), Hungarian (`hu`), Persian (`fa`), Russian (`ru`), Romanian (`ro`), Finnish (`fi`), Urdu
  (`ur`), Bulgarian (`bg`), Korean (`ko`), Thai (`th`) and Azerbaijani (`az`). They were chosen from lordos.org's own
  visit statistics (CloudWatch, the 30 days to 2026-11-12): every language spoken in a country with at least 5
  distinct visitors. Each is an `assets/locales/<id>/` folder with `meta.json` (its name in its
  own language, the main region, `rtl` for Arabic, Persian and Urdu) and `format.json` for that region: month and
  day names from glibc 2.41 or CLDR 45's format forms (the genitive or partitive months a date needs: «12 ноября
  2026 г.», «torstai 12. marraskuuta 2026»), CLDR 45's full-date patterns («2026年11月12日木曜日», «الخميس، ١٢ نوفمبر
  ٢٠٢٦»), separators, and the 12- or 24-hour clock glibc has for the region. Every one of them is complete: all
  12,436 keys of every app, window and message, the emoji names and keywords and the country names included, with
  its own plural forms (`node tools/i18n-check.mjs` shows `12436/12436 keys` for each and no partial language). They
  began on 2026-11-12 as partial languages (`"partial": true`) with the core set below; on 2026-11-15 the rest was
  translated, under the maintainer's business rule that a language ships complete, never partial, and that every
  text changed in English reaches every language in the same release or pre-release, and `"partial"` was dropped from
  their `meta.json`. A computer whose LANG is one of them starts in it, on the desktop and on the login screen.
  Settings → Language & Region, the installer and the login screen list them from their `meta.json`, with no code
  list to edit.
- **Catalan, Filipino and Swahili, each one complete** (maintainer's request, 2026-11-15; added and completed the same
  day): Catalan (`ca`, Català, region `ca_ES`), Filipino (`fil`, Filipino, `fil_PH`) and Swahili (`sw`, Kiswahili,
  `sw_KE`), chosen from lordos.org's visits as the 26 were: Spain, the Philippines and Kenya. That makes 35 interface
  languages, every one with all 12,436 keys (`node tools/i18n-check.mjs`: `12436/12436 keys` for `ca`, `fil` and
  `sw`), the emoji names and keywords and the country names included. All three are left to right, write 0–9 and use
  Inter. Their `format.json` comes from glibc 2.41 and CLDR 45: Catalan writes its months with «de» («diumenge, 15 de
  novembre de 2026», «d’abril»), a 24-hour clock and «1.234.567,89»; Filipino puts the month first («Linggo, Nobyembre
  15, 2026», 11/15/2026), a 12-hour clock with AM/PM and «1,234,567.89»; Swahili writes «Jumapili, 15 Novemba 2026»,
  15/11/2026, the 12-hour clock glibc has for `sw_KE` and `sw_TZ`, «1,234,567.89», and glibc's short days (J1–J5,
  Alh, Ij). Catalan and Swahili use the `one-other` plural rule; Filipino brings a **new plural rule, `filipino`**
  (`sdk/plurals.js`, CLDR 45 for whole numbers): `other` only for numbers ending in 4, 6 or 9 (4, 14, 26, 109), `one`
  for every other (0–3, 5, 7, 8, 10–13, 21, 100), checked against CLDR's samples in `server/tests/locales_test.mjs`
  and accepted by `tools/i18n-pack.mjs new`. `fil` is the **first language with a three-letter ISO 639 code**, as glibc
  names its region; the folders, `languageOfLocale`, `i18n-pack`, Settings, the installer and the login screen
  already took two or three letters, and Read aloud's fallback language for a text too short to tell (`uiLang` in
  `sdk/voice.js`) now takes the whole id instead of its first two letters (`fil`, not `fi`). `tools/brand-check.mjs`
  allows two Swahili words that are spelled like brand names: the word for March (the month in glibc `sw_KE` and
  CLDR `sw`) and the word for journey (in the wallpaper names). Like the 26, they have had no review by native
  speakers yet (the Translation review issue form asks for one). Docs: docs/LANGUAGES.md's section "Catalan, Filipino
  and Swahili", the plural rules table and the count of 35 languages; docs/TRANSLATING.md.
- **The core set** a new language translates first, in `tools/i18n-core.json` (Lithuanian's first part, 1,052 of
  12,415 English keys): the login screen, the desktop, Files, the installer, About, the app names, the file dialogs,
  the force-quit and calculator texts, and Settings' sections, Language & Region and Date & Time formats.
  `node tools/i18n-check.mjs` prints a partial language's coverage of it (`core set (tools/i18n-core.json): N/1052`)
  and fails when a core entry no longer matches an English key.
- **Romanian plurals** (`romanian`: 1 → one; 0, 2–19, 101–119 → few; 20–100 → other). The plural rules moved
  from `sdk/i18n.js` to `sdk/plurals.js` (pure, with `pluralCategories(rule)`), and the new
  `server/tests/locales_test.mjs` (in `make -C server test`) checks every rule against CLDR 45's whole-number samples
  and every bundled language's `meta.json` and `format.json` (a known rule, a region of the language, the direction,
  12 months and 7 days, only LordOS's date placeholders, the clock's AM/PM words, native digits).
  `tools/i18n-pack.mjs new` refuses an unknown plural rule.
- **Native digits** in `format.json` (`"native": { "digits", "decimal", "group" }`): Persian writes «۱٬۲۳۴٬۵۶۷٫۸۹ ·
  ۲۱:۰۵», Arabic «١٬٢٣٤٬٥٦٧٫٨٩» (ar_MA, ar_DZ and ar_TN keep 0–9, as CLDR has them) and Bengali «১,২৩৪,৫৬৭.৮৯»,
  in dates, times and numbers, only when the region is of the language itself: English with region fa_IR keeps
  «1,234,567.89».
- **Screen-sharing API: the visitor picks the display, and text no key types still arrives.** Two changes to the
  public sharing API that Desk go-link uses (docs/SCREEN-SHARING.md):
  - **Displays.** A share still starts on the display Settings → Displays → "Screenshots and sharing" names (the main
    display by default, or all of them), with no chooser: the app's one-time permission and the visitor's own
    acceptance are unchanged. New in the wire format: `SHARE_DISPLAYS` (63) lists the session's displays to the
    holder of a running share (each one's id, the connector's, its place and logical size, the picture's pixels, a
    main flag and its name; with more than one display, last, "all of them" as one picture, `SW_DISPLAY_ALL`) and says
    which one the picture is of; it comes when the share starts, after each request and whenever a display is
    plugged, unplugged or moved. `SHARE_DISPLAY` (57, a u32 id; 0 is the default again) moves the picture to another
    display: the frame that feeds the session's encoder becomes that display's (`feed_out` in `server/src/main.c`),
    the whole of it is painted again with a keyframe before anything that depends on the old one, and pointer
    positions stay in the shown picture's pixels, so a click lands where it was aimed on any display. An id that is
    gone changes nothing; a display that leaves while shown sends the picture back to the default. Viewing another
    display needs nothing beyond `screen-share`: the indicator is on every display. A recording made while a share
    runs follows the share's display (one door at a time, so no 5673 viewer can see the difference). A client that
    never reads the list never sees a difference (`server/src/remote/share.c`, `sharewire.c`).
  - **`SHARE_TEXT`.** Text from a visitor's input method (an accent, ñ on a US layout, €, Japanese) was typed only
    where a key of the active layout types each character, and the rest was dropped: on VM 127, with a US layout,
    " ñandú ÁÉ ¿€?" arrived as " and  ?". Now a Latin letter with a mark that the layout has as a dead key goes as
    the dead key and then the letter (`sw_dead_split`), and anything else goes as an input method's finished text to
    the field that has the keyboard (`js_commit_text` in `server/src/ui/js.c`): a LordOS field, or a Linux app's
    field with text input on, which gets the whole text in one commit (GTK 4 put committed letters ahead of typed ones
    when the two were mixed). An app without text input (X11, a terminal) still gets only what keys type. The same
    checks as before run first (system surfaces, protected windows, the holder's windows, the authentication prompt).
  - Tests: `share-test` 342 checks (the list byte for byte, names cleaned and cut at a code point, `SHARE_DISPLAY`'s
    lengths, dead-key splits), `share-fuzz` with `SHARE_DISPLAY`, `osk-test` (`osk_room`), and six new checks in
    `server/tests/share_e2e.sh` (`share-client` learned `pick` and `shown`); on VM 127 (2026-11-12) 59 of its 61
    checks passed in isolated headless sessions, and the two that failed count `lord-media` processes of the same
    user, which a second LordOS session on that machine had running. With a real visitor from desk.go-link.org on
    VM 127: no chooser, the main display shown, the pointer, clicks, the wheel, Ctrl+A, End and Enter, and " ñandú
    ÁÉ ¿€? 日本" into Notes and into GTK 4's Print Editor on a US layout. **Not tested:** switching to a second
    display, because VM 127 has one (a QEMU `std` VGA); the pointer on a scaled or rotated second display.
- **The source of every image, listed and offered** (GPL compliance, maintainer's decision, 2026-11-15). Each image
  (both live ISOs, the OVA and the Raspberry Pi image) is published with `<image>.sources.tsv`: one line per source
  package and version in it, the binary packages built from it, and where that exact source is:
  `https://snapshot.debian.org/package/<source>/<version>/` for Debian's, LordOS's own copy in
  `lordos.org/apt/pool/rpi/source/` or Raspberry Pi's archive for the Pi's (FFmpeg, firmware, utilities), this
  repository at the release tag for LordOS's packages (with a note that `lord-doc` and `lord-media` link
  GPL-2.0-or-later builds of Poppler and FFmpeg), Raspberry Pi's kernel tree at the exact commit plus
  `tools/rpi/build-kernel.sh` and `/boot/config-<release>` for the LordOS Raspberry Pi kernel (6.18.57: commit
  `234188315037`), and rclone's tag for `lordos-rclone`. `tools/release/image-sources.sh` writes it from the image's
  own dpkg database (`dpkg-query --admindir`, `${source:Package}` and `${source:Version}`), deduplicated by source;
  `tools/iso/build.sh`, `build-ova.sh` and `tools/rpi/build-img.sh` run it on the image's system before the APT lists
  are removed, so each package's origin (Debian or Raspberry Pi) comes from the lists, and the OVA's list is dated
  with its build clock like the rest of the OVA. It also reads a published file without root, a mount or a loop
  device: an ISO's `live/filesystem.squashfs` in place (`unsquashfs -o`, its offset found in the ISO 9660 and Rock
  Ridge directory), the Pi image's or the OVA's ext4 system partition with `debugfs` at its offset (MBR or GPT)
  after `xz` or `qemu-img` into `$TMPDIR`. It warns about a package in no APT list or a Pi kernel with no known
  commit, and names the Raspberry Pi sources LordOS keeps no copy of. Tested on synthetic MBR and GPT images
  (`.img.xz`, an OVA with a stream-optimized VMDK) and on a real xorriso-made live ISO; not yet run on a LordOS
  image. The written offer is new: [docs/SOURCE-OFFER.md](docs/SOURCE-OFFER.md) and
  [lordos.org/legal/source-code](https://lordos.org/legal/source-code/) offer the complete corresponding source of
  any copyleft program in any image or package LordOS has published since 0.8.0, for at least three years after it
  was last published, free as a download, asked for through a new "Source code request" issue form
  (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/source-request.yml`) or the iPERFEX contact form. The 0.8.8 images, published before the
  lists, get theirs from the published files (docs/RELEASING.md, "Source code"). The ISO and arm64 build chroots
  need `python3` (docs/ISO.md).
- **LordOS keeps the kernel sources of its Raspberry Pi images itself** (GPL compliance, maintainer's decision,
  2026-11-15: "si, guarda la copia del kernel"). The 0.8.8 Pi image's GPL sources that only third parties served are
  now pinned for lordos.org's APT pool, `pool/rpi/source/` (unindexed, append-only, next to FFmpeg and kms++), so the
  offer no longer depends on Raspberry Pi's archive or GitHub keeping them:
  - **Raspberry Pi's kernel** `linux 1:6.18.50-1+rpt1` (`linux-image-6.18.50+rpt-rpi-v8`, the Pi 4 kernel, and
    `linux-image-rpi-v8`, `linux-base-*`), **`firmware-nonfree 1:20260519-1~bpo13+1+rpt1`** (`firmware-brcm80211`)
    and **`raspi-firmware 1:1.20260915-1`** (the boot firmware and the kernel hook), in
    `tools/release/rpi-mirror.list`. Raspberry Pi's signed `Sources` index keeps only the newest version of each
    source (on 2026-11-15: `linux 1:6.18.60-1+rpt1`, `firmware-nonfree …+rpt2`), so `linux 6.18.50` and
    `firmware-nonfree +rpt1` are no longer in any of its signed indexes (trixie, bookworm, forky; main, beta,
    untested), though its pool still has the files. A new line kind, `source-pool`, pins such a version: the `.dsc`
    from the pool over https, accepted only with the SHA-256 recorded in the list, then every file it names by the
    `.dsc`'s own `Checksums-Sha256`. Checked independently: `linux_6.18.50.orig.tar.xz` is kernel.org's
    `linux-6.18.50.tar.xz` (SHA-256 `d2fc041d…`) and `firmware-nonfree_20260519.orig.tar.xz` is the one Raspberry Pi's
    signed index lists for `+rpt2`; only the two `.dsc` and `.debian.tar.xz` files rest on the recorded pin (the
    `.dsc` are signed by Raspberry Pi's uploaders, whose keys LordOS doesn't pin). `raspi-firmware 1.20260915-1` is
    still in the signed index and is an ordinary `source` line.
  - **The LordOS Raspberry Pi kernel** `linux-lordos-rpi-2712 6.18.57-3+lordos`: another new line kind, `tarball`,
    pins Raspberry Pi's tree at commit `234188315037848e5b07d65b85d38edc64095caa` by URL (GitHub's tarball of the
    commit) and SHA-256 (`d56a9ef7…`, 257,630,958 bytes). Uncompressed it is byte for byte `git archive
    --format=tar` of that commit (SHA-256 `688210f7…`, checked with git 2.47.3; its pax header names the commit),
    and `apt-repo.sh` checks that too when it downloads it. It is published with the new
    `tools/rpi/kernel/linux-lordos-rpi-2712_6.18.57-3+lordos/`: the exact `.config` of the 0.8.8 image's kernel
    (`/boot/config-6.18.57-lordos.3-rpi-2712`, read from the published image; SHA-256 `65f4a3ed…`), `build-kernel.sh`
    as it built revision 3 (LordOS commit `ee1f03f4`, unchanged since) and `SOURCE` (the commit, the hashes, the build
    command). `tools/rpi/build-kernel.sh` now writes the tree's `tar_sha256` into `out/SOURCE` and prepares that
    folder for every future kernel in `out/source/`.
  - `tools/release/apt-repo.sh`: `rpi_src_import` handles `source-pool`, and a `.dsc` already in the cache with the
    pinned SHA-256 no longer needs Raspberry Pi's index (before, a pinned source dropped from the index stopped every
    `--rpi` build); the new `rpi_tar_import`; only each pinned version's files are copied to the pool; the `.config`,
    `SOURCE` and scripts are served as text; without `gpgv` (this Debian host has none) Raspberry Pi's `InRelease` is
    checked with `gpg` in an empty home holding only Raspberry Pi's key, requiring its fingerprint in `VALIDSIG`.
    `tools/release/image-sources.sh` points these sources and the LordOS kernel at `lordos.org/apt/pool/rpi/source/`
    and warns about a LordOS kernel whose source isn't kept. The files were fetched and verified on
    2026-11-15 (`apt-repo.sh rpi-fetch`, and an offline build with a throwaway key) and are published at
    https://lordos.org/apt/pool/rpi/source/ (checked the same day: the `SOURCE` file and the three `.dsc` files answer).
- **A web app's own Appearance: Automatic, Light or Dark — shipped hidden until WPEPlatform** (maintainer's
  approval, 2026-11-15; held back the same day by the maintainer's decision: "when we move to WPEPlatform we'll have
  dark mode"). **What ships now:** the code and the registry key stay, but Light and Dark are unavailable. WPE 2.48's
  legacy API can't set `prefers-color-scheme` for CSS, so a site that picks its theme with CSS (WhatsApp, for
  example) never saw the choice and it only half worked. Settings → Web Apps → the app's page shows Appearance with
  Automatic selected and Light and Dark dimmed (`Segmented` options can now be marked unavailable: `[value, label,
  true]`, not chosen by click or key), and the note "Light and dark per app arrive with LordOS's new web engine
  (WPEPlatform), which we're moving to. For now each web app follows LordOS's mode, and a site with its own theme
  setting (WhatsApp, for example) keeps it." (`webapps.appearance.later`, all 35 languages). The Appearance submenu
  is gone from Lord Flow's app menu (`webAppearanceItem` stays in `sdk/appcontrol.js` for then). lord-server reads a
  stored `light` or `dark` as Automatic (`WEBSCHEME_PER_APP 0` in `server/src/web/webscheme.h`; `webscheme_for_app`
  gives the desktop's mode for every value), so an app already set to Dark doesn't keep a half-working state; the
  key is still parsed, accepted by `lord.webapps.setColorScheme` and written back, and no user file is rewritten.
  `sdk/webappsmodel.js` gains `COLOR_SCHEMES_AVAILABLE` (`['auto']`) and `shownColorScheme`. Bringing it back is
  `WEBSCHEME_PER_APP 1`, `'light'` and `'dark'` in `COLOR_SCHEMES_AVAILABLE` and the menu item; it is part of the
  WPEPlatform item in docs/ROADMAP.md (#142). Tests: `build/webapp-test` (a stored light or dark follows the desktop),
  `build/webreg-test` (an app stored as Dark or Light starts with the desktop's word, and with none while the desktop's
  is unknown; the stored value is kept) and `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs` (`shownColorScheme`). **As designed,
  for when it returns:** each web app has
  its own choice of the light or dark preference its pages are told (`prefers-color-scheme` through `matchMedia`,
  and the dark background while a page loads): Automatic, the default, follows LordOS's mode as before; Light and
  Dark keep that one whatever the desktop does, so a messaging app can stay dark on a light desktop. It is in
  Settings → Web Apps, on the app's page (Appearance, three choices with a hint each), and in Lord Flow in the app
  menu of the web app's window (Appearance ▸ Automatic, Light, Dark, the current one checked; Lord Classic flattens
  submenus, so there it is in Settings only). It applies **at once to the app's open windows**, every profile: a
  change writes the registry's new optional `colorScheme` key (`auto`, `light`, `dark`; written only when not `auto`,
  anything else refused, `server/src/web/webreg.c`) and lord-server sends the app's running `lord-web` processes the
  same closed `SetColorScheme("light" | "dark")` call it already sends for the desktop's mode
  (`webask_app_scheme`). lord-server picks the word per app everywhere it tells one (`webscheme_for_app`: the app's
  own for Light or Dark, else the desktop's): the environment at start, a desktop mode change and a lord-web's bus
  name appearing. `lord-web` reads nothing new and the page gets no new API: only what it is told changes, never the
  site. The same limit as before holds: sites whose dark mode is only CSS `@media` rules stay light. New:
  `lord.webapps.setColorScheme(app, value)` (desktop only, not in the broker; a bad value is `sys.badArgument`),
  `colorSchemeOf` and `COLOR_SCHEMES` in `sdk/webappsmodel.js`, `webAppearanceItem` in `sdk/appcontrol.js`, and the
  `webapps.appearance.*` texts (8 keys) in all 35 languages (the 29 new ones get their first `webapps.json`).
  Tests: `build/webapp-test` (the key read and written back, the defaults not written, seven bad forms refused,
  `webscheme_for_app` for every pair; 461 checks), `build/webreg-test` (an app set to Dark or Light starts with that
  word whatever the desktop says, `webmgr_scheme_of`; 332 checks) and `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs`. No migration: a missing key is
  Automatic. Not yet checked on screen on the development VM.
- **A web app profile's Browser identity: four Linux browsers to choose from** (maintainer's request,
  2026-11-15). Which browser a profile's pages are told it is, chosen from a closed list, never typed, per profile
  (two accounts of one messaging app can differ), Linux identities only. Settings → Web Apps has a *Browser identity*
  section on the app's page, one pop-up per profile with a hint for each choice and a footer that says LordOS still
  uses its own engine (WebKit), that Chrome, Edge and Firefox are names of their owners, that some sites check the
  browser and refuse it when something doesn't match (then choose another identity, such as LordOS (WebKit)), and
  that a site that already linked the device keeps the name it saw until it is linked again;
  in Lord Flow the web app window's app menu has *Browser identity ▸* the four, for that window's profile. The
  strings (lord-web's `webpage_user_agent`, in C; JS and the page never pass one; `<version>` is always the installed
  `LORD_VERSION`; quoted in full in docs/WEBAPPS.md), in the list's order:
  - Chrome on Linux (the default): exactly what desktop Chrome 157 on Linux sends, nothing added: its reduced
    string (`X11; Linux x86_64` with its `AppleWebKit/537.36` and `Chrome/157.0.0.0` tokens and the closing
    WebKit-era token, also on ARM, as Chrome itself sends there);
  - Edge on Linux: the same reduced string followed by `Edg/157.0.0.0`, what desktop Edge on Linux sends, for the
    office, mail and team chat sites of its own maker;
  - Firefox on Linux: `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux <machine>; rv:160.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/160.0` (`x86_64`,
    `aarch64`);
  - LordOS (WebKit): the string every app had until now, `X11; Linux <machine>` with WebKit's own frozen
    `AppleWebKit/605.1.15` tokens and `LordOS/<version>`;
  The maintainer tested each with a messaging web app on 2026-11-15: LordOS (WebKit), Firefox on Linux and Edge on
  Linux link (the phone lists each under its browser's name, on Linux). Two first versions were refused and
  changed before any release: Chrome's string with LordOS's token after Chrome's last token ("works with Chrome
  100 or later"; the site reads the last token as the browser, since Edge's `Edg/` token there works),
  so Chrome is now sent exactly as Chrome sends it; and a fifth identity, *LordOS (experimental)* (`Mozilla/5.0
  (X11; Linux <machine>) LordOS/<version>`, LordOS alone; "browser not supported"), removed from the UI, both C
  lists, `lord.webapps.setUserAgent` and the model. A profile that stored `experimental` is read as Chrome on Linux
  (the registry parser still accepts the word, so the file loads; it isn't rewritten).
  The majors are constants (`WEBPAGE_CHROME_MAJOR`, `WEBPAGE_EDGE_MAJOR`, `WEBPAGE_FIREFOX_MAJOR` in
  `server/src/web/webpage.h`) that docs/RELEASING.md now bumps each release. It applies **at once**: a change writes
  the profile's new optional `userAgent` key in the registry (`chrome`, `edge`, `firefox`, `lordos`; written only
  when not `chrome`; an old `experimental` read as `chrome`; anything else refused, also at the app's level) and lord-server sends that
  profile's running `lord-web` a new closed D-Bus call, `org.lordos.WebApp1.SetUserAgent(word)` with one of those
  four words, which lord-web runs only when the bus says the caller is the lord-server that started it (as `Edit` and
  `SetColorScheme`); lord-web sets WebKit's user agent and loads the app's page again, since a document keeps the
  `navigator.userAgent` it started with (a sign-in on another site in the window is left alone and gets it with its
  next load). lord-server sends it again when a lord-web's bus name appears, so a change made while it was starting
  is not lost; the same word is ignored. WebKit's site-specific quirks keep today's rule (off on the app's own pages,
  on for other sites). New: `lord.webapps.setUserAgent(app, profile, value)` (desktop only, not in the broker; a bad
  value is `sys.badArgument`), `USER_AGENTS` and `userAgentOf` in `sdk/webappsmodel.js`, `webUserAgentItem` in
  `sdk/appcontrol.js`, the `webapps.identity.*` texts (11 keys) in all 35 languages; they name no company or service
  beyond the three browsers. Tests: `build/webapp-test` (the four strings, Chrome's exactly Chrome's with no LordOS
  token on every machine and version, Edge's on every machine, the LordOS token from the version given, Firefox's
  processor, unknown kinds and the word `experimental` refused as identities, the key per profile read, written only
  when not `chrome`, `experimental` read as `chrome` and not written back, twelve bad forms refused; 600 checks),
  `build/webreg-test` (`webmgr_user_agent_of`, an old file with `experimental` still loads as Chrome and isn't
  rewritten, a new profile is Chrome again; 352 checks) and `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs` (`experimental` shown as
  Chrome). Not yet checked on screen on the development VM.
- **Files and Disks mount a free partition of the system disk** ([#122](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/122),
  thanks to pct06, approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-15 as "only mount by hand"). In a dual boot on one disk the
  other installed system's partition (its NTFS volume, say) never showed up, because Files skipped the whole system
  disk and the root side refused any partition on it. Now an administrator can mount and unmount it from Files' sidebar
  or from Disks, under `/media/<user>/<label>` with `nosuid,nodev`, like any internal disk. Root decides partition by
  partition, from the kernel and the udev database, never from what the app sends (`target()` in
  `server/src/disk/disk_admin.c` with the new `SYSPART_OK`, and the new `server/src/disk/diskuse.c`): only
  `disk-mount` and `disk-unmount` accept the system disk, only one of its partitions, only for an administrator (also
  when the system disk is a removable live stick), and `disk-mount` refuses a partition that is mounted anywhere (by
  major:minor; a btrfs by its source or, for a multi-device one, by `/sys/fs/btrfs/<UUID>`), held by anything
  (`holders/`: LUKS, LVM, RAID, bcache), an active swap, or claimed by anyone in the kernel (an `O_EXCL` open answers
  `EBUSY`), and on the system disk a table entry the system keeps for itself: the GPT types EFI System, BIOS boot,
  the other system's Reserved, Recovery and LDM partitions, XBOOTLDR, Linux swap, LVM, RAID and LUKS, any GPT entry
  with attribute bit 0 ("required", OEM recovery partitions), the MBR types `0x05`, `0x0f`, `0x85`, `0xef`, `0x27`,
  `0x42`, `0x82`, `0x8e`, `0xfd` and `0xee`, and an entry udev can't name (fail closed). New codes
  `disk.partInUse`, `disk.partReserved` and `disk.partUnknown`. Format, rename, erase, eject, the image copy and the
  Imager still refuse the system disk, and another disk keeps its rules (only "in use" is checked there, so another
  disk's EFI partition still mounts). Nothing is mounted at boot; that, and a read-only or read-write choice, are for
  later. **NTFS left hibernated is never mounted read-write**: Debian 13's `ntfs3` (kernel 6.12) refuses a dirty volume
  read-write but never looks at `hiberfil.sys`, so a volume left by fast startup or hibernation was mounted read-write
  and the other system then resumed over a file system changed under it. `disk-mount` now mounts every NTFS read-only,
  `nosuid,nodev,noexec`, in a folder only root can enter, reads 4 bytes of `hiberfil.sys` there (`O_NOFOLLOW`, a regular
  file only; the helper parses nothing), and unmounts it; `hibr` in any case, a link, a folder, a FIFO or a read error
  make the real mount read-only, with a `LOG` line that Files and Disks show (`disk.readOnlyHibernated`,
  `disk.readOnlyUnchecked`). This applies to NTFS on any disk. `lord.disks.list()` gives each partition `inuse` and
  `reserved` from the same check, and the new `sdk/diskplaces.js` decides what Files and Disks offer (Files' own copy
  of that logic moved there). Disks' note on the system disk, the three new errors and the two new statuses are in all
  35 languages; the Disks help article (en, es, pt), `docs/SYSTEM.md` and `docs/FILES.md` describe it. Tests: the new
  `build/disk-test` (every refusal and the allowed case on a fake sysfs, udev and `/proc` tree of a dual-boot NVMe disk
  and an MBR disk, the GPT and MBR type table, and the `hiberfil.sys` check on real folders; 82 checks) and
  `tests/diskplaces_test.mjs`. Not checked on screen or on real hardware: no development VM has a dual boot or a
  hibernated NTFS volume.

- **Files says why it can't change a folder, and where to change it**
  ([#139](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/139), thanks to Irh18; the maintainer chose to improve the
  notice only). Files writes only in the home folder and the user's disks (`lord.fs`, `fsops_allowed`); elsewhere,
  such as `/opt/lampp/htdocs` even after `chown` to the user, it only browses, and New Folder, Paste, Rename,
  Duplicate, Move to Trash and Cut were greyed out or did nothing, which looked like a bug. A folder Files only browses
  now shows a bar under the toolbar: "Files can only view this folder: it is outside your home folder and your disks.
  To change it, use the Terminal or another app.", or, for a folder inside them whose permissions don't allow changes
  (or a read-only disk), that the folder is read-only, with an Open in Terminal button. Those actions stay in the menus
  and the toolbar, and using one, or its key (Delete, ❖⌫, ❖X, Ctrl+V, ❖D, ↵, ❖⇧N), opens a sheet that says the same
  with Open in Terminal at that folder. `lord.fs`'s write rules are unchanged. Pure logic in `apps/files/colview.js`
  (`readOnlyWhy`), tested in `server/tests/files_colview_test.mjs`; three new texts (`files.readOnly.*`) in all 35
  languages. Not checked on screen yet.
- **Bigger disclosure triangles and accounts gear in Mail, and the same triangles in Files, Monitor and Terminal**
  (issue [#143](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/143), thanks to pct06 for the suggestion; approved by the
  maintainer on 2026-11-15). Mail's folder and account triangles were a font's ▸ ▾ at 10 px in a 12 × 20 box, hard to
  see next to 13 px folder names and hard to hit; the gear next to «Add account» was the font's ⚙ at 13 px. The SDK
  now has one drawn disclosure triangle: `Disclosure` (a 12 px chevron made of two borders of a rotated square, so it
  no longer depends on a font, in a 16 px hit box whose click does not reach the row; `state` `'open'`, `'closed'` or
  `'none'`, an empty box that keeps rows lined up; `onDown` for a row whose press selects, as in Files) and
  `DisclosureGlyph` (the chevron alone, for a header whose whole row folds), in `sdk/controls.jsx`, with the
  geometry in `sdk/controlmodel.js` (`disclosureDir`, `chevronGeometry`: the square moves back by side / (2√2) so the
  visible strokes, not the square, are centred). Open it points down; closed it points toward the text, right in left
  to right and left in right to left. Mail's folders and account headers use it (the box overlaps the gap before the
  icon by 6 px, so the folders move only 2 px), and so do Files' list view (it was ▶ ▼ at 9 px, and pointed
  right in right to left too), Monitor → Network's app rows, connection tree and folding sections, Monitor's
  firewall rules per app and Terminal's profile groups (Preferences and the Profiles window, ▶ ▼ at 9 px). The
  accounts gear is drawn at 16 px. Tests: `tests/control_model_test.mjs` (the four directions, right and left and
  up and down mirror each other, the tip and both arm ends inside the box and centred for 10, 12 and 13 px; 90
  checks). Not checked on screen: there was no VM access for this change.
- **Control Center: Do Not Disturb, Night Light and brightness, one-click switch tiles, Wi-Fi signal bars, and Log
  Out can be hidden** (issue [#114](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/114), thanks to pct06 for the
  proposal; the maintainer approved the recommended part on 2026-11-15). In Lord Flow's Control Center
  (`themes/default/components/ControlCenter.jsx`): new **Do Not Disturb** and **Night Light** tiles (the same
  `settings.notifications.dnd` and `setNightManual` as the notifications panel and Lord Classic's Quick Settings);
  Dark Mode, Transparency, Bluetooth, Do Not Disturb and Night Light are switch tiles that a click anywhere turns on
  or off, with their state in the tile (the accent color and white when on, grey when off, and «On» or «Off» under
  the name), while the name and the › at the end open the tile's Settings page (Appearance, Bluetooth,
  Notifications, Displays); a **brightness slider** under the volume when LordOS can set a backlight (a laptop's or
  tablet's own panel), through the same closed admin action as the brightness keys and Settings → Displays
  (`display-brightness`, validated on the root side: no new root action), sent at most every 120 ms with the
  slider's last position (`setBacklight`, `useBacklight` in `sdk/hwkeys.js`); and the **Wi-Fi tile's icon shows the
  signal's bars**. The panel is 340 px wide (was 320) and scrolls when a short screen can't hold it. CPU and memory
  and Log Out stay by default; Settings → Desktop & Dock → Control Center can now turn off Do Not Disturb, Night
  Light, the brightness slider and **Log Out** (`ccDnd`, `ccNight`, `ccBrightness`, `ccLogout` in
  `sdk/menubarmodel.js`, all on unless turned off, so a settings.json from before shows the same panel plus the new
  tiles: no migration). Lord Classic's Quick Settings (`themes/classic/components/QuickSettings.jsx`), which already
  had one-click Do Not Disturb and Night Light tiles, gets the same brightness row (with a › to Settings → Displays)
  and the signal's bars on its network glyph, in the tray too. The signal comes from lord-server:
  `lord.net.interfaces()` gives a Wi-Fi interface a `signal` in dBm read from `/proc/net/wireless` (readable by
  anyone; `net_wireless_level` in `server/src/net/state.c`, only a real reading from -110 to -1 dBm, never past its
  line), and `wifiBars` (`sdk/menubarmodel.js`) lights 4 bars from -55 dBm, 3 to -67, 2 to -78 and 1 below, the steps
  of Settings → Network → Wi-Fi; with no reading all four stay lit, as before. The moon, sun, contrast, layers,
  Bluetooth and signal glyphs moved from Lord Classic to the SDK (`sdk/quickglyphs.jsx`), so both themes draw the same
  ones. Not done, as recommended: CPU/Memory and Log Out are not removed by default, there is no one-second On/Off
  notice, and Settings stays a text button. Brightness over DDC/CI (external monitors) does not exist in LordOS yet,
  so the slider shows only with a backlight. New texts in all 35 languages: `shell.cc.openSettings`,
  `shell.cc.displaySettings`, `settings.dock.cc.{dnd,night,brightness,brightnessHint,logout,logoutHint}`. Tests:
  `build/net-test wireless` (16 cases: dBm with and without the update mark, not associated, -256, a cut line, a name
  that is only a prefix, no reading past the line, out of range), `tests/menubar_model_test.mjs` (the new choices on by
  default, Log Out hidden alone, the bars' steps, the backlight picked and never set to 0), `tests/menubar_test.mjs`
  (the new tiles and slider shown, a click turns Do Not Disturb on and off and changes its tile to the accent, Night
  Light and Dark Mode in one click, three slider moves send one `display-brightness intel_backlight 650`, each new
  tile and Log Out hidden from Settings while CPU/memory and Settings stay) and `tests/classic_taskbar_test.mjs` (the
  Quick Settings brightness row only with a backlight). Not checked on screen and not tested on hardware: there was
  no VM access for this change. The `display-brightness` action behind the slider already drives real backlights
  through the brightness keys (two laptops in `docs/HARDWARE-REPORT.md`, #12); the slider itself has not been tried
  on one.

- **Developer tools for web apps: Inspect, per window, after asking** (maintainer's request, 2026-11-15: "seria bueno
  agregar ... Inspecionar 'DevTools'", "a lo que es app webs"). Settings → Web Apps has a new *Developer* section with
  one switch for every web app, *Developer mode*, off by default. With it on, each web app window's Window menu has
  *Inspect (developer tools)*. Choosing it asks first, Cancel focused: "Developer tools can see everything in this app,
  including messages and sessions. Turn on for this window?", with a line that says the window opens again with them on,
  that they open in the browser, that they stay on until the window closes and that meanwhile any program on this
  computer can connect to them. Only *Turn On* goes further.
  - *How (WPE 2.48):* WPE WebKit has no inspector inside the window and turns its remote inspector on only as the
    process starts, from `WEBKIT_INSPECTOR_HTTP_SERVER=<ip>:<port>` (read when the first web context is made; port 0
    is refused, "invalid address"). So `lord.webapps.inspect(app, profile)` (desktop only, not in the broker) has
    lord-server end that app and profile's `lord-web` and start it again as `lord-web --app <app> --profile <profile>
    --inspect` (`webmgr_inspect`; `webargs.c` accepts `--inspect` only last, once, with an app). lord-web refuses
    `--inspect` unless developer mode is on (it reads the file itself), hands WebKit `127.0.0.1:<port>` with a port
    browsers refuse to reach (below), turns the view's developer extras on, and checks that the port listens from one
    of its own sockets (`/proc/self/net/tcp` against `/proc/self/fd`, `webinspect_listening`) before it opens its gate's
    one-time address in the person's browser through OpenURI, with a notification that says the tools are on, without
    the address, and whose action (*Open in browser*) opens them again. The page lists that window's page; *Inspect*
    there opens WebKit's Web Inspector over a WebSocket. Checked on the development machine against a headless
    lord-server: the off switch refuses (`exit 2`), with it on lord-web listens only on 127.0.0.1 (the gate, WebKit's
    HTTP port and WebKit's own inspector server on another random port), the target list names the page, `Main.html`
    loads, the WebSocket upgrade answers 101, and a start without `--inspect` listens on nothing.
  - *The gate* (after a security review: WebKit's inspector server has no authentication, and a web page open in
    the person's browser could have reached `127.0.0.1:<port>` by scanning ports, over a WebSocket, which no CORS rule
    stops, or through DNS rebinding, then read the web app's page, for example its messages, and run script in it):
    - WebKit's HTTP server now listens on one of 15 ports of the browsers' "bad port" list (WHATWG Fetch: 6665–6669,
      6697, 10080, 1719, 1720, 1723, 3659, 4045, 5060, 5061, 6566; `WEBGUARD_BACKEND_PORTS`). Chrome, Chromium and
      Firefox refuse every navigation, `fetch`, image and WebSocket to them, so no page reaches it. X11's 6000 and NFS's
      2049 are left out, and 4190 and 6679 too: on the spec's list, but Chromium 156 connected to them in our test.
    - The browser is pointed only at lord-web's own gate (`server/src/web/webproxy.c`, checks in `webguard.c`): a
      listening socket on another port of 127.0.0.1 in lord-web's GLib loop (no thread, no other process, no new
      library, nothing executed). It forwards one request per connection, or one WebSocket upgrade, to WebKit only when
      the head is complete within 10 s, at most 16 KB, well formed (CRLF lines, no control bytes, no folded lines, a
      `GET` in HTTP/1.1 with no body); `Host` is exactly `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>` (DNS rebinding);
      `Origin`, if any, is the gate's own (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `http://localhost:<port>`); `Sec-Fetch-Site`,
      if any, is `same-origin` or `none` (a page on another port of this computer is the same *site* for cookies); and
      the request carries the window's cookie `lordos-inspect-<port>`. Anything else is a 403 and the connection closes.
    - The cookie (32 random bytes from `getrandom`, base64url, compared in constant time) is set only by the one-time
      address `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<secret>/` (another 32 random bytes) that OpenURI is handed: it answers a
      redirect to `/` with `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` and then no longer works, so the address in the
      browser's history is dead; the notification's action makes a new one. A cookie, not the secret in every path,
      because WebKit's inspector pages build their WebSocket address from `location.host` and an absolute path
      (`Main.html?ws=` + `location.host` + `/socket/1/1/WebPage`), and the browser sends the cookie on it too.
    - A plain request goes to WebKit with `Connection: close` and nothing the browser sends after it (a browser may
      reuse a connection for another page's request, so each one is checked on a connection of its own); a WebSocket's
      bytes go both ways only after WebKit answers 101. At most 16 connections; a plain answer must end within 60 s.
    - Checked end to end with lord-web, WPE 2.48.3 and headless Chromium 156 driven over the DevTools protocol: the
      one-time address leads to the target list, the inspector's WebSocket opens through the gate and runs script in
      the app's page; the address then answers 403; a page on another port of 127.0.0.1 opened no WebSocket to the gate
      or to WebKit's port and read nothing; a rebinding name (`rebind.test` mapped to 127.0.0.1) got 403; curl
      confirmed every refusal, the bounds and the 16-connection limit. The notification no longer shows any address.
  - *Limits:* WebKit's own ports still have no token or secret path, and WPE 2.48 accepts only `<ip>:<port>` for them
    (no unix socket), so while it is on any process on this computer that can reach 127.0.0.1 can connect to them
    directly (a browser page can't: above); WebKit's second listener, its inspector server on a random port, speaks
    its own length-prefixed protocol, not HTTP, so a browser's request can't be a message there (no answer, no memory
    growth, checked). That is why it is per window, asked every time, and ends with the window:
    closing a window with developer tools on ends its lord-web even for an app that runs in the background, the next
    start is a normal one, and turning developer mode off ends every window that has them. A second *Inspect* on that
    window only brings it forward (the item is checked and unavailable while they are on). The page never gets a way
    to turn them on: no D-Bus method was added, the menu item and the question are the shell's, and lord-server
    checks the switch again.
  - *Storage:* `~/.config/lordos/web/developer.json` (`{"developerMode": true}`, 0600), written only by
    `lord.webapps.setDeveloperMode` (the folder is in `fsops_protected`); a missing or invalid file is off. New
    `lord.webapps` calls: `developerMode()`, `setDeveloperMode(on)`, `inspect(app, profile)`; `running()` says which
    windows have developer tools (`inspect`). New error code `webapps.developerOff`.
  - *Texts:* `webapps.inspect.*`, `webapps.settings.developer*`, lord-web's own `inspect.title`, `inspect.body` ("They
    opened in your browser and stay on until you close this window.", no address), `inspect.open` (the notification's
    *Open in browser*) and `inspect.failed`, in all 35 languages.
  - *Tests:* `tests/webapp_test.c` (argv with `--inspect`, the switch's file, the address, who listens on the port:
    ours, nobody yet, another process's socket, ours on every address, another listener on the same port; the gate:
    the backend ports, base64url, the head's end and its 16 KB bound, the one-time address (exact, once, a letter off at
    either end), the cookie among others and every wrong form of it, Host, Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site in all their
    refused forms, the WebSocket upgrade, POST, bodies, HTTP/1.0, bare LF, folded lines, control and NUL bytes, the
    rewritten head, the replies and the 101 check),
    `tests/webreg_test.c` (refused while off or with an invalid file, the profile checked first, the old process
    ended and a new one started with `--inspect`, a second Inspect only shows it, off ends it and not the other
    profile) and `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs` (the Window menu item: only with developer mode on, checked while on,
    a click only asks).

### Changed

- **A tablet sleeps on a tap of the power button and shuts down on a 5-second hold** (issue
  [#131](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/131), thanks to Touchgg; maintainer's decision, 2026-11-15). Before,
  a tap shut a tablet down, as on any computer, and each person had to change it in Settings. A tablet is a machine
  whose SMBIOS chassis type (`/sys/class/dmi/id/chassis_type`) is 30 (Tablet) or 32 (Detachable), read on the root
  side (`tablet_chassis` in the new `server/src/hw/tabletpower.c`); a missing file or anything else is not a tablet.
  31 (Convertible, a laptop whose screen folds back) keeps a laptop's defaults: it is used with its keyboard most of
  the time and its lid already decides sleep. Nothing else changed in how it is stored: the same
  `/etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/lordos.conf` the closed `power-buttons` action writes, with `HandlePowerKey=suspend`
  and `HandlePowerKeyLongPress=poweroff`, so Settings → Energy (Battery) → Power button and lid shows the values in
  effect and changes them as before. No new admin action.
  - **New installs:** the disk installer writes that file into the new system when the machine it runs on is a
    tablet (`tablet_power_install`), with the lid values of the new system's `logind.conf` (logind's defaults:
    sleep). It never replaces a `lordos.conf` already there, and leaves everything alone when `logind.conf` sets
    `HandlePowerKey` or `HandlePowerKeyLongPress` itself. If it can't write the file the install goes on, with a
    warning (`install.tabletPowerWarning`, in all 35 languages).
  - **Systems already installed:** migration `packaging/migrations/008-0.8.8.9-tablet-power.sh` (root, once,
    idempotent) does the same on a tablet only where the person hasn't chosen: no `lordos.conf`, or one written by an
    older Settings with the short press on shut down (the old default) and no hold line, whose lid values it keeps.
    A `lordos.conf` with a hold line (every Settings since #131 writes one), another short-press choice, a link
    where the file goes, an administrator's `HandlePowerKey`/`HandlePowerKeyLongPress` in `logind.conf` or another
    `/etc` drop-in, or a lid value Settings can't show are all left as they are. It reloads `systemd-logind`. It
    does nothing in the chroot where the live image is built (no systemd there; the installer covers new installs).
  - **Tests:** `build/settings-hw-test` (fake sysfs and `/etc` trees: chassis 30 and 32 are tablets, 31, 9, 10, 3,
    1, empty, junk, ` 30` and `300` are not; the file the installer writes is byte for byte what `power-buttons
    suspend suspend suspend poweroff` writes; never replaces a file, never follows a link, keeps the lid values,
    defers to an administrator) and `tests/migration_tablet_power_test.sh` in `make test` (20 cases over fake
    system trees, each migrated twice: the second run must change nothing). Not yet tried on a real tablet; the
    live session on a tablet still shuts down on a tap until it is installed.

- **One administrator list, everywhere.** The last three hand-written copies of the `sudo`/`admin`/`wheel` list are
  gone: `lord-sessiond` (the login screen's users and who may restart or shut down with other sessions open),
  `lord-fand` (who may change the fans) and lord-server's `lord.sys.info().admin` and `lord.users.list()` now ask the
  shared list in `server/src/users/admingroups.{h,c}`, like `admin.c`, Settings → Users, the admin rescue and
  `lordos-firstrun`. Each keeps its own rule: by account (`admin_membership_read`, primary or supplementary group, an
  unreadable list is not an administrator) for sessiond, fand (uid 0 still counts, by `SO_PEERCRED`) and
  `lord.users.list()`; by the session process's own groups for `lord.sys.info().admin`, through the new
  `admin_gids_any()` (a gid list against the list, by group name). The groups are matched by name now in sessiond
  and `lord.users.list()` (they looked up each list name's gid before), and fand reads up to 256 groups (was 64).
  `lord-sessiond` and `lord-fand` link `admingroups.c`. `build/admin-groups-test` grows to 45 checks (a gid list:
  each administrator group, `adm`, `root` and `sudoers` that aren't, a gid with no group, an empty or failed read).
  The lists of reserved user names in the installer, the first run and the VM installer still name these groups:
  they are names an account can't take, not an administrator check.

- **Web apps tell sites they are Chrome on Linux, exactly as Chrome says it, by default** (maintainer's request,
  2026-11-15), instead of LordOS's WebKit string, whose browser token made a messaging app's phone list the linked computer under another system's
  browser. Every existing profile changes too (no stored key is the default; no migration). A profile set to *LordOS
  (WebKit)* in Browser identity (above) gets the old string back. A device a site linked before keeps the name the
  site saw then: unlink it on the phone and link it again to see the new one. Why it showed another system: WebKit's
  site-specific quirks hand that messaging site another system's browser string whatever the setting, and lord-web
  only turned them off on an app's own pages on 2026-11-11, after the first web apps were linked.
- **Chinese by script.** `languageOfLocale` (`sdk/localename.js`) picks the interface language for a locale: its
  language part, or `zh-Hant` for `zh_TW`, `zh_HK` and `zh_MO` and `zh-Hans` for `zh_CN` and `zh_SG`; the first
  session and the login screen use it instead of cutting LANG to two letters. The installer keeps the full id
  (`zh-Hant`, not `zh`) and lists every `zh_` region for both, and a language's own region gets its own
  `format.json` for any id with a script (`zh-Hant` with `zh_TW`). Settings' **+** no longer lists "中文" as not
  translated once either Chinese is installed.
- **Plural forms are checked.** `node tools/i18n-check.mjs` fails when a translated plural object lacks a form of
  its language's rule or has one the rule never gives (`few` in Japanese; `other` is always allowed), and when a
  language names an unknown rule. Every existing catalog already passes.
- tools/brand-check.mjs allows the Malay name of March in `ms/format.json` (it reads as a computer brand).

### Removed

- **RustDesk is no longer in the Store** (#66; maintainer's decision, 2026-11-12: LordOS doesn't distribute it for now).
  It was offered in Store → Remote access from 0.8.8.6 as its maker's `.deb` (1.5.1, amd64 and arm64), to be mirrored
  in LordOS's signed repository; its entry is gone from `apt/catalog.json`, so the Store no longer lists it, offers it
  in search or installs it. LordOS doesn't redistribute it; people who want it can get it from its maker. Tailscale
  stays in Remote access, unchanged. No migration: the package was never published in lordos.org/apt's pool (the
  live amd64 index has no `rustdesk`), so no installed system has it from LordOS. The Remote access intro no longer
  mentions seeing and controlling other computers, and the "Remote access" kind label (`store.ai.kind.remote`), used
  only by that entry, is removed in all six languages. store-search-test now checks that "remote desktop" brings no
  Remote access app and that "private network" brings Tailscale. docs/UPDATES.md, PACKAGES.md, COMPLIANCE.md (the
  AGPL-3.0 source gap no longer applies), ROADMAP.md and apt/README.md say so; ROADMAP.md (0.8.8.9) notes how it could
  come back without LordOS distributing it: a "direct deb" delivery where the person's computer downloads the maker's
  `.deb` and checks the pinned SHA-256.

- **Cookies and statistics: LordOS's update checks are counted from 2026-11-12.** Until 2026-11-11 the requests
  LordOS makes to `lordos.org/apt` were left out of every count. The policy (Cookies and statistics and the Privacy
  policy, in English, Spanish and Portuguese, both dated 2026-11-12) now says exactly what is counted from the same CDN
  request logs: how many distinct computers check for updates each day, and how many download each version of LordOS
  and each package (LordOS's own packages, the voices and the Store's apps), by country, architecture and update
  channel (the normal repository or the test one). The IP address is used only so the same computer is not counted
  twice in a day (or in the week or month a total covers) and is not combined with anything else; from the user agent
  only the program that asked (LordOS's package engine or apt, and its version) is taken. No identifier of the
  computer or the person, no cookies, nothing installed, the same 13 months of retention. To avoid it, turn off Store
  → Updates → "Check for updates automatically"; checking or installing by hand still asks for the index and is
  counted the same way. The Privacy policy's default connections table, its "No telemetry" and "Store and updates"
  sections and the "Does LordOS collect telemetry?" FAQ answer say the same. A new private dashboard,
  `LordOS-Usuarios`, built by `node tools/web/stats.mjs dashboards`, shows it (every query starts at
  2026-11-12T00:00:00Z, so nothing logged before the change is counted): computers today, in the last 24 hours and 7
  days, index checks, packages downloaded, countries and GB served; computers per day and per hour and by hour of
  day (UTC); computers by country (table and pie); architecture from the package index asked for; update channel;
  client (LordOS's package engine or the apt version); LordOS versions downloaded (adoption) and by architecture;
  LordOS's packages, the Store's catalog apps and the voices; repository errors (4xx, 5xx and cut requests) by path;
  GB served per day; and the test repository's use by day, country and client. There is no "new or returning
  computers" view: it would follow an IP address from one day to another, which the policy does not cover, and
  dynamic addresses would make it mostly noise. `stats.mjs test` takes an optional number of hours and a query-name
  prefix. The downloads dashboard's note now points to `LordOS-Usuarios` for updates.

  their own names, with the site language's name under each and a "right to left" tag for Arabic, Persian and Urdu:
  the six released ones (English, the default, Español, Português, Français, Italiano, Lietuvių) and, under "New in
  the next pre-release", the 26 new languages, complete like them and in development (Bahasa Indonesia, 日本語, Deutsch, हिन्दी, Bahasa Melayu, বাংলা,
  简体中文, 繁體中文, Українська, Polski, العربية, Tiếng Việt, Svenska, Ελληνικά, Nederlands, Türkçe, Magyar, فارسی,
  Русский, Română, Suomi, اردو, Български, 한국어, ไทย, Azərbaycan). It says every language LordOS ships is complete
  (about 12,400 texts, with its own plurals, dates and numbers; native digits for Arabic, Persian and Bengali; right
  to left for Arabic, Persian and Urdu), that a language ships only when it is complete and every change reaches

  new languages are chosen: at least 5 people from a country where the language is spoken visiting lordos.org in 30

  Portuguese. The list is built from every `assets/locales/<id>/meta.json` plus `web/content/languages.json` ("next":

### Fixed

- **The arm64 build has no compiler warnings again.** `lord-media`'s SVG check read nanosvg's dash count, a plain
  `char`, as if it were signed; on arm64 `char` is unsigned, so the "negative count" check could never fire and gcc
  warned. It is now read as signed on both architectures, so a corrupt count is refused the same way everywhere.

- **A web app set to Chrome on Linux is no longer refused by a messaging site** (maintainer's test, 2026-11-15, in
  development, never released). The site read the last token of the user agent as the browser, and Chrome's
  string ended with `LordOS/<version>`: it answered that it works with Chrome 100 or later. `chrome` now sends
  exactly what desktop Chrome on Linux sends, nothing after its last token. *LordOS
  (experimental)*, which the same site refused as an unsupported browser, is gone; a profile that chose it is
  Chrome on Linux again, read so without rewriting its file.
- **A web app with Appearance set to Light or Dark didn't open when only `lordos` was updated** (found testing
  0.8.8.9 on the maintainer's PC, 2026-11-15): the web runtime is its own package, `lordos-web`, and a 0.8.8.8
  `lord-web` refused the app's registry entry with the new `colorScheme` key ("unknown key colorScheme"), and kept
  sending the old browser identity. `lordos-web` already depended on `lordos` of its exact version; now `lordos` also
  `Breaks: lordos-web (<< <its version>)`, so dpkg and the Store update both together.
- **Updating `lordos` and `lordos-web` together failed in one dpkg run** (found installing 0.8.8.9~test2 over ~test1
  on the maintainer's PC, 2026-11-15, in development, never released). dpkg unpacks a run's packages in the order
  given and checks a `Breaks` when it unpacks, against what is installed at that moment; a `Depends` waits for the
  configure step. `lordos` first was refused ("installing lordos would break lordos-web, and deconfiguration is not
  permitted"), and `lordos-web` was left unpacked and unconfigured until `lordos` was installed again and
  `dpkg --configure -a` ran. LordOS's package engine put `lordos` first too (dependency order, `lordos-web` depends on
  it), so the Store's Update all and updating LordOS from Store → Updates hit the same error. Now `plan_order`
  (`server/src/pkg/resolve.c`) unpacks, inside one `dpkg --install` run, a package whose installed version another one
  in the run breaks or conflicts with before that one (the two architectures of a multiarch pair move together),
  and `apply_plan` passes `--auto-deconfigure` to those runs, as apt does, for a cycle or a package broken by an
  earlier run; a local `.deb` still installs without it, so it is refused with nothing changed. The relationships
  stay as they are. The engine already brought `lordos-web` into an update of `lordos` alone; with no newer
  `lordos-web` published, updating `lordos` asks to remove it and Update all holds `lordos` back. By hand:
  `dpkg -i` with `lordos-web` first, or `dpkg --auto-deconfigure -i` in any order; `lordos` alone over an older
  `lordos-web` is refused before anything changes (docs/PACKAGES.md, "Breaks inside one run"). Tests: `pkg-test`
  checks the plan and the order for `lordos` alone, Update all and `lordos-web` alone, and the plan with no newer
  `lordos-web` (the generic `libfoo` / `oldtool` order case now expects `oldtool`, the one broken, first); the new
  `tests/pkg_breaks_dpkg_test.sh` builds two dummy packages with the relationships read from `tools/iso/mkdeb.sh`
  and `mkdeb-web.sh`, runs the engine's order (`pkg-test order`) and both plain orders through the real dpkg in a
  throwaway `dpkg --root`, and checks that `lordos` alone leaves both configured (skipped without dpkg-deb).
- **A one-line APT source with `arch=` before `signed-by=` lost its `signed-by`** (found while adding Steam, 2026-11-15):
  the engine split the options with `strtok` and the inner split of the `arch=` list reset it, so Valve's
  `deb [arch=amd64,i386 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/steam.gpg] …` line was read without its keyring and verified with
  apt's trusted keys instead (and failed). Both splits use `strtok_r` now (`parse_list` in `server/src/pkg/pkg.c`).

- **The web apps model test covered only six languages** (`server/tests/webapps_model_test.mjs`): it expected exactly
  en, es, fr, it, lt and pt to have `webapps.json` and crashed on a language with no `store.json`. It now checks the
  catalog's texts and the Edit words in every complete language (no `"partial"` in `meta.json`), so a new language
  can't ship without them.

- **A web app opened without network loads by itself once the network is back** (issue
  [#144](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/144), thanks to pct06). WhatsApp opened before the Wi-Fi was
  connected showed WebKit's error page («Error resolving “web.whatsapp.com”: Name or service not known») and kept it:
  lord-web handled no `load-failed` on the app's view, so nothing loaded the page again, and since WhatsApp runs in the
  background (`"background": true`), closing and opening it again from the Dock only hid and showed the same window
  with the same error, until the session ended. Now lord-web (`server/src/web/webengine.c`) takes a main frame load
  of the app's own address (inside its scope) that failed for lack of network: GResolver's errors, GIO's connection
  errors (timed out, host or network unreachable, refused, proxy failed, closed, not connected) and WebKit's
  transport error (`weboffline_is_network_error`, `server/src/web/weboffline.h`, pure). Instead of WebKit's page it
  shows its own, "No connection" with the site's host and "Press Ctrl+R to try now", in the person's language (three
  new keys in `webruntime.json`, `offline.title`, `offline.body` and `offline.hint`, in all 35 languages) and the
  desktop's light or dark colors (again in the new colors when the mode changes); the page is `about:blank` HTML with
  a Content-Security-Policy that allows no script, so it has none of the app's origin. lord-web then loads the failed
  address again after 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and then every 60 s (`weboffline_delay_s`), at once when GIO's
  `GNetworkMonitor` reports the network available again (the waits start over at 2 s), at Ctrl+R or F5, after a
  crash of the web process, and when the window is shown again from the Dock, the launcher or the tray. A cancelled
  load, a download, a TLS error, an HTTP answer and any address outside the app's scope (a sign-in on another site)
  keep WebKit's own handling, and an address outside the scope is never loaded again by lord-web. Tested in
  `server/tests/webapp_test.c` (`build/webapp-test`: which errors are the network's, the delays, the page's escaping,
  no script, both color schemes, a buffer too small); the GIO and WebKit codes the header mirrors are checked against
  GLib's at compile time. Not yet checked on screen or on hardware. Docs: docs/WEBAPPS.md, "No network".
- **Electron apps no longer crash at start (GitHub #150), and probably Steam's window loop (GitHub #157).** Since
  0.8.8.8 lord-server exported `GTK_IM_MODULE=wayland` to every app it starts (`server/src/wl/toolkitenv.h`), so
  GTK 4 on Wayland would use LordOS's text-input-v3 input methods. Every GTK reads that variable, also the GTK 3 that
  Electron and Chromium load while they run on X11 (Xwayland): it loaded the Wayland input-method module on an X11
  display, failed `gdk_wayland_display_get_wl_display: assertion 'GDK_IS_WAYLAND_DISPLAY (display)'` and crashed,
  and forcing X11 didn't help. The variable is gone. Instead LordOS's Settings portal (`server/src/ui/portal.c`)
  serves `org.gnome.desktop.interface` `gtk-im-module` = `wayland`: GTK 4 on Wayland reads it from the portal before
  it chooses a module itself (when the key was missing it used its default, `simple`, which is why 0.8.8.8 needed the
  variable), and GTK on X11 never reads the portal, so Electron and Chromium go back to GTK's own default. GTK 3 on
  Wayland already chooses text-input-v3 by itself. An IBus or Fcitx user's own `GTK_IM_MODULE` still wins, and is
  passed through untouched. Steam's web helper is Chromium on X11 too; a helper that crashes and is started again
  matches the window JrocMD saw recreated every ten seconds, but that is not confirmed. Tests: `build/toolkitenv-test`
  checks the variable is not exported and a person's own value is kept; `build/portal-gs-test` (over a private session
  bus) reads `gtk-im-module` with `ReadOne` and with `ReadAll("org.gnome.*")`, the call GTK 4 makes, and checks it is
  not in another namespace. Not checked on a screen yet: the GTK 4 Hangul field of 0.8.8.8 and an Electron app on X11
  still need a run on VM 127. On 0.8.8.8, `env -u GTK_IM_MODULE <app>` from the Terminal works around it.
  Thanks to Irh18 for the report with the exact assertion and the variables that fixed it, and to JrocMD for the
  Steam report and its log. Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("How to open an app", "Input methods").
- **Files: New Folder goes in the selected folder in the column and list views**
  ([#134](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/134), thanks to MacNB). The toolbar button, File → New Folder,
  the empty-space menu and ❖⇧N always made the folder in the place shown (the first column, or the list's top
  folder), even with a folder picked in a deeper column or selected inside an unfolded one. Now it goes where a desktop file manager
  puts it: in the column view, in the last column's folder (the folder picked there, or the folder of the file
  picked); in the list, in the selected folder (unfolded so its name can be typed) or in the folder the selected items
  are in; in the icon and gallery views, which show one folder, and with nothing selected, in the folder shown. It is
  never outside the folder shown, and a target Files can't write in says why (#139 below). Checked in every view: the
  list also counted only its top folder's items as the selection, so what was selected inside an unfolded folder had
  nothing for Copy, Rename, Duplicate or Move to Trash to act on (the list view's side of #100); those items are part
  of the selection now (`listEntries`). Pure logic in `apps/files/colview.js` (`newFolderDir`, `listEntries`), tested
  in `server/tests/files_colview_test.mjs`. Not checked on screen yet.
- **Files: the column view keeps every column, and Back goes back up the columns**
  ([#133](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/133), thanks to MacNB). Since 0.8.8.8 (#99) the column view
  showed only the last columns that fit next to the preview, so widening a column or opening a subfolder dropped the
  first ones out of the view with no way to reach them. Every column is now drawn, side by side, and when they don't
  fit they scroll sideways, as in other column views: a sideways swipe or tilt of the wheel, or the bar along the bottom edge.
  Opening a deeper folder scrolls to it with the preview in sight; widening a column keeps the scroll, so the first
  columns stay where they are. The preview takes what is left of the view, at least 200 px (`colStrip`, replacing
  `colsThatFit`). Back also left the column view: a click in a column was no step in the history, so Back went to the
  place before in that place's own view (Home in icons). Each folder opened down the columns is now a step: Back and
  Forward walk the columns and stay in the column view, and only a step to another place opens it in its own view
  (`chainStep`, `historyStep`; leaving a place keeps its columns for Back). The view stays left to right in every
  language. Tested in `server/tests/files_colview_test.mjs` and in the scene `server/tests/files_colview_scene.mjs`
  (five columns drawn where 0.8.8.8 kept one). Not checked on screen yet. MacNB's other suggestion in
  the issue (← → to the parent or child folder and ↑ ↓ in the column, as other column views do) is not part of this change.
- **A tablet's volume buttons change the volume** (issue [#131](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/131),
  thanks to Touchgg, on a Chuwi Hi12 and a Teclast X98 Pro). lord-sessiond and lord-server opened only full
  keyboards (with A and Enter), mice and tablets, so the `gpio-keys` node that carries a Cherry Trail tablet's volume
  buttons (`soc_button_array`) was closed unread, and so was a keyboard's separate "Consumer Control" node. A third
  kind of device, **system keys**, now opens too (`input_is_system_keys` in `server/src/inputkind.h`, used by
  `useful()` in `server/src/remote/monitor.c` and `add_device()` in `server/src/input.c`): sound or player keys and no
  letters or pointer buttons. It is not grabbed, because logind reads the power key from the same `gpio-keys` node,
  and only the keys `keygrab_system_key` lists pass on (volume, mute, player, brightness, keyboard light, Print
  Screen; the list now lives in `input_system_key`, shared by both), never `KEY_POWER`, so the power button is never
  acted on twice. A "Power Button" (power key only) and a "Video Bus" (brightness only, which the kernel's ACPI video
  driver may already change) are still left alone. These devices are not keyboards, so the tablet's on-screen
  keyboard still appears, and they don't count as a way to answer a password prompt. Tested in
  `build/inputkind-test` (a Hi12's `gpio-keys`, an ACPI Power Button, a Video Bus, a Consumer Control node, a keyboard
  and a mouse with volume keys, and what passes); not yet tried on a tablet.
- **A mouse's back and forward buttons work in Linux apps** (issue
  [#159](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/159), thanks to getsugah, with a Logitech MX Master 2S).
  `server/src/main.c` turned only BTN_LEFT, BTN_MIDDLE and BTN_RIGHT into buttons, and BTN_SIDE and BTN_EXTRA (codes
  above the keyboard's range) were dropped; the Wayland side (`wl.c`) and isolated apps (`appclient.c`) knew only three
  buttons too. `input_dom_button` (`server/src/inputkind.h`) now numbers them as the DOM does, 3 back (BTN_SIDE,
  BTN_BACK) and 4 forward (BTN_EXTRA, BTN_FORWARD), and `input_evdev_button` gives a Wayland app BTN_SIDE and
  BTN_EXTRA, as libinput does: GTK, Qt and the browsers go back and forward, Xwayland makes them X buttons 8 and 9, and
  LordOS's web apps (`webwin.c`, which already handled them) now get them. The desktop's own press handlers don't see
  buttons 3 and 4 (`runtime/events.js`): most of them don't look at the button, and a thumb press must not drag a
  window or press a control. The remote desktop still sends three buttons. Tested in `build/inputkind-test` and
  `tests/side_buttons_test.mjs`; not yet tried with a real mouse.
- **Files no longer opens an AppImage in TextEdit** (issue [#159](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/159),
  thanks to getsugah). A file with no known kind was offered to TextEdit, so double-clicking a program showed its
  bytes. `isProgram` (`sdk/filekinds.js`) marks `*.AppImage` files: TextEdit is no longer offered, an app that declares
  `application/vnd.appimage` still is, and with none Files says that no app opens it, that it is a program and that
  Files doesn't run programs (`files.programNoOpener`, in all 35 languages). Running AppImages from Files is a
  separate decision, not made here. Tested in `tests/filekinds_test.mjs`.

- **lord-web picks the right language for three-letter ids and for Chinese.** The LordOS Web Runtime's own texts
  (`server/src/web/weblang.c`) took only the first two letters of `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES` or `LANG`, so `fil_PH.UTF-8`
  loaded Finnish (`fi`) and any `zh_*` looked for a `zh` folder that does not exist and fell back to English. It now
  uses `weblang_id()` (`server/src/web/weblangid.h`, pure): the whole language part, two or three lowercase letters
  (`fil_PH` → `fil`), and Chinese by the script its country writes, as `languageOfLocale` in `sdk/localename.js` does
  (`zh_TW`, `zh_HK`, `zh_MO` → `zh-Hant`; any other `zh` → `zh-Hans`); anything else (`C.UTF-8`, `POSIX`, empty,
  `Fil_PH`) is English. Tested in `server/tests/webapp_test.c` (`build/webapp-test`).
- **lord-server no longer aborts at start when built with `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`** (pull request
  [#138](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/pull/138), thanks to Kiisanz). `realpath()` may write up to `PATH_MAX`
  bytes, but the Terminal's shell-integration folder (`server/src/term/pty.c`, 1,024 bytes) and the fan helper's device
  paths (`server/src/fan/fanhw.c`, 320 bytes) were smaller: with fortify (the default of several distributions'
  compilers) glibc's `__realpath_chk` aborted lord-server before the login screen, and without it a very long path
  could overflow those buffers. Both now use `PATH_MAX` buffers (the fan helper copies the result cut to its field).
  Built with `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`: no warnings; `fan-test` 4,224 checks.
- **The administrator group is `wheel` where a system has no `sudo` group** (pull request
  [#141](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/pull/141), thanks to Kiisanz): Settings → Users (`users_admin.c`) and the
  first run (`firstrun_apply.c`) gave administrators only `sudo`, so on such a system nobody could be made one, though
  `admin.c`'s `is_admin` and the admin rescue already accepted `sudo`, `admin` and `wheel`. Nothing changes where a
  `sudo` group exists (Debian, the ISO and the Raspberry Pi image); LordOS still supports only Debian 13.
- **Turning "Administrator" off in Settings → Users now really takes the user's administrator rights away** (a
  follow-up to pull request [#141](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/pull/141) by Kiisanz). LordOS treats as an
  administrator anyone in `sudo`, `admin` or `wheel` (`admin.c`'s `is_admin`, the admin rescue), but Settings → Users
  looked at a single group: `user-admin name 0` removed the user only from `sudo` (or `wheel`), so someone also in
  another of them stayed an administrator for LordOS while Settings said they weren't; and the last-administrator
  protection (`user-del`, `user-admin`) and the "already an administrator" check counted only that one group, a
  different rule from `is_admin`. There is now one closed list of administrator groups and one rule, in
  `server/src/users/admingroups.{h,c}`, fixed in the code and never configurable from JS or any input, used by
  `admin.c`, `users_admin.c` (Settings → Users and the rescue) and `lordos-firstrun`:
  - a new administrator joins `sudo`, or `wheel` where there is no `sudo` group (#141's choice; never `admin`). With
    neither group, `user-add` with "Administrator" refuses before creating the account (`users.groupFailed`) instead
    of creating it silently without the right;
  - `user-admin name 0` runs `/usr/bin/gpasswd --delete` for **every** administrator group the user is in, then
    reads the system again and fails with `users.groupFailed` if they still are one. A user whose primary group is an
    administrator group can't be taken out with `gpasswd`: refused before anything changes, with the new error
    `users.adminPrimaryGroup` ("…as root, change its main group first (usermod -g)"), in all 35 languages;
  - "the last administrator" counts people's accounts (uid 1000–59999) that are in any of the groups, primary or
    supplementary, as `is_admin` does.
  New suite `build/admin-groups-test` (36 checks: the closed list, the group for a new administrator on Debian,
  Fedora-style and bare systems, a user in `sudo` and `wheel` revoked from both, the last administrator counted across
  groups, a `wheel`-only system, the primary-group refusal, an unreadable group list). Built with
  `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`: no warnings. Documented in docs/SESSIONS.md ("Who is an administrator").

- **Choosing an entry in the tray menu of go-link Desk (and other fyne.io/systray apps) did nothing.** These apps build
  their com.canonical.dbusmenu menu anew, with new ids, every time they change it: go-link Desk refreshes its menu at
  each status update, about every 1 to 2 seconds (`ResetMenu` and `AddMenuItem`, 21 `LayoutUpdated` signals each
  time, seen with `busctl monitor` on VM 127: the ids went from 101–110 to 529–538 in a minute). LordOS read the
  layout once when the menu opened and never listened to `LayoutUpdated`, so a choice made more than a moment later
  sent `Event` with an id the app no longer had (406 for "About go-link Desk" while its menu was at 529–538) and the
  app ignored it. lord-server now listens to the menu's `LayoutUpdated` and `ItemsPropertiesUpdated` and, while the
  menu is open, reads the layout again (one `GetLayout` at a time) and sends it to the theme, which replaces the rows
  of the open menu (`"sni-menu"` with `update: true`; `lord.sni.closed(id)` when it closes). A choice is also matched
  by its place and label (a key per entry, `sni_menu_json` in `server/src/ui/snimodel.c`): an id of the layout before
  the current one is found again in the current one, and when the app changed its menu after the last layout we read,
  a fresh layout is asked for and the `Event` goes to the entry's new id. The `Event` call itself was already right,
  `(isvu)`: the entry's id, `"clicked"`, an `int32` 0 variant and a timestamp, to the bus name and object path of the
  item's `Menu` property (it is now built by `sni_event_body` so it can be tested). Apps whose ids stay the same
  (pasystray's Ayatana menu) worked before and still do.
- **The tray menu of a Linux app opened on every display**, with "Show the menu bar on every display" (the default)
  and more than one display. Each display's bar draws its own copy of a tray icon, and the menu the app sent was kept
  once for the item, so every copy drew it: clicking go-link Desk's icon on one of three displays opened its menu on
  all three. The copies on the other displays then saw a press on a row as a press outside themselves and closed the
  shared menu before the click reached the row, which also kept a choice from reaching the app. The click now records
  the display of the copy that was clicked, the layout is kept with that display, and only the copy on it draws the
  menu (`trayAsk`, `trayMenuShow`, `trayMenuHere`, `trayMenuUpdate` in `sdk/traymodel.js`, used by
  `sdk/trayitems.jsx`).
- Tests: `build/sni-test` (a menu built again with new ids: About, Quit and a submenu entry found by their key, a
  changed label or another place is another entry, two alike entries are refused; the `Event` call parsed back as a
  real message) and `server/tests/tray_model_test.mjs` (the menu drawn on one display out of three, the clicked one;
  an open menu updated with new ids on the same display, a closed one left closed). Checked on VM 127 (one display)
  with the generic go-link Desk 1.8.2-dev1 (Fyne): before, "About go-link Desk" did nothing; after, it opens the About
  window after the menu had been open for a few seconds, and "Quit" quits; pasystray's menu and About work as before.
  The several-display part is covered by the model tests only: VM 127 has one display and a headless lord-server has
  only one output.
- **Settings → Cloud: turning an account off no longer says "1 file in it is open" when nothing is open** (issue
  [#146](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/146), thanks to pct06). The switch counted open files with
  rclone's `vfs/stats` `inUse`, which is not a count of open files: it is the VFS's reference count, set to 1 when the
  mount is made and kept there while it lasts (rclone's `vfs/vfs.go`, `inUse`, `AddRef`). So every mounted account was
  "busy" with one open file, the sheet asked Cancel / Turn Off Now / Wait each time, and **Wait never ended**, because
  the count never went down to 0. `lord-server` now counts the files really open: this user's file descriptors that
  point under the account's folder in `~/Cloud`, read from `/proc/*/fd` (`cf_open_count` in
  `server/src/cloud/cloud_files.c`, the same walk Free Up Space already used, only the processes of the same user),
