  when the switch is used and once a second while an account waits to turn off. A change waiting to go up or a
  transfer still asks first, as before. `vfs/stats` is no longer called every second for each account. Free Up Space
  and the automatic pass looked in `/proc` only when `inUse` was above 0, which was always the case while mounted;
  they now always look, and treat a file used in the last 10 s as open only while its account is mounted (rclone
  keeps a closed handle 5 s), which is what they did in practice. Tests: `build/cloud-test` opens a file under an
  account and checks the count (1, then 0 once closed; another account, `..` and an empty name count 0), the switch's
  answer with the file open (`"open":1`) and with only a change waiting (`"open":0`), and Free Up Space refusing the
  open file with no `inUse` set. Not checked on screen or with a real rclone mount (no VM access for this change).
- **The Cloud menu's panel no longer runs off the screen** (issue
  [#145](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/145), thanks to pct06). With many accounts and recent files (8
  accounts and 5 recent files at 150% scale) the panel grew taller than the display, and Pause All, Show in Files and
  Cloud Settings… ended below its edge or under the Dock, out of reach. The panel had no height limit and its list no
  scrolling. It now gets the room between its item and the far edge of the display's work area, so the Dock or a
  Classic taskbar on that side is left out, less an 8 px margin, and never less than 160 px (`panelRoom` in
  `sdk/statusplace.js`, pure; `statusPanelRoom(button)` in `sdk/statusitems.js` for any status item's panel). The
  title and the buttons always show, and the accounts and the recent files scroll between them (`sdk/cloudstatus.jsx`).
  It works the same in Lord Flow (menu bar at the top, panel opening down) and in Lord Classic (taskbar at the bottom
  by default, panel opening up; at the top, down). Tests: `server/tests/statusplace_test.mjs` (a 1280×720 logical
  screen, which is 1920×1080 at 150%: under the menu bar down to the Dock, with no Dock, with no work area, a work area
  larger than its display, above a bottom taskbar, on a second display, a tiny display). Not checked on screen (no
  VM access for this change); the other status panels (network, cleaner, an app's menu) keep their behavior.

## [0.8.8.8-beta] - 2026-11-12

### Added

- **Mail: fold a whole account in the sidebar.** The account's name in the sidebar now has a disclosure triangle,
  and a click on the name folds the account to that one line. A folded account shows its unread mail on the line
  (every folder but Sent, Drafts, Junk and Trash, so folding never hides new mail), and the line is highlighted
  while one of its folders is the one shown. The choice is kept per account in Mail's accounts file (`folded`,
  next to the folders' `collapsed` list), so the sidebar looks the same at the next launch; the ⚠ mark still opens
  the password or certificate sheet without folding (`apps/mail/index.jsx`, `accountUnread` in
  `apps/mail/foldertree.js`, tested in `server/tests/mail_foldertree_test.mjs`) (GitHub #121).
- **Text Editor: File → Open recent.** A submenu under Open folder lists the last 5 files the Editor opened or
  saved, newest first; choosing one opens it (or switches to its tab). A file that is not there now (deleted, or on
  a drive that is not mounted) is greyed out, and one that is gone by the time it is chosen leaves the list with a
  note in the status bar. Two files with the same name show their folder. *Clear menu* empties the list. The list
  is kept in `settings.json` as `editor.recent`, a new key, so no migration (`apps/editor/recent.js`, tested in
  `server/tests/editor_recent_test.mjs`; texts in every language) (GitHub #113).
- **Logs move to `/var/log/lordos`, one per app, rotated, and the previous session is kept.** Every LordOS log now
  lives under `/var/log/lordos` (`server/src/lordlog.c`, docs/SYSTEM.md "Log files"):
  - **The root daemons:** `lord-sessiond.log`, `lord-netd.log`, `lord-fand.log` and `admin.log` (the administration
    helper's refusals by action name, never an action's arguments, plus the output of the programs it runs: dpkg,
    wpa_supplicant, openvpn, pppd; its stderr used to go nowhere), root's, mode 0640. Their lines
    still reach the journal as before; lord-netd's own lines no longer pass through lord-sessiond's file.
  - **Each user's:** `/var/log/lordos/users/<user>/` (mode 0700, the user's) with `compositor.log` (lord-server),
    `shell.log` (the shell's React/QuickJS `js:` lines and their stack lines, which used to be mixed into
    `session.log`), `xwayland.log`, `cloud.log` (rclone), `apps/<app>.log` (each isolated native app and each Linux
    app, which used to share `apps.log`, or, for isolated apps, the compositor's log) and `web/<app>-<profile>.log`
    (each web app's lord-web, which used to share `web.log`; `web/probe.log` for the Store's probe). Ids become safe
    file names (`[A-Za-z0-9._+-]`, no leading `.` or `-`, at most 96 bytes).
  - **The folder is made by lord-sessiond at each login, before the session starts** (and for the login screen's
    `lordos-greeter`): each step is an `openat` from a folder opened with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY`; `/var/log/lordos`
    (0755) and `users/` (0711, so nobody can list the names) must be root's and writable by nobody else; the user's
    folder is fixed with `fchown`/`fchmod` on its own descriptor. A symlink, a file or another uid's folder in its
    place is refused and left untouched, the session then logs to `~/.cache/lordos`. Root never touches anything
    inside the user's folder, and root's logrotate has no rule there (see Rotation).
  - **Fallback:** a nested or development lord-server, one without lord-sessiond, or one with another `$HOME` (the
    test harnesses) writes the same names under `~/.cache/lordos`, so development keeps working and a test never
    rotates the running session's files.
  - **Lines carry a timestamp, a level and a subsystem:** `2026-11-11T12:43:56.123-03:00 INFO  xwayland: starting
    Xwayland on :0` (local time with milliseconds and offset; `ERROR`/`WARN`/`INFO` from the message's words; the
    line's own `name:` prefix or `compositor`/`shell`/the daemon). A small `lord-log` child stamps them, reading
    lord-server's (or the daemon's) stderr through a pipe; it ignores SIGTERM and drains the pipe until the last
    writer is gone, so a crash loses nothing already written. Linux apps, Xwayland, lord-web and rclone write their
    own output as is, after a stamped "starting …" line written by lord-server before it forks.
  - **The previous session is kept:** at login `compositor.log` and `shell.log` become `.prev` (not `.1`, which is
    logrotate's own numbering); `session.log` used to be opened with "w", losing the crash that ended the previous
    session. Only that makes a `.prev`: what the 16 MB cap moves aside during a session goes to `.old`, so a long or
    noisy session never overwrites the previous one's log.
  - **Rotation:** `/etc/logrotate.d/lordos` rotates only the root daemons' files directly in `/var/log/lordos`:
    daily, 7 copies, compressed, `copytruncate` (each daemon's `lord-log` child holds its file with `O_APPEND`).
    logrotate is now a Recommends of the lordos package and in every image's tool list. It has no rule inside
    `users/<user>`: those folders and their `apps/` and `web/` are the user's, and logrotate works on path strings,
    so a user could swap a subfolder for a symlink during a run and have root create its copies (owned by the user,
    holding the user's text) in any folder, the known attack on logrotate in user-controlled folders.
  - **The cap:** every file is capped at 16 MB by its own writers, as its owner: above that the newest part goes to
    `<name>.log.old` from a line start and the file is emptied in place, so writers holding it go on. It is checked
    when a log is opened, after every MB a `lord-log` child writes, and every minute by the session's `lord-log`
    child for the other files, so the disk never fills even without logrotate. An isolated app (`lord-server --app`)
    no longer holds its `apps/<id>.log`: before its sandbox and before any of its code runs, a `lord-log` child takes
    the file over and the app writes to a pipe; the child copies the bytes as is (it never parses the app's output)
    and checks the cap after every MB, so an app writing in a loop can't fill `/var` between the minute's checks
    (`RLIMIT_FSIZE` was not an option: it would also stop the app's window buffers, memfds larger than 16 MB). The
    old 1 MB truncations of `apps.log`, `xwayland.log` and `web.log` are gone.
  - **The Logs app** lists the session's files (each previous session's as "<name> (previous session)", each `.old`
    as "<name> (older part)", a new `logs.older` key in all six languages), then
    **Apps**, **Web apps** and **Older logs** (what earlier versions left in `~/.cache/lordos`), shows each stamped
    line's real time, level and subsystem (`sdk/logfile.js`), and follows `apps/` and `web/` live. `lord.logs` still
    reads only the user's own logs: a name is `[<apps|web|cache>/]<safe name>.log[.prev|.old]`, opened with `openat` and
    `O_NOFOLLOW`; `lord.logs.dir()` is new. Settings → Cloud's "copy the log" reads rclone's log through `lord.logs`.
  - **Migration** `007-0.8.8.8-logs.sh` makes `/var/log/lordos` (0755) and `users/` (0711), root's, moving aside
    anything there that is not a folder without following it. The old `~/.cache/lordos/*.log` are left where they
    are (migrations never touch home folders). `lord-fand.service` gains `LogsDirectory=lordos` (it runs with
    `ProtectSystem=strict`); purging the package removes `/var/log/lordos`.
  - `lordos-issue` reads the new places and adds the shell's log, the previous session's last lines and the five
    most recent apps' logs; `tools/diag/keylag.sh`, `tools/rpi/verify-board.sh`, the e2e scripts and the docs use the
    new names.
  - Tests: `build/lordlog-test` (121 checks: names and sanitizing; the root side's folder against a symlink, a
    dangling symlink, a file, a symlinked or group-writable root and a symlinked `users/`, in a temporary folder; the
    cap and rotation, never through a symlink or a FIFO; the line format; `lord-log` end to end with the previous
    session kept as `.prev`, also after a third session writes 18 MB and its overflow goes to `.old`; an isolated
    app's output copied as is through `lord-log` and capped while it writes 19 MB) and `server/tests/logfile_test.mjs` (the Logs app's parser and order).
- **Web apps: editing like in a browser.** The Edit menu of a web app's window now has Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste
  and Select All (Speech stays below them): the shell asks lord-server, which sends `org.lordos.WebApp1.Edit(command)`
  to that window's lord-web, and lord-web runs it only when the bus says the caller is the lord-server that started it
  (its parent's pid). The commands are a closed list checked on both sides (`server/src/web/webedit.c`). Copy and Cut
  reach the session's clipboard at once, Paste of an image goes the image way, and Undo and Redo are sent as Ctrl+Z
  and Ctrl+Shift+Z, which a page with its own history (a rich text editor) handles; WPE 2.48 keeps no undo stack of
  its own, so a plain text field has none.
- **Web apps: a right click opens LordOS's own menu.** Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Copy Link Address, Open Link in
  Browser and Copy Image, whichever fit what is under the pointer. A script of lord-web's in an isolated world reports
  a right click the page left alone; lord-web asks lord-server with `org.lordos.WebApps1.Menu(app, profile, items)`,
  whose items are names from the closed list, never text, checked with the same pid check as Ask; the shell shows the
  menu at the pointer in the person's language and a press elsewhere closes it. Copy Image reads the image with the
  page's own origin (a PNG unless it is a PNG or a JPEG) and offers it as an image.
- **Web apps: Settings… and Help in the menu bar.** A web app's Settings… (was greyed out) opens Settings → Web apps
  on that app, and Help starts with "<app> on the Web", which opens the app's site in the browser.
- **Web apps follow the desktop's light or dark mode.** WPE WebKit 2.48 has no way to set a page's
  `prefers-color-scheme`, so every web app saw light. lord-server now starts lord-web with `LORDOS_WEB_SCHEME=light`
  or `dark` (the mode the theme gives the Settings portal) and, when the mode changes, sends
  `org.lordos.WebApp1.SetColorScheme(scheme)` to every running lord-web; the word is `light` or `dark` only, and
  lord-web applies it only when the bus says the caller is the lord-server that started it, the same pid check as
  Edit (`server/src/web/webscheme.c`). A script of lord-web's at document start in every frame
  (`server/src/web/webscheme.js`, no privileges and no message handler) makes the page's `matchMedia` answer any query
  about `prefers-color-scheme` with the desktop's mode: the query is rewritten so WebKit's own `matchMedia` answers
  the rest of it (`not`, `and`, `only`, commas, other features), the page gets a `MediaQueryList` of its own
  (`matches`, the original `media`, `onchange`, `addEventListener`, `addListener` and their removals, `instanceof
  MediaQueryList`), and it sends `change` when the mode flips, live, without reloading; same-origin frames follow at
  once and frames of other origins with their next load. In dark mode the view's background is the desktop's dark
  window color while a page loads, so no white flashes before the page paints. Checked on the test VM with a page
  that prints `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches`: true when started in dark, false when started in
  light, and switching the mode in Control Center flips it at once (one `change` event each way, the same-origin frame
  too), and a call from another process is refused. A lord-web that takes its bus name after the mode changed (the
  change came between its start and that moment, so the call went to a name nobody owned) gets the mode when its name
  appears: lord-server watches `NameOwnerChanged` and sends `SetColorScheme` to the running lord-web whose name it is.
  A page's `{ once: true }` listener that ran and a `{ signal }` listener whose signal aborted are released, so a page
  that keeps making such lists does not keep them all alive. Limit: a page that picks its colors only with CSS
  `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` rules stays light until a newer WebKit (rewriting those rules was weighed and left
  out: style sheets from other origins can't be read); a site with its own theme setting can be set by hand, and the
  Store's page of the messaging app now says so under Known limitations (new limitation key `theme`, in every
  language). Tests: `tests/webapp_test.c` (the two words, the environment's value, the script's and the hook's text,
  bad keys refused), `tests/webscheme_test.mjs` (the script against a stand-in `matchMedia`, with `once` and `signal`
  listeners released) and `tests/webreg_test.c` (`LORDOS_WEB_SCHEME` absent until the theme tells the mode, `dark`
  and `light` after, absent again for any other value). See
  `docs/WEBAPPS.md`, "Light and dark".
- **Web apps: hidden windows stop working for nothing.** A window that is minimized, on another desktop, closed into
  the background or wholly covered by an opaque window now tells its page it is hidden: the page stops painting, its
  animations pause and its timers run at most once a second, while its network, audio and notifications go on. Measured
  on the dev VM: a busy page went from 115 % CPU to 0.4 %, and the compositor from 5 % to 0.3 %, while minimized. It
  paints again at once when shown (frame gate `server/src/wl/framegate.h`, `coveredIds` in `sdk/desktopmodel.js`).
- **Linux apps: a window wholly covered by an opaque window** is paced once a second and told "suspended", like a
  minimized one.
- **Web apps use less memory.** The lighter cache model now takes effect (it is set before the web context exists), so
  no idle ~130 MB web process is kept per profile. A page above about 600 MB no longer throws away its caches every
  10 seconds: WebKit's memory pressure now starts from the computer's memory (up to 3 GB) and checks every 30 s.
- **Web apps: the memory and CPU limits shared by an app's profiles are sized to the computer.** They used to be 2 GB
  (memory.high) and two cores, which kept two profiles of a messaging app throttled and made them freeze for moments.
  Now memory.max is ¾ of the RAM (1 to 16 GB), memory.high ⅛ below it and the CPU half the cores, at least two
  (`webpage_scope_limits`).
- **Web apps: crash stacks.** If lord-web crashes (an abort, an uncaught C++ exception, a bad access), its stack is
  written to the web apps' log, and lord-server reaps an ended lord-web instead of leaving it as a zombie.
- **Monitor: memory counted once.** The memory view counts processes by proportional memory (PSS) and doesn't count
  sandbox wrappers as processes: a web app showed "28 processes, 2.3 GB" for ~1.5 GB across 4 processes.
- **Web apps: the site's own icon.** With lordos-web installed, LordOS fetches each app's icon from the site itself with
  the same probe as "Add from an address" (PNG or SVG up to 1 MB, kept only when the probe ended on the app's own
  origin). The icon is cached as `~/.cache/lordos/web/icons/<app>.png|svg` (a protected folder, named by app id only) and
  used by the Dock, launcher, switcher, Store and Settings. The Store asks for icons lazily, one probe at a time, and an
  installed catalog app gets its icon on its next launch without blocking it. Settings → Web apps → Refresh icon fetches
  it again. The repository still ships only LordOS's letter tiles. New `lord.webapps.fetchIcon`, `iconResult` and
  `icons`; `list()`/`get()` give the cached icon as `iconPath`.
- **Web apps: unread count on the Dock.** lord-server serves `org.lordos.WebApps1.SetBadge(app, profile, count)`,
  accepted only from the lord-web it started for that app and profile (the same pid check as Ask; tested in
  `webdock-test`). The count is clamped to 0..9999, sent to the shell as `webapps-badge`, and reset to 0 when that
  lord-web leaves the bus. The Dock and Lord Classic's taskbar draw a red badge with the sum of the app's profiles ("99+"
  over 99), and the Dock's window list shows each profile's own count. Settings → Web apps → "Show unread count on the
  Dock" (on by default).
- **Web apps, Settings: "Show in the menu bar" and "Notification sound".** "Show in the menu bar" is registry `tray`
  (`lord.webapps.setTray`). "Notification sound" offers Automatic (LordOS's sound only when the page plays none of its
  own), The app's, LordOS's and None (registry `notifySound`, `lord.webapps.setNotifySound`). Settings → Notifications
  shows the same choice for each web app.
- **Notifications: a sound per app.** Default, None, Pop, Chime, Ping or Drop (new sounds synthesized in `snd.c`), heard
  when chosen. Stored values stay `true`/`false` or the sound's name, so no migration is needed. For a lord-web that
  lord-server verified from the sender's pid, notifyd adds the app, profile and `app_icon`, never trusting the
  desktop-entry a process wrote. A web app's banner is filed under `lordos-web.<app>`, shows the app's name, and shows its
  icon with the profile's dot. An `app_icon` path is shown only when it is exactly one of that app's icon files.
- **Web app profiles told apart by color.** Each profile has a color from the tag colors of Files and Databases (registry
  `color`; `lord.webapps.setProfileColor`; a new profile gets none for the first, then orange, purple, blue…), chosen
  with color dots in Settings → Web apps. With more than one profile, the frame and the switcher read
  "<app> — <profile>" and the frame has a thin strip in the profile's color. The Dock's window list reads
  "<title> — <profile>" with a colored dot. Icons get a dot with the profile's initial. lord-server writes each colored
  profile's icon as `~/.config/lordos/web/icons/<app>.<profile>.png` for lord-web's tray icon. Optional "Each profile has
  its own Dock icon".
- **Web apps: files dragged onto a web app's window reach the page as a real drop.** WPE WebKit 2.48 cannot take an
  external drop, so lord-web is the drop target: it reads the drag's text/uri-list, keeps only local regular files (at
  most 64 MB each, 20 files) that really are in the person's places (home, mounts, `/tmp`; never a hidden folder such
  as `~/.ssh`, since any app can start a drag with any list), reads them itself and gives them to the page through a script in an isolated world. The
  page then gets dragenter, dragover and drop with a DataTransfer whose types include "Files". A drop with no local
  file gives the page its text.
- **Web apps: image paste and copy.** An image on the clipboard (image/png or image/jpeg, up to 32 MB) is pasted into
  the page with Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert as a paste event carrying the image as a file. WebKit's pasteboard is emptied
  when such an image arrives, so text copied earlier is never pasted instead. Pages can copy images and text to the
  session through navigator.clipboard.write and writeText, which lord-web adds because WPE 2.48 lacks them; lord-web
  accepts them only on the app's own pages, from the app's top frame (a random key a frame of another site doesn't
  have) and right after a key, click or touch in the window.
- **Web apps: the mouse wheel scrolls pages again.** WebKit 2.48 reads a line scroll event by its signs alone, so the old
  event also scrolled one line sideways and pages didn't move. Each notch is now one line on its own axis,
  high-resolution wheels add up their partial notches, and touchpads scroll in pixels with an end-of-gesture event.
- **Web apps: clicking a notification opens what it is about.** lord-web runs the page's own click handler (a messaging
  web app opens that chat) and then brings the window forward. The shell now sends the notification's default action
  on a click instead of only dismissing it (`defaultAction` in `sdk/notify.js`).
- **Web apps: notifications show the web app's name and icon** instead of an empty square. notifyd accepts a
  `lordos-web.<app>.<profile>` desktop entry only from the lord-web that lord-server started for that app and profile.
- **Web apps: no more double notification sound.** When a page plays its own sound within 1.5 s of a notification,
  LordOS suppresses its own and remembers this per profile (`state.json`). The new registry key `notifySound` (auto,
  app, system, none) overrides it, and notifyd now honors the suppress-sound hint.
- **Web apps: a Linux user agent** with WebKit's usual browser tokens and `LordOS/<version>`. WebKit's site-specific quirks are
  off on the app's own pages, so sites no longer offer a download for another system.
- **Web apps: unread count.** The count a page puts in its title ("(3) …") is sent to lord-server with
  `org.lordos.WebApps1.SetBadge` when it changes.
- **Web apps: tray icon is optional.** New registry key `tray` (default off). An app in the background keeps running
  without it, and the Dock or launcher brings its window back.
- **Web apps: the catalog grows from 6 to 37 apps.** Every new one passed `lord-web --probe` on 2026-11-11 and starts at
  the service's own address (its mail, calendar, documents or player, never its marketing or sign-in page): team chat
  and video meetings, social networks, mail and calendars, cloud files, documents and spreadsheets, notes and task
  lists, office suites, AI assistants, video and music streaming, photos, design tools, a whiteboard, an image editor
  and ride hailing. Only one chat app is marked tested (checked on LordOS with two accounts, `verified` 2026-11-11); the
  rest say "not tested yet". Two sites were left out: one answers "unsupported browser" to WPE WebKit and one no longer
  loads. Each app has a generic description in all six languages, its publisher, a LordOS letter tile as its icon
  (128×128, a color close to the service's) and its known limitations: protected music (`drm`) for two music services,
  calls (`calls`) for five chat and meeting apps, notifications only while running (`push`). Two apps on one origin keep
  to their own path (`docs.google.com/document/` and `/spreadsheets/`), and `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs` now checks that
  no app starts inside another's scope, that no two share one and that every icon is used. The mail web app moved to its
  work-and-personal address (`outlook.office.com/mail/`). docs/WEBAPPS.md has a new "The catalog" section.
- **Store → Installed: remove any Linux app a Debian package brought, and deactivate the LordOS apps you don't use.**
  A read-only `lord.pkg.ownerOfApp(desktopId)` finds an app's package from dpkg's own lists (`dpkg_owner` in
  `server/src/pkg/status.c`; only the id comes from JS, `/usr/share/applications` only), so a `.deb` installed from a file
  or an app the index doesn't name gets Remove, through the same plan sheet and `pkg-remove`; never for Essential,
  Protected or required packages, nor when the plan would remove `lordos`. 21 built-in apps can be deactivated (the core
  never can: `sdk/appsoffmodel.js`): out of the launcher, the Dock, search, Open With and default apps, opening one shows
  Activate, and its background work stops (lord-maild pauses mail accounts with `mailPaused`, alarms don't ring, backups
  turn manual; Machines can't be deactivated while a VM runs). Checked on VM 127 that the Store opens. Tests:
  `test_dpkg_owner` in `build/pkg-test`, `tests/apps_off_model_test.mjs`.
- **Store: web apps in Discover, the web engine installed with the first one, and a page for each.** A banner and a shelf
  of web app cards in Discover (also in search and categories), each tagged "Web app". Installing the first one without
  `lordos-web` shows the engine's size from the package plan, installs it with the Store's package job and then the app,
  with no other click. A web app's page lists version (always up to date), tested on LordOS, size on disk per profile,
  memory (live from `lord.webapps.memory`, `server/src/web/webmem.c`, or the catalog's measured figure), publisher,
  verified origin, source, engine, permissions, profiles, background mode and known limitations. Checked on VM 127: the
  banner, the page, Install, and Open bringing up the app's own window with its Dock and tray icons. Tests:
  `build/webmem-test`, `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs`, `tests/webapps_get_scene.mjs`.
- **Cloud: an on/off switch for each account that keeps its settings and sign-in, and a password account that asks for a
  new code at every start turns itself off.** Off, an account is never given to rclone (no mount, listing, token check or
  sign-in prompt) and leaves Files, the file dialogs, Photos and the menu bar; its `accounts.json` entry, `rclone.conf`
  section, keyring item and waiting changes stay, so turning it on needs no new sign-in. An `iclouddrive` account that
  needs a new sign-in before its first good mount of the session turns off with a reason instead of notifying at every
  login (rclone issues 9966 and 9658, still open in rclone 1.76.0). Tests: `t_onoff` in `build/cloud-test`,
  `tests/cloud_signin_fake.sh` parts 6 and 7, `tests/cloud_model_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/CLOUD.md` 6.4.
- **Wayland drag and drop: between Linux apps, from Files to a Linux app, and from a Linux app to Files.** Checked on VM 127: a file dragged from Files opened in Chromium, and a GTK 4 drop target got copy, or move with Shift held.
  - `wl_data_device.start_drag` is implemented in `server/src/wl/wl.c` (`dev_drag` and the `dnd_*` functions). The serial must be the one of a current press of that client on the window that got it. Any other serial, or a second `start_drag` while one runs, is cancelled.
  - While the button is down no app gets the pointer. The surface under it gets `enter`, `motion` and `leave` with a new `wl_data_offer` each time it enters, with the source's types and, from version 3, `source_actions`.
  - `accept` and `set_actions` reach the source (`target`, `action`). The action is the target's preferred one, else copy, move or ask. A source without `set_actions` copies.
  - The release over a surface that accepted a type (and agreed an action) sends `drop` and `dnd_drop_performed`, then `dnd_finished` after `finish`. A v3 offer destroyed before `finish` cancels the source. Anywhere else, or Escape, cancels.
  - The icon (role "dnd icon", moved by its attach or `wl_surface.offset`) is drawn above everything on the CPU and GPU paths and stops direct scanout while shown.
  - These are protocol errors: an icon that has another role, a source used both for a drag and as the selection, and action masks with unknown bits.
  - A source, icon, target surface, data device or client that goes away mid-drag ends cleanly. A destroyed source cancels the drag and the target gets `leave`. A window move that takes the pointer cancels the drag.
  - Files hands the paths it drags to lord-server through `lord.wayland.dragFiles`, which only takes absolute, existing paths without a NUL or a newline, at most 256. Over a Linux window the compositor is the source: it offers `text/uri-list` (percent-encoded `file://` URIs, CRLF separated) and `text/plain` and writes them non-blocking from the event loop.
  - A Files drag into a Linux app only copies, whatever the app prefers: dropped on a file manager, a move would take the file out of its folder unasked. With Shift held it may move. The ghost shows the + once the app agreed (`lord.wayland.dragTaken`).
  - Drags from an isolated LordOS app, a Flatpak, or any client that is not positively unsandboxed (same root and mount, pid and user namespaces as lord-server, `server/src/wl/dndgate.c`) never hand files to LordOS. A drop on LordOS can be claimed only while the UI handles the release that made it; one nobody claims is cancelled at once, and a claimed list that doesn't arrive in 5 s is cancelled (`build/dndgate-test`).
  - A Linux app's drag of `text/uri-list` released over LordOS is read by the compositor (at most 1 MB, non-blocking) and claimed by Files at the release (`lord.wayland.takeDrop`). Its local `file://` paths are then copied into the folder under the pointer. A drop nobody claims is cancelled.
  - Xwayland windows and isolated LordOS apps take no drop.
  - New `server/src/wl/urilist.c` encodes and decodes the file lists, with `build/urilist-test` in `make -C server test`. New `build/dnd-client` (`server/tests/dnd_client.c`) runs inside a session: without input it checks the refused serial and the protocol errors; with two presses it checks offers, actions, receive, drop and finish, a second drag, and the icon and source destroyed mid-drag.
  - Also fixed: a `wl_surface` destroyed before its `wl_subsurface` no longer leaves the subsurface pointing at the freed window. A second subsurface for the same surface, or one for a cursor or drag icon, is refused.
  - Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Drag and drop"). The `docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md` row is 🟨.
- **LordOS's input methods now compose inside Linux apps (`zwp_text_input_v3` complete).** Korean, Japanese and Chinese typing now works in any Wayland app that enables a text-input-v3 field (GTK 3 and 4, Qt 6). Before, the protocol was only the on-screen keyboard's hint. While such a field is enabled on the window with the keyboard and an input method is on, each key goes through `server/src/ime.c` before the app (`ime_to_app` in `server/src/ui/js.c`). A key the method uses never reaches the app, and neither does its release. The composition goes to the app as `preedit_string`, which the app draws in place. Its cursor is given in bytes: over the focused segment of a Japanese conversion, otherwise at the end. Finished text goes as `commit_string`, and each batch ends with `done` carrying the number of `commit` requests the app sent on that object. A `done` is sent only when it carries something, so an app that commits again on every `done` cannot loop. The candidate window (`ImeOverlay`) opens at the app's `set_cursor_rectangle`: the new `lord.wayland.textCaret()` (`wl_text_caret` in `wl.c`) adds the window's on-screen origin to it each time it is drawn, so it follows a window that moves. Password and PIN fields, and fields marked hidden, sensitive or Latin, never compose. The composition is discarded when the app disables the field, enables it again for another widget, or loses the keyboard, and the "off" now goes to the window that had the field. Nothing the app sends is trusted (`server/src/wl/tiutf8.c`): surrounding text is cut to valid UTF-8 and 4000 bytes, and dropped when its cursor or anchor is not a character boundary. The cursor rectangle is clamped to ±32767 and to the window's edges. `delete_surrounding_text` is clamped to whole characters of the app's text, and every offset LordOS sends lands on a character boundary. Tests: `build/textinput-test` (`server/tests/textinput_test.c`, in `make -C server test`) covers UTF-8 prefixes, preedit cursors, surrounding-text and delete clamps, and rectangles. `build/textinput-client` (`server/tests/textinput_client.c`, run inside a session) checks the sequence end to end: enter, enable, no `done` for bare commits, garbage requests, a second text input, out-of-order destruction, and with `type 30` every serial and offset while you type. Docs: `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Input methods"), `docs/LANGUAGES.md`.
  - GTK 4.18 doesn't choose its text-input module by itself when no input-method framework runs, so lord-server sets `GTK_IM_MODULE=wayland` for the apps it starts, unless one is already set (an IBus or Fcitx user keeps theirs). Checked on VM 127: a GTK 4 field got the Hangul composition as preedit and then 한글.
- **Now Playing and the media keys work with Linux players (MPRIS).** Browsers, video players and music apps publish `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.*` on the session bus. lord-server now follows them on its own connection, using our own D-Bus client (`server/src/hw/mpris.c`, `server/src/vault/dbus.c`, no new library). `ListNames` and `NameOwnerChanged` tell it which players exist. `GetAll` reads `Identity`, `PlaybackStatus`, `Metadata` (`xesam:title`, `xesam:artist`, `xesam:album`, `mpris:length`, `mpris:trackid`, `mpris:artUrl`), `Position` and the `Can*` properties, and `PropertiesChanged` and `Seeked` keep them current. Only signals and replies from the name's current owner count. Nothing waits for a player: every call is asynchronous, a reply that doesn't come within 3 s is forgotten, and the controls (`PlayPause`, `Play`, `Pause`, `Next`, `Previous`, `SetPosition` or a relative `Seek`) are sent without asking for a reply. Limits: at most 16 players and 48 calls in flight. Strings are cut at a UTF-8 boundary with control characters removed (`server/src/hw/mprismeta.c`). Lengths and positions are clamped to a week, and a seek is clamped to the track's length. Cover art is kept only when it is a local `file://` path (no `..`, no query, no encoded NUL or slash) and is shown through lord-media's thumbnails; remote and `data:` art is dropped. The new `lord.mpris` (`list()`, `control(name, cmd, ms)`, `refresh()`, `server/src/ui/js_hw.c`) exists only in the desktop's own context and has no broker message, so isolated apps can't reach it. The media keys go to LordOS's Player while it plays. Otherwise they go to the Linux player that is playing, or the one that started last when several are; with nothing playing they go to whichever was active last, so a paused track resumes (`sdk/mprismodel.js`). Control Center's Now Playing (`NowPlayingTile`, both themes) lists up to three players, the one the keys reach first. It dims the controls a player doesn't offer, moves the progress bar every second, and seeks when you click a Linux player's bar. The SDK exports `linuxPlayers` and `useLinuxPlayers`. Tests: `build/mpris-test` (GetAll and PropertiesChanged dictionaries, Metadata replacing the track, every integer type for lengths, clamps, broken UTF-8, cover-art URLs, player names, Get(Position)) and `server/tests/mpris_model_test.mjs` (where the keys go, ordering, recency, position estimate, seek clamping), both run by `make test`. Docs: docs/MEDIA.md ("Linux players"), docs/WAYLAND.md, docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md.
  - Checked on VM 127 with mpv and its MPRIS plugin: the tile showed the title and app, its pause button paused and resumed mpv, and the play/pause key did the same.
- **Tray icons of Linux apps (StatusNotifierItem) now show next to LordOS's status items, with their menus.** Checked on VM 127 with a GTK app using the Ayatana indicator library: it registers and shows; an app that names only an SVG icon shows its first letter, since LordOS draws PNG icons only. lord-server owns `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` on the session bus and acts as its own host (`server/src/ui/sni.c`, using Passwords' own D-Bus client). What it serves:
  - `RegisterStatusNotifierItem` in both forms: an object path on the caller's connection, or a bus name with the item at `/StatusNotifierItem`. A unique name is accepted only from its own connection. At most 32 items, 4 per connection.
  - `RegisterStatusNotifierHost`, the `StatusNotifierItemRegistered`/`Unregistered` and `StatusNotifierHostRegistered`/`Unregistered` signals, and the `RegisteredStatusNotifierItems`, `IsStatusNotifierHostRegistered` and `ProtocolVersion` properties.

  How an item is read and shown:
  - Its properties are read with `GetAll`, and again on every `New*` signal, one read at a time. It shows `Title` (or `Id`) and uses the `ToolTip` title as the menu header.
  - `Status` `Passive` hides the item. `NeedsAttention` switches to `AttentionIconName` or its pixmap.
  - The item goes away when its connection or the name it registered leaves the bus, or when its first `GetAll` fails.

  Icons:
  - `IconName` is looked up as a plain name, never a path, in hicolor's `status` and `apps` folders at the bar's sizes, then in `/usr/share/pixmaps` (`apps_status_icon`, `server/src/apps.c`).
  - Otherwise `IconPixmap` is used: network-order ARGB32, the size nearest 22–32 px. Each entry is at most 256×256 and must have exactly w×h×4 bytes; at most 16 entries and 2 MiB in all.
  - `IconThemePath` is not read.

  Clicks and menus:
  - A click sends `Activate(x, y)` and the middle button `SecondaryActivate`. An `ItemIsMenu` item, or one whose app answers `Activate` with an error, opens its menu instead.
  - A right click calls `AboutToShow` and then `GetLayout` on the `com.canonical.dbusmenu` object. The menu is shown with the SDK's `ContextMenu`: mnemonics removed, separators, check marks and radios, disabled and hidden entries, submenus up to 4 levels and up to 256 entries.
  - Choosing an entry sends `Event(id, "clicked")`, only for an entry of the menu just shown. An item with no menu gets `ContextMenu(x, y)`. A menu that arrives more than 5 s after the click opens nothing.

  Every call is asynchronous in the main loop, so an app that hangs only loses its own icon or menu. Texts are cleaned (valid UTF-8, no control or bidi formatting characters, 128 bytes).

  The JS side is `lord.sni` (`list`, `pixels`, `activate`, `menu`, `clicked`) plus the `sni`, `sni-gone` and `sni-menu` events. It exists only in the desktop's own context, never in an isolated app. The shell side is `sdk/trayitems.jsx`, with the pure logic in `sdk/traymodel.js`; the new string is `shell.tray.noMenu` in all six languages.

  Tests:
  - `build/sni-test` (`server/tests/sni_test.c`, 40 checks): both registration forms, pixmap picking and validation, text cleaning, and dbusmenu layout parsing within the depth and item caps, over messages built and validated by `vault/dbus.c`.
  - `server/tests/tray_model_test.mjs` (26 checks).

  Documented in docs/WAYLAND.md, "Tray icons".
- **Files puts copied files on the session clipboard the way Linux file managers do, and pastes files copied in a Linux app.** Copy or Cut in Files still fills Files' own clipboard, so a cut still moves only between Files windows. It now also calls `lord.clipboard.setFiles(paths, { cut })`, which accepts only a list of absolute UTF-8 paths with no NUL, CR or LF, at most 65536 of them. The clipboard's text becomes the paths, one per line, and Wayland apps are offered `text/uri-list` (`file://` URIs, percent-encoded, CRLF) and `x-special/gnome-copied-files` (`copy` or `cut`, then the URIs, LF) next to the text formats. The X window manager offers the same two targets to X11 apps (`xwm.c`). In the other direction, when a Wayland app's selection offers `text/uri-list` (or else the gnome list), the compositor reads it next to the text and ties it to that text the same way it does rich text. An app that offers only files gets their paths as its text. Only file URIs of this machine are kept: an empty or `localhost` host, valid escapes, no query or fragment, and a decoded path that is absolute, valid UTF-8 and free of NUL and line breaks. Other hosts and schemes are dropped. A list that was cut short, has too many files, or comes from a secret selection is dropped whole. Paste in Files (`apps/files/clipfiles.js`) copies those files with `lord.fs.copy` and its usual checks. Another app's cut is always pasted as a copy, and the Paste menu item turns on for files copied outside Files. `lord.clipboard.files()` returns `{ paths, cut, own, gen }`. New module `server/src/wl/urilist.c` encodes and parses both formats. It is tested by `build/urilist-test`, which covers encoding and decoding, other hosts, bad escapes, NUL and line breaks, overlong UTF-8, the copy or cut header, the path and file-count limits, and 16 MiB input. `server/tests/files_clipfiles_test.mjs` (in `run_suites.sh`) tests which clipboard a paste uses. `build/clipfiles-client` (built by `make -C server build/clipfiles-client`, run inside a session) copies files as a Linux app would and checks what LordOS keeps and offers back. Docs: `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Clipboard", protocol table, X11 bridge), `docs/FILES.md`, `docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md`.
  - A file list from another app is kept only from an app that is positively unsandboxed (never an isolated LordOS app, a Flatpak, or an X11 app) and only when its text names the same files. Pasting it in Files first asks "Paste N items copied in <app>?", listing the first names, with Cancel as the default (`apps/files/clipfiles.js` `pasteAsk`, the SDK `ConfirmDialog`'s new `cautious` prop). Checked on VM 127: Copy in Files offers `text/uri-list` and `x-special/gnome-copied-files`; a file copied by another client asked first, Enter cancelled, Paste copied it.
- **A keyboard focus model for every app: Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls, a focus ring appears only after the keyboard is used, and Space and Enter press.** `sdk/focus.js`, with its pure logic in `sdk/focusmodel.js`, walks the window's node tree in tree order. `runtime/index.js` now keeps `host`, `first`, `last`, `prev` and `next` links on each node, so mounting or reordering a row costs constant time even in a 5000-row folder. Tab skips nodes hidden with `display: 'none'` and disabled ones, and wraps at the ends. While a shell sheet or prompt is open (the modal, system, overlay or capture layer), Tab goes round that sheet's controls instead, and inside a View with the new `modal` prop while it is shown. Ctrl+Tab and ⌥Tab still belong to the apps and the shell.
  - New host props on `View`: `focusable`, `disabled`, `onKeyDown(e)` (return true when the key was used), `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `focusRing={false}` and `onRevealFocus`.
  - `runtime/events.js` gives the focused control each key before any listener sees it. A key the control uses reaches no `useKeyboard` handler, so Space on a toolbar button in Files presses it and opens no preview. Tab moves the focus only after every listener has had the key, and not at all if one called the new `e.preventDefault()`. The Terminal, the Text Editor, a virtual machine's screen and console, the remote desktop, the Databases completion list, the Imager's own focus and the Overview call it and keep Tab.
  - The ring works like `:focus-visible`. It is a 2 px line 1 px outside the control that follows its corners. The runtime draws it as a node of its own (`setFocusRing`), drawn inside the box for a node that clips its children. Its color is the new theme token `focusRing`, or the accent when the theme sets none. A press of the pointer ends the focus and hides the ring, and the next Tab continues from where the press was.
  - Checked on VM 127 in Settings: Tab moved the ring through the search field, the content and its switches and selectors.
- **Every shared control can be focused, unless it is disabled or has `focusable={false}`.** These are `Button`, `ToolbarButton`, `Toggle`, `Segmented`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `TextInput`, `TextArea` and Settings' `PopUp`, plus a `ScrollView` whose content doesn't fit.
  - Sliders and steppers: ← →, ↑ ↓, Page Up/Down, Home and End move them. `Slider` gains an optional `step`.
  - `Segmented`: ← → change the selected segment.
  - `MenuButton` and Settings' pop-up buttons: ↓, Space or Enter opens the list. ↓ ↑ move the highlight, skipping separators and disabled items. Enter chooses, and Escape or Tab closes the list. A menu opened with the mouse takes these keys too.
  - Right to left: ← and → swap in sliders, steppers, segmented controls and horizontal scroll views. A `Slider` now starts at the right edge in RTL, so its minimum is on the right.
  - A `TextInput` reached with Tab has all its text selected. Tab leaves a text field for the next control unless the field is inside a `FormFields` or its `onKeyDown` used the key. An app's own text field (`takeTextFocus`) keeps Tab.
  - Files' icon, list and column views pass `focusable={false}`, so the arrows still move the selection there. In Files, Tab during a rename keeps the new name, as Enter does.
  - Confirmation dialogs (`sdk/dialogkeys.js`) keep Escape, Enter and Tab while they are in front, and the focus ring comes back when they close. Their own focus ring used a `boxShadow` spread, which the engine's shadow parser ignores, so it never showed; it is now drawn like the others.
- **`ScrollView` scrolls with the keyboard and can scroll sideways.** A focused scroll view, or one with a focused control inside it, scrolls with ↓ ↑, Page Up/Down, Space and ⇧Space, Home and End. A control Tab moves to inside a scroll view is scrolled into sight. The new `horizontal` prop scrolls along a row, with ← →, a sideways swipe or wheel tilt, or Shift and the wheel, and puts its scroll bar along the bottom edge.
- Tests: `tests/focus_model_test.mjs` (102 checks: tree order, skipping, a modal node, the focus-visible state, the keys of every control, RTL) and `tests/focus_scene_test.mjs` (41 checks with the controls rendered through AppHost and driven by the server's own `__lordKey` and `__lordEvent`). Both are registered in `tests/run_suites.sh`. The docs are updated: `docs/DESIGN.md` gains a "Keyboard focus" section and a `focusRing` row in the token table, `themes/README.md` and `docs/THEMES-GUIDE.md` list the token, and two rows of `docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md` phase 4 are set to built, to check on the VM.
- **Menus work from the keyboard in both themes and in the apps' right-click menus.** In an open menu, ↑/↓ move the highlight and wrap at the ends, skipping separators, headers, swatches and disabled rows. Home/End (and Page Up/Down) jump to the first or last row, Enter or Space choose, and letters typed close together (0.9 s) jump to the row they start; the same letter again goes on to the next such row. → opens a submenu with its first row highlighted and ← closes it (the other way round in Arabic and Hebrew), and Escape now closes one level at a time. The pointer works as before, except that a submenu opens after a 180 ms pause on its row instead of as the pointer passes over it. It also stays open while the pointer crosses other rows on its way there: the safe triangle, with a 400 ms grace. Submenus open on the side with room, the reading direction's side first, so in right-to-left languages they no longer cover their parent menu. F10, or the left ⌥ pressed and released alone, opens the first menu of Lord Flow's lit menu bar or of Lord Classic's menu strip under the focused window, with its first row highlighted. ← and → then move between the bar's menus, and the same key closes it. The Terminal keeps F10, AltGr never counts, and Linux apps keep their own menus. A menu opened from the keyboard returns the keyboard to the text field that had it, unless the click that closed the menu went to another field. The rules are pure functions in the new `sdk/menunav.js` (`stepIndex`, `edgeIndex`, `menuAction`, `typeAhead`, `matchIndex`, `subPlace`, `aiming`, `barIndex`). They are used by `themes/default/components/Menu.jsx`, `themes/classic/components/Menu.jsx` and `sdk/contextmenu.jsx`, and the bars register with `addMenuBarKeys({ can, run })` in `sdk/shortcuts.js`. A new "Open the menu bar from the keyboard" row in Settings → Keyboard shows F10 · ⌥. Tests: `server/tests/menu_nav_test.mjs` (68 checks) and `server/tests/menu_keys_test.mjs` (31 checks: both themes' menus, the hover pause, F10 and ⌥ alone), both registered in `run_suites.sh`. `textfield_menu_scene.mjs` now checks that the open field menu takes the keys (type-ahead, Enter, arrows wrapping) and gives them back. Documented in `docs/SHORTCUTS.md`.
  - Checked on VM 127: F10 opened the app menu, ↓ skipped a disabled item, → went to the next menu.
- **Primary selection everywhere: select to copy, middle click to paste, in LordOS's own text fields and the Terminal as well as Linux apps.** The compositor already had `zwp_primary_selection_v1` (0.8.3) and the X PRIMARY bridge (`xwm.c`). Now LordOS's own text takes part too. Selecting text in a `TextInput` or `TextArea` (by drag, double or triple click, Shift with the arrows, or Ctrl/⌘+A) publishes it as the primary selection, never from a password field. So does a mouse selection in a Terminal pane. A middle click in a field pastes the primary selection at the click point, not over the selection, and it can be undone as its own step (`sdk/primarymodel.js`). A middle click in a Terminal pane pastes the primary selection instead of the clipboard, unless the program in the pane takes the mouse (`term_mouse` returns 4, `apps/terminal/Panes.jsx`). The new `lord.primary.set(text)` publishes text, up to 16 MB. `lord.primary.get()` returns the text only while lord-server is handling a middle-button press (`js_primary_gesture` in `ui/js.c`), so what a Linux app selects can't be read at will. Isolated `.lpk` apps have no `lord.primary`, and no broker message was added. `zwp_primary_selection_device_v1.set_selection` now also needs a click, key or keyboard-enter serial that the app got in the last 10 s (`xact_serial_recent`); a made-up serial is ignored. If an older selection's pipe is read after a newer one arrives, the older text is dropped (`prim_req`). **Settings → Mouse & Trackpad → Middle click pastes** (`trackpad.middlePaste`, on by default, applied through `lord.input.configure` → `wl_primary_paste`) turns it off. Selecting still sets the selection, but no Wayland or X11 app is offered it, and fields and the Terminal paste nothing. Tests: `server/tests/primary_model_test.mjs` (new, in `run_suites.sh`), `textfield_menu_test.mjs` (6 new checks: a double click publishes, a middle click pastes at the point and is undone, line breaks in a one-line field, Ctrl+A publishes), and `build/primary-client` (`tests/primary_client.c`, a Wayland client run inside a session: a made-up serial is ignored, the enter serial gets the source asked once for `text/plain;charset=utf-8`, the offer lists three text types and gives the text, an unlisted type gives nothing, a replaced source is cancelled, a source with no text type is never asked). Docs: `WAYLAND.md`, `TRACKPAD.md`, `TERMINAL.md`, `DESKTOP-PARITY.md`.
  - Checked on VM 127: a word selected in Chromium was the primary selection, and a middle click pasted it into the Files search field.
- **Password fields have a show-password eye and a Caps Lock warning, everywhere LordOS asks for a password.** Built once in the SDK's `TextInput` with `secure` (`sdk/components.jsx`), so the login and lock screen (greeter), Wi-Fi and VPN, the Passwords vault and keyring unlock, Users, Sharing, Machines, Databases, Mail, Backup, the Installer, Files' network sign-in and remote desktop all get it. An eye at the field's trailing edge (leading edge in a right-to-left UI) shows the text, with a "Show Password" / "Hide Password" tooltip through `t()`. The text is hidden again when the field loses focus (also when its window is minimized or leaves the desktop in view, which already moves the focus away) and on Enter. It stays a password field while shown: no undo history, no input method, and Copy and Cut still copy nothing. While the field has focus with Caps Lock on, it shows "⇪ Caps Lock is on" before the eye, or just ⇪ when the words do not fit. `eye={false}` leaves the eye out where a view has its own Show (Passwords' entry editor, the Imager). Caps Lock state reaches JS as `caps` on every key event (`runtime/keymap.js`, from the bit lord-server already sent in `__lordKey`'s flags) and as `capsLock()` from `@lordos/runtime`. No new permission, broker message or `lord.*` call. In isolated apps, `kb_set_locked()` (`server/src/keyboard.c`) now applies the compositor's locked modifiers from `wl_keyboard.modifiers` (`server/src/app/appclient.c`). Before, a window that got the keyboard started with Caps Lock off even when it was on. The pure state is in `sdk/passwordfieldmodel.js`. Tests: `server/tests/password_field_test.mjs` (32 checks: shown/hidden transitions, the hint's visibility, masking), `server/tests/password_field_scene.mjs` (run by `textfield_menu_test.mjs`, 16 checks on a real TextInput driven with `__lordEvent`/`__lordKey`) and `test_locked` in `server/tests/osk_test.c`. New keys `shell.password.show`, `shell.password.hide` and `shell.password.capsLock` in all six languages.
  - Checked on VM 127 in Settings → Users: with Caps Lock on the field said so, and the eye showed the typed text.
- **Terminal: port forwards over the tab's own ssh.** Profile → SSH lists forwards, each "server host:port →
  127.0.0.1:port", with the local port automatic (a free one) or fixed (1024–65535) and an on/off switch. When an ssh
  started in that profile's session connects, they open through its own control socket (`MUX_C_OPEN_FWD`, the
  connection sharing Files mode uses): no second login, no program run, listening on 127.0.0.1 only. A forward waits
  for the control socket while ssh is still signing in, and they all end with the connection. The tab shows a badge,
  `⇄ 18080→36169` (and `+n` for more), and the footer how many are open; a click opens their list with Open (in the
  browser), Copy and Close, and a field to add one for this connection only (`8080` or `host:5432`). A notice says
  when they open, with Open in Browser for a web port. Checked on a real session against a private sshd: a page
  served on the server's 18080 came through the automatic local port, a forward added from the list opened, Close
  and `exit` removed their listeners.
- **Terminal: drop files on an ssh pane to upload them.** A file or a folder dragged from Files onto a pane that runs
  ssh goes up to the server over the same connection, in the background: nothing is typed and the terminal is never
  blocked. A floating notice lists each file with an orange bar, Cancel and Hide, and the footer shows `↑ n · %` while
  it is hidden. A name already on the server is never replaced: the upload takes a free name (`notes (2).txt`) and a
  notice says so. ⌥ while dropping pastes the paths, as before, and a pane without ssh still gets the paths. Links are
  never followed, there or in Files mode's uploads (a link inside a dropped folder could lead to `~/.ssh`): they are
  left out and a notice counts them. The notice shows the folder the files go to.
- **Terminal: the remote shell's directory.** While ssh runs, the directory its shell reports (OSC 7) is the
  server's: it no longer replaces the local one (used by new tabs and the footer). Since it is the server's output, it
  is kept only as an absolute path without control characters. Drops go there and Files mode opens
  there instead of the remote home. Checked on a real session: a folder with a subfolder, a 3 MB file (identical
  after the upload) and a name that was already there (kept, the copy saved as `notes (2).txt`) went to the reported
  `~/srvdir`, and Files mode opened in it.
- **Terminal: ❖ + click on a name in `ls` output downloads it.** In a pane that runs ssh, a file name printed by `ls` or
  `ls -l` (quoted names, long-iso dates, links and devices included) comes down to Downloads over the same connection,
  resolved against the remote shell's directory; a folder comes down whole, links are not followed and a name already
  in Downloads gets a free one. The notice shows the downloads in blue. A right click on a name offers Download and
  Copy Remote Path. New: `term.lineAt(sid, x, y)` (the line under the pointer, split at its cell) and
  `apps/terminal/lsnames.js` with `terminal_lsnames_test.mjs` (21 checks). Checked on a real session: a file and a
  folder with a subfolder.
- **Terminal: Open, Open With and Edit for a file on the server (Files mode).** Open and Open With (the app LordOS
  picks, then each Linux app that declares the type) bring the file down to a folder of its own under
  `~/.cache/lordos/terminal-remote` and open it. Edit opens it in the Text Editor and sends each save back up to the
  same path, while Files mode is open; it is the only upload that replaces a file without asking, since that file is
  the one chosen for editing. Checked on a real session: an edit saved with ❖S reached the server's file.
- **Terminal: triggers in a sheet.** Settings → Triggers lists each trigger on one line (its switch, expression,
  action and parameter) with Edit… and −. Edit… and Add Trigger open a sheet with the expression, the action, the
  parameter with what it means for that action (`\0` the match, `\1…\9` its groups, `\n` Enter, `#text,#background`),
  the switch, and a line to try it on: it says whether the expression is valid, what it matches and what the action
  would do (a notice with this text, this title, types this…). `apps/terminal/triggers.js`, as the triggers run, with
  `terminal_triggers_test.mjs` (13 checks).
- **Terminal: "Send text at start" is a box of several lines, and each line runs.** Settings → General edits the text in
  a field of several lines (long lines wrap, ↑ ↓ keep the column, Home, End and a click place the caret, a paste keeps
  its line breaks). Each line is typed and sent with Enter, the last one too, so a command runs without a `\n` at its
  end; a `\n` written in a profile saved before (or imported) still counts as one line break, and a `\n` at the end
  is not sent twice. `initialKeys` in `apps/terminal/profilefields.js` (`terminal_profilefields_test.mjs`, 22 checks).
  The field is the SDK's new `TextArea` (`sdk/textareamodel.js`, `textarea_model_test.mjs`, 26 checks).
- **Terminal: a profile's tags are edited in Settings → General.** One field, separated by commas; the Profiles menu and
  the lists regroup at once. Tags imported from another emulator (shown next to the name) can now be renamed or removed.
- **Terminal: a tab opened with a profile is named after it.** A tab whose profile is not the default one shows the
  profile's name until it is given a title of its own; the window's title keeps the session's (user@host, directory).

- **Share a screen or a window with a Linux app: LordOS serves the ScreenCast portal itself, and the frames go out through the new sandboxed helper `lord-screencast`.** A browser's video call, a recorder or a chat app asks through `org.freedesktop.portal.ScreenCast` (version 4: `CreateSession`, `SelectSources`, `Start`, `OpenPipeWireRemote`, the `Session` object), served by `server/src/ui/portal.c` with no `xdg-desktop-portal`. Checked on VM 127 with a browser's screen-sharing test page: 176 frames in 10 s at 1280×800, `lord-screencast` at about 2 % of a CPU, and no helper running when nothing is shared.
  - The sessions are a state machine with no I/O (`server/src/cast/castsm.c`). Each session belongs to the bus name that made it. Limits: 16 sessions, 4 per app and one chooser at a time. Monitors and windows can be shared, one or several, with the pointer hidden or drawn in. Cursor metadata isn't offered, and no `restore_token` is ever given, so the person picks every time.
  - `Start` shows LordOS's own chooser (`sdk/screencast.jsx`, `sdk/screencastmodel.js`): the displays and the open windows, each with a live picture (`lord.portal.castThumb`, only while the chooser is up), under the name of the app asking. That name is only an identity LordOS checked (the app id of its launcher's scope), never `/proc/<pid>/comm`. A process LordOS can't identify is "An unknown program", with a warning. Nothing is shared until the person presses Share. Cancel answers 1. An app with the "no screen capture" restriction gets 2 without a question. An unknown sender gets 2 too while any app with that restriction runs, so the chooser fails closed (`csm_gate`).
  - While a session shares, the screen-sharing indicator shows a pill for it with a Stop button, and no frame is sent until that pill is on screen. Stop, a lock, a user switch, the shared window closing, the helper failing, or the app's `Close` or exit ends it, and the app hears `Session.Closed`. A share holds each window by node id and by a serial that is never reused (`node_ref`), so a later window that gets the same id is never captured.
  - The pixels are painted again in capture mode, as Screenshots does: a display at its own scale, or one window and its sheets alone. Protected windows such as Passwords are black. Only damaged areas are repainted. They reach the helper through a sealed three-frame memfd ring (`server/src/cast/castproto.h`), at most 60 frames a second and only while the consumer streams. Each side checks every message (`cast_check_helper`, `cast_check_server`).
  - `lord-screencast` (`server/src/cast/lordscreencast.c`) is the only binary that links `libpipewire-0.3` (approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-10). It runs one per session. `lord-server` connects the user's PipeWire socket and hands the fds over. The helper loads no real-time module, no D-Bus and no devices, then calls `sandbox_apply_helper` (scope `lordos-screencast`; the only extra syscalls are the three `timerfd_*`) before the connection says a word. It then cuts its own PipeWire permissions to read-only, full only on its own nodes. The app's connection (`OpenPipeWireRemote`) sees only the core, the client-node factory and the session's nodes. The PipeWire guard (`sec/pwguard.c`) hides every shared screen from apps with "no screen capture".
  - Each buffer is a sealed memfd of its own (`PW_STREAM_FLAG_ALLOC_BUFFERS`), filled in the graph cycle that `pw_stream_trigger_process` starts. Left to PipeWire, the buffers were one shared block with no fd, which a browser's WebRTC capturer drops, so the page's video stayed black.
  - Cost, measured on the main machine (`make -C server screencast-bench`, 1920×1080 at 30 frames a second, every frame different): about 1.1 ms a frame in `lord-server` and 3 % of a core in `lord-screencast`. Nothing runs and nothing is copied when nothing is shared. Not done yet: dmabuf buffers, cursor metadata, restoring a choice, popup menus in a window share, and audio.
  - Building it needs `libpipewire-0.3-dev` (recorded in `docs/VM-SETUP.md`). Without it, `make` skips the helper and the portal offers no source types.
  - Tests: `build/castsm-test`, `build/castproto-test` (with ASan and UBSan), `build/screencast-test` (`tests/screencast_test.sh`, against a private PipeWire daemon: the app's connection sees only the stream, and frames arrive pixel for pixel), `test_node_ref` in `build/engine-test`, `build/pwguard-test` and `tests/screencast_model_test.mjs`.
  - Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Sharing a screen or a window"), `docs/SCREEN-SHARING.md`, `docs/PRIVACY.md` and `docs/FLATPAK.md`.
- **SVG icons: `lord-media` draws them with vendored nanosvg, so tray and Dock icons that ship only as SVG show.** Checked on VM 127: the volume applet's symbolic tray icon is drawn in the bar's text color.
  - `server/src/iconfind.c` looks for PNG first, then SVG, then symbolic SVG. A `src` of `svg:<px>:<rrggbb|->:<path>` (`sdk/iconsrc.js`) or an `.svg` file goes to `server/src/media/svgicon.c`. `lord-server` checks the path after `realpath` (only under `/usr/share`, `/usr/local/share`, `/opt`, the Flatpak exports or the user's icon folders) and opens it with `O_NOFOLLOW`. The file must be a regular file of at most 1 MB. Only the fd goes to the helper, in an `MW_SVG` job, and `lord-server` never parses SVG.
  - `lord-media` (`helper/lm_svg.c`, in its sandbox) counts the elements (at most 20,000) and the nesting (at most 64) with a dry run of nanosvg's own tokenizer. A separate scan would read quotes, comments, CDATA, `<?` and `<!` differently from nanosvg, and could miss markup hidden there. It then limits shapes (4,000), points (200,000), numbers, gradients, strokes and dashes before rasterizing. A symbolic icon takes the requested color. A job has 3 s before the worker is killed.
  - The pictures are kept in the image cache under path, modification time, size and color.
  - Tests: `build/svgrast-test` (in `make test`), `build/media-test svg` (`test-full`), `build/iconfind-test` and `tests/iconsrc_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/MEDIA.md` ("SVG icons"). nanosvg (zlib) is added to the dependency table in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **A virtual machine, a remote desktop or a game can take ❖, ⌥Tab and the other shortcuts while it is in front, once the person allows it (`zwp_keyboard_shortcuts_inhibit_manager_v1`).** ❖Esc always gives them back. Checked on VM 127: the prompt names the app by its verified identity.
  - The answer is the new `shortcuts` permission (`server/src/sec/perms.c`), listed and changed in Settings → Privacy → Keyboard shortcuts. It can't be declared in a manifest or asked for through the broker.
  - The decision goes by who `lord-server` checks the client is (`kbi_identity`, `server/src/wl/kbinhibit.c`), never by the app_id it sets. The check reads `/proc/<pid>` through the socket's pidfd when the client connects. A Flatpak app is `flatpak:<id>`; a process in `lord-server`'s own namespaces is `program:<resolved path>`. Anything else gets no identity, and its inhibitor never holds. Xwayland, isolated LordOS apps and the login screen never get it. The prompt shows the identity under the app's name. The name comes from an installed `.desktop` entry only when its Exec runs that very program (`apps_name_of_program`).
  - These keys always stay LordOS's: ❖Esc, the lock, Ctrl+Alt+F1…F12, the media, sound and light keys, Print Screen, ⌃⌥⌫ and ⌃⌥⇧Esc. ❖Esc turns the inhibitor off for that window, together with a locked pointer and fullscreen; pressed again, it turns it back on. A window that holds the shortcuts also gets its key presses before any Linux app's global shortcut.
  - Machines' VM window does the same inside the session (`sdk/kbinhibit.js`, `sdk/kbinhibitmodel.js`).
  - Tests: `build/kbinhibit-test`, `build/apps-actions-test`, `tests/kbinhibit_model_test.mjs` and `build/kbinhibit-client` (inside a session). Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Keyboard shortcuts inhibit"), `docs/SHORTCUTS.md` and `docs/PRIVACY.md`.
- **Global shortcuts for Linux apps (`org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts`, version 1), so push-to-talk and a recorder's hotkeys work while another app is in front.** Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - `lord-server` serves `CreateSession`, `BindShortcuts`, `ListShortcuts`, `Activated` and `Deactivated` (on press and release) and `ShortcutsChanged` (`server/src/ui/portal.c`, with the rules in `server/src/ui/gshort.c`).
  - The person chooses the keys in LordOS's own sheet (`sdk/globalshortcuts.jsx`). Nothing is bound until they press Save.
  - An app never gets a ❖ combination, the media keys, Tab or Esc with a modifier, ⌃⌥ with F-keys, Backspace or Delete, a typing key without ⌃ or ⌥, or anything LordOS's own tables keep. A key one app holds is refused to every other.
  - A bound key goes only to the app that holds it, and only to the connection that opened the session.
  - The decisions are kept per app scope in `~/.config/lordos/global-shortcuts.json` (added to `fsops_protected`). Settings → Keyboard changes or forgets them.
  - A shortcuts session and a screen cast session never share an object path, and `Session.Close` reaches the one the path belongs to.
  - Tests: `build/gshort-test`, `build/portal-gs-test` (on a private session bus) and `tests/global_shortcuts_model_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/SHORTCUTS.md` and `docs/FLATPAK.md`.
- **Drag and drop with X11 apps: the window manager bridges XDND (version 5) both ways between X11 apps, Wayland apps and Files.** Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - **Into an X window.** For a drag from Files or a Wayland app, the window manager (`server/src/wl/xwm.c`) is the XDND source over an `XdndAware` window. It answers a `ConvertSelection` only for a window of that window's client, with at most 16 MB in 10 s (`INCR` for large ones).
  - **Out of an X app.** For an X app's drag, an invisible `XdndAware` window turns the drag into a Wayland drag for the window under the pointer.
  - **What is trusted.** The data is read only from the X server's own `SelectionNotify`, never one another client sent. Before every read, the selection's owner and its client's pid must still be the ones of `XdndEnter`.
  - **Files from an X app.** They reach Files only when X-Resource ties the owner to an unsandboxed process and no client of the display is sandboxed. A Flatpak app with the X11 socket therefore turns X drops onto Files off until it closes.
  - **HiDPI.** A Wayland drag's `XdndPosition` is sent in X pixels, so drops land under the pointer on HiDPI displays.
  - Tests: `build/xwm-test`. Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Drag and drop") and `docs/PRIVACY.md`.
- **X11 apps are sharp on HiDPI displays: they scale themselves.** Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - **One scale per run.** Xwayland gets the largest display scale for as long as it runs (`server/src/wl/xwscale.c`). On the densest display, one X pixel is one device pixel. `wl.c` and `xwm.c` convert sizes, places, input and the caret for Xwayland's connection alone.
  - **How apps learn the scale.** The root window's `RESOURCE_MANAGER` carries `Xft.dpi` (96 × the scale). LordOS sets no `GDK_SCALE` or `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`, so an app that reads neither looks small.
  - **The setting.** Settings → Displays → X11 apps offers «Scale themselves (sharp)», the default, and «Scaled by LordOS (blurry)», the old way (`settings.x11Scaling`, `lord.wayland.x11SelfScale`). A change applies the next time Xwayland starts.
  - **Not done.** The scale doesn't follow a display change while X11 apps are open, and scroll deltas are not converted.
  - Tests: `build/xwscale-test`. Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("X11 apps on HiDPI displays") and `docs/DISPLAYS.md`.
- **Security contexts (`wp_security_context_manager_v1`): a sandbox engine such as Flatpak 1.15 or later gives each app a Wayland socket of its own, and its clients count as sandboxed.** Built; not yet checked on the VM with a real Flatpak.
  - **The context.** `server/src/wl/secctx.c` accepts on the listening socket until `close_fd` hangs up, with at most 64 contexts. The metadata (engine, app id, instance id) is checked: 1 to 255 bytes of printable ASCII, set once.
  - **Who may make one.** Only a client `lord-server` knows is outside any sandbox. Asking from inside a context is the `nested` error.
  - **Its clients.** They carry the metadata and never hand files to LordOS. They don't see the trusted-only globals (`secctx_hidden`: capture, other windows, virtual input, layer shell and others, listed ahead of time so that one added later is hidden from the start).
  - **Its identity.** A Flatpak context's app id is the client's identity for the shortcuts permission.
  - Tests: `build/secctx-test` (the protocol end to end over socketpairs). Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` ("Security contexts") and `docs/FLATPAK.md`.
- **SDK widgets with the keyboard built in: `List`, `Table`, `Dropdown`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Tabs`, `Popover`, `Tooltip` and `ProgressBar`, and the wheel on sliders and steppers.** Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - **Lists and tables** (`sdk/lists.jsx`, `sdk/listmodel.js`) are one Tab stop. They select with ↑ ↓, Home, End and Page Up/Down. With `multiple`, Shift extends a range, Ctrl toggles a row and Ctrl+A selects all. Typing a name jumps to it, and a `Table` sorts from its header.
  - **Choice controls** (`sdk/controls.jsx`, `sdk/controlmodel.js`). A `Dropdown` opens with Space, Enter or the arrows and jumps by letters. `Tabs` and `RadioGroup` are one stop whose arrows choose (swapped in right-to-left). A `Checkbox` flips with Space.
  - **Popups.** A `Popover` is a focus scope: Escape closes only the newest popup and gives the focus back. A `Tooltip` shows after 550 ms on hover or on keyboard focus.
  - **Progress.** A `ProgressBar` is determinate, or a sliding band with no value.
  - **The wheel** moves a slider or a stepper by one step. A touchpad swipe does so only while the control has the focus.
  - **Where they're used.** Reminders' popovers and Monitor's process table now use them.
  - Tests: `tests/list_model_test.mjs`, `tests/control_model_test.mjs` and `list_scene.mjs` through `focus_scene_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/DESIGN.md` and `docs/LAYERS.md`.
- **Text fields place the caret and the selection from the shaped, reordered text, and move by grapheme cluster.** Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - `lord.text.carets(text, size, weight)` (`server/src/ui/caret.c`) gives the screen edges of every code point after bidi reordering. A selection over Hebrew or Arabic mixed with numbers is drawn as one rectangle per piece on screen. ← and → move on screen.
  - `lord.text.graphemes` (`server/src/ui/grapheme.c`, UAX #29 extended clusters) keeps the arrows, Backspace, Delete, clicks and double clicks out of the middle of an emoji ZWJ sequence, a flag, a skin-tone sequence, a letter with its combining marks, a Hangul syllable or an Indic conjunct. The grapheme-break table is generated by `tools/gen-unicode.mjs`.
  - Tests: `build/bidi-test` (the Unicode `GraphemeBreakTest.txt`, 1,187 cases, plus caret cases), `build/engine-test` and `tests/textfield_cluster_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/LANGUAGES.md`.
- **Terminal apps (`.desktop` entries with `Terminal=true`, such as htop or mc) open in a Terminal tab, and the command never passes through JavaScript.** Approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-10. Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - `lord.apps.launch(id)` of such an entry runs nothing. It parses the `Exec` line as for any app and keeps the argv in a one-shot slot (`server/src/term/termapp.c`: a random 128-bit token, 10 s, single use, at most 4 pending). It answers `{ terminal: token }`.
  - The Terminal passes only that token (`lord.term.create({ app: token })`). `lord-server` types the line into the tab's usual login shell once, at its first prompt.
  - The line is built in C: every argument single-quoted, with fish's backslashes doubled. An argument with a control character or invalid UTF-8 refuses the launch. The profile's new "When a program opened from the launcher exits" setting chooses one of three fixed endings.
  - An app with restrictions in Settings → Privacy is refused, since in a Terminal tab it would run with neither its rules nor its sandbox. The launcher shows these apps with the Terminal's icon in a corner.
  - Tests: `build/apps-term-test` and `tests/terminal_profilefields_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/TERMINAL.md` and `docs/WAYLAND.md`.
- **logind's Lock locks the screen.** `loginctl lock-session`, `loginctl lock-sessions` or an admin's `LockSession` now lock the desktop as ❖L does. Built; not yet checked on the VM.
  - The signal is believed only from the connection that owns `org.freedesktop.login1` (`server/src/hw/logindlock.c`, `server/src/hw/lockstate.c`).
  - When the desktop has a logind session of its own, only that session's `Lock` counts, and `LockedHint` follows the lock. Today `lord-sessiond`'s sessions are not logind sessions, so a `Lock` of any session of the same user counts.
  - logind's `Unlock` is never obeyed: only the password on the login screen gives the monitor back.
  - Tests: `build/logindlock-test`. Documented in `docs/SESSIONS.md`.
- **The LordOS Web Runtime: web apps installed as LordOS apps, each app and profile in its own process (`lord-web`, with Debian's WPE WebKit).** Approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-10. Runs on VM 127 since 2026-11-11; what was checked there is in the web app entries of this section.
  - **Packaging.** `lord-web` (`server/src/web/`) is the only binary that links WPE WebKit (`libwpewebkit-2.0` 2.48, `libwpe`, `wpebackend-fdo`). It ships in the optional package `lordos-web` (`tools/iso/mkdeb-web.sh`). Without that package, the rest of LordOS works unchanged, and the Store offers to install it.
  - **Sandbox.** WebKit's own sandbox (bubblewrap, seccomp, `xdg-dbus-proxy`) is always on, and `lord-web` refuses the variable that turns it off.
  - **The manager** (`lord.webapps`, `server/src/ui/js_webapps.c`, `server/src/web/webmgr.c`, `webreg.c`). It keeps the registry in `~/.config/lordos/web/` and the profiles' data in `~/.local/share/lordos/web/` (both added to `fsops_protected`). It starts `lord-web` from the fixed path next to `lord-server`, with exactly `--app <app> --profile <profile>`.
  - **The window.** Each app has its own window (app id `lordos-web.<app>.<profile>`), Dock icon and profiles. A second launch brings the running window forward with an activation token sent over the bus (`Show`), also from the tray.
  - **Where it appears.** The Store has a Web apps section, with a catalog that ships with LordOS and "Add from an address". Settings → Web apps lists profiles, data sizes and permissions.
  - **Adding from an address.** `lord-web --probe` loads the page in a throwaway session, reads its manifest and icons, and answers one JSON line. `--probe-icon` fetches the chosen PNG or SVG (at most 1 MB). The probe never follows `https` to `http`, or a public address to this computer or a local network. It resolves names itself, treats LAN names, single labels and private addresses as local, and checks every hop: once public, always public. Its errors are `web.probe.*` codes in every language.
  - **Permissions.** Notifications, camera, microphone, screen and location are asked once per app through `org.lordos.WebApps1.Ask`, answered only for the `lord-web` that `lord-server` started for that app and profile. The answer is kept in Settings → Web apps. Only the app's own pages get them: outside its scope, or for another origin, a request is denied and never asked.
  - **Background mode.** With `background` on, closing the window keeps the app running behind a tray icon with Open and Quit.
