  - **Isolation of `lord-web`.** Its own firewall scope (`lordos-web-<app>`), a cgroup with memory and CPU limits, Landlock's scoping and `no_new_privs`. In a managed session it refuses to start without them.
  - Tests: `build/webreg-test`, `build/webapp-test`, `tests/web_probe_test.py` (headless probes of a page the test serves; 224 MB PSS at the peak on the main machine), `tests/webapps_model_test.mjs` and `webapps_sheet_scene.mjs`.
  - Documented in `docs/WEBAPPS.md`. The packages to build it are recorded in `docs/VM-SETUP.md`. WPE WebKit is added to the dependency table in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Photos: Move to Trash.** The File menu, a right click on a thumbnail, a button in the viewer's toolbar and the Delete
  key (or ❖⌫) move pictures to the Trash with `lord.fs.trash`, as Files does: nothing is asked for a picture on this
  computer, a picture on a network share goes off the interface thread (`fs.trashAsync`), and a picture in a cloud
  account's kept folder is deleted in that account after the same question Files asks ("Delete from {provider}?",
  saying whether it goes to the provider's trash). The library now selects several pictures: ❖-click adds or takes one
  away, Shift-click selects a range, ❖A selects all, Escape clears; the right-click menu acts on the selection, and the
  title line says "N of M selected". The library has a File menu of its own (Open, Select All, Move to Trash). In the
  viewer the next picture opens, or the previous one after the last, and the library comes back when none is left. A
  toast says how many went. Pure logic in `apps/photos/trash.js` with `photos_trash_test.mjs` (20 checks); new keys
  `photos.menu.*`, `photos.trashed`, `photos.selectedOf` and `photos.cancel` in en, es, pt, fr, it and lt. No new
  permission: Photos already had `fs:home:write` (GitHub #119).
- **Settings → Cloud: an account's Details.** The account's page has a Details box with the provider, rclone's backend
  type (`drive`, `webdav`, `sftp`…), how it signs in (browser, server or object storage), the server and port for a
  server kind, and "Your own app" when it signs in with the person's own client ID (`accountDetails` in
  `sdk/cloudmodel.js`, 6 new checks in `cloud_model_test.mjs`, including one that no secret field reaches the box). It
  shows only what the account's state already carries: the user name or email is not there, because rclone marks those
  options sensitive and they live in the keyring with the password, out of JavaScript's reach. Account colors are kept
  as they were, by the order accounts were added, so two accounts on the same provider still look different and no
  one's colors change after the update (GitHub #115).
- **The paper and the site call 0.8.8.8 released on 12 November 2026, the latest release.** Paper (en, es, pt; meta

- **The paper and the site describe the rest of 0.8.8.8's work (in development; the latest release is 0.8.8.7).** Paper (en, es, pt; meta 2026-11-11): the abstract, §2.3, §3.4, §3.6, §4.4, §5.1, §5.4, §6.6, §6.7, §10.1 to §10.3, §11.2 and the Changelog table now cover screen and window sharing, SVG icons, apps that take the shortcuts, global shortcuts, XDND, security contexts, X11 apps on HiDPI, the SDK widgets, the bidi caret, Terminal apps, logind's Lock and the LordOS Web Runtime. §6.7 no longer says 0.8.8.8 adds no helper. `docs/PAPER-VALIDATION.md` gets rows for these claims. Site: the Linux apps and own-desktop feature pages and the FAQ (Linux apps, and a new web apps answer).
- **The paper and the site describe 0.8.8.8 as in development; the latest release is 0.8.8.7.** Paper (en, es, pt; meta 0.8.8.8 Beta, 2026-11-10): the abstract, §10.1 and the Changelog table call 0.8.8.8 in development. §1.2 says the Terminal's port forwards, drop uploads and `ls` downloads go through the tab's own `ssh` socket and run no program. §5.1 gains three in-development items: the Terminal over `ssh` (forwards, drop to upload, ❖ + click downloads, the remote directory, and Open, Open With and Edit in Files mode), the Terminal's settings (the triggers sheet, multi-line "Send text at start", tags in one field), and text fields with selection, dragged files above every window, Text Editor drops, tag and group colors and one name order (GitHub #64). §6.7 covers the security of these: the 127.0.0.1-only forward, how the remote directory is kept, links never followed, Edit as the only upload that replaces a file. §10.2 adds a limit (one private OpenSSH server), §10.3 drops "not in 0.8.8.7", and §11.2 lists the new suites. The Databases entry no longer says groups had a color in 0.8.8.7. `docs/PAPER-VALIDATION.md` adds a 0.8.8.8 table. Site: an "In development for 0.8.8.8" section on the own-desktop feature page, and the FAQ's latest-release and Terminal Files answers updated; `docs/PAPER.md` regenerated by `web/build.mjs`.
- **Files opens split archives as one archive.** Volumes made by byte-splitting (`name.zip.001`, `name.7z.001`,
  `name.tar.gz.001`… up to 255 of them) and Info-ZIP splits (`name.z01`, `name.z02` … `name.zip`) are recognised by
  name (`sdk/archivevol.js`, an archive kind in `sdk/filekinds.js`). Double-clicking any volume browses the whole set,
  and Extract Here, Extract N Items and Quick Preview work on it, into a folder named after the set (`name`). Files
  finds the sibling volumes in order; if one is missing it names it ("a part of the split archive is missing", in the
  six languages) instead of failing halfway. lord-server validates and opens every volume like a single archive and
  hands lord-doc one fd per volume (`lord.doc.arcList` and `arcExtract` take a path or the array of volumes; the
  request carries `"vols"` with their slots, only `file` slots are accepted); lord-doc reads them as one archive
  through libarchive's own multi-volume support (read, seek and skip callbacks on those fds). No new syscall, path
  or sandbox rule. Tested with split zips of both styles and a split 7z (its index sits at the end, so the reader
  seeks across volumes): `tests/doc_evil.sh` (new `vlist`/`vextract` commands in `build/doc-test`) and
  `tests/archive_vol_test.mjs` (names, order, holes, a lone `.001`, the 255-volume cap). Split RAR sets
  (`.part1.rar`) are not recognised yet: there was no sample to test them with. (GitHub #103)
- **Files' column view: each column can be resized.** Dragging a column's divider widens or narrows it (140 to 600
  px), and a double click on the divider fits it to its longest name, tags included. The width is kept per folder
  in Files' settings (`files.colWidths`, the 200 most recent folders), and the view shows as many of the last
  folders as fit next to the preview instead of always three. The divider reuses the list header's drag handling
  and the view stays laid out left to right in every language. Width logic in `apps/files/colview.js`, tested in
  `tests/files_colview_test.mjs`. (GitHub #99)

### Changed

- **The Dock can be much smaller: icons now go down to 20 px (the minimum was 36).** On a small high-density screen
  the smallest Dock still took a large share of the height. Settings → Desktop & Dock → Size now goes from 20 to
  80 px; the magnified size still starts at the icon size and goes up to 128. The limits live in one place,
  `dockSizes()` and `DOCK_SIZE_MIN`/`DOCK_SIZE_MAX`/`DOCK_MAGNIFY_MAX` in `sdk/dockmodel.js`, which both
  `dockPrefs()` and the Settings sliders use. At small sizes the unread badge on a web app's icon shrinks with the
  icon (`dockBadgeMetrics()`: 12 to 18 px high, never most of the icon) and the bar's rounded corners never exceed
  half its thickness; the running and attention dots, the separators, the Trash, the app launcher icon, the
  tooltip and the drop areas already scale with the icon. Only Lord Flow has a Dock; Lord Classic's taskbar is
  unchanged. A stored size only became valid, so nothing migrates. Tests: `server/tests/dock_model_test.mjs` (the
  clamp, junk values, the old minimum, the badge sizes); docs/DOCK.md (GitHub #128)
- **The Cleaner panel by the clock has one way into the app.** It used to end with three: the button beside the
  last scan, an "Open Cleaner" text and a "Settings" text. Now only the button stays: with a last scan that found
  something it reads "Free up" and opens the cleanup; with no scan yet it reads "Open Cleaner" and opens the scan.
  Cleaner's settings are reached from inside the app. The choice is `cleanerPanelAction()` in
  `sdk/menubarmodel.js`, tested in `server/tests/menubar_model_test.mjs`; the unused `cleaner.panel.prefs` string is
  gone from every language; docs/CLEANER.md (GitHub #116)

### Changed

- **Website: private visit statistics from the CloudFront logs.** Cookies and statistics and the Privacy policy (en,
  es, pt; dated 2026-11-11) say that lordos.org counts visits from the CloudFront request logs it already receives, to
  know how the project grows: page views, distinct visitors (IP addresses), countries (worked out by CloudFront),
  referrers, the visitor's system and kind of device. Nothing is added to the site for it: no cookies, no analytics
  service, no script and no redirect; the download buttons still go straight to GitHub, whose counters stay the only
  download figures. CloudFront's standard (v2) logs go to a CloudWatch Logs group, kept 400 days (13 months), with 13
  fields only (time, IP, country, method, path, status, referrer, user agent, host, edge location, cache result, time
  taken, bytes). Three private CloudWatch dashboards read them with Logs Insights: LordOS-Visitas (summary, visits per
  hour, countries, systems, devices, pages, referrers, language, bots, install.sh, 404s, speed per country,
  CloudFront's own request and error metrics), LordOS-Cruces (country by language, system and device, hour of day,
  referrer by landing page) and LordOS-Historico (per day, week and month, systems per month). Page views exclude
  `/apt/`, the site's assets and bots; LordOS's requests to `lordos.org/apt` land in the same logs, which CloudFront
  can't split, are never counted, and the policy says so. `tools/web/stats.mjs` (`setup`, `dashboards`, `test`)
  recreates everything with the deploy AWS profile; `test` runs every query (23) over the last hour. Only the team
  sees the dashboards. The scripts that reach the AWS account (`deploy.sh`, `cdn-apt- behaviors.sh`, `apt-repo.sh`,
  `stats.mjs`) no longer carry its profile name, bucket or distribution id: they read them from a private file on the
  maintainer's machines, `~/.aws/.lordos-deploy-env`, through `tools/web/aws-env.sh` (parsed, never executed).
  `web/build.mjs` reads the size of JPEG and WebP images itself (as it already did for PNG), so the site also builds
  on Linux without `sips`, which exists only on the maintainer's other computer; checked against Pillow on all 149
  images of the site. Country rows show the name in Spanish, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric, from a
  CloudWatch Logs lookup table (`lordos_paises`, 250 rows) that `node tools/web/stats.mjs countries` builds from
  Debian's iso-codes; the table takes no quoted CSV fields, so the 15 names with a comma get their usual form, and
  `lookup` can't match a field with a hyphen, so `c-country` is copied to `alfa2` first. Referrers without a host read
  "(directo: sin origen)" or "(desde el mismo sitio)" instead of an empty row.

### Fixed

- X11 apps run as root (GParted through `pkexec gparted` or `sudo gparted` from the Terminal) couldn't open their
  window: "Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified" and "cannot open display: :0".
  Xwayland was started without an authorization file, and then lets in only its own uid, so root was refused
  even though pkexec and sudo pass `DISPLAY` on. lord-server now makes a random `MIT-MAGIC-COOKIE-1` for the session
  (16 bytes from `getrandom`), writes it as an Xauthority file in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/lord-xauth.<n>` (0600, created
  with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` under a temporary name, fsynced and renamed into place, with entries for the
  host name and `FamilyWild`), sets `XAUTHORITY` for the apps it starts and adds `-auth <file>` to Xwayland's fixed
  command line (the Xwayland launcher exception in `AGENTS.md`, amended with the maintainer's approval). Any client
  with the cookie connects, whatever its uid; pkexec (GParted's polkit action has `allow_gui`) and sudo keep
  `XAUTHORITY`. The file is written again with the same cookie if it is missing when Xwayland restarts, removed at
  logout, and if it can't be written Xwayland starts as before, without `-auth`. The cookie stays away from what must
  not use X: restricted Linux apps and isolated apps lose `XAUTHORITY` together with `DISPLAY` (`xauth_env_drop`), a
  restricted app's runtime folder is an empty one, `lord.fs` neither reads nor writes the file (`FSOPS_PF_XAUTH`), and
  lord-web's environment is a fixed list without it. New test `build/xauth-test` (file format, 0600, `O_EXCL`, links
  at either name never followed, both variables removed by both launchers) and cases in `fsops-test`;
  checked on VM 127: before, root's `xdpyinfo` was refused; after, `pkexec /usr/sbin/gparted` opened GParted as
  root on the desktop, root with the cookie connects and without it is refused, XTerm opened by LordOS carries
  `XAUTHORITY`, and through the real launcher a `no-files` or `no-mic` app gets neither variable nor the file in its
  runtime folder. Note: a client of the same user without the cookie is now refused as well (everything LordOS
  starts has `XAUTHORITY`). docs/WAYLAND.md and docs/PRIVACY.md (GitHub #107)
- Isolated apps (Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Reminders, Passwords): holding a key did nothing more than one press,
  so Backspace, Delete and the arrows had to be pressed again for every character. These apps run as Wayland clients
  (`lord-server --app`), and the compositor sends its clients only the press and the release of a key, with the rate
  and delay to repeat it themselves in `wl_keyboard.repeat_info` (30/s after 500 ms). The app client ignored that
  event, so no repeat ever reached the JS keymap, which already handles them. It now repeats the held key itself
  (`server/src/app/keyrepeat.h`, wired in `appclient.c`'s poll loop): after the delay, then at the rate, sent as the
  same value-2 key event an in-process app gets from the kernel. Modifiers don't repeat (new `kb_key_repeats` in
  `keyboard.c`, from the keymap); the key's release, another press, or the keyboard leaving or entering a window
  ends it; a rate of 0 turns it off; an app that stalls catches up with one repeat, not a burst. New
  `build/keyrepeat-test` in `make test`; `docs/PRIVACY.md` describes it. Arrows, Home/End and Ctrl+A already worked
  in these fields. (GitHub #130)
- Lord Flow: minimizing a window still played the shrink towards the Dock with Settings → Appearance → Reduce
  motion on, although that setting stops decorative animations. The minimize effect (`themes/default/index.jsx`
  `useMinimizing`) never read it; which windows start the effect is now decided in `themes/default/minimize.js`,
  where Reduce motion starts none, so the window goes at once, as in Lord Classic. Tested by
  `server/tests/minimize_model_test.mjs` (GitHub #112).
- Files: in the column view a tagged file showed no tag at all; only a folder's icon took the tag's tint. Each item
  now shows its tag dots right after the name, as the list view does, and they stay visible when a long name is cut
  short (`apps/files/views.jsx` `ColumnView`). Tested by `server/tests/files_colview_scene.mjs`, run through
  `menubar_test.mjs`, which now takes a scene as its argument (GitHub #99).
- **The built-in panel turns off when the lid is closed on an external display.** lord-server never
  looked at the lid: `display_plan` put every connected connector in the plan, so with the lid
  closed and a monitor connected the laptop panel stayed lit (`/sys/class/drm/*-eDP-1/enabled` read
  `enabled`, a laptop's logo stayed lit), kept part of the desktop and windows could sit on a panel
  nobody sees. lord-server now reads logind's `LidClosed` on the system bus (Properties.Get, then
  PropertiesChanged believed only from logind's own connection; new `hw/lid.c`, no grab and no
  polling, logind's own lid handling unchanged). While the lid is closed and another display is
  connected, the eDP, LVDS or DSI panel leaves the plan: its head is closed as on an unplug, its
  windows move to the other displays and the external display becomes the main one if the panel
  was. With only the panel connected it is kept (the only display is never turned off), and it comes
  back when the lid opens. Settings → Displays lists the panel as off because of the lid (new
  `lidClosed` in `lord.display.list()`, text in every language). New `build/lid-test` (28 checks:
  the logind side with the bus replaced, and the plan with the card replaced) (GitHub #97).
- A moment of noise on the screen between the console and the login screen and between the login screen and the
  desktop, on older graphics cards run by the `radeon` kernel driver. At each hand-off lord-sessiond keeps every lit
  display on a black frame of its own mode (added in 0.8.8.7 so DisplayPort monitors keep their signal), and that
  frame was a new dumb buffer put on the screen as it came: the code assumed it was zeroed, but `radeon` gives one
  in video memory with whatever was there last, so the "black" frame showed leftover pixels until the next session
  drew. The buffer is now mapped (`DRM_IOCTL_MODE_MAP_DUMB` + `mmap`) and cleared before it becomes a framebuffer;
  if it can't be mapped, that display is not blacked out and is turned off with the rest of the leaving session's
  framebuffers, as before 0.8.8.7 (`server/src/remote/blackfb.c`, used by `monitor.c`). New `blackfb-test`: a fake
  card (ioctl and mmap wrapped) whose new buffers are full of noise checks the whole buffer, pitch padding
  included, is black before `ADDFB`, and that a failed map, mmap or `ADDFB` leaves nothing behind. (GitHub #94)
- Wi-Fi: a saved network with a password could not be joined again after it was lost; only Forget and joining
  with the password again worked. A click on a saved network in Settings → Network → Wi-Fi sends the join without
  a password, and `net-wifi-connect` saved the network again with that empty password: its `.json` said `open`, its
  `.key` lost the password (or the derived key a first-run file leaves), and with wpa_supplicant running the network
  was reloaded with `key_mgmt NONE`, which never associates with a WPA network. A join without a password for a
  network saved with a key now joins it with the saved key and leaves its files as they are (`server/src/net/wifi.c`);
  a new password still replaces the saved one. A network an earlier version already overwrote can't be repaired by
  an update (the key is gone, and a real open network looks the same), so Settings now asks for the password when a
  network saved as open is secured in the scan, and joining with it saves it again. Checked on VM 127 with a
  simulated radio (`mac80211_hwsim`, a WPA2 access point from wpa_supplicant in AP mode) through `net-test act`:
  joined with the password, disconnected, joined again with no password; the build before saved it as `open` and
  stayed `SCANNING`, this one reached `COMPLETED` with the key kept. New `net-test wifi-saved`. (GitHub #124)
- Files and Settings → Default Apps: VLC was missing from Open With for common video files (MP4, Matroska, WebM,
  QuickTime) and couldn't be chosen as the video app. The launcher read each `.desktop` line into a 2 KB buffer and kept
  `MimeType` in 1 KB, and VLC's `MimeType` line is 2.4 KB: only its first 1023 bytes were kept (`audio/mpeg` and
  `video/x-msvideo` survived, `video/mp4` did not), and the rest of an over-long line was read as a line of its own.
  `.desktop` lines are now read whole (`getline`), `MimeType` holds 8 KB, and a list longer than that keeps only its
  whole types, so a cut type never matches another. `tests/defaults_test.c` covers a type after 2 KB of `MimeType`, a
  long line whose tail looks like a key, and a list longer than the field; checked against this machine's real VLC
  3.0 `.desktop`: before, `video/mp4` had no app; now VLC is the declared app for MP4, Matroska, WebM and QuickTime.
  Dragging a file from Files onto a Linux app's window is new in this version (Added, Wayland drag and drop)
  (GitHub #123).
- Linux apps: a Qt app whose Qt Wayland platform plugin isn't installed (Debian's `qtwayland5` or `qt6-wayland`, which
  no Qt app depends on) didn't open at all: MusicBrainz Picard from the Store stopped at start with "Could not find the
  Qt platform plugin "wayland"". The session set `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland`, which leaves Qt no other platform. It now
  sets `wayland;xcb` (Qt tries them in order), as GTK already got `wayland,x11`: Qt apps still open on Wayland, and
  those without the plugin open through Xwayland. The toolkit variables moved to `server/src/wl/toolkitenv.h`, checked
  by the new `tests/toolkitenv_test.c`. Checked on VM 127 with Picard (Qt 5) and Qt 5's Wayland plugins hidden in a
  private mount namespace: `wayland` alone aborted with the reporter's message, `wayland;xcb` opened Picard's window
  through Xwayland, and with the plugins present Qt still chose Wayland (GitHub #96).
- Text Editor: the end of a long line was drawn under the vertical scroll bar, and typing at the end of a line
  could leave the caret there. The bar now has its own column at the right edge, painted with the editor's
  background, and the view scrolls sideways so the caret stays left of that column. Without the bar (a file that
  fits) the text keeps the full width. A regression case is in `editor_scrollbar_test.mjs`. (GitHub #109)

- Memory figures: the Control Center worked out memory in use as total minus the kernel's "available" figure, which
  also counts its own reserve, so it read 1.9 GB where Monitor, About and Settings → General read 1.7 GB at the same
  moment. Every place now takes the one figure the server reports (in use, without the page cache or the reserve;
  `sdk/memfigure.js`). The Cleaner panel by the clock showed memory "available" and disk "free" with no total; both
  cards now read "used of total", like the bars under them and the rest of the system. Monitor → Memory keeps its
  breakdown (in use, cache and free add up to the total). New test `mem_figure_test.mjs`. (GitHub #118)
- Notes: there was no way to copy or paste except the keys, which only work while a note is being edited; the menu
  bar had no Edit menu, the Format menu's rows were always off and a right click in the editor offered only Speech.
  Notes now has an Edit menu (Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All) and its Format rows work while editing; each
  row sends the editor's own key, so it does exactly what the key does (`apps/notes/editmenu.js`). From the reading
  view, Paste and Select All open the editor first (pasting at the end of the note, or selecting all of it to copy).
  A right click in the editor offers Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All before Speech, and on a desktop note it no
  longer drops the note back to reading while the menu is open. Ctrl/⌘+Shift+C copied instead of making a code
  block as its Format row says; it now makes the code block. Test: `notes-editor-scene` (GitHub #117).
- X11 apps: pasting text copied in LordOS, a Wayland app or a web app into an X11 app whose clipboard library
  opens its own X connection (Rust apps using arboard) said "Clipboard empty". The window manager
  answered a paste request only from a window of the focused window's X client, and that library asks from a helper
  window on a second connection. It now also answers when the X server's X-Resource extension ties the requestor's
  client and the focused window's client to the same process (the pid Xwayland reads from the socket, never a
  property the client sets), checked again when the answer comes back: the focus must not have moved, and the
  selection must still be LordOS's and not a secret. Any other requestor, a client without a known pid, or a server
  without X-Resource is still refused, so only the app with the keyboard gets the clipboard (`x11_same_process`,
  `build/xwm-test`; docs/WAYLAND.md "Clipboard and primary selection", docs/PRIVACY.md "X11 apps") (GitHub #125).
- **Files: copying or moving many items at once copies all of them.** lord-server runs at most 8 copy or move jobs
  at a time and refused one more with "Too many copies in progress", and Files started one job per selected item with
  nothing to hold the rest: a paste, a drop or a Duplicate of more than 8 items copied the first 8 and the others failed
  at once (moves on the same disk too, since a finished job keeps its slot until Files reads it). The items past the
  free slots now wait in Files and start, in the order chosen, as the running ones finish; moves on the same disk all
  go in one pass. The status bar says how many more are left next to the one in progress, and its ✕ stops that copy and
  drops the ones still waiting. An item that fails for its own reason (the name was taken meanwhile, a protected
  folder) is reported and the rest go on. Suite `files-jobqueue-test` (GitHub #104).

- **Files: in Home, and in the column view, Move to Trash, Cut, Paste and New Folder work, and a file picked in a
  deeper column can be copied.** Two causes. Files greys out what changes a folder when the folder is read-only, and the
  home folder's own entry reads as read-only (its parent is outside what LordOS writes), so in Home those actions were
  disabled and a drop on the Dock's Trash did nothing; what is inside the home folder now counts as writable, as the
  file chooser already did. Also the selection was looked up only among the first column's items, so with Pictures →
  Screenshots open a file picked in the last column was selected on screen but ⌘C copied nothing and the menus had
  nothing to act on. Every column's items now count. Shift + click selects a range inside the clicked column, and
  Duplicate, Compress and New Folder with Selection put what they make next to the item, not in the first column's
  folder. Suite `files-colview-test` (GitHub #100).
- Text fields on a display at 125 % or 175 %: the caret drifted away from the text as you typed, a few pixels more with
  every character, in Notes, Text Editor and the text boxes of Settings. Glyphs are drawn at the display's size
  rounded to half a pixel (13 px text at 125 % is 16.25 px and draws at 16.5), and the pen moved by those rounded advances,
  while the caret and the line breaks use the logical ones. The pen now moves by the logical advance times the scale,
  so text, caret and selection line up at every scale; 100 %, 150 % and 200 % were already exact. `engine-test`
  checks the caret edge against the drawn ink at 125 % and 175 % (GitHub #110).
- Lord Classic's taskbar: with many pinned apps the row of app buttons grew past its room, ran over the tray
  (quick settings, status items, the clock) and, centered, kept growing toward both edges of the display. The
  taskbar now fits its row to the room left by the tray, which it measures from the last frame: the app buttons get
  smaller first (down to 30 px from 40, with a smaller icon), then the apps that still don't fit go into a "more
  apps" button at the end of the row, whose menu lists them and opens them like a click on their button. A centered
  row stays in the middle of the display while there is room and moves toward the start once the tray would be in
  its way. ❖1 to ❖9 still count every app, also those in the menu. Folders of apps on the bar were not added.
  (GitHub #111)
- Files → Network: signing in to a desktop computer's shared folders said the password was refused although it
  was right and the command-line SMB client connected with it. `lord-lan` asked for SMB signing to be enabled but not
  required, and in dialects 2.0.2 and 2.1 a server signs its final session setup answer only when the session
  requires signing (MS-SMB2 3.3.5.5.3); a desktop system that doesn't require signing (the default on many) sent
  that answer unsigned, and `lord-lan` takes an unsigned answer as "not the server you signed in to". The
  NEGOTIATE and both SESSION_SETUP requests of the sign-in now mark signing as required (`smb_negotiate_signed`,
  `smb_session_setup_signed` in `lan/lanparse.c`), so the server must sign that answer. Nothing is weakened: the
  answer must still carry a valid signature with the session key, a wrong password is still refused, and the
  anonymous pass is unchanged. `build/lan-test` checks the security mode of each request. On VM 127, `build/lan-list`
  listed the shares of a test server with its signing set to default, disabled and mandatory, refused a wrong
  password in each, listed through a proxy that leaves the answer unsigned when the client doesn't require signing
  (the build before this fix said "denied" there) and was still refused through one that always leaves it unsigned.
  Not yet tried against the reporter's kind of server (GitHub #101).

- Notes and Mail's message editor at 100 %: the caret and the selection drifted to the right of the text, 0.6 px more
  with every character (20 px at the end of a 33-character line with 14 px text). Both editors measure each character
  once with `lord.measureText`, which rounds a width up to a whole pixel, so an 8.4 px JetBrains Mono character
  counted as 9. Each character is now measured as 64 copies and divided, which keeps the rounding under 0.02 px.

- Notification banners: a long message (a whole chat paragraph from a web app) made the banner as tall as the
  screen. Its text is now cut to 4 lines with an ellipsis, and up to 12 while the pointer is on the banner; the title
  to 2 lines. Notification Center already showed 3.

- Web apps: pasting a file copied in Files (or another file manager) pasted its path as text, so a chat page could not
  send it; and any text past ASCII pasted by WebKit came out garbled (a path in `Imágenes` as `ImÃ¡genes`). WebKit
  2.48's pasteboard for WPE holds text only, and it reads its stored bytes back as Latin-1 while it writes them as
  UTF-8 (`PlatformPasteboardLibWPE.cpp`, `readString`). Now, at the person's own paste (Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert, the
  Edit menu's or the context menu's Paste; never at any other moment), lord-web looks at the session's selection
  first: when it offers `text/uri-list` (or `x-special/gnome-copied-files`), lord-web reads the list then (at most
  1 MB), opens its local files with exactly the drop's checks and limits (`file://` without a host, the person's
  places, no hidden folder or file, no link on the resolved path, a regular file, at most 64 MB each and 20 files)
  and dispatches a `paste` event on the focused element whose `DataTransfer` holds them as `File`s (`types`
  `["Files"]`, no text); when every file is refused it pastes the selection's text as before (the list itself when the
  selection has no text). A text that isn't plain ASCII is pasted by lord-web too: a `paste` event with it as
  `text/plain`, and when no listener takes it the text is inserted at the caret (WebKit's `InsertText`); ASCII text is
  still WebKit's own paste. The session's text is read as `text/plain;charset=utf-8`, then `UTF8_STRING`, then
  `text/plain` (UTF-8 when it is valid, else converted from Latin-1), then `STRING` (Latin-1); `TEXT` is never read,
  and a UTF-8 type that isn't valid UTF-8 is refused. A selection with no text (only a file list or an image) now
  empties WebKit's pasteboard, so an older text is never pasted in its place. A copy from an isolated LordOS app or a
  sandboxed (Flatpak) client reaches lord-web without its file lists: lord-server leaves `text/uri-list` and the
  other file-list types out of that selection's offer to a lord-web client and refuses them at `receive`
  (`OfferRef.nofiles`, the same rule as for drags), so it pastes as text only. The log says `paste: N files from the
  clipboard accepted[; others refused: <reason>]`, `paste: no file from the clipboard accepted (...); pasting its
  text`, `paste: text (N bytes, <type>[; WebKit's own paste])` and `paste dispatched (...)`, sizes, types and reasons
  only. Tests: `build/webapp-test` (the text type order, UTF-8 checks, Latin-1 conversion and the `Imágenes` case,
  which text WebKit's own paste reads right, gnome and uri lists, a pasted list's files through the drop's checks).
  Checked on VM 127 (2026-11-11): `hacker.jpg` copied in Files from `~/Imágenes` and pasted with Ctrl+V, and with
  the Edit menu's Paste, into a test page arrived as `hacker.jpg image/jpeg 6753` (`types` `["Files"]`, the page
  showed the picture); a text `/home/alex/Imágenes/hacker.jpg` pasted into a text area arrived as it is (the build
  before pasted `/home/alex/ImÃ¡genes/hacker.jpg`), and `Fotos en ~/Imágenes: café, niño, €` from the context
  menu's Paste into an editable box too; a list naming a hidden file was refused and its text pasted instead.
- Web apps: copying from a page that handles the copy itself put nothing on the session's clipboard (copying
  messages from a chat, then pasting in another app, pasted what was there before). Such a page handles the `copy`
  or `cut` event, writes its own text into the event's `clipboardData` (messages with their sender and time, emoji
  pictures as text) and prevents the default, or runs `document.execCommand('copy')` with such a listener from its
  own Copy item. WebKit 2.48 for WPE throws that data away: WebCore commits it through
  `Pasteboard::writeCustomData`, which is empty in `PasteboardLibWPE.cpp`. lord-web's isolated script now reads the
  event's data after the page's listeners (a listener of its own on each node of the event's path, both phases, so
  a page that stops the propagation is seen too) and, when the page prevented the default and left text, posts the
  text and its HTML; lord-web offers both to the session only within 5 s of the person's own key, click or touch in
  the window, at most 16 MB each, trusted events only, and writes the text into WebKit's pasteboard so pasting back
  into the page works. Ctrl+C with the focus in a message box but the selection on the messages now copies too
  (decided by where the selection is). Checked on VM 127 with a test page that imitates this: a two-message
  selection reached `wl-paste` as `[10:01] Ana: ... 😀 ?` and `[10:02] Bruno: ...` lines (with `text/html`), and its
  Copy button (`execCommand` plus a listener that stops the propagation) as its own text; the build before left the
  clipboard as it was.
- Web apps: dropping a file on a chat page to send it did nothing. Such a page
  draws its drop area only after `dragenter` (a render a frame later) and has its only `drop` listener there;
  lord-web sent `dragenter`, `dragover` and `drop` together at the drop, so the drop landed on the element under an
  area that didn't exist yet. lord-web now sends `dragenter`, `dragover` and `dragleave` to the page while the drag
  moves over the window (one call at a time, the latest position kept; `types` `["Files"]` and no data, as a
  browser does before the drop), `dragleave` when the drag leaves or its drop can't be handed over, and at the drop
  waits two frames (at most 150 ms), finds the element at the drop point again and sends `dragover` and `drop`
  there. Checked on VM 127 with a page whose drop area appears a frame after `dragenter`: a JPEG and a text file
  from Files arrived (`foto.jpg (6753 B, image/jpeg)`), and the area went away when the drag left without dropping;
  the build before left the area up and the page got no file.
- Web apps: lord-web's log now says what happened to copies and drops, sizes, types and reasons only, never their
  contents, at most 20 lines in 10 s: `page copy offered (N bytes, editing command|copy event|clipboard API)`,
  `page copy refused (...)`, `drag over the page (files, first target DIV)`, `drop received (text/uri-list, N lines,
  M local files accepted)`, `drop refused: <reason>`, `drop dispatched (N files, target DIV, a listener took it)`.
- Web apps: dragging the mouse across text selected nothing (a message couldn't be selected to copy it). WPE WebKit
  2.48 is built without drag support, which in WebCore also holds selecting by dragging; lord-web now extends the
  page's own selection while the left button is held (a script in an isolated world: `caretRangeFromPoint` for text
  and editable content, the character under the pointer measured with the field's font inside a text field).
  Double click (word), triple click (paragraph) and Shift+click were already WebKit's and still are. A motion also
  names the button held, so a page's own drag code sees it.
- Web apps: Ctrl+C (and Ctrl+Insert, Ctrl+A) did nothing on text the page shows, outside a text field: WPE's key
  bindings run only where the page can be edited. lord-web now runs Copy or Select All for those keys when the page
  didn't take them itself.
- Web apps: pasting text copied in another app did nothing, and sometimes closed the app. The text was written to
  WebKit's pasteboard with strings that weren't zeroed first, and libwpe keeps a string that already holds data, so
  stack garbage went in instead (or a crash, seen on VM 127).
- Web apps: after one right click in a page that doesn't handle it, the window took no more clicks, drags or wheel
  until it was restarted: WPE 2.48 waits forever for a menu its embedder is never asked for. The right click's
  default is now always prevented and LordOS's own menu shown instead (above).
- Web apps: files dropped on a page and images pasted into it never arrived ("Invalid parameter types"): WebKit 2.48
  takes no arrays as a called function's arguments, so the files' list now goes to the page as one JSON text.
- Web apps said their notifications were off after every start (a messaging web app showed "notifications are
  disabled, turn on") although LordOS allowed them: WebKit wasn't told the app's choice, so each new web process
  started at "default". lord-web now hands WebKit the allowed or denied origin before the page loads
  (`webkit_web_context_initialize_notification_permissions`); "ask" still lets the page ask.
- Settings → Web apps showed "Data: none yet" for a profile added during the visit even after it was in use. Its size is
  now measured again when a profile is added or starts, and every 30 s.
- The Dock menu's "New window: <profile>" showed a check mark as if it were a selected option, and the second profile's
  window showed only the page title.
- **A browser's profile picker no longer flickers between dark and light while Notes is open.** Every `ThemeProvider`
  told Linux apps (the Settings portal, `lord.portal.set`) and isolated apps (`lord.broker.publish('theme')`) its
  colors, not only the theme's. Notes draws its paper with a nested light provider, so each render of a note sent light
  mode and each render of the desktop sent dark mode back: the portal's `color-scheme` and GTK theme went back and forth
  (56 `SettingChanged` signals in 20 seconds on VM 127), and a window that follows the system's mode, such as the
  profile picker of a browser whose profiles each chose a theme, flickered with it. Only the outermost provider, the
  theme's, speaks for the desktop now; a nested one colors its own subtree. It showed only now because the session's
  apps only now have a session bus and `lord.portal.set` only now reaches the portal. Checked on VM 127 in an isolated
  session with a browser's profile picker over Notes: light frames while typing in a note before, none and no signal
  after. Test: `tests/theme_portal_scene.mjs` (through `tests/textfield_menu_test.mjs`).
- **Notifications from Chromium-based browsers are LordOS banners, and their own popups no longer take the keyboard.**
  The session started without `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, and those browsers don't look for `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`
  themselves: they had no session bus at all, so no notification service (they drew their own windows), no tray icon and
  no portals. lord-server now sets it for the apps the session starts when it is unset and the socket is the user's
  (`dbus_session_export`). A browser's own notification popup (a nameless, notification-sized toplevel, at most 480x300)
  floats in the top corner without the keyboard instead of opening in the middle with it. Checked on VM 127 with a
  browser. Tests: `build/notifyd-test`, `tests/desktop_model_test.mjs`.
- **Opening the Store's web apps no longer takes the whole desktop down.** The desktop's JavaScript engine has no
  `TextEncoder` or `TextDecoder`; the web apps model, Remote Desk's `.rdp` reader and the isolated apps' file dialog used
  them. `sdk/utf8.js` does UTF-8 by hand and `tests/utf8_test.mjs` keeps those globals out of desktop code.
- **Linux apps follow LordOS's light or dark mode, accent and title-bar buttons through the Settings portal again.** Since 0.8.8, `lord.portal` was made twice. The FileChooser's functions (`js_hw.c`) replaced the object that held `lord.portal.set` (`js_wm.c`). The theme's call then failed silently, and the portal kept answering dark mode, blue and the default buttons. The FileChooser's functions now go on the same object. Found while adding the global shortcuts.
- **The permission prompt wraps a long title whole.** Its title, the app line and the note took their own width instead of the box's, so a long title was cut (`sdk/privacy.js`).
- **Security fixes from the reviews of this work (two automated security scans of the branch and the review of each feature).** None of them is in a release: each was found and fixed before 0.8.8.8.
  - **Scan of 2026-11-10** (three LOW findings, fixed in one commit):
    - A container that controls its own root could write a `.flatpak-info` and pose as any Flatpak app for the shortcuts permission. A Flatpak identity now also needs Flatpak's own record of that instance outside the sandbox (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/.flatpak/<instance>/info`, owned by the user), and the client must be in the pid namespace of that instance's `bwrapinfo.json` child. New cases in `build/kbinhibit-test`.
    - The prompt slot counter (`ksim_inhibit`) was a `static int` that could go negative after about 2^31 requests and write out of bounds. It is now unsigned and kept in range.
    - `dnd_tick` in `xwm.c` kept a saved next pointer across a flush that could free every pull, a use after free. The walk now starts again from the head after each pull ends.
  - **Scan of 2026-11-11** (one MEDIUM finding): `lord-web` could free a DmaBuf while its `zwp_linux_buffer_params_v1.create` was still unanswered. The reply then wrote to freed memory and freed it again, in the process outside WebKit's sandbox, and a compromised renderer could trigger it. A `pending` flag now holds the buffer until `created` or `failed` answers. A second candidate, about the activation token sent to a predictable bus name, was refuted 0 to 3.
  - **SVG icons.** The element and nesting limits used to come from a separate scan. They now come from a dry run of nanosvg's own tokenizer, so quotes, comments, CDATA, `<?` and `<!` can't hide markup from them.
  - **XDND.** An X drag's data is read only from the X server's own `SelectionNotify`, never a `SendEvent` copy. Each read happens only while `XdndSelection`'s owner window and client pid are still those of `XdndEnter`.
  - **ScreenCast.** A share holds each node by id and a serial that is never reused, and ends when that node goes. The chooser names only a verified app. An unknown sender is refused while any app with "no screen capture" runs.
  - **Shortcuts.** The shortcuts permission goes by the checked identity (Flatpak id or resolved program), not the app_id a client sets.
  - **Web apps.** The probe never follows `https` to `http`, or a public address to a local one. It resolves names itself, treats LAN names, single labels and private addresses as local, and checks every hop without caching. Permissions are only for the app's own pages: outside its scope, or for another origin, a request is denied and never asked. Under `lord-sessiond`, `lord-web` gets `LORDOS_SESSIOND=1`, so it never runs without its scope.
  - Test results after the fixes: the suites passed, 139 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
- **A paste into the Terminal can no longer end bracketed paste early and run a command.** `term_paste` removed the
  end marker `ESC[201~` in one pass, so text such as `ESC[201` `ESC[201~` `~` rebuilt it: with middle-click paste
  taking the primary selection, which any app or a selected web page fills, the shell ran what followed without
  Enter. Every control character but tab and the line ends is now dropped from a paste, as xterm and VTE do
  (`server/src/term/pastefilter.c`, `build/pastefilter-test`). Found by Claude Security before release.
- **Now Playing titles that don't fit end in "…".** The tile cut a long title mid-word.
- **The live ISO's boot menu no longer reads "{live}".** GRUB draws the 16 px Inter bitmap without smoothing, and its
  3-pixel "(" looked like "{" in every entry. The entries now use " · " ("LordOS 0.8.8.8 · live", "Install automatically ·
  lordos-auto.conf: erases the disk it names"), in `tools/iso/build.sh`, `docs/ISO.md` and `docs/UNATTENDED.md`.
- **Sidebar labels that don't fit end in "…".** `SidebarItem` cut long labels mid-word ("Teclado y métodos de entra" in
  Help in Spanish); it now ends them with an ellipsis.
- **The unattended install's `ssh_key` and `after = poweroff` are tested.** On VM 127, an install with both powered off when
  done, and with Settings → Sharing → Remote login turned on, `ssh` with the file's key logged in, with the host key
  fingerprint Settings shows (`docs/UNATTENDED.md`, `docs/VM-SETUP.md`).
- **Terminal: Profiles → a profile's item is its name.** It read "New Tab: name" in every item of the submenus.
- **Terminal: a new tab goes last.** It was placed right after the tab in front, in the middle of the others.
- **Terminal: "Choose Location…" in Settings → Config File shows the whole file chooser.** It was drawn inside the
  section's box, with no room for the folder list; it now covers the Settings window, as Import does.
- **Linux apps: `xdg_activation_v1`, so a link opened from LordOS raises the browser that is already open, and a window that asks for no reason never takes the focus.** The compositor now offers `xdg_activation_v1` v1 (`server/src/wl/wl.c`), generated from `staging/xdg-activation/xdg-activation-v1.xml` like the other protocols. Tokens are kept in a new module with no Wayland types, `server/src/wl/xdgact.c`: 32 random hex characters, single use, 60 s for tokens LordOS issues and at most 10 s for tokens an app asks for, 32 kept at once (a new one replaces the oldest). Every launch through `apps.c` (the launcher, Open With, `launchUri`, desktop actions, so the whole `lord.apps.launch*` family) puts a token in `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` of the child. A browser that is already running gets the link from the new process together with the token, and its window comes forward, switching to its desktop if needed. A click on a notification's button now sends the Desktop Notifications `ActivationToken` signal before `ActionInvoked` (`server/src/hw/notifyd.c`). An app's own `get_activation_token` … `commit` is granted only when that client has the keyboard, or when its `set_serial` is a pointer button, key or keyboard enter that the compositor sent to the same client in the last 10 s (input serials are recorded through `input_serial()`, and a client's serials are dropped when it disconnects). An app's outstanding tokens are revoked as soon as the keyboard leaves it and when it disconnects (`xact_focus_moved`, `xact_client_gone`), as KWin and Mutter do, so a token taken while in front can't be kept to steal the focus later; LordOS's own launch tokens are not. `activate` with a granted token raises and focuses the window (a popup or subsurface counts as its toplevel). An ungranted, expired, unknown or reused token only marks the window as wanting attention: a new `attention` flag on the window (`wm.setAttention`, cleared whenever the window comes to the front, `sdk/windows.js`, `sdk/wayland.js`), a dock entry `attention` (`sdk/dock.js`), a larger accent dot under the Dock icon in Lord Flow and a long accent bar on the taskbar button in Lord Classic. A click on that icon brings the waiting window first. The decision on the theme side is `activationOutcome` in `sdk/desktopmodel.js`. Tests: new `build/xdgact-test` (`server/tests/xdgact_test.c`, in `make test`: format, single use, expiry, ungranted tokens, a full table, input serials per client and their expiry), and new cases in `tests/desktop_model_test.mjs`. Documented in `docs/WAYLAND.md` (protocol table, the launcher, and a new "Activation" section).
- **Linux apps' dialogs stay with their window: xdg-foreign-v2 and xdg-dialog-v1.** lord-server now offers `zxdg_exporter_v2`/`zxdg_importer_v2` and `xdg_wm_dialog_v1`. It keeps each toplevel's owner, set by `xdg_toplevel.set_parent` (until now only a "dialog" flag) or by another process with `zxdg_imported_v2.set_parent_of`, plus the modal flag, and tells JS in `map` (`parent`, `modal`) and in a new `parent` event. `sdk/dialogmodel.js` (`overParent`, `followParents`) opens a dialog centered over its parent, inside that display's work area and on the parent's desktop. The dialog moves with the parent (once the parent's drag ends), is minimized, restored and moved to another desktop with it, and a modal dialog is kept right above its parent. In `wl.c`, `modal_over` stops the parent getting presses and wheel events while a modal dialog is up (releases still go through), and the parent's keyboard goes to the dialog. A window that closes hands its dialogs to its own parent, and a parent that would make a loop is ignored. Each export gets its own handle: 128 random bits from `getrandom`, in hex. A handle stops working when its export or its surface goes away; every import of it is sent `destroyed`, and an unknown handle gets `destroyed` straight away. The file chooser portal (`server/src/ui/portal.c`) now reads `parent_window` "wayland:<handle>" through the new `wl_foreign_surface()`, and `PortalFilePrompt` (`sdk/filepicker.jsx`) draws the dialog over that window instead of in the middle of the screen. Tests: `server/tests/dialog_model_test.mjs` (22 checks, in `tests/run_suites.sh`) and `build/dialog-client` (`tests/dialog_client.c`, 12 checks over two connections, passing against a headless lord-server). Docs: `docs/WAYLAND.md` (protocol table and a new "Dialogs" section).
  A wl_surface destroyed before its xdg_toplevel no longer leaves the toplevel holding the freed window: `surface_gone`
  clears the toplevel's, popup's and xdg_surface's link to it, `set_parent` takes only a live toplevel, and an
  xdg_surface whose surface is gone is refused (a use-after-free a client could reach through `set_parent` and
  `get_xdg_dialog`, found by Claude Security before release; a case in `tests/dialog_client.c`).
  A second xdg_surface for the same wl_surface, a second toplevel or popup for the same xdg_surface, and a second
  xdg-decoration for the same toplevel are now protocol errors (as the protocols say), so no extra object is left
  pointing at a freed window; a second KDE decoration object detaches the first. The "gone" handlers clear a link
  only when it is their own object. Two more cases in `tests/dialog_client.c` (18 checks).
- **Portals: OpenURI and Inhibit, and `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver`, served by lord-server.** `server/src/ui/portal.c`, which already served Settings and FileChooser without xdg-desktop-portal, now serves `org.freedesktop.portal.OpenURI` (version 3). `OpenURI` sends http and https to the default browser, and a `file://` address is handled like a file. `OpenFile` and `OpenDirectory` get the file as an fd. lord-server never reads or writes through that fd and only takes its name, which must still lead to the same file (same device and inode). The file must be inside the home folder or the user's disks and outside `fsops_protected`, and opening never takes an executable or a `.desktop` file (`NotAllowed`). The shell opens the request the way LordOS opens everything else (`sdk/sysopen.js`: our apps, the default app for the type, Files on the folder with the file selected). If the app that asks is not the one with the keyboard, the person is asked first, with the host or the file name in front. lord-server gets the caller's pid from the bus (`GetConnectionUnixProcessID`) and checks it against the focused Wayland client (new `wl_focus_pid()`) or the same app scope. The request answers with `Request.Response`. `org.freedesktop.portal.Inhibit` (version 1) and the `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` bus name (`Inhibit`/`UnInhibit` with a cookie, `GetActive`, on `/ScreenSaver` and `/org/freedesktop/ScreenSaver`) take idle and suspend holds. While a hold is on it counts as the compositor's idle inhibition next to `wl_idle_inhibited()` (`portal_inhibited()` in `main.c`), which keeps the screen-off, lock and sleep timers from running. A hold ends with `Request.Close` or `UnInhibit`, and when the caller's connection leaves the bus (`NameOwnerChanged`), which also drops that app's pending opens and file dialogs. Logout and user-switch flags are accepted and do nothing. Limits: 8 open requests at a time, 64 holds (8 per app). The bus connection now accepts fds (`dbus_open_fds`). The new shell call is `lord.portal.opened(id, code)` (`server/src/ui/js_hw.c`), and the question is `<PortalOpenPrompt />` (`sdk/hardware.jsx`, system layer), with new `shell.portalOpen.*` keys in all six languages. The pure decision logic (web addresses, files, when to ask) is in `sdk/portalopenmodel.js` and tested by `server/tests/portal_open_model_test.mjs` (25 checks, in `tests/run_suites.sh`). Web addresses go through one strict grammar in JS and in C (`portal_web_host`, `server/src/ui/portalcheck.c`): http or https only, printable ASCII only (an international name as its xn-- form), no backslash, no user part, no `%` in the host, a plain dotted IPv4 or a valid bracketed IPv6, so the host shown is the host opened. A file is checked again right before it opens (`lord.portal.still`: the same path, device, inode and type, and the same rules), refused if it was swapped. `tests/portal_check_test.c` (100 checks). No new root action, helper, library, broker message or permission. ScreenCast and Screenshot are still not offered. docs/FLATPAK.md, "Portals", now has a table of every portal interface and its status; docs/WAYLAND.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md are updated.
- **Notes, Photos, Player and PDF Viewer take files dragged from Files.** This uses the same onFilesDrop/onFilesOver mechanism as the Terminal and the Text Editor. While the drag is over the window, a dashed accent outline is drawn last, above the panes. It says what letting go will do, and a second line says how many dropped items the app will not use. If the app can use none of them, the outline says so. Notes copies the files into the open note, or into a new note when none is open: PNG and JPEG files become images and every other file becomes an attachment, as the ⊕ menu does. Folders are left out. Photos opens a single image together with the other images in its folder, as Open With does. Several images become the viewer's list. When only folders are dropped, the library shows the first one. Player plays the dropped music and videos right away, and a folder adds all of its music and videos in name order (`mediaIn` in `apps/player/library.js`). With ⌥ held, they go to the end of the queue instead, and the hint says so. PDF Viewer opens the first PDF in its window and each of the others in a new window. The shared pieces are new in the SDK: `useFilesDrop` and `FilesDropHint` in `sdk/components.jsx`, and a pure module, `sdk/filedrop.js` (`sortDrop`, `dropCount`, `dropSorter`). The pure module sorts the dropped paths into files the app takes, folders and skipped items. It sorts each drag only once, and it does not stat paths on network mounts. New test: `server/tests/filedrop_test.mjs` (18 cases), registered in `server/tests/run_suites.sh`. New `drop.*` keys are in the notes, photos, player and pdf locale files in all six languages.
- **Text fields can undo and redo, have a right-click menu and select a line on a triple click.** `TextInput` and `TextArea` (`sdk/components.jsx`) keep a history of `{ value, pos, anchor }` states in `sdk/textfieldmodel.js`. The new functions are `newHistory`, `record`, `undo`, `redo`, `canUndo`, `canRedo` and `historyKey`, and the history keeps the last 200 steps. Ctrl/⌘+Z undoes, and Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes. Characters typed in a row are one step until a one-second pause, the start of a new word or a caret moved elsewhere. Single-character Backspace and Delete presses join in the same way. A paste, a cut, a deleted selection, a word deleted with Ctrl or ⌥, and a value changed from outside are each a step of their own, and undoing one brings back the selection it removed. Password fields keep no history at all: Undo and Redo do nothing there and are disabled in their menu, and a field's history is dropped when it turns into a password field or back (`historyFor`). A right click opens Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete and Select All (the SDK `ContextMenu` in an `Overlay`, labels in `shell.textMenu.*` in all six languages). Each item sends the field's own key. Cut and Copy are disabled without a selection and in password fields. The menu keeps the field focused (`keepFocus`), stays on the display (or, in an isolated app, inside the window), and takes the right click from any menu of the view the field sits in. A right or middle click no longer moves the caret or drops the selection. `runtime/events.js` now counts clicks: `onClick` and `onDoubleClick` carry `detail` (1, 2, 3, and a fourth click starts over), and `onDoubleClick` still fires once, on the second click. A triple click selects the whole value of a `TextInput` and the logical line of a `TextArea` (`lineAt`, up to its line breaks, not the wrapped row). Tests: `server/tests/textfield_model_test.mjs` covers the history (grouping, pauses, words, caret jumps, pastes, deleted selections, outside changes, the 200-step cap and the keys) and `textarea_model_test.mjs` covers line selection and undo across lines. The new `server/tests/textfield_menu_test.mjs` with `textfield_menu_scene.mjs` renders both fields over a stub `lord` and drives them with `__lordEvent` and `__lordKey`: a right or middle click keeps the caret, the menu's items work, Escape closes it, the keys undo and redo, and triple and double clicks select. It is registered in `server/tests/run_suites.sh`.
- **Databases: favorites of type SSH connect through an SSH tunnel.** They used to say the tunnel came in a later
  version. lord-server runs `/usr/bin/ssh -W <db host>:<db port>` to the favorite's SSH server and gives lord-sql
  ssh's stdin and stdout as the server's stream; nothing listens on this computer and the tunnel ends with the
  connection. ssh never reads `~/.ssh/config` (`-F none`), runs in batch mode with only the favorite's key (a file
  nobody else can read), and every argument comes from the validated favorite with `--` before the server. The
  first connection shows the SSH server's key fingerprint to trust ("First connection to this SSH server"); the
  accepted key is kept in the favorite (`ssh.hostKey`) and from then on only that key is accepted. ssh's errors are
  told apart: the key refused, the key file unusable, the database's port not opened, the server key changed.
  `server/src/sql/sshtun.c` with 41 more checks in `tests/sqlc_test.c` (the fingerprint against `ssh-keygen -l`,
  hostile hosts, users and paths); end to end through a real sshd to MariaDB 11.8 on a VM.
- **Text Editor: files dragged from Files open in it.** A file opens in a tab and a folder becomes the project; while
  the drag is over the window it is outlined and says so.
- **Files: what is dragged keeps following the pointer into another app.** The dragged icon was drawn inside the Files
  window and vanished at its edge; it is now in the desktop's drag layer, above every window, and shows a green + over a
  window that takes files (the Terminal, for one).
- **Text fields select and edit as in any desktop (every LordOS app).** The SDK's TextInput and TextArea had a caret but
  no selection: Ctrl/⌘+A, Shift with ← → ↑ ↓ Home End, a drag with the mouse (also past the field's edges), a double
  click on a word, typing or pasting over the selection, Backspace and Delete on it, Ctrl/⌘+C and X (never from a
  password field), and Ctrl or ⌥ with ← → and Backspace by word now work. The text is drawn in one piece with the caret
  and the selection over it: placing the caret in a word no longer opened a gap in it (it was drawn between the two
  halves). A value longer than a one-line field scrolls to keep the caret in sight. `editKey`, `replaceSel`,
  `selRange`, `wordAt` in `sdk/textfieldmodel.js` (23 more checks) and `areaEdit` in `sdk/textareamodel.js` (6 more).
- **Terminal: files dropped on an ssh pane go to the remote shell's directory**, found as for a download from `ls` (the
  reported one, the prompt's, the title's, then the home), not always to the home on a server without the LordOS
  integration.
- **Terminal Files mode in a narrow window keeps the names readable**: below about 1100 px Permissions is hidden, below
  820 px Modified too, and the transfers' speed graph narrows; before, the fixed columns left the Name column empty.
- **Terminal triggers fire once per printed line, so a line printed again fires again, and a line that only scrolled does not.** Until now `runTriggers` (apps/terminal/state.js) kept the set of texts on the screen and skipped any line whose text was in it, so `echo error` run twice notified only once. The engine now gives each screen line with the absolute row it starts on (`lord.term.text(id, 'screenLines')`, `vt_screen_lines` in server/src/term/vt.c; a wrapped line is one entry and one that starts above the screen is given whole). The decision is a pure function, `freshLines` in apps/terminal/triggers.js: a line is new when its row held something else at the last look; a line whose text left its row while still on the screen is taken as moved (scroll regions, full-screen programs) and does not fire; after a resize, which renumbers the rows, lines go by how many times each text was on the screen. The main and alternate screens keep separate snapshots, so leaving a full-screen program does not fire the shell's lines again. Tests: the freshLines cases in server/tests/terminal_triggers_test.mjs (repeat, two at once, scroll, clear, partial redraw, typing, full-screen moves, resize) and the vt-dump suite "screen lines with their rows" (server/tests/vt_dump.c `--lines`, server/tests/run_suites.sh).
- **Terminal: a port forward whose fixed local port is already taken says so and offers a free port.** Before this, a second tab with the same profile, or another program already listening on that port, showed only "The server refused it". Now lord-server tries the bind on 127.0.0.1 first (`port_taken` in `server/src/term/sftpc.c`, with `SO_REUSEADDR` the way ssh binds, so connections that are still closing don't count) and lord.sftp's `forward` answers `inuse` without asking the ssh master. The forwards panel shows "Port N on this computer is taken (another tab with this profile, or another program)" and a **Use a Free Port** button. The tab's badge turns red, shows the taken forward as `⇄ 80→8080 !`, and its tooltip gives the error. One notice per session and port names the taken ports and offers the same action. The forward then reopens on an automatic port, and that session's next ssh connections use an automatic port for it too. Forwards added from the panel show the error in place and get no notice. The pure logic is in `apps/terminal/fwdports.js` (`applyFree`, `takenPorts`, `badgeItem`, `badgeText`), tested by `server/tests/terminal_fwdports_test.mjs` (15 checks, registered in `tests/run_suites.sh`). `tests/sftpc_test.c` now asks for the same local port twice against a real ssh master and expects `inuse` (19 checks). There are new keys `terminal.fwd.err.inuse`, `fwd.takenTitle`, `fwd.takenBody` and `fwd.useFree` in en, es, pt, fr, it and lt, and the "Port forwards" section of docs/TERMINAL.md is updated.
- **Terminal: stale ssh control sockets no longer make Files mode and forwards say "no ssh".** An ssh killed hard leaves its control socket behind. `sshmux_find()` (`server/src/term/sshmux.c`) looked at no more than 32 entries of the folder and counted those sockets too, so with many of them the live master was never reached. Now only names of the shell integration's form (`<hex>-<pid>`, `sshmux_name_ok()`) are tried. A socket that refuses the connect (ECONNREFUSED, the new `Mux.refused`) does not count against the 32 masters asked, and the scan stops after 4096 entries. Such a socket is removed when it is still the user's socket, checked again with `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` against the same device and inode, through `unlinkat` in the folder that was opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and checked by `fstat`. Plain files, links and sockets with other names are left alone. `build/sftp-test` (`server/tests/sftp_test.c`) adds a fake master on a control socket and cases for 200 stale sockets around the live master, a plain file and a link with valid names, a live master and a stale socket with other names, and a folder that others can read. It also checks the name pattern. `docs/TERMINAL.md` "How the session is reused" describes this.
- **Confirmation dialogs no longer press a destructive button on Enter, and take keys only when they are in front.** `ConfirmDialog` (`sdk/controls.jsx`) used a global key listener: Enter confirmed in any window, even one behind, and even for «Empty Trash». Now, as in libadwaita, a `destructive` dialog's default is Cancel, so the action needs a click, or Tab to it and then Space; Escape cancels and Enter does the default. A dialog takes keys only while its window is focused (a dialog of the desktop itself, like the Dock's «Empty Trash», is always in front) and it is the newest dialog open; while one has the keys, `useKeyboard` gives the app under it none, and a key the dialog acted on does not reach the app after the dialog closes. A text field under a dialog that opens in front loses focus. The default button is drawn as the default (an accent edge and a heavier label), and a ring shows the keyboard focus that Tab moves. Files' own confirm sheet (`apps/files/panels.jsx`) is now the SDK's `ConfirmDialog`, so it gets Escape/Enter for the first time, and «Delete Immediately» and «Empty Trash» in Files are marked destructive (red, Enter cancels). The decision logic (default button, what each key does, which dialog owns the keys, when the app's keys wait) is in `sdk/dialogkeys.js`, tested by `server/tests/dialog_keys_test.mjs` (40 checks, registered in `tests/run_suites.sh`).
- **Databases: choosing a favorite's color shows which one is chosen, and it is kept at once.** The ring around the
  chosen dot was drawn with two shadows and a spread, which the interface engine doesn't draw, so nothing seemed to
  happen; it is a border now. The color is also written at once (the dot in the list changes) without Save Changes.
- **Terminal Settings: drop-down lists (font, non-ASCII font, a trigger's action) float over the form.** They pushed
  the rest of the section down while open. A click outside or Escape closes them.
- **Terminal Settings: a new port forward shows no error before its port is typed**, and the scrollback sizes are
  written as numbers are in the interface's language (1,000 in English, 1.000 in Spanish).
- **Terminal: a tab title next to a port forward badge is shortened from its start with "…"**, not cut on both sides.
- **Terminal: ❖ + click (or the menu's Download) on a name in `ls` output finds the file on a server without the LordOS
  shell integration.** With no directory reported (OSC 7), the name was looked up in the remote home only, so a file
  listed in `~/Downloads` on a Raspberry Pi was "not in the remote home". It is now looked up, in order, in the reported
  directory, the one the nearest prompt above the clicked line shows (`user@host:~/dir$`), the one in the title (Debian
  and Ubuntu put `user@host: dir` there), and the home; the first that has it wins. Copy Remote Path takes the same one.
  `promptDir`, `titleDir`, `expandHome` in `apps/terminal/lsnames.js` (16 more checks in `terminal_lsnames_test.mjs`).
- **Terminal Files mode: which side is which, and a menu on the whole list.** A click anywhere in a side makes it the
  one in use, marked in the accent color; the headings read "This Computer" and "Server · user@host". A right click where
  there is no file opens the folder's menu on either side: New Folder, Upload or Download the other side's selection
  here, Refresh, Hidden, Enclosing Folder, Copy Path, and Show in Files or Open Terminal Here (cd). The server side
  starts in the directory the remote shell's title names when the shell reports none. Its menus stay inside the view.
- **Terminal: files dragged from Files onto an ssh pane say where they will go before you let go.** While the drag is over
  the pane it is outlined and reads "Drop to upload N item(s) to user@host:~/dir" (with ⌥, that the paths are pasted
  instead). Files tells a window under the drag through a new optional `onFilesOver(paths, how)` prop next to
  `onFilesDrop` (null when the drag leaves or drops).
- **Terminal Files mode: each transfer shows where it comes from and where it goes**, on a line under its name and
  progress bar ("~/notes.txt → user@host:/srv/www/", "user@host:/var/log/app.log → ~/Downloads/"). `transferRoute` in
  `apps/terminal/sftp.js` (4 more checks in `terminal_sftp_test.mjs`).
- **Databases: a group of favorites has a color too.** Its folder is drawn in it; it is chosen in the group's sheet (New
  Group, Rename Group…) or from the group's menu (Color › Red … Gray, None). Kept in `favorites.json` as the group's
  `color` (0–6, as a favorite's), which lord-server now checks like a favorite's (`sqlc_test.c`, 5 more checks).
- **Files: a tagged folder is drawn in its tag's color** (its first tag), in every view and in Get Info,
  and in the list view the tag dots sit right after the name instead of at the far end of the Name column.
- **Terminal Settings: Escape closes what is open, not the whole window.** With a list, the trigger sheet, Import or
  the file chooser open, Escape closed Settings; it now closes the newest of them, and the window only when none is.
- **Releasing ❖ after a ❖ + click no longer opens the app launcher.** The shell took any press and release of ❖ with no
  key between as a tap, and a click in between didn't count, so ❖ + click on a link or a file name in the Terminal also
  opened Apps. A click while ❖ is held now cancels the tap (`sdk/shortcuts.js`).
- **Apps whose name starts with a lowercase letter are in their place in the Apps grid (GitHub #64).** "go-link Desk"
  showed after every other app, below the last row, so it looked missing from the grid while Files → Applications
  listed it. The grid, Lord Classic's start menu and Files sorted names with `localeCompare`, and in the desktop's
  JavaScript engine that compares character codes and ignores its options (`sensitivity`, `numeric`): every name
  starting with a capital came first. They now share `compareNames` (`sdk/collate.js`, from Cloud's account order,
  #86): case and accents aside, numbers by value. Checked in a session and on a Raspberry Pi 5 with go-link Desk
  1.8.0 installed from its own `.deb`. Test: `files_model_test.mjs`, with the engine's comparison swapped in.
- **Every list of names is in the same order.** The same comparison now sorts the rest of the lists people read:
  Contacts and their groups, Passwords (titles and tags), Player (artists, albums, songs), Fonts, Disks, Photos and
  its cloud places, Calendar (events and calendar groups), Mail's folders, Machines, Databases, the Firewall's apps,
  the Network monitor, Remote Desk, Settings (themes, notifications, Bluetooth devices, languages), Help, the file
  dialog, Cleaner, the Terminal (tags, actions, secrets), the installer and the Imager's countries. Lists sorted by
  internal keys (hashes, ids, dates, paths) are unchanged.
- **Documentation: what a remote desktop host's generic Linux build shows on LordOS.** A host that captures a Wayland
  session only through the RemoteDesktop and ScreenCast portals together finds no RemoteDesktop portal on LordOS, never
  asks for a screen, and streams its own fallback picture; one such host's fallback is the same PM5544 test card as
  `lordos-testbench`'s, which made it look as if LordOS shared the test bench. Nothing in LordOS sends that card: the
  ScreenCast portal shares only what the person picks in the chooser. `docs/WAYLAND.md` now says RemoteDesktop isn't
  offered and why, and `docs/UPDATES.md` no longer says LordOS has no ScreenCast portal. Checked on VM 127: the portal
  answers `ScreenCast.AvailableSourceTypes` 3 and has no RemoteDesktop interface.

### Security

- **Web apps: a page's clipboard writes can no longer be forged by another site.** lord-web's `navigator.clipboard`
  shim posted to a message handler visible to every frame, guarded by one random key per process that the shim put
  in the page's own world, in every top-level document (also another site's page reached by a redirect or a script)
  and that never changed; a page could read it (a setter on `Object.prototype` during `Object.assign`, or a replaced
  `postMessage`) and hand it to a frame of another site, which could then overwrite the session's clipboard after
  any click. The handler now lives in lord-web's isolated world (`lordos-web-xfer`), where only a bridge script runs
  (top frame, and only in documents of the app's scope through the scripts' allow-list, `weburl_scope_pattern`); the
  page's shim, which holds nothing secret, asks it through document events with JSON text and builds only fresh
  objects. At each write lord-web checks that the document's address (read in the isolated world), the main frame's
  committed address and the view's are all in scope, besides the user-activation rule. Tests: `build/webapp-test`
  (the scope pattern). Checked on VM 127 (2026-11-11): the page still has `navigator.clipboard` and its
  `writeText` after a click reached the session's clipboard and pasted back; the handler was not visible to the page
  or to a frame of another origin inside it, and a write the page sent without a click was refused.
- **Web apps: drops from sandboxed apps no longer hand files to a page.** lord-web opened every local file a drag's
  `text/uri-list` named, so an isolated LordOS app or a Flatpak could make lord-web read and give a web page files it
  can't reach itself, past the rule that keeps those drags from handing files to LordOS. lord-server now leaves
  `text/uri-list` and the other file-list types (`x-special/gnome-copied-files`, the portals' lists) out of
  such a drag's offer to a lord-web client (known by its pid, `webmgr_owner`; `dndg_file_mime`, `DOffer.nofiles`,
  also refused at `receive`), so the drop arrives as text only. A dropped file is now opened with `openat2` and
  `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` on its resolved path (else one component at a time with `O_NOFOLLOW`), so a folder swapped
  for a link after `realpath` is refused, and the page's `File` has the name of the file opened, not the one in the
  list. Tests: `build/webapp-test` (a link in place of a folder, both open paths), `build/dndgate-test` (the file-list
  types). Checked on VM 127 (2026-11-11): a JPEG dragged from Files onto a page's drop zone still arrives as a file
  (`types` `["Files"]`, its name, type and size). A drag from a sandboxed app was not tried there (no Flatpak on the
  VM).

## [0.8.8.7-beta] - 2026-11-09

### Added

- **Lithuanian is complete** (GitHub #45). 0.8.8.6 translated the login screen, the desktop, Files, the installer and
  part of Settings. Now every app and message is translated, 11,909 keys, with Lithuanian plurals (one, few, other). The
  emoji names and keywords and the country names come from CLDR 45. Settings no longer lists Lithuanian as partly
  translated.
- **Files and Disks: CDs and DVDs show up and mount read-only (#92).** Optical drives (`sr*`) used to be left out of `lord.disks.list()` and refused by every `disk-*` action, so an inserted disc, such as the VirtualBox Guest Additions image, never appeared anywhere. A drive that holds a disc is now listed with `transport: "optical"` and `ro: true`; an empty drive is not listed. Files shows the disc in Locations, and a click mounts it at `/media/<user>/<label>`. `disk-mount` always mounts a disc read-only (`nosuid,nodev`). `disk-unmount` and `disk-eject` accept it, and eject unlocks the door and opens the tray with `CDROMEJECT`; in a VM this removes the image. Format, rename, erase, image copies, SMART and the LordOS Imager refuse an optical drive on the root side (`disk.opticalReadOnly`). Disks now offers Mount, Unmount and Eject for read-only disks too (discs, locked cards). A disc inserted during the session brings a notice whose Open mounts it and opens it in a new Files window.
- **Files: a New Folder button in the toolbar, next to the back and forward arrows, makes a new folder in the folder shown and opens its name for editing, like Ctrl+Shift+N.** It is disabled where the folder is read-only. Mail: the message editor in the compose and reply window now has a right-click menu with Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All, and a right click inside the selection keeps it. Ctrl+V already pastes, since the compositor lets isolated Mail read the clipboard once for a paste it saw (#64). Paste from the menu is a click the app draws itself, so when Mail has no clipboard permission yet it shows the system prompt ("Mail wants to read the clipboard") and pastes only if you allow it (GitHub #93).
- **Terminal: Files mode, the server's files over the tab's own ssh session.** It is one view per tab: this
  computer on the left and the server on the right, in the terminal's look. It is turned on with the footer's Files
  switch, View → Server Files (SFTP) (❖⇧F) or a right click on the tab. It covers the panes and the shell stays alive
  behind it.
  - It uses the same connection, with no second login and no password or code asked again. The shell integration's
    `ssh` (bash, zsh, fish) makes the connection a connection-sharing master, with one socket per shell in a 0700 folder
    of the session and `ControlPersist=no`. Options the user passes are left alone, and `LORD_SSH_MUX=0` turns this off.
    lord-server finds that master by its pid being the tab's foreground process and opens a new channel on it with
    OpenSSH's own multiplexing protocol. It runs no program.
  - SFTP is spoken by **lord-sftp**, a new sandboxed helper that gets the channel and the local file as descriptors,
    never a path. Names with `/` or control characters, and odd owner names, are left out of listings.
  - **Toolbar:** New Folder, Refresh, Hidden, Filter, and As Root, which uses the server's sftp-server through `sudo`;
    when sudo needs a password, a sheet asks for it once and it isn't kept. The local side refreshes every 3 s and the
    server's every 5 s and after each change.
