  - **Right click on the server:** Download, Rename, New Folder, Permissions (boxes and octal), Change Owner, Information
    (`file`, size, owner, permissions, and SHA-256 computed on the server), Copy Path, Open Terminal Here (`cd`),
    Delete. **Right click on this computer:** Upload, Rename, New Folder, Copy Path, Move to Trash.
  - Double click opens a folder or transfers a file. The arrows between the sides upload and download the selection,
    folders included.
  - **Transfers** run on channels of their own, so the listing stays usable and each one can be cancelled. Uploads are
    orange and downloads blue, with a speed graph of the last minute. A download never replaces a file unasked, and
    the local files follow lord.fs's rules.
  - An upload never replaces a file on the server unasked: when names are already there, a sheet asks Replace, Keep
    Both (a free name such as `notes (2).txt`) or Skip, and the choice applies inside existing folders too.
  - Not shared: an `ssh` opened before this version, or one made from inside another server.
- **Terminal: the Claude Code footer inside screen or tmux, and over ssh.** The footer showed Claude Code's state,
  context and limits only when `claude` was the pane's own process. Inside `screen` or `tmux`, or on a server reached
  with `ssh`, the pane's process is `screen`, `tmux` or `ssh`, so nothing showed. Now the Terminal reads Claude Code's
  status line on the pane's screen every 2 s, the line lord-claude-status prints:
  `Opus 5.5 | LordOS | main | ctx 44% | 5h – | sem 26%`. "esc to interrupt" on screen tells it Claude Code is working.
  - In a local screen or tmux, the session with the same model, context and folder in `~/.claude/sessions` gives the
    exact state, tokens, resets and cost.
  - Over ssh, the screen's numbers are shown. The server's Claude Code has to print that line.
  - The footer says `✳ Claude Code · screen` (or tmux, ssh).
- **Terminal: a Profiles window (❖O, Profiles → Profiles…).** It works like the Profiles window of other terminals: a search by name or tag, the
  profiles grouped by tag (the folders fold), each with its star when it is the default and what it runs (its ssh line
  or the login shell). **One click opens the profile**, with no Enter or double click. The arrows move the selection and
  Enter opens it; Esc closes the window. Below the list, a choice of where one click opens it: New Tab, New Window,
  Split Right or Split Down, in the terminal window used last. "Close this window after opening a profile" (on by
  default) and Edit Profiles…, which opens Settings, complete it. Both choices are remembered in `terminal.json`.
- **Terminal: profiles grouped by their tags.** Importing another terminal's profiles keeps each profile's tags, and
  Shell → Profiles and the Dock's menu list the profiles without a tag first, then one submenu per tag in name order (a
  profile under each of its tags), instead of one long list of every profile.

- **Passwords fills and saves sign-ins across LordOS.** The password fields of Settings → Cloud (adding an account and
  Sign In Again), Files' shared-folder sign-in and Connect to Server (sftp, ftp, WebDAV), and Remote Desk's sign-in and
  credentials now have the 🔑 of Passwords, as Databases and Wi-Fi already did. For a server it lists only entries whose
  host field or site is exactly the address the password goes to, never a guess from a title and never the name a
  machine announces on the local network, so a device can't take a kept server's name and be offered its password; for
  a cloud provider, the entries kept under its sites. When a server accepts a password typed in the form (not one
  filled from Passwords or the keyring), the app asks whether to save it in Passwords; nothing is saved until Save is
  chosen, and the password never goes to a file or a log. Sign In Again for a cloud account keeps the saved user and
  password when the fields are left empty. Isolated apps (Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Reminders) can still only use their
  own keyring items.

- **Cloud: pause one account and filter Recent from the menu bar** (GitHub #83). Each account in the menu bar's Cloud
  panel has its own Pause or Resume button (or Unlock Keyring / Sign In Again when needed). Clicking accounts shows only
  their recent files; click again to remove one, or Show All to clear. With one account chosen, Show in Files and Cloud
  Settings open that account.

- **Window buttons on the left or the right in both themes** (GitHub #58). Settings → Desktop & Dock → Title bars →
  Window buttons: Automatic, Left or Right. Automatic keeps each theme's side (mirrored in right-to-left languages as
  before); Left puts close, minimize, maximize at the left edge and Right puts minimize, maximize, close at the right
  edge, in Lord Flow and Lord Classic alike. Linux apps that draw their own title bar get the same side.

- **Thumbnail size in the file dialog** (GitHub #58). In Thumbnails, the system file dialog (adding a wallpaper, a
  Notes image, a contact photo, a Linux app's file chooser) has Files' size control: seven steps, pictures from 48 to
  200 px, Ctrl + and Ctrl −, remembered for picture dialogs and for the rest.

- **Control Center opens every tile's Settings page** (GitHub #58). As Wi-Fi and Bluetooth already did, a click on a
  tile's name in Lord Flow opens its page: Dark Mode, Transparency and Accent Color open Appearance, Sound opens Sound,
  Wallpaper opens Wallpaper. In Lord Classic's quick settings, Do Not Disturb, Dark Mode and Transparency get the "›"
  half, and a new "›" at the end of the volume row opens Sound.

- **Photos: the cloud folders kept on this computer** (GitHub #89). A Cloud section in the sidebar lists every folder a
  cloud account keeps on this computer (Keep on This Computer); their pictures are all local, so they open without the
  network. Folders only in the cloud are left out, and these folders are read off the compositor's thread, so Photos
  never waits for a provider.

- **Text Editor: a scroll bar** (GitHub #84). Drag it, or click the track to jump there; Ctrl+End (❖↓ in Lord Flow)
  still goes to the last line. With it, the editor reads its real height: until now it kept 600 × 400, so Page Up and
  Page Down, keeping the cursor in view and the end of the scroll were off in any other window size.

- **Terminal: its own configuration file, wherever you want it.** Profiles, colors, key mappings, shortcuts, the hotkey
  and the windows to restore move out of `settings.json` into `~/.config/lordos/terminal.json` (with a schema number),
  so they can be backed up, versioned or synced on their own. The move is automatic and loses nothing: `settings.json`
  is backed up first (`settings.json.pre-terminal-migration.bak`) and the section leaves it only after the new file reads
  back the same. Preferences → Config File shows where it is and can put it anywhere in your home folder or on a mounted
  disk (move the current configuration there, or use the file already there), and back. Every write is atomic, `0600`,
  with five rotating backups beside it. If the chosen place isn't there (a disk not mounted, a renamed folder), the
  Terminal keeps working from the last good copy, read-only, says so, and goes back to the file when it returns; a file
  changed from outside (a restore, a `git pull`) is read again within 2 s. Export Profiles… and Import Profiles… take
  LordTerminal JSON as well as other terminal emulators' files; a profile that would type into the shell by itself
  (initial text, a trigger that sends text, a key that types text) never replaces the default profile, the import list
  says what it would type, and global key mappings that type text come in only when you turn that option on. The file is protected from other apps' file operations
  wherever it is (`lord.termconf`, docs/TERMINAL.md "Configuration file").

- **Databases (new app): a MySQL and MariaDB client.** Favorites in groups with a color each; Standard, Socket and
  Cloud connections (managed MySQL services: writer or reader endpoint, TLS required and the provider's
  certificate checked); passwords kept in Passwords. Per connection: a database pop-up and a table list with filter;
  Structure (fields and indexes; every change is shown as the ALTER TABLE before it runs); Content (filter rules,
  sort, 1000-row pages, edit a cell, add, duplicate and delete rows, keyed by the primary key); Query (line numbers,
  highlighting, completion of tables, fields and keywords, Run Current with Ctrl+Enter and Run All, one tab per
  result, Explain, history per favorite, and a safe mode that asks before an UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE);
  Table Info; and a Console with every query the app sends, passwords hidden. A favorite marked production opens
  read-only until you unlock it. On first run it finds the favorites saved by the SQL client of another computer's system on the home folder or a
  mounted disk and imports them with their groups and colors (passwords stay in that system's keychain: each is
  asked once). SSH tunnels, IAM tokens, relations and triggers editing, users, processes, import and export come
  in a later phase (docs/DATABASES.md).
  - Each connection runs in its own sandboxed helper, `lord-sql`, that speaks the MySQL protocol itself (TLS,
    `mysql_native_password` and `caching_sha2_password`), with no sockets of its own and no files: lord-server
    connects only to a saved favorite, through a connector of its own, so the firewall and Monitor show it as
    "Databases" (`lordos:sql`). Everything a server sends is parsed bounds-checked and fuzzed in the tests.
  - A password is sent as such (MySQL 8's first login of a user) only over TLS whose certificate was verified or
    trusted by fingerprint, never to an unchecked certificate, so a machine in the middle can't read it.
  - Values written back into SQL (editing, deleting or duplicating a row) quote a `'` as `''`, which no stored value
    can turn into the end of the string under any `sql_mode` (`NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` included); completion compares
    table names as words and never builds a pattern from what the server returns.
  - Integrated with Passwords: every password field has the 🔑 button, which offers the password kept for that
    connection and the Passwords entries whose host is exactly the connection's (a Database, Network or SSH
    entry's host, or a site), each shown with its host, while Passwords is unlocked; the password leaves Passwords
    only when you pick one.

- **Machines: shared folders.** Up to four folders of this computer inside a machine, read-only unless you turn writing
  on for one (Configure → Sharing → Add a Folder; the bar's folder button lists them, opens each in Files and copies the
  command that mounts it in a Linux guest: `mount -t virtiofs <tag> /mnt/<tag>`). Each folder is served by its own
  `virtiofsd` (Debian's), started by `lord-vm` as you, in its own namespaces with only that folder mounted and its own
  seccomp filter; QEMU gets an already connected socket and never the folder. Only a real folder inside your home (not
  all of it) or on a disk under `/media` or `/mnt` can be shared, never a hidden one nor the machines' library, checked
  when it's chosen and again at every start; virtiofsd gets the folder as it was checked (opened once without following a
  link), so swapping a folder of its path for a link afterwards changes nothing. The guest's memory is shared with the helper only on machines that share a
  folder. Suspend, resume and snapshots with memory keep the folder mounted. `machine.json` schema 4 (`shares`);
  `lord-vm --set --share ro|rw:TAG:FOLDER`, `--shares none`. "What Machines Needs" installs `virtiofsd`.

### Changed
-- **`whiptail` and `zstd` come with LordOS.** They are now in every image (the live ISO and the Raspberry Pi image)
  and among the lordos package's Recommends, so an update brings them to installs that lack them.
  - `whiptail` (61 KB) shows the questions a package asks while it installs, as dialogs in the terminal. Without it
    debconf said "unable to initialize frontend: Dialog" and fell back to plain text.
  - `zstd` (2.3 MB) is the compressor Debian prefers for the initramfs. Without it `update-initramfs` warned "No zstd
    … using gzip" and made a slower one to build and unpack at boot.
- **Updates bring the Recommends a new version adds**, as apt's full upgrade does, in Update All and when one package
  is upgraded. Before, the package engine followed only Depends on an upgrade, so a tool newly recommended by the
  lordos package (`whiptail`, `zstd`, and earlier the command-line tools) reached a system that was already installed
  only through apt. A group is added only when none of its names were recommended by the installed version, so a
  recommended package the user removed stays removed. One that can't be installed doesn't stop the update.
- **Terminal: Settings open in a window of their own.** They used to cover the terminal window they were opened from,
  so nothing could be done in it meanwhile. Now ❖, (or Terminal → Settings) opens one Settings window, or brings it to
  the front if it is already open, and the terminal stays usable beside it. The profiles on the left are grouped by tag,
  the same groups as the Profiles menu: the untagged ones first, then one folder per tag that can be folded, with how
  many profiles it holds; a profile with two tags is in both. A search field filters by name, and by tag: a tag that
  matches shows its whole folder. The profile's sections (General, Colors, Text, Window, Terminal, Keys, Triggers and
  Config File) are tabs centred above the form, under the profile's name, its star and its tags, instead of a second
  list in the sidebar. Changes are still saved as they are made; Done or Esc closes the window.
 **Cloud: "Only in the cloud" or "In sync with this computer", said plainly.** Adding an account now asks how to use
  it, and its page has the same choice in place of the "Files on demand" switch, each with what it means: only in the
  cloud (every file listed, a file comes down when it is opened and what is copied in goes up, nothing kept on this
  computer) or in sync (a whole copy here and in the cloud, a deletion on one side goes to the other and the
  provider's trash keeps it). The browser sign-in's done card asks the same in place of "Keep everything on this
  computer".

- **Passwords has a new icon**: a gold key on graphite, unlike the Store's blue bag it was taken for in the Dock.

- **Cloud settings**: an account's Pause Syncing switch shows only its own pause and says when Pause All (or the
  battery, a metered network) paused it, with Resume All beside it; Check This Account has Close and waits for an
  account that works before it runs.

- **Cloud: accounts in name order** (GitHub #86). Files' sidebar, Files → Network, the file dialog, Settings → Cloud
  and the menu bar panel list accounts by name, ignoring case and accents and ordering numbers by value ("Drive 2"
  before "Drive 10"), instead of the order they were added in. Each account keeps its color.

- **Cloud: two more providers verified, and clearer check results** (GitHub #80, #81). Two providers whose Check This
  Account reports passed on 0.8.8.6 are listed as verified in Add Account, with the issues as evidence. A step skipped
  because the provider lacks the feature, such as links, says "Not offered by this provider, not a failure" on screen
  and in the report instead of a bare "skipped".

- **Every app that changed has a new version** (GitHub #91). 0.8.8.6 changed Files, Monitor, Settings and others and
  the Store still showed their old versions. Each app changed since 0.8.8.5 gets its next version, and a release
  package is refused when an app changed and its version didn't (`tools/app-versions.mjs`).

- **Files: a connected share shows its server's name** (GitHub #88). A share found on the network by its name showed
  as "software on 192.168.1.25" once connected; Files now keeps the name the server was found or typed under and shows
  it in the sidebar, the title and Network's list. The folder on disk keeps the address (a name is never resolved for
  the mount).

  A folder shared with write access can't be, sit under or hold a file this computer protects (settings.json, the
  Terminal's configuration wherever it is, launchers): the machine could change what this computer runs. Checked when
  the share is made and again before every start; read-only sharing is unaffected.

- **Passwords: copy anything, and know what became of it.** An item's title and notes have a copy button like every
  field; a right click on an item in the list copies its title, any field, its 2FA code or its notes without opening
  it. A copied password shows how many seconds it has before it is cleared, with **Keep** to leave it there. If
  something replaces it right away (another app, or a running machine), Passwords says so instead of failing
  silently. lord-server tells the app only whether its own copy is still on the clipboard, never what the clipboard
  holds, only for a few seconds after the copy, and not under the firewall's no-clipboard restriction
  (`BOP_CLIP_STATUS`). A secret replaced by a picture leaves the picture on the clipboard, and its text is still
  wiped on time.

- **Machines' library looks like Remote Desk.** A toolbar of icons, each named in its tooltip: Storage, what Machines
  needs (only when something is missing), Add (New Machine, Import a machine), pictures or a list, Sort (by name,
  running first, last used, disk space), Show (all, running, off) and a search over the name, the system and the
  architecture. The view, the order and the filter are remembered (`settings.machinesView`). The list view has one row
  per machine: picture, name and system, what it's doing, CPU, memory and disk. The summary of machines running, memory
  in use and free space moved to a status line under the library; a click on free space opens Storage. An empty library
  says "No machines yet" in the middle with New Machine and Import, and a search with no match says so.
- **The machine window's bar is icons in groups.** The agent and what it brings (clipboard, shared folders, Apps mode) |
  resolution and devices | shell, logs, screenshot, record | start, pause or resume, and power | Configure and full
  screen. Each group sits in one rounded container, with a thin line between groups, and every button has its tooltip.
  The clipboard button shows which ways it works for the machine and leads to Configure to change them; the folder button
  lists the shared folders; Apps mode is shown, dimmed, with "coming in a later version".
- **A machine that is off shows one round Play button** over its last picture, dimmed, with its name and state; a
  suspended one resumes from the same button.

### Fixed

- **Screenshots: a capture or recording that fails says the real reason (issue #77).** 0.8.8.6 shipped without the lord-media helper. Window captures were neither saved nor copied, though the thumbnail said "Copied to clipboard". Screen recording said "Could not start recording (is another recording running?)" with an Open Privacy button, and the markup editor's Save said only "Could not save". The 0.8.8.7 package has lord-media again. In addition, a recording that cannot launch the helper now says "The media helper (lord-media) is not available" (`src/ui/js_media.c`), and the Screenshots notice offers Open Privacy only when a permission or a restriction is the cause. The editor's Save adds the reason, and a failed Copy says the picture was not copied instead of "Could not save".
- **Cloud: a provider that stops answering no longer freezes the desktop (#85).** After a paused account was resumed while its provider could not be reached (pCloud, "dial tcp: lookup eapi.pcloud.com: i/o timeout"), Keep on This Computer walked the kept folders through the mount. rclone held each folder about 15 seconds while it tried the provider, one folder after another for minutes, and anything else reading those folders waited with it. The desktop froze for 2 to 3 seconds again and again. Now the keeper does not walk an account that is offline, or one not checked since it was mounted or resumed (Pause, Pause All, back on power). The account is listed once first, and the keeper comes back when it answers. A call through the mount that fails with an I/O error or a time out ends the pass at once and checks the account right away. Listing ~/Cloud (or any folder holding a cloud or network mount) no longer stats each mount's root, which on the interface's thread meant a round trip to the provider.
- **Remote desktop: no more "connected but 0 frames decoded" when the graphics card's H.264 encoder produces a stream browsers can't play (#94).** The session's live encoder used VA-API whenever the driver opened the H.264 encoder (even with LORD_GPU=0), and switched to libx264 only if opening failed. Some drivers, likely older AMD cards on the radeon kernel driver (VCE 2.0), open it and then return a stream with no SPS/PPS or a broken picture: every browser connected and showed nothing. lord-media now decodes VA-API's first keyframe with FFmpeg's software H.264 decoder before any packet goes out. The keyframe must decode on its own to a picture of the right size that looks like the frame that went in (a grid of luma samples). If it doesn't, if the card refuses a frame, or if it gives no packet for 8 frames, the same encoder goes on with libx264 from the current frame and the journal says why. When no picture arrives, the page's details also show how many video packets and frames the browser received, its decoder, and whether the computer encodes in hardware or software. New tests: `encheck-test` and `lmstream-test` (lord-media end to end with libx264, VA-API, and a build whose check always fails), in `make -C server test-full`.
- **Xwayland: GTK programs that only allow X11 open again; VMware clipboard, partly (#76).** The session set `GDK_BACKEND=wayland`. GTK then skips every backend a program doesn't allow, so a program that only allows X11 couldn't open any display. That included VMware's `vmware-user` agent from `open-vm-tools-desktop`, which stopped at `gtk_init`. The session now sets `GDK_BACKEND=wayland,x11`: GTK apps still open on Wayland, and X11-only GTK programs get Xwayland. With `vmware-user` running, what the host copies reaches LordOS through the X11 clipboard bridge. Copying from the guest to the host works for text copied in X11 apps. LordOS doesn't start the agent by itself yet (`setsid vmware-user &` from the Terminal), and text copied in LordOS or Wayland apps doesn't reach the host yet. Both need security review; see docs/WAYLAND.md, "VMware Tools". Not yet tested on a VMware host.
- **`lordos-issue` now includes the last 40 lines that Linux apps printed (`~/.cache/lordos/apps.log`) and the last 20 lines of Xwayland's log (`~/.cache/lordos/xwayland.log`, without xkbcomp's keymap warnings), with the same name and address replacement as the rest of the report.** When a Linux app closes as soon as it starts, its reason was only in those files, so reports did not show it (#95, WordCraft from the ArtCraft launcher on a Raspberry Pi 500). TROUBLESHOOTING.md gains "A Linux app doesn't open".
- **A "More" menu near the bottom of a window opens upward.** Every app's ⋯ button (the SDK's `MenuButton`) opened
  its menu downward, so a button in a footer, like the favorites' ⋯ in Databases, had its menu cut off by the window's
  bottom edge. The menu now opens upward when it doesn't fit below the button and there is more room above.
- **Databases: a folder of favorites can be deleted or renamed even when it is empty.** Rename Folder and Delete
  Folder were only in the ⋯ menu, and only for the folder of the selected favorite, so a folder with no favorites
  could not be removed. A right click on a folder now opens its own menu with New Favorite, Rename and Delete.
  Deleting a folder still moves what was in it up one level.
- **Displays keep their signal across lock, logout and login, and logging out doesn't freeze the desktop.** At every
  hand-off of the monitor, lord-sessiond removed the leaving session's framebuffers while they were still on the
  screen; amdgpu refuses to turn a plane off that way ("atomic remove_fb failed with -22" in the kernel log at every
  lock and logout) and the displays went dark, and a DisplayPort monitor put to sleep like that may not wake up until it
  is unplugged. Every lit display now gets a black frame of its own mode first, let go with CLOSEFB (it stays until the
  next session or the login screen shows its own), so nothing of the session stays visible and no link drops. Logging
  out asks lord-sessiond for the login screen at once; the session then closes its apps and unmounts its cloud folders
  off the screen, instead of leaving the desktop frozen for seconds meanwhile.

- **A click anywhere in a window brings it forward, and the keyboard with it.** A sheet or dialog that keeps its clicks
  to itself (Settings → Cloud's sign-in, Mail's, Contacts' and Calendar's sheets, the file dialog, Monitor's map
  buttons, and more) stopped the click before the window could come forward. With another window in front (Passwords,
  opened to unlock it for the 🔑), the code typed into the Settings sheet went to that window instead. The runtime now
  has a capture phase for presses (`onMouseDownCapture`, outermost first, which nothing inside can stop), and windows
  come forward there.

- **Cloud: an account signed in with a password and a device code no longer asks for a new sign-in after every logout or reboot.** rclone keeps the
  account's session (cookies, trust token) in its options and updates it in memory, but only accounts signed in
  through a browser were read back into the keyring, so rclone started again with the session of the first sign-in,
  which the provider refuses. Every account is now read back every 5 minutes and once more before rclone stops. An
  option rclone gives back stays out of `rclone.conf` unless it is known not to be secret. When the provider refuses a saved
  session the way rclone sometimes does for a password provider after a restart (its issue 9658: "Missing
  WEBAUTH-TOKEN cookie", whether or not the account has end-to-end encryption), the session is dropped once and rclone signs in
  again with the password and the kept trust token, which asks for no code while the token lasts. If that fails too, the account says Sign In Again (instead of "couldn't open the account's folder") and is tried
  again after 30 minutes instead of every 30 seconds.

- **Files: a folder of photos no longer runs the desktop out of memory** (GitHub #71, #82). Each JPEG or PNG icon was
  the whole picture, decoded on lord-server's interface thread and kept until the session ended: a 12-megapixel photo
  took 48 MB, so opening a folder of phone photos (a cloud account kept on this computer, for example) froze the
  desktop and lord-server ran out of memory and the session ended. Icons and the preview are now thumbnails made by two
  background threads at the size shown; pictures no window shows are kept up to 64 MB and then let go, and nothing over
  67 megapixels is decoded. Measured with 1,520 12-megapixel photos: from 10 GB in 23 seconds (then killed) to 265 MB
  at most, no pause over 0.4 s; with 300 of them, 154 MB once the thumbnails are made.

- **Thumbnails: a big folder of videos no longer keeps the desktop busy.** Every thumbnail asked lord-server again on
  each redraw, and every answer, or failure, redrew all of them; with 1,500 videos and no media helper (as 0.8.8.6
  shipped) the desktop stayed unresponsive for minutes. Each thumbnail is now asked once (again at most every 5 s while
  it is being made, every minute once known) and an answer redraws only the items that show it.

- **Bluetooth headsets play in high fidelity** (GitHub #78). A headset that paired but stayed silent as the output now
  plays. The sound server switched a headset to its low-quality hands-free mode whenever anything recorded (even the
  level meter in Settings → Sound), which some adapters can't carry at all. That automatic switch is off
  (`/etc/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/lordos-bluez-profiles.conf`) and LordOS picks the profile itself: choosing a
  headset as the output gives it high-fidelity playback unless its microphone is the chosen input, which Settings →
  Sound offers as "(headset mode)". Settings → Bluetooth no longer offers the low-energy side some headsets also
  advertise as "LE-<name>" when the headset's own entry is listed, and a failed pairing of it says why instead of "the
  code did not match". Not yet tested with a real headset.

- **Cloud: Tell Us on GitHub works** (GitHub #79). After Check This Account the button opens the provider issue form
  with the report filled in. The browser launcher refused any web address over 300 characters and the report's
  parentheses went unencoded, so nothing happened. A web address may now be up to 3000 characters (other schemes keep
  300, same allowed characters), and when no browser takes it the report is copied with a note saying where to paste it.

- **Cloud: a second browser sign-in no longer fails after the provider's success page** (GitHub #87). When a provider
  listed first a drive that can't be opened, setting up the account stopped and Settings said the sign-in didn't
  finish. LordOS now tries the next drive (up to four); if the account has no usable drive it says so (open the account
  once on the provider's website), shows rclone's own message and removes the half-made account. Tested against a
  local stand-in for rclone, not a real account.

- **Cloud: Keep on This Computer shows a steady badge, and the check understands kept accounts** (GitHub #71). A kept
  folder keeps the "coming down" badge until every file in it is on this computer, instead of flashing the green check
  between files. On an account kept on this computer, Check This Account skips Free Up Space ("Kept on this computer,
  so not freed: not a failure") instead of failing after 40 seconds.

- **Window screenshots include the window's open dialog** (GitHub #58). Choosing a window with ❖⇧4 and Space left out a
  dialog the window had open (the file dialog of Settings → Wallpaper → Choose picture…). A sheet an app opens is now
  painted over its window in the capture; other windows' sheets, menus and the Dock are still left out, and protected
  windows stay black.

- **Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Reminders and Passwords can paste** (GitHub #64). These apps run isolated, and reading
  the clipboard needs a permission they never ask for, so Ctrl+V did nothing. Now a paste the person asks for in the
  app's window (Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert, which lord-server sees reach it, or the clipboard panel) lets that app read the
  clipboard once within 2 seconds. The app can't fake the keys, and any other read still needs the permission.

- **Photos: a picture that can't be opened says why** (GitHub #90). 0.8.8.6 shipped without the media helper and every
  picture showed as a black screen with nothing said, because the decoding failed before the picture could be told.
  It now shows "This image cannot be opened" and the reason. 0.8.8.7's package has the helper again (and the
  packaging refuses a package without it).

- **The package can't be built without its helpers.** 0.8.8.6 shipped without lord-media (screenshots, video, music,
  camera) and lord-vmdisplay, because the machine that built it lacked FFmpeg's and libsystemd's -dev packages and
  `make` skips a helper quietly when its libraries are missing. `tools/iso/mkdeb.sh` now stops and names each missing
  helper and what it needs; `ALLOW_MISSING="name …"` leaves one out on purpose.
- **Screenshots says when a capture couldn't be saved or copied.** A notification names why (for example, the media
  helper is missing), and the thumbnail says so instead of "Copied to the clipboard".
- **Media jobs no longer wait forever when lord-media is missing.** A job that failed at once (no lord-media) was freed
  before lord-server returned its id, so the app got a wrong id and never heard the job end: Screenshots saved and
  copied nothing and said nothing. The id is now taken first (`src/media/media.c`).

- **Migrate from another app: an encrypted VMware machine is called encrypted.** A machine VMware Fusion encrypted as a
  whole (as it does for a virtual TPM) keeps only its name and the wrapped key in the clear in its `.vmx`; the importer
  said "not a .vmx settings file". It now names the machine and stops with *encrypted*, which tells to remove the
  encryption in the app that made it.
- **Files: a Cloud or network folder never freezes the desktop any more.** Deleting a file inside a Cloud account's folder
  (any Cloud account, mounted by rclone through FUSE) froze the whole desktop, pointer and every window, until rclone
  finished, and going back to the parent folder could freeze it again until rclone answered. lord-server is one thread
  for input, layout, painting and JS, and Files read those folders with synchronous `lord.fs` calls on it: the folder's
  listing (`lord.fs.list`: a `readdir`, a `stat` per item and a `realpath` per subfolder, `apps/files/locations.js`), a
  `lord.fs.stat` per row for the list view's extra columns, the folder's own `stat` (is it writable) and `statvfs` (free
  space). On a FUSE mount each of those waits for rclone, which asks the provider when its listing is old or was just
  changed; and while the delete (on the Cloud's own thread since 0.8.5) runs `unlink`, the kernel holds that folder's lock,
  so the listing Files asked for right after waited for the provider too. Now:
  - New `lord.fs.listAsync / statAsync / trashAsync / freeAsync / mkdirAsync / renameAsync` run on a small pool of
    worker threads (`server/src/fsasync.c`, at most 6 threads and 256 requests; a full queue answers `fs.busy` at once)
    and answer through an eventfd the main loop polls (`__lordFsReply`). A worker resolves and checks each path with
    exactly the functions the synchronous calls use, now shared in `fsops.c` (`fsops_resolve_readable / _target /
    _stat`, `fsops_list`, `fsops_stat`): the writable roots, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev` and `/run`, the `fsops_protected`
    deny list (also for a parent of a protected path), a share that stopped answering, and only the Trash as a way to
    delete. No new operation and no way to run commands.
  - `lord.fs.mounts()` gives the mount table, and `fs.isRemote(path)` in the SDK says from it (no file system call)
    whether a folder is on a Cloud account, Connect to Server, SMB, NFS or other FUSE mount.
  - Files lists those folders off the thread and keeps each listing (`apps/files/remotedirs.js`): a folder opens at once
    with "Loading…" the first time, a folder seen before (going back) shows its last listing while a new one comes, the
    status bar says "Waiting for the folder to answer…" when a listing takes longer than 0.4 s, and the window, the
    Dock and every other app keep answering meanwhile. The listing brings what the list view's columns need, so rows
    aren't asked one by one. Deleting in a Cloud account, or moving to the Trash on a share, takes the items off the view
    at once; a new listing when it ends brings back any the provider refused, with the reason in the status bar. New
    Folder, Rename, the folder's write permission, its free space, Get Info, the column view, unfolded folders in the
    list view, favorites and the names a copy or paste picks run off the thread there as well.
  - A move inside a Cloud account or a share (a rename at the provider) runs on the copy job's thread instead of the
    interface's.
  - Local folders keep the synchronous calls (nothing changes there).
  - Tests: `build/fsasync-test` holds requests in a fake slow file system and checks that submitting never waits, that
    other folders answer meanwhile, a full queue, every answer, and that each refusal is the synchronous call's own
    (outside the roots, `/proc`, protected files and their parents, renaming onto an existing name);
    `tests/files_remote_test.mjs` checks the listings Files keeps (one at a time per folder, the last one shown while a
    new one runs, items hidden during a delete and back only if still there) and which folders count as slow.

### Known issues and limitations

- **A cloud account signed in with a password and a device code may ask for the code again after every logout or
  restart.** The session is kept in the keyring, but the provider refuses it when rclone starts again, and signing in
  with the kept trust token asks for a new code (an open problem in rclone's backend for that provider: its issues 9658
  and 9966, with fixes proposed and not released yet). LordOS says so when the account is added and asks for a new
  sign-in instead of failing quietly. An account waiting for a sign-in is no longer tried again by itself: not every 30
  minutes, and not when its folder is opened in Files, because each try could send a code to the person's devices. The
  account's page in Settings explains it and links rclone's issue. It also has **Copy Log for rclone**: the last lines
  of rclone's log about that backend, with the account's name, e-mail addresses, the home folder, query strings and
  long tokens taken out, ready to paste in the issue. In Files, the account's folder says that it needs a new sign-in
  instead of "Folder is empty", with **Sign In…** (it opens the account in Settings) and the issue's link. lordos-rclone
  will follow rclone's release with the fix. A build with the proposed escrow fix (rclone PR 10048, reviewed line by
  line) was tried with a real account and did not help, so it is not shipped.
- **The browser sign-in drive and the password-and-code drive (`onedrive`, `iclouddrive`) are verified providers now:** tested end to end by the maintainer with their own accounts
  on a bare-metal machine. They are listed first in Add Account, and **Check This Account** for them moves under
  **Advanced**.

## [0.8.8.6-beta] - 2026-11-08

An update for 0.8.8 to 0.8.8.5 through Store → Updates and `apt` (no new ISO: the 0.8.8 live image stays the current one), with **Voice**: text to speech on the computer, without the internet (`say`, read aloud anywhere with a player, Live Speech, voices you choose in Standard or HD quality, and a Personal Voice made from your own recording); **Monitor → GPU**; the menu bar and the taskbar on every display; and the 34 issues reported on GitHub since 0.8.8.4 (#42 to #75), with the fixes found while checking them.

### Added

- **Monitor → GPU** (new tab): each graphics card drawn live (its fans turn with the real fan and stop at 0 RPM), load, temperature and fan history (Cooling's chart), the apps using it (each engine's share, their graphics memory and the APIs they use, from the kernel's DRM usage stats of your own processes), graphics memory, clocks, power, the graphics APIs installed for the card (Vulkan, OpenGL, OpenCL, video decoding, CUDA/NVENC on NVIDIA, ROCm on AMD, WebGPU through browsers), and LordOS's AI engines (the voice on the graphics card through Vulkan or on the processor, its quality and language, speaking or saving: `lord-say` leaves a status note in `~/.cache/lordos/say/<pid>`; `lord-tts` stays sandboxed, so its memory shows as hidden). The Overview shows the main GPU, the AI status and running virtual machines. Administrators can set an AMD card's fan by hand (30–100 %, `GPUFAN` through lord-fand only): it goes back to automatic above 85 °C, after repeated errors, when the session that set it ends, and on lord-fand's stop, restart or crash, and it is never saved. Everything is read without root, about once a second, only while the tab or the Overview is on screen. Tests: `gpustat-test` (63), `gpu_model_test.mjs` (69), `fan-test` (4224).
- **Menu bar on every display (Lord Flow).** Each display now has its own full menu bar: the L menu, the app's menus, the status items (Cleaner, keyboard layout, on-screen keyboard, Search, Control Center, the bell) and the clock. The app's menus are lit on the display with the window you're using and dimmed on the others; a click there lights that bar and opens the menu on that display. The Control Center, the clock's notifications and calendar panel, and Search open on the display whose bar you clicked, under the item. Menus stay inside one display. Maximized and snapped windows on every display stay below its bar. A monitor you plug in gets its bar, and one you unplug takes its bar and any panel open on it. All the bars share one clock timer (`sdk/ticker.js`). On by default; turn it off in Settings → Desktop & Dock → Menu Bar → "Show the menu bar on every display" (the same switch as Displays → "Show menu bar on all displays", whose choice is kept if you had turned it off). 
- **Lord Classic: the taskbar on every display**, on by default (Settings → Desktop & Dock → Taskbar → "Show the taskbar on every display", the same `menuBarAllDisplays` as Lord Flow's menu bar; one bar when off or mirrored). Each bar is whole: start, pinned and running apps (all apps on every bar), Trash, tray and clock. The start menu, power menu, quick settings, notifications and calendar open on the clicked bar's display and stay inside it; ❖, ❖A and ❖N open them on the display under the pointer. Each display's work area reserves its bar, monitors plugged or unplugged add or remove bars, and jump lists stay inside their display. One clock timer and one network poll serve every bar, and pins can be dropped on any bar (`registerDockTarget` takes several targets). Tested by `server/tests/classic_taskbar_test.mjs` over three monitors.
- **the first community hardware report in the tested-hardware catalogue**: a Dell Latitude 7480 (Intel Core i5-7300U, Intel HD Graphics 620 on i915, Intel Wireless 8265, LordOS 0.8.8.4-beta, installed). It was validated by tools/hwreport/validate.mjs (report:valid) and committed unchanged to web/content/hardware/reports/ with its issue number in index.json. assets/hwreport/snapshot.json was rebuilt from 3 reports (15 device entries; to be signed with tools/release/sign-hwsnapshot.sh). Its one limit is a worn battery (48% health); the touchpad problem reported separately (#43) is fixed in this version. hwreport_test.mjs now accepts the x.y.z.w versions the catalogue and hwsnap.c already accepted (#42)
- Store → Remote access now has two third-party apps, Tailscale (#68) and RustDesk (#66), for amd64 and arm64, and the section appears in the sidebar. Tailscale installs from Tailscale's official signed APT repository (pkgs.tailscale.com/stable/debian, suite trixie) with Tailscale's key pinned in apt/keys/tailscale.asc (2596 A99E AAB3 3821 893C 0A79 458C A832 957F 5868); updates come from Tailscale, and installing it enables and starts tailscaled. RustDesk 1.5.1 is the maker's .deb from its GitHub release, checked against a pinned SHA-256 per architecture and mirrored in LordOS's signed repository. On LordOS it connects to other computers; being reached from another computer is not supported, by design. Summaries are in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French and Italian, and there is a new kind label, 'Private network (VPN)'.
- docs/UPDATES.md records the maintainer scripts of tailscale 1.104.5, tailscale-archive-keyring and rustdesk 1.5.1. It also explains how the firewall treats tailscaled (a system service, outside per-app rules) and tailnet addresses (100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 count as local network for app rules), how MagicDNS goes through systemd-resolved, and why RustDesk can't be reached from another computer on LordOS. store-search-test now also checks that every catalog kind and section has its label in every locale (#66, #68).
- Automatic screen rotation for tablets and convertibles (#60, #61). lord-server reads the IIO accelerometer directly from sysfs (in_accel_{x,y,z}_raw with scale and offset), with no extra service or library. It applies the mount matrix from the systemd hwdb (ACCEL_MOUNT_MATRIX), or else the driver's in_mount_matrix, and skips a sensor in a keyboard base. Reads run every 0.4 s on a small thread, only while the option is on and the screen is lit. An edge counts as up past 35° of tilt and stays up until it falls under 20°. A new position must hold 0.9 s, and lying flat, a corner or shaking changes nothing. The orientation is added to the built-in panel's chosen rotation, without the Keep countdown, and is never saved. Settings → Displays shows a new 'Rotate automatically' switch for the built-in display only when an accelerometer exists. It is saved as autoRotate in displays.json and is on by default for tablet, convertible and detachable chassis. New lord.display.setAutoRotate(); lord.display.list() reports accelerometer, autoRotate and per-output autoRotation.
- **Files → Network starts with a 'Connected' group**: mounted shares and remote folders (Open, Open in New Tab, Keep in Locations, Disconnect), servers kept in Locations that are not connected (dimmed, connected only when clicked, so Files never reconnects anything at startup) and Cloud accounts (Open, Cloud settings). Found machines follow under 'On this network' (#59).
- every one-line text field (SDK TextInput) has a caret that ←, →, Home, End and a mouse click move. Typing, Backspace, Delete and paste work at the caret, so a typo in a server address no longer means retyping it (sdk/textfieldmodel.js, new textfield_model_test) (#59).
- Settings → Desktop & Dock → Menu Bar (Taskbar in Lord Classic) can hide Cleaner's crown (the same switch as Cleaner → Settings), the keyboard layout indicator, the on-screen keyboard's button, the notifications bell and the calendar in the clock's panel, in both themes. The choices are kept in settings.menuBar and are on unless turned off, so existing settings need no migration (sdk/menubarmodel.js) (#58).
- Lord Flow's Control Center has new Wi-Fi and Bluetooth tiles. Bluetooth has an on/off switch, both tiles open their Settings page, and each appears only with that hardware. Settings → Desktop & Dock → Control Center can turn off the processor and memory meters, the network and VPN tile, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (#58).
- choosing the audio output next to the volume, in Lord Flow's Control Center and Lord Classic's quick settings. With more than one output, a chevron lists them; a click makes that output the default (the same call as Settings → Sound), and PipeWire brings back that output's own volume (sdk/soundoutputs.js) (#58).
- in Lord Flow, a click on the clock opens the notifications (Do Not Disturb, Clear all) and a month calendar, as in Lord Classic, and a bell next to the clock shows a dot for unread notifications (#58).
- **Settings → Default Apps → Calendar (text/calendar). A day in either theme's clock calendar opens the chosen app**: LordOS Calendar on that day, or another app such as Thunderbird. Only apps that declare text/calendar itself are offered, not every text/* editor (#58).
- Settings → Wallpaper → Thumbnail size, a Small–Large slider for the built-in, Your pictures and dynamic wallpaper grids (80–240 px) (#58).
- Mail's folder sidebar has disclosure triangles. A folder with subfolders opens and closes like a file tree, a closed folder adds the unread mail it hides to its own count, and the open or closed state is kept per account in the accounts file (`collapsed`), so Mail shows the same tree at the next launch (#51).
- accounts can be disconnected from Calendar and Contacts. A ⋯ menu (or right click) on a synced account's header offers Account Settings… and Remove Account…, which open Mail's accounts panel on that account. Removing now asks for confirmation and says what goes: the mail, calendars and contacts downloaded to this computer and the keyring password, with nothing deleted on the server. The panel also shows a CalDAV/CardDAV account's user, URLs and what it syncs (#50).
- Dock "When covered" hiding mode for the Lord Flow theme (#46). Settings → Desktop & Dock → "Hide the Dock" is now a choice of Never, When covered or Always (it was an on/off toggle). With "When covered", the Dock stays visible on an empty desktop. It slides away 300 ms after a window covers its resting area and comes back as soon as nothing covers it. The pointer at the screen edge still shows it over the windows, and it leaves 500 ms after the pointer moves away. The windows that count are on the current desktop and not minimized or picture-in-picture. Each is checked at the frame it is drawn with (a maximized window fills its work area), and a fullscreen window covers its whole display. LordOS apps and Linux (Wayland/X11) windows count the same way. A window on another display never covers the Dock, which stays on the main display. The setting is stored as the existing dockAutohide plus a new dockIntellihide key, so no migration is needed. Meta+Alt+D toggles between Never and the chosen hiding mode. The pure overlap logic (dockCovered, dockHideMode, dockHideSettings in sdk/dockmodel.js) is covered by server/tests/dock_model_test.mjs.
- **Lithuanian (Lietuvių) as the first partial language (meta.json "partial"**: true). It covers the login screen, the desktop (menu bar, Dock, Control Center, power dialogs, clipboard, search, window menus), Files, the installer, About, app names, file dialogs, and Settings' section names, Language & Region and Date & Time: 961 of 11,075 keys (8.7%), with the rest in English. It comes with a Lithuanian plural rule (`lithuanian`) and its own format.json: «2026 m. lapkričio 8 d., sekmadienis», 2026-11-08, 24 hours, «1 234 567,89» (#45).
- partial languages. Settings → Language & Region marks them "partly translated" in Preferred languages and in the + list. `node tools/i18n-check.mjs` prints a partial language's coverage and its complete and started namespaces instead of failing on missing keys, but variables must still match (#45).
- **Screenshots**: a window capture (❖⇧4, then Space) keeps the window's rounded shape. The corners outside the frame are transparent (PNG alpha, also when copied to the clipboard) instead of showing the wallpaper. App windows record the radius the theme draws them with (`wm.cornerRadius`), and `media.crop` takes an optional radius applied by the new `img_round_corners` (antialiased, premultiplied). The shadow is left out, as other desktops do. (#70)
- **Displays**: scales up to 300 % (was 200 %), for 4K laptop panels (a 3840 × 2160 panel at 300 % is a 1280 × 720 desktop). Settings → Displays offers every 25 % step that still leaves a 1024 × 600 desktop (always 100–200 %), as five tiles spread over that range that always include the current and the recommended scale, and as the full list. A scale in `displays.json` that is out of range or not on a 25 % step is no longer silently replaced by the recommended one: lord-server uses the nearest valid scale and logs a warning. The scale recommended from the EDID stays at most 200 %, so displays without a saved scale keep their scale after the update. The pointer is still drawn at most 64 px (the cursor plane). (#47)
- **CPU microcode updates on amd64**: `intel-microcode` and `amd64-microcode` (Debian's non-free-firmware) are in the live ISO and a `Depends` of the `lordos` package on amd64, so the update to 0.8.8.6 installs them where they were missing (they load on the next boot). Without them the kernel kept the BIOS's microcode, often years old: an i9-10900 on a 2022 BIOS ran revision `0xec` and the kernel reported MMIO Stale Data, SRBDS and GDS as "Vulnerable: no microcode".
- **Screenshots: a magnifier and a color picker.** While selecting an area, a magnifier follows the pointer on the display it is on: the capture's 15 × 15 pixels around it enlarged eight times with a pixel grid, the middle pixel's color as #RRGGBB and its coordinates in the capture; C copies that color and ends. The panel (❖⇧5) has a Color mode: a click copies the color under the pointer. While a selection is open, Esc, Space and C are taken by the shortcut dispatcher, so they no longer reach the app under it as well (a Space or a C was typed into a Terminal behind the overlay). `media.pixels(id, x, y, w, h)` reads up to 64 × 64 RGBA pixels of a screenshot or picture (`server/src/ui/js_media.c`); the enlarging is done in `apps/screenshots/geometry.js` (`server/tests/screenshots_model_test.mjs`, 30 checks).
- **Terminal: Claude Code's context and plan limits in the status bar.** While Claude Code runs in a pane, the status bar shows `✳ Claude Code · Opus 5.5 · ● working · ctx ▰▱▱▱▱ 24% · 5h 37% · week 61%`, in the same height: whether it is working or waiting for you, the context window used, and the plan's 5-hour and weekly limits (green, amber past 50 %, red past 80 %; a narrow window drops the model, then the week, then the 5 hours). A click on a percentage shows the exact tokens, when each limit resets and the estimated cost. Working or waiting comes from `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, matched to the pane's foreground process (`term.info().fgPid`, new). The context and limits come from Claude Code's status line JSON, after **Connect**: it asks, then puts the new `lord-claude-status` (`server/src/term/claudebridge.c`, no libraries) in front of the user's status line command in `~/.claude/settings.json`, keeping everything else and a `settings.json.lordos-backup`; Disconnect restores the original command. The bridge keeps the JSON as `~/.cache/lordos/claude/<session>.json` (0600, checked session ids, no links followed, a week kept) and runs the user's command with the same input, so Claude Code's own status line doesn't change. lord-server runs nothing; the Terminal only reads those files. Tests: `terminal_claude_test.mjs` (39 checks, including that a wrapped command prints what the original did) and `claude_bridge_test.sh` (12), both in `make test`; checked in an isolated session (the segments, the details, Connect and Disconnect giving the original file back).
- **Voice, phase 1: `say` and its engine, lord-tts.** Text to speech on the computer, without the internet, with a `say` command: `say "Hola"`, `echo texto | say`, `say -f notas.txt -o notas.wav`, `say -l en|es|pt`, `say -v <voice>`, `say -b auto|cpu|gpu`, `say --voices`. Speech comes from Kyutai's **Pocket TTS** (weights CC-BY-4.0: usable, redistributable and commercial with credit) through **audio.cpp** (Apache-2.0) and its ggml, on the CPU (kernels for every x86-64 generation, picked when it starts) or the GPU (Vulkan; the RX 580 works). A voice is cloned from a short WAV; English carries one (alba). `say` cleans terminal colors and control characters out of the text and sends it a sentence at a time, each one playing through PipeWire while the next is synthesized: on an i9-10900 with an RX 580, about 10 s of speech in 1.3 s on the GPU and 3 s on the CPU, using 220 MB. **Off by default: no voice model ships with LordOS** (Settings → AI → Voice comes in phase 3). The engine is **lord-tts** (`server/src/doc/h_tts.c` on lord-doc's helper loop), the only binary that links audio.cpp and ggml (`/usr/lib/lordos/lib/tts`); `say` (`lord-say`, `server/src/tts/`) has no speech code. Its sandbox reads `/usr`, its libraries and the models folder it gets as an fd, writes only `~/.cache/lordos/voice`, has no network, sockets, fork or exec; on the GPU only, it opens the render node with DRM ioctls and may list `/dev/dri` without opening anything else in it (`list_dirs`, a new Landlock read-dir-only rule in `sandbox.c`), never `card0`. A voice file is untrusted: its WAV reader checks every size. audio.cpp is fetched at a pinned commit by `tools/tts/fetch-audiocpp.sh` and built with Pocket TTS only (`server/mk/tts.mk`); the package depends on `libvulkan1`, `libgomp1` and `libstdc++6` when it ships lord-tts, and `/usr/bin/say` is an alternative. Tests: `saytext_test.c` (14, in `make test`) and `tts_test.sh` (17: speech in es/en/pt on the CPU and the GPU, the confinement in both modes, a voice file that isn't audio, a voice name that is a path), with `doc-test selftest-tts`. docs/VOICE.md.
- **Voice: no more hiss under a sentence.** Now and then Pocket TTS made a sentence with a bed of broadband noise under the voice, heard as a rough, "saturated" start; it depends on the sentence and the random seed, not on the GPU (the CPU made the same) or on loading the model (the same sentence repeated after loading came out the same). lord-tts now measures each sentence (`server/src/tts/hiss.c`: the median share of the energy between 6 and 11 kHz over the spoken frames; clean speech is about -27 to -30 dB, a noisy sentence -25 or more) and, above -26 dB, makes it again with another seed, at most twice, keeping the cleanest. A clean sentence costs nothing more; a noisy one on the RX 580 adds about 0.4 s per try. A try the model ended early never wins for being cleaner ("Hola, LordOS ya puede leer en voz alta." came out as just "Hola"): one under 60 % of the longest try, or faster than 7.5 syllables a second (whole sentences measure 3.8–7.4), is set aside, and when every try is cut the longest is kept (`tts_cut_short`, `tts_syllables`). Test: `hiss_test.c` (15, in `make test`).
- **Voice, phase 3: voices you choose, HD quality, your own voice and Live Speech.** **Settings → AI → Voice** now downloads and removes everything: per language (Spanish, English, Portuguese) the **Standard** model (128 MB, fast anywhere) and the **HD** one (Kyutai's 24-layer model: 672 MB, English 1.3 GB; more natural), and **23 voices**, each speaking every language, 11 female and 12 male. **▶ plays a recorded sample** of any voice before it is downloaded; Download shows a progress bar; Try, Use and Remove for those installed; Quality: Automatic (HD when installed), Standard or HD. Lola is Spanish's default, Rafael Portuguese's and Alba English's. They come as **signed LordOS packages** from the signed APT repository (`lordos-voice-<lang>[-hd]`, `lordos-voice-<lang>-<voice>[-hd]`, `lordos-voice-previews`; `tools/voice/`, reproducible), never from Hugging Face: only voices whose recordings allow redistribution and commercial use (Kyutai's own, voice-zero CC0, Alba McKenna and VCTK CC-BY-4.0; EARS's jean, non-commercial, and three voices of undocumented origin are left out). **Personal Voice**: your own voice in about a minute, ready at once and used in every language: read six short phrases one at a time (each stops by itself when read), or **speak freely** 15–30 s about anything, for anyone reading aloud is hard for; the room is checked first (too noisy, or a microphone that sends nothing, says so), the consent asked before anything is recorded, the recording kept only in your account. **Use a recording…** does the same from an audio file (WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, Opus or FLAC). **Live Speech** (❖⇧Esc): type, Enter, and it is said with your voice; recent phrases can be said again. **Spanish sounds right now**: checked against Kyutai's own Python code, lord-tts now does what it does and audio.cpp didn't: temperature 0.3 for every language (audio.cpp used 0.7 outside English, which made Spanish drag and stumble) and the model's character replacements before speaking (`¡ ¿ « »`, quotes and brackets dropped, curly apostrophes and dashes changed). Speech starts at once: the model's 0.3–0.9 s of silence at the start (Kyutai's code has it too) is cut. `say -v <voice>`, `say -q auto|standard|hd`, `say --voices` by language and quality, `say --preview <lang> <voice>`. How: lord-tts reads Kyutai's HD folders with audio.cpp's own description of the model (`lib/tts/pocket_tts_dir.json`, made at build time) and accepts only the three HD language names; `lord.voice.speak(text, lang, voice)` and `lord.voice.preview(lang, voice)` pass only plain names to lord-say. Tests: `voicecatalog_test.mjs` (21), `voicerec_model_test.mjs` (20), `hiss_test.c` (15), `tts_test.sh` passes with the new engine. docs/VOICE.md.
- **Voice, phase 2: read aloud anywhere, with a player.** Everywhere there is text there is **Speech**: *Edit → Speech* in the Text Editor and the Terminal (Notes: View) and in the **right-click** menu of the Text Editor, the Terminal and Notes, with *Start Speaking*, *Stop Speaking* and *Save as Audio…*; Start Speaking reads the selection, or the whole text when nothing is selected. A **Linux app** (Firefox, foot…) gets an *Edit* menu with Speech in the menu bar (Lord Classic: its window's menu strip) that reads its own selection. **❖Esc** reads what the window in front has selected and, pressed again, stops. While it reads, a small **player** shows the voice's **wave in color** (16 bands from 80 Hz to 8 kHz, measured by `say` as it plays and kept in step with what is heard; still in a pause), with ↻ read again, ⏸/▶ pause and go on, ■ stop and ✕ stop and close; drag it by its grip anywhere, also to another display, and the next reading opens there (a display that is gone falls back to the main one). **Save as Audio…** asks where with the save dialog (the Music folder, the name from the first words) and makes a WAV without a sound. The language is told from the text (Spanish, English or Portuguese), else the interface's. **Settings → AI → Voice** (new page): *Read aloud* (Speech and ❖Esc go away without it; `say` keeps working), *Keyboard shortcut ❖Esc*, *Show the player*, all on by default, and *Process with* Automatic / Processor / Graphics card. Without a voice model, a notice says so. How: lord-server starts `lord-say` (`server/src/tts/speak.c`, `lord.voice` in `ui/js_voice.c`; a new exception in AGENTS.md) from the fixed path next to it, never with the text in its arguments (stdin is a sealed memfd), with every one of its fds closed, a minimal environment and its own process group (stop is SIGTERM, a pause SIGSTOP/SIGCONT to the group); `say --levels` writes the wave's bands on fd 3 (`server/src/tts/levels.c`) and `say -o -` writes a WAV to stdout. A Linux app's primary selection never reaches JS: the compositor keeps who made it and reads it only while that app has the keyboard. Saving checks the path as `lord.fs.write` does and wants `.wav`; lord-server opens the folder, creates the file there with `O_EXCL` and renames it when `say` ends well, so `say` never sees a path. The right-click menu with submenus moved from Files to the SDK (`sdk/contextmenu.jsx`), now shared by Files, the Terminal, the Text Editor and Notes. Isolated apps get no `lord.voice`. Tests: `levels_test.c` (9) and `voiceplayer_model_test.mjs` (17) in `make test`; `saytext_test.c` now 25 (telling the language); `tools/vm/e2e/ui.py` gained `down:`/`up:` to drag. docs/VOICE.md.
- **Markup editor: Transcribe.** A Ⓣ button next to Undo in the markup editor (after a capture, and on any picture opened from Photos or Files' Quick Preview): drag over text and it is copied to the clipboard, or click once to copy all the text in the picture. It reads the picture itself, not the arrows or boxes drawn on it, with the same sandboxed `lord-ocr` and languages as ❖⇧4 then T; the area shows as a blue box while dragged and is never kept as an annotation. `apps/screenshots/editor.jsx`; the area's math in `ocr.js` (`transcribeRect`, 4 checks in `screenshots_model_test.mjs`, 40 in all); checked in an isolated session (a drag over one line copied just that line, accents included; a click copied both lines).
- **Screenshots stay on the clipboard as well.** A capture (❖⇧3, ❖⇧4, the panel) is saved to `~/Pictures/Screenshots` and copied to the clipboard too, so it can be pasted right away: ❖V in a Terminal (or Ctrl+V in Claude Code) types its path, which Claude Code attaches as `[Image #n]`. With ❖⇧3 on several displays, the first display's file is the one on the clipboard. The panel's toggle is now "Only copy to the clipboard (don't save)" (the same setting: on, nothing is saved, as before).
- **Screenshots: copy the text in a selection (OCR).** While selecting an area, T switches to text mode (the panel, ❖⇧5, has a Text mode too): drag over any text on any display and it is read and copied to the clipboard, with a toast saying how many characters ("No text found" when there is none). It reads in the interface's languages first, then English, Spanish, Portuguese, French and Italian (so accents survive with an English interface; about 0.3 s a selection). The recognition runs in a new sandboxed helper, `lord-ocr` (`server/src/doc/h_ocr.c`): lord-doc's helper loop built with Tesseract only, the only binary that links libtesseract. It receives the cropped pixels in a sealed memfd, never a path, reads only `/usr` (the language data), has no network, sockets, fork or exec, runs one thread, and lord-server never waits for it (`media.ocr(id, langs)`, through the lord-doc session thread). The picture is turned to gray, made dark-on-light and enlarged twice before reading, so a screen's small text reads well (a Terminal line in about 200 ms). Language names are checked in lord-server and again in the helper. The `lordos` package depends on `libtesseract5` and `tesseract-ocr-eng` when it ships `lord-ocr`, and recommends Spanish, Portuguese, French and Italian; the ISO and the Raspberry Pi image include all five. Tests: `server/tests/ocr_test.sh` (a picture LordOS rendered, "Configuración rápida: año, niño, acción" read exactly; bad and missing languages; the confinement: no `~/.ssh`, no home folder, no writing `/tmp`, no network, no sockets, no fork), in `make test-full`, and the language choice in `screenshots_model_test.mjs` (35 checks).
- **Screenshots on every display**: ❖⇧3 saves one file per display, each at its own resolution, and ❖⇧4 opens the selection on all of them at once (a capture and an overlay per display, one shared selection that stays inside the display it began on), with a crosshair across the display and the pointer's coordinates; Space still switches to picking a window on any display. Before, both took only the main display unless Settings → Displays → "Screenshots and sharing" was set to all displays. `media.screenshot(app, { display: id })` captures one display (`server/src/media/capture.c`); `apps/screenshots/geometry.js` and `server/tests/screenshots_model_test.mjs` (23 checks).
- **Terminal: files and images go in as their paths**: a file dragged from Files onto a pane is pasted as its shell-quoted path (a generic `onFilesDrop` prop: Files hands a drop outside its own targets to the window under the pointer), and ❖V with an image on the clipboard pastes the image file's path; in Claude Code Ctrl+V does the same (it looks for images with xclip or wl-paste, which don't reach LordOS's clipboard). Claude Code attaches a pasted image path as an image, so a ❖⇧4 area capture copied to the clipboard goes straight into it (`apps/terminal/paths.js`, `server/tests/terminal_paths_test.mjs`).
- **Claude Code's status line from LordOS**: `lord-claude-status` (what the Terminal's Connect puts in `~/.claude/settings.json`), with no status line of the user's to wrap, now prints LordOS's own instead of nothing, with the footer's numbers in one line: `Opus 5.5 | LordOS | main | ctx 11% | 5h 37% | sem 5%` (model, folder, git branch read from `.git/HEAD` without running git, worktrees included, context used, the plan's 5-hour and weekly limits, labels in the user's language; control characters and `|` from the input are left out). A user's own status line still runs unchanged. A subscriber's 5-hour window now shows as `5h –` in the line and the footer while Claude Code leaves it out (its status line JSON drops a window once it resets, and may omit one) instead of vanishing. `server/tests/claude_bridge_test.sh` covers the line.
- **Terminal: a color per tab** from the tab's right-click menu (with Edit Tab Title and Close Tab), over its profile's; a colored tab is tinted whole instead of a thin line under it.
- **Terminal: the status bar names Claude Code** (✳ Claude Code in its color) when it is the running program, instead of the process name.
- **Save to Passwords from the Terminal**: a password you type (or paste) when ssh, sftp, scp, rsync, mysql, psql, redis-cli, mongosh or git asks, once the program accepts it, is offered for saving ("Save the password for ssh ec2-user@host in Passwords?"), in the SSH, Database, Internet or Network category with its host, port and user, tagged Terminal and the program. lord-server keeps it in one locked page (mlock, MADV_DONTDUMP), wipes it on every way out (rejected, Ctrl+C, no Enter, declined, saved, closed, 60 s), never captures the user's own login password (sudo, su, passwd, pkexec…) or anything while traced, and sends it to lord-vault on the private channel; JS gets only the program, host, user and a random token. The program and host come from the asking process's own `/proc` arguments, and the Passwords bar now says which program asks, so a script printing a fake prompt shows as itself (`server/src/term/tcapture.c`, `build/term-capture-test` 28 checks, also under ASan/UBSan; `terminal_secret_test.mjs` 16). Approved as a security exception in AGENTS.md.
- **Passwords in the Terminal**: when ssh, sudo, git or gpg asks for a password, a bar offers your Passwords logins (the ones for that host first) or **Type It**. The picked password goes from `lord-vault` to the terminal in `lord-server`'s C code on the private channel and never passes through JavaScript, the screen or the session log; it is written only while the program is still asking. Detected from the pty itself (echo off with line input) and a prompt that names a password (`server/src/term/tsecret.c`, `termfill.c`; `build/term-secret-test` on a real pty, 10 checks; `server/tests/terminal_secret_test.mjs`, 9). Approved as a security exception in AGENTS.md.
- **Monitor → Memory says what is using it**: the memory in use is split into **Apps** (what programs hold: `AnonPages + Shmem`) and **System and drivers** (the rest: the kernel's tables and buffers, the graphics driver's), and a new **Using the most memory** card lists the 8 apps holding the most, each app's processes added up (a browser's tabs, LordOS's helpers) with their count (`apps/monitor/memtop.js`, `server/tests/monitor_memtop_test.mjs`).
- **Shake the pointer to find it** (Settings → Mouse & Trackpad, on by default): a few quick left-right strokes with the mouse or the trackpad make the cursor grow for a moment toward 200 %, the largest the cursor plane takes, and shrink back half a second after you stop. The detector (`server/src/shake.c`) is pure logic with its own test, `build/shake-test` (12 checks: quick strokes grow it; short, slow, vertical or single long moves don't).
- **Command-line tools, the same in every image**: `curl`, `wget`, `rsync`, `screen`, `htop`, `vim`, `mc`, `tcpdump`, `net-tools`, `fdisk`, `rfkill` and `jq` (JSON on the command line; Claude Code status line scripts use it), from one list (`tools/iso/packages-tools.sh`) that the live ISO and the Raspberry Pi image both read, and Recommends of the `lordos` package, so the update brings them. Before, the ISO had no `curl` or `wget`, and `rsync`, `fdisk` and `rfkill` were only in the Raspberry Pi image.
- **The SSH server in the live ISO, off**, as in the Raspberry Pi image: `openssh-server` and `openssh-sftp-server` are installed with `ssh.service` and `ssh.socket` disabled and no host keys in the image (every computer installed from it would share them). Settings → Sharing → Remote login makes this computer's keys and turns it on for good, without downloading anything. The ISO also has `bluez-firmware` (Broadcom Bluetooth chips), like the Pi image.

### Fixed

- **The voice engine builds on arm64** (Raspberry Pi 5, generic arm64): lord-tts's seccomp allow list named `SYS_mkdir`, `SYS_rename`, `SYS_unlink`, `SYS_rmdir` and `SYS_readlink`, which only x86-64 has, so `lord-tts` didn't compile for aarch64. They are now listed only where they exist; aarch64's C library uses the `*at` calls, already allowed. Nothing more is allowed than before.
- **`make` builds the voice again**: `lord-say`, `lord-tts` and `pocket_tts_dir.json` were added to `ALL` in `server/mk/tts.mk`, which the Makefile includes after reading `all: $(ALL)`, so a plain `make` never built them and `tools/iso/mkdeb.sh` stopped on the missing `lord-say`. They are now prerequisites of `all` directly, as the other `mk/*.mk` do.
- **Bluetooth: a paired mouse or keyboard reconnects at boot, at the login screen** ([#75](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/75)). bluetoothd only lets a returning device in without asking if it is Trusted; at the login screen no agent runs, so a paired device that wasn't trusted (a pairing that reported an error after the bond was made, or a device paired with other tools) was turned away until someone logged in. LordOS now also trusts a paired device when it answers `AlreadyExists` to Pair, when you connect it, and when it uses a service in your session (`bt_should_trust`, `build/bt-test`). The Bluetooth switch (Settings, Control Center, Quick Settings) is now remembered (`bluetoothOff` in settings.json): BlueZ powers the adapter at every boot, which a mouse at the login screen needs, and your session turns it off again at login if you left it off. The ISO enables `bluetooth.service` explicitly, as the Raspberry Pi image does. No change to `/etc/bluetooth`: BlueZ 5.82's defaults (AutoEnable on, ClassicBondedOnly on) are right.
- **Cloud: browsing an account no longer waits for the provider** ([#71](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/71)). rclone listed a folder from the provider again on the first read once its 5-minute listing had expired, and Files waited for it; Files also re-listed the open folder every 4 seconds and asked its free space, which makes rclone ask the provider. Now the mounts keep a listing for an hour and follow the provider's changes every minute where it reports them (`ChangeNotify` from `operations/fsinfo`: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, pCloud). A folder Files shows is listed again in the background (`lord.cloud.browse`, through the allowed `vfs/refresh`) only when it is 5 minutes old on a provider without change notifications (WebDAV, S3, SFTP…), and its subfolders are listed ahead, so the next click doesn't wait. Files lists a cloud folder again when that background listing finishes or once a minute, and no longer asks its free space. Keep on This Computer's background re-listing of kept folders was refused by rclone ("recursive" sent as a JSON true) and never happened; it works now. Measured against a WebDAV server 250 ms away with 2,040 files: a subfolder opened the first time went from 256 ms to 5 ms, and the top of an account after 5 minutes from 377 ms to 43 ms.
- **LordOS Imager for other computers (`lordos_imager_*_x64_setup.exe`): no more PowerShell window popping up every two seconds** ([#73](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/73)). The app started `powershell.exe` (`Get-Disk`) to list drives on every 2 s poll without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, and as a window-subsystem program each start opened an empty console window over it, even as administrator. Every helper process now starts with no window (`drives::command`). The drive list also lists again only when the disks change (each `\\.\PhysicalDriveN` asked its size, no process) or every 30 s; a failed listing is retried after 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and then 60 s, never in a tight loop, and the app never runs two listings at once (a `setTimeout` chain instead of `setInterval`). A drive is still listed afresh right before it is written. Not compiled on this build host (no Rust toolchain): the next Imager build checks it (`cargo test -p lordos-imager-core`, `scripts/build-windows.sh`).
- **Terminal: a program keeps the window's size and all of its output.** Any other lord-server of the same user (a headless one for tests, for example) took the desktop's shells from their holders: it read part of their output (an ESC lost, so "[14G" printed and half a frame went missing) and set their size to its own windows (Claude Code drawing in 80 columns of a 260-column window). A holder now serves one lord-server at a time and holders live in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/lordos-term`; the pty's size comes only from the pane's logical box, the same at every display scale and in the overview or minimize, and a pane too small for one cell no longer sends 2×1; the pty's size is read back while output arrives and set again if anything else changed it; and the parser no longer drops an ESC or a control byte after the ESC that ends an OSC or an APC. Shells opened before the update keep their old holder until they are reopened. `build/term-resize-test` (29 checks: a Claude-Code-like frame cut at every byte and resized at every cut, the grid at 18 scales, the holder handover).
- **Monitor and firewall: a running virtual machine's network traffic now belongs to Machines.** QEMU and passt run in the machine's own scope (`app-lordos-lordos-vm-<id>.scope`), which lord-netperm and Monitor read as an app with no `.desktop` file, so the guest's connections showed up as an app named "?" with no icon, and a rule for Machines didn't reach them. The scope now maps to `lordos:machines` (`fw_scope_app`, shared by lord-netperm and Monitor), so the kernel applies the Machines rule to the guest. lord-netperm adds up the counters of every scope that shares an app and keeps their rules installed while any of them runs. Monitor also maps the scope's `qemu`/`passt` leaves and names the row "Machines · <machine name>" with the Machines icon; the row is now called "Machines" (not "Machines downloads") and its hint says the rule covers running machines too.
- Firefox and other GTK and libadwaita apps that draw their own title bar showed only a close button, on the right, when they couldn't read LordOS's settings: an app restricted to "no access to your files", one started outside the session, or one running on X11 (Xwayland). Debian's default for that layout is 'appmenu:close'. The lordos package now ships a GSettings schema override (/usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas/90_lordos.gschema.override, compiled by GLib's dpkg trigger) and /etc/gtk-3.0/settings.ini and /etc/gtk-4.0/settings.ini (gtk-decoration-layout), both with Lord Flow's close,minimize,maximize:. They are defaults only: a layout the user or the theme stored still wins, and Lord Classic's right-hand layout still applies live through the keyfile and the settings portal. New files, so no migration. Tested by server/tests/gtk_defaults_test.mjs (16 checks: compiled with --strict next to Debian's schema and read back with gsettings, a stored value still wins, and the override, settings.ini, sdk/theme.js and portal.c agree) (#52)
- the Store's Remote access intro said the section's apps reach this computer from another one, with each visitor accepted at the computer. It now describes what the section offers: apps that reach other computers or join a private network, which are not LordOS's Remote Desktop on port 5673. It also says that some of them install a system service that starts with the computer and isn't held to the per-app firewall (tailscaled, and RustDesk's root rustdesk.service, which its package always enables) (#66, #68).
- A touchscreen now follows its screen's rotation, whether set by hand in Settings → Displays or automatically (#60). Taps, drags, two-finger scroll and pinch land under the finger on a turned panel. Before, only an absolute pen tablet was mapped back, and only with a single display; a multitouch screen kept its unrotated coordinates.
