- Files → Network no longer lists every device that answered on the LAN. Wi-Fi repeaters, printers and other devices with nothing to open are hidden, the status line says how many, and the page's right-click menu has 'Show every device' (settings.files.netAllDevices) (#59).
- Connect to Server no longer sends WebDAV addresses written as http:// or https:// to the browser. A path that names WebDAV (/dav, /webdav, /remote.php/…) opens as a Files folder (rclone mount as webdav:// or davs://), and any other http(s) address asks 'Open as a folder' or 'Open in the browser' (#59).
- the default app for a MIME type now comes first from the category that lists that exact type, then from the family, so text/calendar no longer falls to the text editor's category (sdk/defaults.js) (#58).
- when adding a mail or calendar-and-contacts (CalDAV/CardDAV, cloud preset) account fails because of a wrong password, an unreachable server or a certificate, the result screen offers Edit Details. It removes the half-made account and returns to the form with every field as typed (servers set by hand are kept). Remove Account there now also removes the companion calendar account instead of leaving an orphan, and a re-added account no longer shows the previous attempt's "wrong password" (#50).
- a region whose language LordOS has no translation for (English with lt_LT, de_DE, pl_PL…) used the interface language's formats, so it showed a 12-hour clock and month/day/year. LordOS now reads the region's clock, numeric date order and number separators from glibc's own locale data (LC_TIME and LC_NUMERIC through a new read-only lord.locale.formats, converted in sdk/regionformat.js). Isolated apps receive the same data with the language (#45).
- with no region chosen in Settings, formats followed the interface language even when the computer was installed for another region. The region is now the session's LANG: the user's ~/.config/locale.conf, which the installer writes, else /etc/default/locale. The login screen follows the computer's region, also when it changes while the screen is shown, so a computer set to lt_LT shows 24-hour time there too (#45).
- the installer's default region for a language outside its built-in list was en_US; it is now the language's own region from its meta.json (lt → lt_LT) (#45).
- **Displays**: the pointer now follows the display scale up to 300 % (80 px at 250 %, 96 px at 300 %), multiplied by the Pointer size setting. Before, it was capped at 200 % (64 px), so on a 4K panel at 250-300 % it looked smaller than at 200 %. When the pointer is larger than the GPU's hardware cursor plane (64 px on many drivers), lord-server draws it in the composition while it lasts and logs 'gpu: a WxH pointer is larger than the cursor plane (…): drawn in the composition'; it goes back to the plane when it fits again (`kms_cursor_fits`, `update_cursor`). Big cursors from Linux apps (up to 256 px) take the same path instead of being replaced by the arrow. Shake to find it grows toward 200 %, and toward 300 % when the pointer is already 200 % or larger. New `build/cursor-test` (21 checks). (#47)
- **Screenshots**: a window capture (❖⇧4, Space, click) is now the window alone. Other windows, menus or the Dock that covered it are left out, and the covered parts show the window as it is, with the transparent rounded corners as before. lord-server paints the screen in capture mode up to the window's frame node and no further (`paint_capture_until`, ui/paint.c), so translucent and blurred parts of the window match the screen. `media.screenshot` takes it as `until` (`wm.frameNode(id)`). A window without a frame node falls back to cropping the still. Covered by a new engine-test case. (#70)
- **Settings → AI → Voice → Create a Personal Voice**: after a room check that was too noisy, "Check again" did nothing: no sound wave, no message, and reopening the sheet did not help. Every take was written to a fixed file name, lord-media never writes over a file, and the resulting media.fileExists error was swallowed. The same broke "Read again" on a phrase and every Personal Voice after the first. Each take now has its own name, every way out of a recording (done, too noisy, silent microphone, Cancel, closing the sheet, an error) releases the microphone and wipes the take, and errors are shown translated. A noisy room now says so in its title, gives the noise level and what to do, and offers "Try again" and "Go on anyway" in place.
- **Settings → AI → Voice → clone from a file**: a second file kept the first clip, because the conversion wrote to the same clone.wav and its failure was not checked. It now uses a new file each time and shows the error.
- **Screenshots**: the ❖⇧4 area selection (and the window, color and text modes started from ❖⇧5) now works with a sheet, alert, menu, system prompt, Live Speech or the voice player open. Before, with Settings → AI's "Create a Personal Voice" sheet open, you could not select over the sheet: the selection is a fullscreen window drawn in the `floating` layer, and the sheet (in the `modal` layer) stayed live on top of the still and took the clicks. The selection now goes in a new `capture` layer above every other one (`wm.setFullscreen(id, true, { capture: true })`). A press on it does not close or blur what is open under the still. Esc stays the selection's own key. While it shows, Linux apps lose the keyboard and close their open menus, as they do with a sheet. New `capture-layer-test` (11 checks). Its keyboard rule now counts the capture layer too (docs/LAYERS.md).
- **Lord Classic**: Lock Screen, Switch User, Log Out, Restart… and Shut Down… in the start menu's power menu did nothing, and the start menu's right-click menu (Open, Pin to Start, Pin to taskbar) did not work either. These menus are drawn in the popover layer, outside the start menu's own node, so the start menu treated a press on one of their rows as a press outside itself and closed. The menu closed with it before the click arrived. The start menu now counts a press in its open menu as a press inside itself. A new scene test (`classic_startmenu_power_test.mjs`) renders the real start menu and clicks the power rows (#48).
- **Remote desktop**: from a browser on another system, Ctrl no longer stays stuck after Ctrl+A, Ctrl+E or any other shortcut. Before, every later key carried Ctrl until logout, even after the remote connection was closed (#44). Some systems repeat a held Ctrl as more keydown events, the page sent each one as a new press, and xkbcommon counts the presses of a modifier, so the single release left Ctrl down. Now lord-server keeps the keys each viewer holds (`sw_held_key`, shared with the screen-sharing API). A press of a key that is already down becomes a repeat, and a release of a key it never saw go down is dropped. Whatever a viewer still holds is released when it disconnects. The page sends repeats as repeats. It releases its keys when it loses focus or is hidden, and it re-syncs Ctrl/Shift/Alt/Meta from each key or click, for when the system kept the release (Win+L, Alt+Tab). AltGr keeps working, and on a system that holds back key releases while Cmd is down, the keys pressed with Cmd go up with it. `share-test` (313 checks) and `remote-sec-test` cover the pairing and the parser (#44).
- **Mail**: account passwords are no longer lost at every boot when the session keyring is locked, for example with automatic login or after the login password was changed outside LordOS (#63). lord-maild asks the session for each account's password once. The session used to read a locked keyring as "no password" and never try again, and the Password needed sheet's "Save to Keyring" failed without saying so, so Mail asked again at every reboot. Now the session keeps those accounts waiting, shows the system keyring prompt once (3 s after the first account asks, so the login's own unlock is not taken for a locked keyring) and answers every waiting account as soon as the keyring opens: from the prompt, a screen unlock with the password, or the login itself. The keyring prompt closes by itself when the keyring opens by other means. The isolated Mail app clears an account's "password needed" mark once it connects. When a password cannot be kept, the sheet and Add Account say why (keyring locked, never created, or another error) and how to fix it, instead of closing as if it had been saved. The pure logic is in `sdk/mailauthmodel.js` with a node test (`server/tests/mail_auth_model_test.mjs`).
- **Touchpad**: Alps I2C touchpads handled by the hid-alps driver (044E:120B on the Dell Latitude 7480 and 5289, and others) now move the pointer with one finger and click with taps. The driver declares a pressure range of 0..64 but sends the sensor's raw 7-bit value (0..127), and T4 pads send a fixed 62, so LordOS took every firm finger for a palm. The pointer only moved after starting on the top or bottom edge, with three fingers, or for a few frames before stopping. On these pads palms are now recognised by the edges only, and any touchpad that reports a pressure above its declared maximum stops using pressure for palms (logged once). Other touchpads are unchanged. Covered by a new tp-test case built from the driver's report format (#43, #54, #67).
- **Keyboard**: the Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock lights now follow the keyboard state. lord-server holds the keyboards exclusively, so the console no longer lit them and nothing else did. It now writes the lights (EV_LED) to every keyboard that has them, including keyboards plugged in later or handed over again after a session switch (#67).
- **Dock**: the Files icon can now be moved like any other app. Drag it anywhere before the Trash on the Lord Flow Dock or the Lord Classic taskbar, and the launcher or another app can go first. Files still cannot be removed, the Trash stays last, and Reset Dock to defaults puts Files back in the first place. Before, sdk/dockmodel.js forced Files back to the front after every pin, move or settings read. Saved Dock orders are kept as they are. (#62)
- **Files**: Open With now lists the apps installed for .xlsx and the other office documents (.doc, .docx, .xls, .ods, .odp, .ppt, .pptx, .rtf, .epub), in the context menu and in Get Info, and a double-click opens the default app (for example WPS Spreadsheets as set with xdg-mime or mimeapps.list) instead of Quick Preview. Files used to match apps only against its own small type table, which had no entry for these files, so they were typed as application/octet-stream and no app matched. Files now also uses the system's MIME database (/usr/share/mime/globs2) to match apps, and the table covers every document, image, audio, video, archive and .deb extension Files knows. (#49)
- **Photos and the markup editor**: toolbar tooltips no longer appear behind the picture. A toolbar button's tooltip was drawn in place with a zIndex that only orders siblings, so anything the window drew after the toolbar (the picture, the editor's canvas) covered it. Tooltips now go through `<Overlay>` in the tooltip layer, above the whole window (in an isolated app, in the window's overlay host). (#72)
- **Lord Flow**: the ×, − and + shown on the traffic lights on hover are now exactly centred. They were text glyphs placed by font metrics, a little left of and below the centre. They are now bars drawn from the light's centre in a solid color, so the crossing of the × and + does not darken. Lord Classic already drew its window buttons as centred shapes. (#69)
- **Installer and Settings: every region glibc lists can be chosen** (#53). `/usr/share/i18n/SUPPORTED` names 175 UTF-8 regions without the codeset (`en_IN`, `en_IL`, `en_NG`, `ca_ES@valencia`…). The installer and Settings added `.UTF-8` at the end, and install-run, `locale-gen` and `system-locale` compared the result with the listed name exactly, so the install stopped with "Unsupported region". Modifier regions also became names glibc does not accept. The region is now kept without the codeset and sent as `xx_YY.UTF-8[@modifier]` (`sdk/localename.js`). The root side accepts both spellings of a listed region (`server/src/localename.h`). The installer's region list shows the country ("Australia · en_AU"), so a search by country finds it. The time zone list is sorted and shows all 312 zones; 13 were cut off before. `install-plan-test` checks every UTF-8 region and every zone in `zone1970.tab` against the root side; `localename_test` checks every region's round trip. Settings → Language & Region's region list names the country too ("Australia · en_AU"), as the installer's does, so a search by country finds it there as well.
- **The keyboard follows the computer, never a default Latin American layout** (#55). A user who never chose a keyboard typed with `latam`, the SDK's default, and `settings.json` saved that default as if it were a choice. After `install.sh` on a Debian system set to US or UK English, the desktop typed Latin American Spanish. Without a choice, the session now uses the computer's layout: `XKBLAYOUT`/`XKBVARIANT` in `/etc/default/keyboard` (`lord.keyboard.system()`), or US without that file. lord-server's first keymap uses the same file, and the login screen falls back to US. Settings migration 4 removes the saved `latam` default; a keyboard list the user chose is kept. Tests: `osk-test` and `keyboard_default_test`.
- **Emoji & Symbols: no more empty boxes** (#56). The font catalog stopped at 1024 font faces, in whatever order the folders were read. On a Debian desktop with many font packages it could stop before Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans and Noto Color Emoji, and every emoji and most symbols then drew a missing-glyph box. The catalog now holds 8192 faces. `lord.text.covered()` tells whether an installed font draws a character, and the emoji picker and the Emoji & Symbols window leave out characters no font draws. The `lordos` package also recommends `fonts-noto-color-emoji` and `fonts-dejavu-core`. `engine-test` checks the coverage.
- **GPU switches reach every session, and the log gives the cursor plane's size** (#57). `LORD_GPU=0` set in the service did reach new sessions. But `KillMode=process` keeps open sessions across `systemctl restart lordos`, so logging in returned to the session started before the change. lord-sessiond now logs this when it finds such a session. `docs/GPU.md` explains where these switches go (the kernel line or `systemctl edit lordos.service`, not `session.conf`) and to log out first. `LORD_SW_CURSOR=1` in the service, or `lordos.swcursor=1` on the kernel line, now reaches every session: it keeps the GPU without its cursor plane. The log line now reads `gpu: cursor by hardware (cursor plane, 128x128)`. The squashed pointer on a FirePro W6150M (Bonaire, radeon driver) is the same picture the cursor-plane fix above already addresses.
- **Cloud**: pCloud accounts in Europe work. `rclone authorize` was started without a config blob, so it printed only the token and dropped the API host that pCloud's sign-in returns for the account's region (`eapi.pcloud.com`). A European account then sent its token to `api.pcloud.com`, Files stayed empty, Settings → Cloud showed errors, and rclone logged "Invalid 'access_token' provided. (2094)" on every call. lord-server now passes `{}` as a config blob (`e30`), reads the base64 options rclone returns and saves `hostname` with the account; a client's id or secret and any option refused by name are never taken from that output. pCloud's "Invalid 'access_token'" and OAuth's `invalid_token` now show Sign In Again, which also fixes an existing account (#71).
- **Cloud**: adding the `iclouddrive` rclone account now says up front to use the account's regular password with its code, not an app-specific password, which rclone's backend for that drive refuses. A refused password repeats the note under the error, and the drive's "incorrect username or password" counts as a refused password and highlights the field (#65).
- **Cloud**: in the top-bar panel, Pause All changes to Resume All once it takes effect, also when an account has an error or needs a sign-in. Before, the button looked only at the accounts' states, and an error is shown before "paused" (#71).
- **Cloud**: the three buttons of the top-bar panel wrap a long label (French "Tout mettre en pause", "Afficher dans Fichiers") inside the button instead of running past it (#71).
- **The live ISO's boot menu shows all eight entries**: with *Install automatically* it had eight, and the theme had room for seven, so the last could not be seen or reached by sight (GRUB's theme has no scrollbar). The menu is 410 px high with 12 px between lines; `server/tests/livestart_test.mjs` counts them as GRUB does.
- **A new Terminal tab ran the imported profile's command**: importing another terminal's profiles could make the default a profile that types a command when it opens (an `ssh …`), so every [+] ran it. Such a profile is no longer made the default by an import, and settings migration 3 makes a plain profile the default where it happened (a new Default one if there is none); the imported profile stays under New Tab with Profile.
- **Shift+Enter in the Terminal** (a new line in Claude Code instead of sending the message): the terminal now speaks the keyboard protocols programs ask for, the kitty keyboard protocol's flag 1 ("disambiguate": CSI > u push, CSI < u pop, CSI = u set, CSI ? u query, a stack per screen) and xterm's modifyOtherKeys (CSI > 4 ; 2 m). With one on, Enter, Tab, Backspace and Escape with modifiers, and Ctrl or Alt with a character, get their own sequences (Shift+Enter is `CSI 13;2u`, or `CSI 27;2;13~`); without, they stay as before, where Shift+Enter is a plain CR. `build/vt-keys-test` checks it (24 checks).
- **Terminal keys on a non-US keyboard**: importing another terminal's profiles brought the numeric keypad's entries (keypad `-`, `/`, `*`, `+`, `.`, digits, Enter) onto the main keys, which the Terminal names by their US position, so on a Latin American keyboard `-` typed `/`, `'` typed `-` and Shift+8 typed `*`. Keypad entries are no longer imported (the arrows, which the other system also flags as keypad, still are), and settings migration 2 removes the mappings that only repeat what a US keyboard's key types (they do nothing on a US keyboard and type the wrong character on any other).
- **`\n` in a Terminal text mapping is a line feed**, as in other terminals (it was a CR, so an imported Shift+Enter → `\n` was a plain Enter; Claude Code takes LF as a new line, the shell as Enter); `\r` is the CR.
- **Terminal zoom by the character**: ❖+ / ❖− (and Ctrl+Shift+ / Ctrl+Shift+−) zoom by the character the key types, as in other terminals. Shortcuts go by the key's US position, so on a Latin American keyboard ❖− was ❖/ (nothing) and ❖+ was ❖] (next pane). `server/tests/terminal_keymap_test.mjs` checks the three (26 checks).
- **Memory in use** in Monitor, About, Settings → General and `lordos-sysreport` no longer counts the kernel's reserve of free pages. It was `MemTotal − MemAvailable`, and MemAvailable also leaves out the zone watermarks, which grow with the RAM and hold nothing: a 128 GB computer showed 2.3 GB in use for 1.2 GB really held (on a 4 GB Raspberry Pi the difference is a few tens of MB). It is now `MemTotal − MemFree − (Buffers + Cached + SReclaimable − Shmem)`, the way htop counts it, from one shared formula (`server/src/meminfo.h`, checked in `sysreport-test`); `lord.sys.info()` gives it as `memUsedKB`. Monitor's used, cache and free now add up to the total.
- **The login screen opens on the main display you chose.** It runs as its own system user and has no `displays.json`, so it always took the first connected connector: with three monitors on a Radeon RX 580 and the first DisplayPort output dark, the password had to be typed blind. The session shown on the monitor now tells `lord-sessiond` its main display's connector when it changes (`{"a":"display","main":"HDMI-A-1"}`, only `[A-Za-z0-9-]`, up to 31 characters); `lord-sessiond` keeps it in `/var/lib/lordos/main-display` (root's, 0644) and starts the login screen with `LORD_MAIN_DISPLAY`, which its display plan uses when that connector is connected (else the first connected one, as before). The connector, not the monitor's identity, because identical monitors can report the same EDID serial (three Samsung S27F350 here).
- **The hardware cursor on amdgpu** (Radeon RX 580): the cursor plane is created at the driver's `DRM_CAP_CURSOR_WIDTH/HEIGHT` (128 there) instead of 64×64. The driver scanned a 64×64 buffer as 128×128, squashing the arrow and showing colored stripes read from past the buffer.
- **"atomic remove_fb failed" kernel warnings** when the GPU path stops (rearranging displays, screen recording, a failed GPU frame): the dumb buffers now go on screen before the GPU's framebuffers are removed. Removing a framebuffer still scanned out makes the kernel try to turn its CRTC off, which amdgpu refuses with a WARNING and a tainted kernel.

### Known issues and limitations

- The voices (`lordos-voice-*`, 142 packages, 4.9 GB in all) come from LordOS's APT repository: Settings → AI → Voice downloads them once that repository is published with them. No voice model is in the `lordos` package or an image.
- Checked with tests and fixtures, not on the hardware: the Alps I2C touchpad (#43, #54, #67), automatic rotation with an accelerometer (#60), the GPU fan by hand on an AMD card, the menu bar and taskbar on three monitors, NVIDIA's CUDA/NVENC rows in Monitor → GPU, Tailscale and RustDesk from the Store, the Magic Mouse reconnecting at boot (#75), and the `iclouddrive` account's sign-in with a code (#65).
- The desktop LordOS Imager 0.8.8.6 (#73) is built and signed on the maintainer's machine; its Rust code was not compiled on the Linux build host.
- Lithuanian is a partial translation (about 9 % of the texts); the rest shows in English.
- Shells opened before the update keep their old terminal holder until they are reopened (the Terminal's size fix applies to new tabs).
- Logitech's special keys and buttons (MX Keys, MX Master 3) and their settings come in 0.8.8.7.

## [0.8.8.5-beta] - 2026-11-07

An update for 0.8.8 to 0.8.8.4 through Store → Updates and `apt`, with two new parts of the system: **Cloud**, your cloud storage accounts in Settings and in Files, built on rclone (which ships in its own package, `lordos-rclone`, rclone's official release, MIT), and **Machines**, virtual machines with their own app, from a downloaded system that installs without questions to snapshots, clones and migrating a machine from another app. Thanks to rclone's authors: Cloud talks to rclone only, over a socket no network can reach.

### Added

- **Cloud, the core** (docs/CLOUD.md; the interface comes separately). `lord-server` runs rclone's remote control for the session on a Unix socket only (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/lordos/cloud/rc.sock`, in a 0700 folder), with a random user and password per start given through a memory file, its configuration in memory, in a scope and firewall app of its own (`desktop:lordos-cloud`), restarted by itself after a crash (at most 5 times a minute). It is rclone's only client, and it can only send the 28 methods of a fixed table: nothing in LordOS can ask rclone to run a command or hand out its stored credentials. `lord.cloud` offers accounts (sign-in in the browser through `rclone authorize`, servers and object storage with their fields checked against rclone's own schema), mounts in `~/Cloud/<account>`, each file's status, **Keep on This Computer** and **Free Up Space** (never for a file that is open, changed here, waiting to go up or kept), freeing space by itself below a threshold, links where the provider has them, Pause and Resume, bandwidth limits and Restart. Tokens and passwords live in the keyring; the files in `~/.config/lordos/cloud` hold none. Signing in again, or adding with an existing account's name, updates that account. Add Account lists every provider the shipped rclone has, under rclone's own names, asked each time; rclone's own setup questions (a choice, a code) reach the person through `cloud.answer`; **Empty Trash** where the provider has one, **Measure** for providers without a quota, and deleting under `~/Cloud` removes in the cloud through the mount instead of making a `.Trash` folder there. Accounts waiting for a locked keyring (as after an automatic login) connect as soon as it is unlocked, without a restart; a folder kept busy by an open file is still unmounted (lazily) and a dead mount is cleared before mounting again; renaming an account and then signing in again updates it instead of saying the name is taken. An account only counts once it answers (a wrong password, port or address is said at once, and nothing is left behind); an SFTP server's host key and an https server's untrusted certificate are shown before the account is added and checked afterwards; no account option can run a program or name a local file; Recents and search no longer walk into cloud mounts, so a cloud server that stops answering can't freeze the desktop; renaming and moving work inside cloud folders; S3 links can be long and say they can't be withdrawn early. With a cloud server down, a file that isn't on this computer fails within seconds and the account says offline until the server answers again; logging out unmounts every cloud folder; a file changed both here and in the cloud keeps the cloud's version next to it as "name (cloud copy)" before ours goes up. SFTP accounts no longer probe the server's key again and again (OpenSSH locked people out after a few tries), a second account on the same server uses the key the first trusts, and the owner can accept a server's new key when signing in again; searching inside a cloud folder works without blocking the desktop. A file edited while the server was really down no longer overwrites what changed on the server meanwhile: every retry of an upload goes through the same check, and the server's version is kept as the cloud copy.
- **`lordos-rclone`**: rclone's official release binary v1.75.2 for amd64 and arm64, unmodified, at `/usr/lib/lordos/rclone/rclone`, apart from Debian's own package. `tools/iso/mkdeb-rclone.sh` checks the release's `SHA256SUMS` signature against rclone's pinned release key and the zip's hash. `lordos` depends on it instead of Debian's `rclone`, and Connect to Server uses it too.
- **Cloud, the interface** (docs/CLOUD.md, docs/FILES.md "Cloud"). Settings → **Cloud**, next to Sharing: every account with its space (an "All accounts" bar and one bar per account), what Cloud keeps on this computer with **Free Up Space** and the free-space threshold, bandwidth limits and pauses, the service (with **Restart**, **Show Log** and "only LordOS can reach it, on no network address") and About rclone. **Add Account…** opens the providers by kind (sign in with the browser, server, object storage, an encrypted folder) with search; signing in waits for the browser with the time left, **Open Sign-in Page Again** and the line saying the provider's page asks to allow rclone; a server's or a bucket's form is made from the provider's fields, secrets masked. An account's page has its space as a ring (files, other uses, trash), the folders kept on this computer, the links made from here, its options (folder name, files on demand, pause, unmetered networks only, upload limit), **Sign In Again**, **Remove Account…** (nothing in the cloud is deleted) and, under Advanced, **Use my own client ID**.
- Cloud: **verified providers** (docs/CLOUD.md 19). WebDAV, SFTP and S3 are verified on LordOS (checked end to end against local servers: `server/tests/cloud_providers_check.sh`); Add Account lists them first and every other provider rclone offers under **Not verified yet**, still addable, with **Tell Us on GitHub**. A browser sign-in provider not verified yet offers **your own app** (client ID and secret) right in the sheet, with how to make one; the same choice comes with Sign In Again. **Check This Account** on an account's page makes a hidden folder, sends 1 MiB up, frees it, brings it back by hash, makes a link where there are links and deletes it all, step by step, then gives a report with nothing personal to copy or send through a new GitHub issue form (`cloud-provider`).
- Cloud (docs/CLOUD.md 17.2, 18.1): **every provider rclone has**, asked fresh each time Add Account opens (a spinner until it answers, Try Again if it doesn't), under rclone's own names and descriptions; **rclone's questions** during setup (a code, a choice, a confirmation) as steps of the same sheet, with notes before the phone maker's drive (its extra encryption off, web access on, a code about every 30 days); **Empty Trash** for providers with a trash; **Measure** for storage without a quota, with Cancel; and in Files, **Move to Trash on a cloud item deletes it in the cloud** after asking ("It goes to its trash on <provider>" or "It can't be undone"), never making a trash folder inside the cloud.
- Cloud: the browser sign-in waits inside the Cloud pane, not in a sheet over the whole screen, so the browser stays usable; Cloud's sheets stay inside the Settings window; the sign-in page opens once.
- Cloud: the account form asks only what a provider needs (SFTP with a password or an SSH key file), with the rest under Advanced options and only passwords masked; an account page in two columns with an editable folder name; **Unlock Keyring…** where the keyring is locked after an automatic login, connecting the accounts at once; the account's own errors instead of "the service isn't running".
- Cloud: trusting a new SFTP server's key or a server's certificate by its fingerprint while adding it; errors shown with their details next to the field they concern, keeping what was typed; short provider names; Measure for S3.
- Cloud: a downloaded file no longer flickers back to "in the cloud"; space without a quota is never shown as a total ("Space not measured" until measured); WebDAV's preset defaults to plain WebDAV; when the service stops, accounts say so and the overview offers Restart.
- Cloud in Files: search inside a cloud account (in the background, saying when it stopped early); conflicts keep your version under the name and the cloud's as "(cloud copy)"; links show their real expiry (S3: up to 7 days); Get Info no longer waits on a cloud folder's size; a cloud folder with more than 5,000 items says it shows the first 5,000.
- Files: a **Cloud** section in the sidebar with each account's usage ring, a **Status** column and icon badges (in the cloud, coming down, on this computer, kept, going up, needs attention), **Keep on This Computer** / **Free Up Space**, **Copy Link**, **Share Link…** (expiry 1, 7 or 30 days or never, Stop Sharing), **Open on Website**, Get Info's cloud part, "N coming down · N going up", the account's space in the status bar and a message when a file isn't here and the cloud can't be reached. Files only in the cloud get no thumbnail, so browsing never brings them down. The file dialog lists the accounts too.
- A **Cloud item by the clock** while an account exists (a moving arrow while files transfer, a badge when an account needs you or changes wait) with each account's state, the recent transfers, **Pause All**, **Show in Files** and **Cloud Settings…**; notifications when an account needs a new sign-in, fills up with changes waiting, or a file changed on another device too.
- Machines (virtualization), alpha internals with no app yet: `lord-vm`, the sandboxed supervisor of one machine (QEMU over QMP, passt networking, cgroup limits, crash recovery), and `lord-vmdisplay`, its sandboxed picture and input helper over QEMU's D-Bus display, with a versioned `machine.json` and an isolation test that passes on the Raspberry Pi 5 and on amd64 (docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md 3.9).
- Machines app (alpha): a library of the machines in `~/Machines` with their state, a New Machine sheet (architecture, vCPUs, memory, disk, import a `.qcow2` disk image or boot from an ISO), and a window per machine with its picture scaled to fit, keyboard and mouse, Pause/Resume, Restart, Ctrl+Alt+Delete, Full screen, Shut Down and Force Off. It installs what it needs (QEMU, firmware, the display module, passt) and lets the account use hardware virtualization with one click each, shows why a machine stopped with its log, and recovers a machine whose supervisor died. Closing a machine's window shuts it down; Delete moves it to the Trash.
- Machines: over a machine's picture the pointer is the guest's own (an I-beam over a text field, its desktop's arrow), at the size the picture is shown; the host's arrow comes back over a text console and outside the picture.
- Machines, redesigned to the approved mocks: a Control Center of cards (each machine's picture, system, state, power and disk-activity lights, CPU and memory bars, disk use, and summary bars for machines running, memory and free space), a right-click menu, a five-step New Machine assistant that recognizes the system in an ISO, a Configure window (CPU, memory, network, disk size and the CD/DVD of a machine that is off, notes), a Logs window, and in each machine's window a toolbar and menus with resolution, Devices, Logs, Screenshot, Pause, Power, Configure and Full Screen, a floating bar in full screen and a page that says why a machine didn't start.
- Machines: **Eject ISO** in the library takes the installation ISO out of a machine that is off; the library marks a machine that still has one.
- Machines: the New Machine sheet installs what an emulated machine of the other architecture needs, and a machine that wouldn't fit in memory beside the ones already running (counting QEMU's own share, larger when emulated) isn't started, with a message that says how much is needed and left.
- Machines (beta): **Suspend** saves a machine's memory to its folder and the next start continues where it was (also when its window closes, if you choose); a saved session made by another engine, processor or machine type isn't loaded unless you ask, and can be discarded. **Keep Running** leaves a machine on without its window, **Start Without Window** starts one that way, and a running machine keeps the computer from sleeping (Configure → Startup and shutdown).
- Machines: **snapshots** with names and pictures, of every disk at once and of the memory when the machine runs, on a timeline (Take Snapshot, Go Back to This with a snapshot of now first, Delete), and starting a machine that is off from a snapshot with memory.
- Machines: **Clone** (a new machine beside the original, with its own identity) and **Duplicate** (the same identity, snapshots and saved session); on btrfs and XFS the copy shares the disk until either changes, on ext4 a Clone makes the original's disk a frozen shared base so both take only what changes, otherwise it's a full copy; Clone from Here makes a machine from one snapshot.
- Machines: the **Storage** window: what machines, disc images, the Trash and other files take on the volume, each machine with its clones and what deleting it would really free, its split into disks, saved session, snapshots and the rest, Reclaim Space (with an estimate first) and shared disks nobody uses any more.
- Machines: **profiles** (Productivity, Software Development, Testing, Design, Light desktop) sized for this computer in the assistant and in Configure; a resolution menu of the sizes that fit the display; **Record** the machine's own picture to a video in Screenshots.
- Machines: the **Shell**, the machine's serial console in a terminal pane marked as the guest's; **Logs** with an Overview that brings together state, sandbox, limits, network, engine, storage, recoveries and problems (Copy Report), level filter, Clear View, and the guest's journal.
- Machines: an opt-in **guest agent** (qemu-guest-agent in the guest, plus Machines' own private channel): its light on the card and the window's bar with what works now, a clean shutdown when the power button isn't heard, the guest's clock set after a pause or resume, the guest kept awake, its journal in Logs, and a **shared clipboard** (text, the directions you choose) through a small helper Machines installs in the guest.
- Machines: the CD/DVD can be changed while a machine runs (Devices → Choose Disc Image, Eject Disc).
- Machines: **Migrate from another app** brings over a machine made by another virtualization app (a `.vmx` or `.vmwarevm` bundle, a `.vbox` with its VDI or VMDK disks, a `.pvm` bundle with its `.hdd` disks, an `.ova` or `.ovf`, or one VMDK, VDI, VHDX or VHD disk) as a clone of itself: the same SMBIOS system UUID as its guest read it, every network card's MAC address and model, disk serials, BIOS or UEFI, vCPU topology, memory, disk sizes and boot order. A plan sheet says first what is kept, what changes and what can't come along (snapshots are flattened, a virtual TPM's keys stay behind, the guest may ask to activate its license again) and refuses a suspended, encrypted or still open machine; the import shows its progress and leaves the original untouched. The machine starts on devices every system has drivers for, and Configure → Disks switches it to the fast virtio ones once the guest has their drivers. Every file of the source is treated as hostile: names that leave its folder, links out, XML declarations and disks that depend on other files are refused, and disks are converted in a sandbox (docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md 6.22).
- Machines: **Download and install** in the New Machine assistant: cards for four Linux systems of this computer's architecture (amd64 or arm64; the other architecture behind *Other architecture…*), each with its release and size. Choosing one reads its maker's own SHA-256 list and takes the newest image of that release; the download shows its progress, can be stopped, and is kept only if its SHA-256 is the one in the list, then the machine is made from it and starts its installer. The list of systems is a data file (`assets/machines/systems.json`) that names, for each one, the maker's folder, its checksum list and the image's file name pattern, so it changes without code. Downloads are their own row in the Monitor and the firewall ("Machines downloads"), and a downloaded image is kept once for every account in `/var/lib/lordos/machines`.
- Machines: `tools/vm/bare-metal-gates.sh` runs the three release gates on a physical PC and writes one results file to attach.
- Machines: the download cards check each maker's **OpenPGP signature** on its checksum list before trusting any hash in it (Debian's `SHA256SUMS.sign`, Ubuntu's and Kali's `SHA256SUMS.gpg`, Fedora's clear-signed `CHECKSUM`), with the makers' keys pinned in the package and their fingerprints in `assets/machines/systems.json`, each compared with the one the maker publishes; a list that isn't signed, or whose signature doesn't verify with those keys, is refused and the card says why.
- Machines: a stopped or cut system download is **continued** where it stopped (Continue Download, or Create again) instead of starting over; a server that doesn't continue sends it again from the start, and the SHA-256 is still checked over the whole file.
- Machines: **Install without questions** for the Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora cards (the assistant's *Set up* step): account name, password, computer name, time zone and keyboard (taken from this computer) become the installer's own answer file (Debian preseed, Ubuntu autoinstall, Fedora kickstart), with the password only as a SHA-512 hash; the first start boots the installer's kernel from the ISO with the answers (inside its initrd, or on a small seed disk), and when the installer restarts the machine, Machines removes them and the ISO and starts the installed system. Ubuntu installs from its server image with the desktop added (without the browser package, which needs the snap system the installer doesn't have; a browser comes from the Store), Fedora from its network installer. Debian's preseed also answers the installed system's keyboard question (the layout's codes and its description).
- Machines: **Shut Down** asks the guest agent first when it's there, and presses the power button too if the guest is still running 10 s later; unattended installs bring the agent (and, on a console-only Debian, what honours the power button).
- Machines: the **Storage** window lists the downloaded systems (and stopped downloads) with their size and the machines whose CD drive has them, and removes one after asking (an administrator's action, refused while a machine using it runs; those machines' drives are emptied).
- Machines: an interrupted suspend, resume, snapshot, compaction or linked clone is finished or undone the next time the machine opens, and the machine's log says which; disks a killed machine left with leaked space are repaired. Release gates for disk integrity, failure recovery and leaks (100 start/stop cycles) are scripts in `server/tests/`.
- Machines: the network heals itself: when its helper (passt) ends, a new one is attached while the machine runs, the guest keeps its network card and address, and the window says it's back (measured: 4 to 7 ms to attach, the guest's next request 0.2 s after).
- Machines: the shared clipboard carries pictures and rich text both ways, beside text; a machine's pictures are re-encoded on this side and its rich text cleaned of scripts, event handlers and links that aren't web or mail, before any app sees them.
- Machines: **Record** has the machine's sound (its new sound card), in time with the picture.
- Machines: a **Clone** gets its own name and machine-id inside the machine and new SSH keys at its first start, through the guest agent (the name is editable in the Clone sheet; **Keep identity (exact copy)** skips it).
- Machines: shutting down, restarting or logging out saves running machines to disk (falling back to a clean shutdown, then off), and they resume where they were; a running machine keeps this computer from going to sleep when idle (visible to the system as an idle inhibitor), and the computer sleeps once none runs.

### Fixed

- Machines: the Snapshots window shows every snapshot, in rows that scroll, instead of one row cut off.
- Machines: the install page says how the download goes in words, and when the network doesn't answer says so (about a minute) instead of "No package source could be verified".
- Machines: finishing an interrupted revert at the next start no longer fails while the killed engine is still exiting.
- Machines: Esc pressed while one of a machine window's menus is open closes the menu without reaching the guest; downloads of the packages Machines needs give up in about a minute when the network doesn't answer, and the page says so instead of waiting forever; when the machine's network helper ends, it's replaced and the window says so.

- Machines on the Raspberry Pi 5: the machine's picture was see-through (the window below showed through the guest's black), because the GPU composition reads the picture's unused fourth byte as transparency. It is drawn opaque now.
- Machines: hardware virtualization allowed with **Allow** was taken away again at the next login of any kind (an SSH login is enough), because the system rewrites `/dev/kvm`'s access list for the screen's session only. LordOS now keeps it.
- Machines: a window of each running machine came back at the next login as one more empty Machines window. Only the library is restored now.
- Machines: after an installation from an ISO, taking the ISO out moved the network card to another PCI slot and the installed system came up without network. Every device of a machine now has a fixed slot.
- A picture shown scaled stayed black after it was replaced by one of another size: the scaled copy was freed but its old size kept, so it was never made again. It turned the Machines window black in full screen and could do the same to a Remote Desk session whose remote screen changed size.

### Security

- Machines: importing a disk image never reads another file: the image's format comes from LordOS's own check of its header (no backing file, no external data file), `qemu-img` runs sandboxed with the format named and backing turned off, and the system disk is checked again at every start.

### Known issues and limitations

- **Backups to Cloud** is not in this version: Backups still writes to disks and folders. It comes in a later update.
- Cloud is verified end to end with WebDAV, SFTP (password and key), S3, FTP and SMB servers and one browser sign-in provider; every other provider rclone has is listed under **Not verified yet**. An S3 account whose server stops answering says "syncing" instead of "offline" until the server is back.
- Machines' install without questions is checked from start to the installed desktop and its login with Debian 13.7 (about 28 minutes on 2 vCPU) and Ubuntu 26.04.1 (about 23 minutes); Fedora 45 runs its unattended install, and its first login is checked in the next update. On a first start the machine's window can stay on "Display output is not active" while the installer runs; the install goes on, and the next start shows the picture.

### Tests

- `cloud_test` (2162 checks, with ASan) and `tests/cloud_integration.sh` (195 checks against a local WebDAV server) pass on amd64 and the Raspberry Pi 5; Cloud's end-to-end bench ran against real WebDAV (http and https), SFTP (password and key), S3 (two servers), FTP and SMB servers. Machines' release gates (disk integrity, failure recovery, leaks) pass on the Raspberry Pi 5, nested amd64 and a physical Xeon server.

## [0.8.8.4-beta] - 2026-11-06

An update for 0.8.8 to 0.8.8.3 through Store → Updates and `apt`: the `lordos` package changes, with the 13 issues reported on GitHub since 0.8.8.3 (#28 to #40), a redesigned Remote Desk with sound, single sign-on for Fortinet VPNs and a Balance control for sound. Thanks to everyone who opened an issue. The installer's manual partitioning (#31) lives in the ISO and reaches people with the next one.

### Added

- **Calendar and Contacts: Add Account…** ([#32](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/32)). Under the calendar list and the address books, it opens Mail's account sheet in *CalDAV / CardDAV* mode with a **Service** choice: **Other server** (server URL, an optional separate contacts URL, user name, password, and Calendars / Contacts switches) or a built-in preset for a large provider's calendars and contacts, which asks only for the account's email and an **app-specific password** and fills in both addresses. A provider that allows its calendars and contacts only over OAuth is listed as **not available yet**, with *Add Account* disabled, until LordOS has a registered sign-in (what to register is in `docs/MAIL.md`). Passwords go to the keyring, as for mail accounts.
- Calendar and contacts sync: **contacts on their own address** (an account's `carddav` URL, with `/.well-known/carddav` discovery), and calendar and address book homes given as **absolute URLs on another host** of the provider (`pNN-…` hosts with an explicit `:443`), which the earlier discovery ignored. Accounts added before from Mail's preset for that provider get the contacts address once, so their contacts start syncing.
- Calendar and contacts sync: **conflicts keep your version.** When an event, to-do or contact changed both here and on the server (`412`), or the server refuses a change for good, the server's version stays in the synced calendar or address book and yours is saved, with a new UID, in a calendar, reminders list or address book on this computer; a notification ("Changed on another device too") names the item and where the copy is. A server that answers `401`, `408`, `429` or `5xx` to an upload no longer drops the change: it waits for the next sync. Tested against Radicale 3.5: offline edits of an event and a contact that changed on the server meanwhile, a new event uploaded, a contact deleted on the server, a cache from 0.8.8.3 updated without downloading anything again. `mail-test` adds checks for href resolution with hostile input, discovery answers, the sync plan, upload outcomes and the copy's new UID on a repeating event with a moved occurrence.
- Settings → Sound: a **Balance** control for stereo outputs (left ↔ right, with Center), for a weak channel on a headset adapter or one-sided hearing; it is kept with the output's volume and survives restarts.
- **Remote Desk, redesigned**: a sidebar with Favorites and Devices, cards with a picture of each computer's last session (taken a few seconds after every connection, kept only on this computer) or a list, sections by group, sort, a filter, search, and a ⋯ menu and a star on each card. Each connection opens its own window.
- Remote Desk: **saved credentials** (user name, optional domain and display name; the password only in the keyring) chosen per computer, or "Ask When Required"; a password typed at sign-in is saved only once the computer accepts it. Remote Desk Settings (❖,) with General, Resolutions, Credentials and Groups.
- Remote Desk: **sound from the remote computer** over RDP, played on this computer (or left on the remote one, or none), through LordOS's own audio path; the helper stays sandboxed.
- Remote Desk: reconnect when an RDP connection drops, administrative sessions, the remote desktop's scale, color quality, custom resolutions, swapped mouse buttons, and import and export of `.rdp` files (never with a password).
- Fortinet VPN with **single sign-on**: Settings → Network → VPN → Fortinet has an **Authentication** choice, **Username and password** or **Single sign-on** (the organization's sign-in page, often with an authenticator-app approval). Connecting opens that page in the default browser and Settings shows "Waiting for you to sign in on the organization's page…" with the time left (5 minutes), **Open sign-in page** and **Cancel**; the VPN connects when the sign-in finishes. LordOS waits for the page's return on 127.0.0.1 only, and checks the server's certificate before the page opens, so a certificate question comes first.
- Fortinet VPN: **more servers** (`+ Add server`, tried in order when one doesn't answer; the row says which one is in use, and a trusted certificate belongs to its server), a **client certificate** chosen with the file dialog (PEM certificate and private key, with an optional key password; kept root-only), a **Description** shown under the name, and with single sign-on a line saying the sign-in page opens in the default browser. PKCS#12 files and IPv6 inside the tunnel aren't available with the Linux client LordOS uses.
- Files: **zoom** for the icon and list views. The icon or thumbnail and the name grow or shrink together in seven steps (icons from 32 to 160 px, list rows from 20 to 48 px with thumbnails from 32 px up), with a slider between a small and a large square at the end of the status bar, View → Zoom In / Zoom Out / Actual Size, Ctrl and + (or =), Ctrl and −, Ctrl and 0, and Ctrl with the mouse wheel or a two-finger scroll. Each folder remembers its own size, separately for icons and list, in LordOS's settings with the folder's view and sort, so nothing is written into the folder ([#33](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/33)).
- Store → **Third-party apps** (until now "Third-party suites"): **VSCodium** (#38), the community build of the open source VS Code editor with telemetry turned off and the Open VSX extension registry, and **Brave Browser** (#39). Both install from their makers' signed repositories (amd64 and arm64) with the key LordOS pins; the Store says which repository it adds before adding it, as for the other apps from their makers. Brave's repository file uses the name Brave's own instructions use, so its keyring package doesn't make Brave's key trusted for every other source. Tested on an amd64 virtual machine: both sources added, verified and installed, and the following updates clean.
- Settings → Appearance → **Browsers: tabs in the title bar** now also changes Brave's profiles (#39). A new Brave profile starts with its "Classic" theme, whose window buttons are Brave's own and look like the Lord Classic theme's next to the other windows; with the switch on (or **Change them**, which now counts those profiles too) Brave shows LordOS's window buttons in its bar. In Brave itself the same is ☰ → Settings → Appearance → Theme → GTK. If Brave is open, its profiles change as soon as it quits.
- A saved IPsec, PPTP, OpenConnect or Fortinet VPN can be changed: **⋯ → Edit…** in its row while it's off (passwords left empty stay as they were). **Delete** is now a trash can button with a tooltip.
- Settings → Mouse & Trackpad has **one section per device**: **Pointer** with a **pointer size** (Small to Largest, on top of the display's scale, so a 200 % display can have a smaller pointer; Linux apps opened afterwards follow it), **Mouse** with speed, natural scrolling and a **primary button** (Left or Right), and **Trackpad** with a new **touch sensitivity** (Low, Medium, High) and **scrolling speed** next to its other settings ([#34](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/34)).
- **Basic image editing without another program** (issue #30). The Screenshots markup editor gains **Crop** (a rectangle with corner and edge handles, moved by dragging its inside, a rule-of-thirds grid and aspect presets **Free**, **Original**, **Square**, **16:9** and **4:3**; the wide presets follow a portrait picture as 9:16 and 3:4), **Resize** (width and height in pixels, **Keep proportions** on by default, up to 8192 per side), **Rotate left / right**, and two redaction tools to hide an area: **Pixelate** (blocks of about 1/60 of the picture's larger side, at least 8 pixels, so text in them can't be read) and **Redact** (a solid fill, black by default, in any of the palette's colors), next to the existing arrow, box, line, text and blur. ❖Z undoes annotations and then crops, resizes and turns (the last six steps), Enter applies a crop and Esc cancels it.
- The markup editor opens on **any picture**, not only right after a capture: **Markup** in Photos' viewer toolbar and in Files' Quick Preview (Space), for the raster pictures lord-media decodes (tested with PNG, PNG with transparency, JPEG, WebP and GIF; Photos plays GIFs as animations, so for a GIF it is Files' Markup). **Save** writes a PNG or JPEG back in place, in the same format, and the previous version goes to the **Trash** (so it can be restored); for other formats only **Save as copy** is offered, and it writes "name (edited).png" (or .jpg for a JPEG) next to the original, never over another file. A picture with transparency keeps it (in the editor and in the saved PNG), and a JPEG's orientation tag is applied when it opens. ❖S saves and ❖⇧S saves a copy.
- Photos → **Edit**: the crop now has corner handles, can be moved, and has the same aspect presets; a new **Size** (width × height, Keep proportions) scales the saved copy after the crop. The crop and the new size are applied by lord-media at the picture's full resolution, as before.
- The ISO's installer can **choose the partitions** ([#31](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/31)): a third way to install, beside **Beside what is there** and **Erase the disk**, on a GPT disk of a computer started through UEFI. The Disk step lists every partition with its size, file system, label and, for an EFI partition, the boot loader folders on it; each one has a menu: leave it, **/ (system)** (formatted, ext4, at least 8 GB), **/home** keeping its files (ext4, ext3, ext2, XFS or Btrfs) or formatted, **swap**, the **EFI partition** kept (LordOS adds its own folder) or formatted (only when chosen; it says the other systems' boot loaders are erased), or **Delete**. New partitions go in free space, including the space of partitions marked for deletion, with a size in GB and a role. A list of every change comes before going on, with "I have checked every change above" and, when data already on the disk would be lost, the disk's name typed; the Summary shows the same list. The root side reads the disk again and refuses a plan that no longer fits it (the table's GUID and entries' CRC are part of the plan), writes the table in one `sgdisk` call after a backup, proves byte for byte that only the planned entries changed (or puts the table back), mounts a kept `/home` only after the live user's folder is gone, keeps the user's own folder and files there (an earlier owner's files become the new user's, without following links), and installs grub in `EFI/LordOS` with its own firmware entry, as beside another system. Not yet: resizing, more than one disk, BIOS boot or MBR disks in this mode, encryption and LVM. Tested on sparse images with loop devices (54 checks, `server/tests/manualpart_loop.sh`) and with a full install through the wizard in a throwaway UEFI virtual machine, which then booted and kept the old `/home`'s files (docs/ISO.md, "Manual partitioning"). It reaches people with the next ISO (the installer lives in the ISO, not in the `lordos` update).

### Fixed

- Installing on Debian with `install.sh` failed with "this release's lordos needs lordos-hwdata, which is neither next to it nor in a configured repository" ([#40](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/40)): the update-only releases 0.8.8.1 to 0.8.8.3 shipped the `lordos` packages without `lordos-hwdata`, which `install.sh` takes from the same release. `lordos-hwdata` was added to the 0.8.8.3 release, and `tools/release/sign-release.sh` now refuses to sign a release folder with `lordos` packages and no `lordos-hwdata`.
- Sound played through LordOS (videos, Remote Desk, the remote camera) could start **muted** for good: the session manager keeps volume and mute per stream role, so one video muted in Settings → Sound muted every later stream of that role. LordOS's own streams now start unmuted and are left out of that restore; their volume is LordOS's.
- Remote Desk sound: **clicks** every few hundred milliseconds and the sound 1.3 s behind the picture. The remote computer sends a little faster than the output plays (measured 48010 Hz in, 47897 Hz out on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a USB adapter), so the buffer filled up and every packet lost its end. The sound now waits 100 to 200 ms at most, held there by a 0.4 % resampling trim nobody can hear; whole packets are skipped only past 500 ms (the burst at the start).
- Lord Classic: clicking the crown by the clock on the taskbar (Cleaner's quick panel) showed only a thin purple line under the taskbar, because the panel opened below the bar, off the screen. Panels of the items by the clock (Cleaner, the network item, third-party apps' menus and the camera/microphone indicators) now open toward the middle of the screen: above a taskbar at the bottom, below a bar at the top, and clear of the bar ([#29](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/29)).
- Touchpads on the bcm5974 driver (laptops up to 2015): a finger just hovering over the touchpad moved the pointer and made light taps miss, and a click could throw the pointer to the bottom-left corner. A touch now counts by its size, a contact that jumps further than a finger can in one frame is ignored, and pressing the touchpad no longer nudges the pointer ([#34](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/34)).
- Touchpad: after Space (opening or closing Quick Preview in Files) a finger put down right away didn't move the pointer until it was lifted. One key now pauses the touchpad for 200 ms (500 ms while typing), and a touch that began after the key moves the pointer once that time passes ([#34](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/34)).
- Touchpad: events for a contact slot the driver doesn't track were written to the previous slot, which could make the pointer jump; touchpads with 16 slots are now covered.

- Mail, Calendar and Contacts: a server certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint was shown and trusted **without its last byte** (31 of 32 bytes). It is now complete; certificates trusted before still match.
- Store search (#37): a search with several words found only names with all of them written exactly that way, so "vs code" didn't find Visual Studio Code. Now case and accents don't matter, the words can be in any order and are also tried joined or apart ("vs code" finds "vscode" and the other way round), and results with every word come first, then those with only some of them. While searching, Discover first shows **From the LordOS catalog** (the catalog's apps that match, from every section, even before their maker's repository is added), and catalog apps can be found by nicknames ("vscode", "vs code", "chrome", "ntfs"…). The catalog pages, categories, Installed and LordOS apps use the same search. Searching takes as long as before (24–33 ms over 75,016 packages).
- Store: a grid of cards whose summaries were long left a blank band under it (the layout measured the wrapped cards with their text's width instead of their card width); it showed under the catalog results of a search.
- Remote Desk said "That computer does not answer." for a computer saved with its name in the address field and its IP in **Domain**, which the old form invited. The form now has a single **Host** field ("Name or IP address, e.g. 192.168.1.20 or pc.local"), the domain moved to the credentials, computers saved that way are corrected once, and a name that doesn't resolve gets its own message: "Couldn't find “name” on the network. Check the name or use its IP address."
- Fortinet: a server whose certificate couldn't be verified (often one that sends an incomplete certificate chain, which other systems complete on their own) showed only `fortinet: ERROR: <long hex number>`. Settings now says "This server's certificate couldn't be verified", with the fingerprint (`AB:CD:…`), who it was issued to and by, and **Trust** / **Cancel**; Trust saves it as the connection's trusted certificate and connects again. If the server later shows another certificate, it says the certificate changed. A trusted certificate typed in capitals or with `:` now works too (openfortivpn compares lowercase only).
- Mail over IMAP showed some special folders twice (two Sent, two Junk) and listed every folder the user created flat, right under Trash, on servers that keep folders under `INBOX.` (Dovecot/Courier style) (#28). Each account now has at most one Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Archive, Junk and Trash: a folder the server flags with SPECIAL-USE always wins, a name ("Sent Items", "Spam"…) counts only when no folder is flagged and only at the top level or right under INBOX, and look-alikes such as "Sent Messages" stay ordinary folders with their own names. Servers that don't flag their folders are also recognized by the usual French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and German names ("Envoyés", "Corbeille", "Indésirables", "Papelera", "Lixeira", "Cestino", "Papierkorb"…), including names the server sends in IMAP's modified UTF-7. The sidebar shows the real tree: special folders first, then every other folder under its parent, one indent per level ("Work → Clients → Acme"), without showing the `INBOX.` prefix as a level; a child of a special folder (Trash → Old) stays under it. Checked against Dovecot with the `INBOX.` prefix and `.` separator and with `/` and no SPECIAL-USE flags; unit tests for both the role choice and the tree.
- Fortinet: openfortivpn's common failures are readable messages instead of its raw output: wrong username or password, server unreachable, secure connection failed, signed in but no VPN for the account, sign-in not completed in time.
- **Security:** closing the lid or pressing the power button (or anything else that puts the computer to sleep) did not lock the screen, even with Settings → Energy → **Require password after the display turns off** set to **Immediately**: waking the computer showed the unlocked desktop, however long it had slept ([#36](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/36)). The lock only followed the inactivity timer, whose clock stops while the computer sleeps, and nothing listened for the system going to sleep. Now the session on the screen holds a short sleep delay from systemd-logind (a "delay" inhibitor, which logind allows to anyone) and, when logind announces the sleep, locks first: the computer sleeps only once the desktop has left the screen (at most 4 s), so it wakes on the login screen. With a longer delay (5 s to 1 h) the screen locks on waking when the computer slept that long or longer, counting the time the display was already off; with **Never** sleep isn't delayed at all. Also, a key or touch that arrived just as the lock was due could cancel it; a lock that is due now always goes first.
- The system bus connection of a session could watch only four services and BlueZ, power profiles and polkit already took them, so a fifth was silently ignored; it now takes eight and says so in the log when full.

## [0.8.8.3-beta] - 2026-11-05

An update for 0.8.8, 0.8.8.1 and 0.8.8.2 through Store → Updates and `apt`: only the `lordos` package changes, with the fixes and ideas reported on GitHub since 0.8.8. Thanks to everyone who opened an issue. It also brings everything in 0.8.8.2 (Italian, preferred languages, the Raspberry Pi 500 in the Imager), which was not published on its own.

### Added

- The system file dialog has a **List / Thumbnails** switch in its toolbar, so pictures can be chosen by how they look (Settings → Wallpaper, Notes' images and every other app that uses the dialog). A dialog that takes only pictures opens in Thumbnails; the choice is remembered. Thumbnails load in the background for the files in sight, and other files show their type icon ([#22](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/22))
- Desktops: **rename** a desktop by double-clicking its name in the Overview, from its right-click menu (**Rename…**) or in Settings → Desktop & Dock → Names; the name shows in the indicator, the Overview, Move to Desktop and the window lists, and an empty name goes back to "Desktop N". **Reorder** desktops by dragging them along the Overview's strip (or **Move Left** / **Move Right** in the same menu); their windows move with them. Names and order are kept across sessions ([#15](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/15))
- An **on-screen level indicator** for the volume, mute, screen brightness and keyboard-light keys: a rounded translucent panel near the bottom of the screen with an icon and a segmented bar, shown for 1.5 s after each press (a held key keeps it up), in Lord Flow and Lord Classic, light and dark. With Reduce motion it appears and goes without a fade ([#24](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/24)).
- Settings → Energy: shorter sleep times, 10 and 20 min on the power adapter and 5 and 10 min on battery ([#17](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/17)).

### Fixed

- Screenshots: a window picked with ❖⇧4 then Space, or an area, came out cropped at a display scale above 100 % (the selection was in logical pixels and the capture is at the display's full resolution). The whole window is captured now, at any scale ([#19](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/19)).
- A maximized window clicked to bring it forward shrank to its own size: the slightest pointer movement during the click counted as dragging it out. It now has to move a few pixels with the button held first, in both themes and for apps that draw their own title bar ([#19](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/19)).
- A full-screen screenshot showed a GPU-drawn app's window (a third-party browser, for example) as an empty frame with its shadow: its content is now read back from the GPU for the capture ([#19](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/19)).
- Mail: some messages, mostly newsletters, didn't open and showed **bad-json**. Their HTML layout nests tables several levels deep, and the check that lord-server makes on every reply of the mail helper stopped at 32 levels. It now accepts the depth the HTML view can produce. Also: a NUL byte can no longer cut a message's text short, a reply too large to show says so ("This message is too large to show here") instead of breaking the event queue, and a message that still can't be shown says so in your language ([#18](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/18)).
- A black screen after logging in again when the screen had locked by itself: the session missed the notice that it had left the screen (it arrived together with the closed connection) and then ignored the screen when it was lent back. The notice is now read before the connection is closed, and a session lent the screen again while it thinks it is still shown leaves the old one first.
- After an update that changes the Store's package list format (0.8.8.2 did, for Italian names), the Store showed only the LordOS catalog until the next check, up to 5 minutes later and only with automatic checks on. The list is now rebuilt 20 seconds after login whenever it can't be read.
- Store: switching category, page or search kept the previous list's scroll position, so a short category could look empty. Each page and each app's page now opens at the top, and back from an app returns to where the list was. The same fix (a `resetKey` on the SDK's `ScrollView`) applies to Settings sections, System Information, Help articles, Monitor tabs, Characters, Backup folders and Files folders ([#20](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/20))
- With "Require password after the display turns off", the login screen turned the display back on and kept it on, and the computer never went to sleep. Now the screen stays off when it locks, the password is asked for when you wake it, the lock screen turns the display off again after the same time, and the computer still sleeps at the chosen time. A sleep time shorter than the lock time also locks first ([#23](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/23)).
- The battery percentage in the menu bar and in Settings → Energy didn't follow the battery on laptops whose battery reports no change events while it discharges, so the low-battery notices at 20 %, 10 % and 5 % never came. It is now read again every 30 seconds ([#25](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/25)).
- Wi-Fi that showed as connected after the computer woke from sleep but carried nothing until the card was turned off and on. LordOS's network service now hears the computer wake: wired connections confirm their address right away, and each Wi-Fi connection is checked a few seconds later (associated, link, address, and the router answering). If it isn't working, it re-associates and renews its address, and if that isn't enough it turns the card off and on by itself, as you had to. Every step is in the log. Needs confirming on the reported hardware ([#14](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/14))

## [0.8.8.2-beta] - 2026-11-04

An update of 0.8.8 and 0.8.8.1 through Store → Updates and `apt`: only the `lordos` package changes. There are no new images: the 0.8.8 ISO, OVA and Raspberry Pi image update to this from the Store.

### Added

- **Italian** as a built-in language ([#16](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/16)): the whole interface, every app, error messages, the login screen, remote desktop's pages, the LordOS Imager, emoji names (CLDR 45), country names (CLDR), Italian dates and numbers (`it_IT`, `it_CH`), and the home folders in Italian for new users (Scrivania, Documenti, Scaricati…). The Store shows apps' Italian names when their metadata has them.
- Settings → Language & Region: **Preferred languages**, a list with English, Español and Português and a **+** to add Français, Italiano or an installed pack (it becomes the first, LordOS's language), **−** to remove one and arrows to reorder them. When a text isn't translated, the next language in the list is used before English. The **+** list also names languages LordOS isn't translated into yet, and says where to ask for them.
- The login screen's language button shows a globe and the language's name; its menu lists English, Español and Português first and then the other languages LordOS ships.
- LordOS Imager: **Raspberry Pi 500 supported**. The Device step is now a Raspberry Pi card and, after it, **Which Raspberry Pi?** with the Pi 5 and the Pi 500 (the same image). With the Pi 500, Cooling has no fan, case or overclock to choose, since it has no fan header. Thanks to Steve Sande for testing it.
- LordOS Imager: the new system's language is chosen with chips (English, Español, Português, and "+ More languages" for the others). A language the chosen image can't start in is shown disabled with the first image version that can (Italian from the 0.8.9 images). The desktop app's own language is a globe at the bottom of its sidebar.

### Fixed

- The desktop LordOS Imager didn't list a card in a laptop's built-in SD card slot: the system reports that slot
  as an internal disk, and the Imager only looked at external ones. It now lists physical disks with removable media
  too; the internal SSD and other fixed internal disks are still never shown. Reported by a user with an SD
  card that showed up in other writers (`diskutil`: "internal, physical", FAT32, 15.9 GB).

## [0.8.8.1-beta] - 2026-11-03

An update of 0.8.8 through Store → Updates and `apt`: only the `lordos` package changes. There are no new images:
the 0.8.8 ISO, OVA and Raspberry Pi image stay current and update to this from the Store.

### Added

- **Unattended install** ([docs/UNATTENDED.md](docs/UNATTENDED.md)): the live ISO's new boot entry, Install automatically,
  never the default, installs LordOS from `lordos-auto.conf` on a disk labelled `LORDOSAUTO`, with install-run's own
  code. The file names the disk and its exact size, says `erase = yes` for an erase install, and carries the password
  only as a yescrypt or SHA-512 hash; it can add an SSH key, automatic login and what to do afterwards. Anything missing
  or wrong stops it before any disk is touched, and the live system starts as usual.
  `tools/iso/make-auto-disk.sh` makes the small ISO with the file for a virtual machine.
- Store: **Third-party suites**, a section for open source suites from other projects that are worth having, starting
  with ArtCraft (its launcher 0.14.0, which installs, updates and opens the Craft apps: a word processor, spreadsheets,
  PDF tools, photo editing and more). The launcher's own `.deb` is mirrored with a pinned SHA-256, for amd64 and arm64.
- The system file dialog, drawn like Files, everywhere: an isolated app's open and save prompt, Passwords (on its lock
  screen too) and Notes use it now, so they reach the local disks mounted for you, and saving asks before replacing a
  file. Passwords suggests English file names.

### Fixed

- Settings → Desktop & Dock → Desktops showed the four finger swipe as on when it had never been changed, while it is
  off by default (as Mouse & Trackpad showed it).

### Known issues and limitations

- **The unattended install needs a new ISO:** the program is in this package, but the boot entry that starts it is
  on the live ISO, and there is no 0.8.8.1 ISO. It comes with the next images. Tested so far: an erase install from a
  BIOS virtual machine; not yet the free space mode, UEFI, a USB stick or the arm64 ISO.
- **Not tested in this update:** the FileChooser portal while two users' sessions start at the same moment.
- Screen sharing on a Raspberry Pi 5 still drops video frames; the work on it continues for 0.8.9.

### Upgrading

- **From 0.8.8:** Store → Updates shows "LordOS 0.8.8.1 is available" with these notes; update, then restart when
  it says "Restart required". With `apt`: `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`.

## [0.8.8-beta] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- **Screen-sharing API** ([docs/SCREEN-SHARING.md](docs/SCREEN-SHARING.md)): a separate door for an app the launcher started, with its own socket and parser, a system prompt on first use, grants in a root-owned file, an indicator with Stop on screen before any frame leaves, and ⌃⌥⇧Esc in C. It ends in `lord-server` the moment the session locks or leaves the monitor, delivers no picture and takes no input until the person signs in again, and doesn't exist on the login screen. One door at a time per session: while a share runs a remote desktop sign-in is told to wait, and a connected remote desktop viewer keeps a share from starting.
- **Packaged apps with a companion** ([docs/PACKAGED-APPS.md](docs/PACKAGED-APPS.md)): a third, root-owned app root, `/usr/lib/lordos-apps/<id>/`, for a package a Verified author signed, checked at every load. Such an app may run one signed helper program in a strict sandbox, started with the app and stopped with it, and may use the screen-sharing API with `screen-share` and `remote-input`.
- Live media for packaged apps: a companion hands what it receives to a sandboxed decoder, and the app shows it in a `<MediaView>`, with sound. The camera and microphone of a call come back through the same link, behind the same permissions and indicators.
- **An item by the clock for any app**, with the `status-item` permission: the app describes it, the system draws it.
- Store: a Remote access section, shown once the catalog has an app in it.
- Settings → Wallpaper: your own PNG or JPEG picture on the desktop and on the login screen, in every theme. It is converted by a process running as you, and the login screen gets its own copy in a system folder, so it never reads your home ([#13](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/13)).
- Install in free space: on a GPT disk with an EFI partition, booted through UEFI, the installer can add LordOS beside what is there, as one new partition, leaving every existing partition as it was ([#7](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/7)).
- An OVA image for amd64 (`lordos-<version>-amd64.ova`, `tools/iso/build-ova.sh`): open it in VirtualBox or VMware. It starts with 4 CPUs and 4 GB of memory, the minimum for a virtual machine; 16 GB is the ideal with many apps. Until you create your own account in the installer's screens on its first boot, it starts in a setup session whose administrator account has no password, reachable only at the machine's own console: finish that step before leaving it running.
- French is now a built-in interface language, selectable in Settings, in the installer, on the login screen and from a boot entry ([#5](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/5)).
- App switcher: 1 to 9 go straight to an app, the selected app's windows show live in a row, Z or the key under Esc moves through them; Settings → Keyboard chooses the keys, which apps show, size and look.
- Settings: Desktops in Desktop & Dock (how many, the Ctrl arrows, the four finger swipe), and Mouse & Trackpad always shows, with a mouse's speed and wheel direction.
- Terminal: ❖+click or Ctrl+click on a web address opens it in the default browser.
- `lordos-issue`: what a bug report needs, with names and addresses replaced, ready to paste into an issue, with an integrity check. `lord-server --check-apps` shows each app's signature state.
- Broadcom Wi-Fi firmware on the ISOs, so a BCM43602 card works from the live system ([#3](https://github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues/3)).
- `.local` names resolve: `libnss-mdns` on the images and in the `lordos` package's recommended list.


### Changed

- The system file dialog looks and works like Files, with Files' own icons, sidebar, list and path: Home, the user's folders and the local disks mounted for the user on the side, name, date and size in the list, a click selects and a double click opens, and Enter, Esc and the arrows work. Local disks are new here: apps that ask through the dialog can now be given a file on one, when the person picks it.
### Fixed
